NOTE: This equipment has been tested and found to comply with the limits for a Class A digital device, pursuant to Part 15 of the FCC
Rules, CISPR 32 and EN 55032. These limits are designed to provide reasonable protection against harmful interference when the
equipment is operated in a commercial environment. This equipment generates, uses, and can radiate radio frequency energy. If the
equipment is not installed and used in accordance with the guidelines in this document, the equipment may cause harmful interference to

Intended audience
This document is intended for the following users:
• Administrators
• Operators
• Maintenance personnel
The 1830 PSS products are meant to be installed, operated, and maintained by personnel who
have the knowledge, training, and qualifications required to safely perform the tasks assigned to
them. The information, processes, and procedures contained in the 1830 PSS product
documentation are intended for use by trained and qualified personnel.
How to use this document
This document is divided into six parts and an appendix:
• Part I: “General information” describes the basic details about the command line interface
supported on 1830 PSS-4/4II/8/16II/16/32/8x/12x/24x, 1830 PSI-4L, and 1830 PSI-8L, including
command syntax and structure, connectivity, navigation, and help.
• Part II: “System and equipment management” describes the general CLI commands including
security, DCN, database, and general equipment management.
Note: The equipment management of all cards is described in Part II: “System and equipment
management”. The functional aspects of core, optical transport (OT), and other (OTH) cards are
described in Part III: “Card (core, OT, OTH) management”. The configuration and management
details of packet transport are described in Part VI: “Packet transport service management”.
• Part III: “Card (core, OT, OTH) management” describes the CLI commands related to the
functional aspects of the core, optical transport (OT), and other (OTH) cards.
• Part IV: “Alarm and performance monitoring” describes the CLI commands related to alarm and
performance monitoring.
• Part V: “Connection and protection management” describes the CLI commands related to
connection and protection.
• Part VI: “Packet transport service management” describes the CLI commands related to the
configuration and management of packet transport.
• Appendix A, “Reference tables” provides additional details including shelf/slot ranges, OTDR-
supported cards, OTDR profiles, ECC slot ranges, port name to port number mappings, PM
counters, channel frequency details, user service interfaces, and common value definitions.

1.2 Command Line Interface (CLI)
1.2.1 Using the Command Line Interface (CLI)
The command line interface (CLI) is a line-oriented user interface that runs on the network element.
You access the CLI using a terminal device connected to the network element. The CLI provides
commands that allow you to configure, manage, and monitor the network element, the network
element interfaces, and the services running on the network element.
1.2.2 Syntax rules
Table 1-1, “CLI syntax rules” (p. 124) describes syntax rules for CLI.
Table 1-1 CLI syntax rules
Syntax format Description Example
name
Text without any brackets or braces (can be in bold) are required
items. Enter these command line arguments exactly as written.
config card
show interface irdm32
<...>
Text inside angle brackets (can be in italics) are variables. Enter a
valid value at the command line.
<cardtype>
<holdoff>
<port-aid>
<otun>
{...}
Text inside brackets is a value or a parameter set. One of the items
must be entered.
{value1 | value2 | value 3}
{value1 | <value2> | value 3}
{laserOn | laserOff}
{enable | disable}
[...] Text inside square brackets are optional keywords or variables.
[detail]
[<power>]
name1 | name2
Text separated by a vertical bar identifies mutually exclusive items.
Choose one command line argument.
{enable | disable}
[laserOn | laserOff]
{provisioner | observer | crypto}
[<hours> | <minutes> | help]
.. Two dots indicate a range of numerical values. {1..10}
1.2.3 Case sensitivity
You can enter characters from the keyboard in upper or lower case. Depending on the type of data
entered, the case is interpreted differently.
Commands
CLI commands are not case-sensitive. You can enter CLI commands in upper, lower, or mixed
case. For example, command, CoMmAnD, and COMMAND are interpreted as the same command.

Strings
Any strings you enter as command variables, such as network element or service descriptions, are
case sensitive. That is, This is a string is not the same as This is a STRING. Strings
containing space(s) must be surrounded by quotation marks.
1.2.4 General CLI command structure
Table 1-2, “General CLI command structure” (p. 124) describes the organization of the command
descriptions.
Note: The packet transport service CLI commands use the structure described in Table 1-3,
“Packet transport service CLI command structure” (p. 126).
Table 1-2 General CLI command structure
Section Heading Description
Purpose Describes the use or effect of the command and discusses the command's functionality.
Command Access Level
Lists the user privileges necessary to access the command or parts of the command and describes
the impact of executing the command.
User privileges are Administrator, Provisioner, Observer, and Crypto.
Input Format
Illustrates the command syntax. The first line defines the basic syntax with parameters that need to
be entered before one of the parameters or sub-commands on the following lines can be entered.
Input Parameters
Lists all parameters or sub-commands listed in the Input Format. Depending on the parameter or sub-
command definition, the following explanations are given:
• Syntax: specifies the syntax of this parameter which can be entered.
• Values: specifies ranges or explicit dedicated value-sets of this parameter.
• Default: specifies the initial value at creation time of this parameter.
• Description: describes the usage and side effects of this parameter.
• Restrictions: specifies if this parameter is supported/not supported on certain cards or shelf types.
Output Parameters
Describes the output parameters and parameter values shown in the output response. If there is no
Output Parameters section, use the example section for the returned parameters.
Examples Provides one or more illustrations on the use of the command.
Related Commands
Provides a list of closely related or prerequisite (commands that must be executed before the
described command can be executed) commands.
General CLI hierarchy
Most of the CLI commands are grouped by function into the following major hierarchical categories:
config - Commands in the config hierarchy allow you to configure the network element and network
services.
show - Commands in the show hierarchy allow you to view the current network element
configuration.
tools - Commands in the tools hierarchy provide miscellaneous tools useful in using the CLI.

configuration. These commands have a command access level of Administrator, Provisioner,
Observer.

commands have a command access level of Administrator, Provisioner.

1.3 Connecting to a network element
1.3.1 1830 PSS interfaces
The 1830 PSS provides four configuration interfaces:
• Command Line Interface (CLI)
• Transaction Language 1 interface (TL1)
• Web User Interface (WebUI)
• Open Agent via NETCONF (NETwork CONFiguration protocol) and gRPC (Remote Procedure
Call)
This section describes how to connect locally to a Network Element to use the CLI. For more details
of the Open Agent solution, refer to 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS) Release 24.12 NETCONF/
gRPC Interface Guide, 3KC-70118-RBAA-TCZZA.
1.3.2 Connecting to 1830 PSS-4
Table 1-4, “Connecting to 1830 PSS-4” (p. 127) summarizes the methods of connecting to the NE
using a CLI session when PSS-4 is the main shelf of the NE.
Table 1-4 Connecting to 1830 PSS-4
Interface Information
CRAFT
(on E4EC)
The console port shares the CIT/CRAFT RJ45 connector and is used to connect serially to the NE.
Recommended for local access to the NE only.
CIT
(on E4EC)
The craft interface port shares the CIT/CRAFT RJ45 connector and is used to connect a telnet or SSH
session via LAN to the NE.
Recommended for local access to the NE only.
OAM
(on E4EC)
The operation and maintenance port and the other extension and auxiliary ports are RJ45 connectors
and can be used to connect a telnet or SSH session via LAN to the NE.
These ports must be configured first before using them for local or remote access connections. The
ports support auto-sensing for cable type (straight through or cross over) and connection speed.
The LAN ports are 10/100-BaseTX.
Directly connect to the 1830 PSS-4 shelf using the CRAFT (RJ45) serial port
You can connect directly to the network element to access the CLI using the serial CRAFT (on
shared CIT/CRAFT RJ45, pin7/8 for Rx/Tx, pin4 GND for RS232) port via your preferred serial
terminal emulator.
Perform the following steps:
1. Configure your terminal emulator connection settings to 38,400 baud, 1 stop bit, no parity.
2. Using a serial cable, connect the CRAFT (RJ45) port to your laptop.
3. Open a terminal session

Connecting to a network element
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 127
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Directly connect to the 1830 PSS-4 shelf using the CIT (RJ45) LAN port
You can connect directly to the network element to access the CLI using the CIT (on shared CIT/
CRAFT RJ45, pin1/2/3/6) LAN port and a telnet or SSH session.
The CIT port autodetects the LAN cable type (straight through connected or cross over connected)
and supports a DHCP Server. When a connection (for example, using a laptop) is detected, the NE
sends out an internal IP address in response to the DHCP request from the laptop. The CIT port
supports local management of the NE.
The default IP address of the CIT port is 172.16.0.1/24 (configurable).
The DHCP server assigns 172.16.0.2/24 to the PC connected to the port.
Note: If you are using a terminal emulator application, check that the Return key sends ASCII
code LF or CRLF.

1.4 CLI navigation
1.4.1 Overview
Since CLI is a text-based interface, all interaction with the CLI is through the keyboard. The CLI
provides keyboard shortcuts, string completion, and help functions to make using the CLI as simple
as possible. Navigate through the menu hierarchy and enter commands by typing the command
name and pressing the Enter key.
1.4.2 Keyboard shortcuts
Table 1-15, “CLI keyboard shortcuts” (p. 139) lists the keyboard shortcuts you can use to make the
most effective use of the CLI. All of the actions are relative to the current position of the cursor.
Previous characters are to the left of the cursor. Backwards moves the cursor to the left. Forwards
moves the cursor to the right.
Table 1-15 CLI keyboard shortcuts
To do this Press these key(s)
Complete the command from the typed abbreviation Tab
List the available choices ?1
Move up one level in the command hierarchy .. or exit
Delete the previous character Backspace
Go to the beginning of the line Ctrl-A
Go to end of the line Ctrl-E
Go forward one character Ctrl-F
Go backward one character Ctrl-B
Delete the current character Ctrl-D
Delete all characters to the beginning of the line Ctrl-U
Delete all characters to the end of the line Ctrl-K
Delete the previous word Ctrl-W
Transpose the current character with the previous character Ctrl-T
Go to the previous line in history buffer Ctrl-P
Go to next line in history buffer Ctrl-N
Go to the top level in the command hierarchy (main menu) Ctrl-Z or mm
Execute the given command in the other CLI environment and return
to the current environment
//<command>
Notes:
1. In CLI, “?” is a hidden key that displays command options/help when entered. If “?” is entered in the middle
of a command, the possible command options are displayed. If “?” is entered after a command, help is
displayed for that command. Therefore, “?” is not an allowed symbol in any CLI command.

CLI navigation

1.4.3 Command history
Use the history command to display a listing of the last 100 commands. You can enter this
command at any level in the hierarchy. For example, the command history displays the last 100
commands. The command history 25 displays the last 25 commands.
Note: Using Ctrl-P (previous line) and Ctrl-N (next line), you can scroll through the commands
in the history buffer:
• ^P - Goes to the previous line in history buffer.
• ^N - Go to next line in history buffer.
You can recall previously entered commands using the ! notation familiar to UNIX users, as follows:
• !! - Recalls the last command.
• !n - Recalls the command at line n.
• !string - Recalls the most recent command starting with string.
Note: In some cases, the command history will fill in optional parameters that were not given
in the original command. Therefore, the history can be used to reveal details of optional
parameters, for example, a card type in a slot.
Example 1:
# show interface 1/12/cit
... display details of interface
# ^P
# show interface 32ec2 1/12/cit
Example 2:
# show card 1/22
Error: no configurable attributes for that location
# history 2
50: show card usrpnl 1/22
51: history 2
1.4.4 Command and keyword expansion
Commands and keywords can be entered partially. They will be expanded automatically as long as
they can be uniquely identified in the command tree.
# con int
(config-interface)#
However, it is encouraged to use the full keyword, or perform command completion (Tab), so the
command is unambiguous.

1.4.5 Confirmation yes/no
Some commands request a confirmation to continue after pressing the Enter key (yes/no).
Example:
# config admin resetNE warm
WARNING: You are about to perform a warm system restart.
Enter 'yes' to confirm, 'no' to cancel:
Note: To bypass the confirmation prompt, “yes” may be entered as part of the command.
Example:
# config admin resetNE warm yes
System is preparing to restart...
1.4.6 Force directive
Some commands include a force directive which suppresses specific errors that occur when a
command is repeated, such as for:
• Attempts to issue an add command using the same settings as already configured will not be
flagged as an error.
• Attempts to delete a non-existent entity (for example, attempting to delete a route that has
already been deleted) will not be flagged as an error.
In addition, for commands that request a confirmation after pressing the Enter key (yes/no) and
also support the force directive, the force directive bypasses the confirmation prompt as though
the operator had included the yes directive at the end of the command line.
The force directive may be used in scripting to suppress unnecessary error messages.
See the descriptions of the commands that support the force directive for details about, and
examples of, the effects of the force directive.
1.4.7 Automatic card name expansion
In several CLI commands, the <card-name> of the addressed equipment entity is required. In some
commands, the <card-name> is optional. If the system can identify the provisioned card, the system
can populate the name automatically. Although <card-name> is not defined as optional in the input
format of the following commands, these commands support automatic card name expansion:
• config card <card-name> <slot-aid>
• show card <card-name> <slot-aid>
• config interface <card-name> <port-aid>
• show interface <card-name> <port-aid>
For these commands, the command history can populate the optional parameters if they are not
included in the original command.

1.4.8 Copying and pasting multiple commands
You can keep frequently-used commands in a text file and paste them into the CLI interface. If the
file contains multiple commands, the commands are executed individually.
1.4.9 Entering credentials
There are CLI commands that prompt for credentials such as a password, passphrase or secret
key. These commands will prompt for a password, and some commands will prompt again to verify
the password. In all cases, the password is not revealed (not echoed) when entered.
Example of two prompts:
# config admin user add NewUser observer
New password:
Verify Password:
With CLI commands that have a single password prompt, the password can optionally be entered
on the command line and will be seen clear text.
Example with prompt:
# config software server userid swUser
Enter password:
Example of password on command line:
# config software server userid swUser SystemSoftwarePasswd

1.5 CLI help functions
1.5.1 Purpose
The CLI provides the following types of help:
• question mark
• help
1.5.2 Question mark (?) help
You can enter a question mark at any time when using the CLI to get a listing of the currently
available options.
Note: If “?” is entered in the middle of a command, the possible command options are
displayed. If “?” is entered after a command, help is displayed for that command. The “?” is
not an allowed symbol in any CLI command.
For example:
# config software ?
server Configure the software download server
upgrade Change system software
# show acl_p?
acl_pattern acl_pattern6 acl_port acl_port6
# show acl_p
1.5.3 Help command
You can display available help topics by entering the help command at the CLI main menu. To find
all commands that contain a particular keyword, enter the help command, followed by the keyword.
For example, to find all commands related to the usrpnlr or 11star1, enter the command help
usrpnl and help 11star1. The following output is generated:
Example for usrpnl:
# help usrpnl
config database usrpnlRepl
Recover from an interrupted User Panel replacement procedure
config interface usrpnl
Configure USRPNL ethernet port parameters
config usrpnl
Configure user interface panel properties
show interface usrpnl
Display USRPNL parameters

1.6 CLI output
1.6.1 Overview
The text-based CLI output structure is “keyword : value”. In many cases, the keyword is descriptive
text that explains the parameter. If the output is a list, the CLI output is presented in a table.
1.6.2 Parameter output
The configuration parameter of a single entity in a node is reported in the form “keyword : value”.
The following example displays the shelf description:
# config shelf 1 description "12345678901234567890"
# config shelf 1 description
Shelf description: 12345678901234567890
1.6.3 Table output
When information for several entities is requested, the CLI displays the output data in a table.
Examples display all shelves in a node, all slots in a shelf, or all cross-connections in a node.
In tables, the column widths are fixed and do not adjust automatically based on content length. If
the displayed content exceeds the column width, a tilde (~) character is displayed at the of the
content indicating additional data that is not displayed.
The following example includes a shelf description that exceeds the column width in the show
shelf * command.
# show shelf *
Shelf Programmed Present Description Connectivity Serial #
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1 PSS-16II PSS-16II - -
# config shelf 1 description "12345678901234567890"
# show shelf *
Shelf Programmed Present Description Connectivity Serial #
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1 PSS-16II PSS-16II 12345678901234567~ - -

2.3 config general
2.3.1 Purpose
This command configures the network element general parameters.
Use this command to access subcommands that will allow you to:
• Configure automatic in-service timer
• Configure the altitude of the node
• Set the expected capacity of the flash-memory
• Specify the textual representation of the CLLI code of the node
• Specify the second user defined life cycle state for the equipment entity
• Specify the name, contact information, text description, date and time for the network element.
• Displays the current setting of the system.
• Configure if shelf user label shall be displayed in alarms
• Enable or disable the network element for extended temperature operation
• Configure the filter check time
• Configure the mode of FIPS Squelch
• Specify the geographical latitude and longitude location of the node
• Configure the NE as a software file server Network Element
• Specify the name, location and identification number of the network element
• Specify the node identification label
• Specify a number assigned to the node
• Configure the Network Time Protocol servers
• Enable Open Agent functionality on the network element
• Specify the network element power-admin-state default for new cards
• Configure the network element restart behavior for cards
• Set the network element time zone settings and userlabel
• Specify the template name used during deployment of the node
• Specify trap-throttling functionality related settings of the network element
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
2.3.2 Command Access Level
Impact: The date and time are used to time stamp events.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner (unless the parameter specification differs)

2.3.4 Input Parameters
ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [<hours> <minutes> | help ]
Values
0..96 - time for <hours>
0..59 - time for <minutes>
help - display the default and valid values
Default
10 minutes
For ports configured to become automatically in service, specifies the amount of time that a
valid signal must be detected on a port before that port becomes automatically in service. From
1 minute to 96 hours. Enter the keyword without any parameter to display the current setting.
altitude
Syntax
altitude [<height>]
Values
0..8 - altitude in km, step size 0.1
Default
0
Configure the altitude of the node above sea level. The altitude is used for FAN control and for
filter clogging rate calculation. The value is entered in km. An altitude of 300m relates to a value
of 0.3 (km). Locations below sea level are to be configured with the value 0. Enter the keyword
without option to display the current setting.
Note: The following shelf types do not include the parameter altitude for FAN control
calculation: PSS-4, PSS-4II, PSS-8, PSS-16, PSS-16II and PSS-32.
Restrictions
Access Levels: Administrator only
Sub-command: atp
Specifies Anti-Theft Protection parameters. See "config general atp".
capacity
Syntax
capacity ec [<flash-size>]

Syntax
date [<yyyy mm dd>]
Values
1970..2038 - yyyy: year
1..12 - mm: month
1..31 - dd: day
Default
1970 01 01
Sets the current date on the network element. Enter this keyword to display the current value.
To change the value, enter this keyword followed by the year (four digits), a space, the month
(two digits), a space, and the day (two digits).
The latest date that may be specified is "2038 01 18". Warning: setting the date into the past
will potentially corrupt logs and databases.
Do not use this command to change the date if the NE is using NTP. The values are overridden
if an NTP server has been configured to provide network element date/time See "config general
ntp".

2.6 config general ftpserver
2.6.1 Purpose
Use this command to configure the system as a Software file server Network Element, or "SWNE",
which will allow this NE to be a software server for other NEs in the DCN network. Specifically, use
this command to:
• Enable or disable the SWNE feature.
• Set the password for SWNE FTP or SFTP user.
• Display the SWNE status.
The provisioned parameters will be used in the ui mode normal mode by the FTP server and in ui
mode encrypted or fips by the SFTP server.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
2.6.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Enable a NE to SWNE may be opened to malicious attacks. The default ACLs will protect
the NE from FTP/SFTP connection attempts from the outside DCN, but the ACLs can be further
enhanced to disallow FTP/SFTP requests from unspecified sources.
Access Levels: Administrator
2.6.3 Input Format
config general ftpserver
detail
disable
enable
password
2.6.4 Input Parameters
detail
Display the SWNE status and FTP/SFTP server user ID.
disable
Disable SWNE. When SWNE is disabled, NE will deny FTP/SFTP user login.
enable
Enable SWNE. When SWNE is enable, NE will accept FTP/SFTP user login.
Note: A pair of default FTP/SFTP user ID and password is created in NE regardless the status
of FTP/SFTP server. The user ID is fixed ('UserSWNE'), but the administrator can change the
password (see 'password' option).
General CLI commands

2.7 config general ntp
2.7.1 Purpose
This command adds or deletes Network Time Protocol (NTP) servers that are used to provide time
for the network element.
You can configure each network element to use up to eight NTP servers, indexed by number. The
network element automatically selects the highest stratum NTP server with which it can reliably
communicate. If the network element loses communications with an NTP server, it automatically
selects the next best available server.
Note: The NTP servers can be a mixture of IPv4 and IPv6 servers.
This command applies to all 1830 shelf types.
2.7.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Adding an NTP server causes the network element to automatically get its time from the
NTP server.
Access Levels: Administrator
2.7.3 Input Format
config general ntp

delete <index>

<index>

1..8
Default
Entry required
Identifies one entry by <index> in the NTP servers list.

2.7.5 Examples
Displaying the current NTP servers
The following command displays the current NTP server configuration:
# config general ntp detail
Network Time Protocol Properties
NTP Client : Enabled
Clock Mode : NTP Sync Redundant
Current NTP Server : 129.006.015.028
Estimated Drift : 0.000000 us/s
Estimated Time Offset : -0.001315 s
Network Time Protocol Servers
Sl IP RefID str t poll rch delay offset jitter Key(Idx)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
+1 064.090.182.055 135.112.008.016 3 u 1024 377 43.597 -0.876 2.116 0
*2 129.006.015.028 GPS 3 u 1024 357 42.032 -1.315 1.612 51
3 132.163.004.101 192.168.010.251 3 u 1024 000 --- --- --- 0
Notes
Possible S1 states represented by the NTP algorithm state symbols in front of the provisioned NTP
server index number (1 up to 8) are:
* : provisioned server in service and working
+ or # : provisioned server in service and hot standby
x or - or space : provisioned server is out of service
Possible Clock Mode States are:
• FREE-RUNNING NTP is not enabled, or the NE is not synchronized to an NTP server and is
instead using its own internal clock as a source.
• HOLDOVER NTP is enabled but the NE has lost NTP server connectivity, and is using the last
known clock update to synchronize its clock
• NTPLOR Network Time Protocol Synchronized but Loss Of Redundancy - multiple references
are provisioned, but only one is reachable and eligible for synchronization.
• NTPSYNC Network Time Protocol is enabled, and the NE is using the NTP protocol to
synchronize to an NTP server. A single reference is provisioned.
• NTPSYNCR Network Time Protocol Synchronized Redundant NTP is enabled and synchronized
to a reference server and a backup reference is also eligible to become the primary reference.
The value in the Current NTP Server field specifies the NTP server that the NTP client has
synchronized with. A failure in communications with the current server may not result in a switch to
another server until the failure has persisted for up to 2.5 hours. The fail-over interval depends on
the time-keeping quality of the current server and the communication link quality.

config general ntp

time zone when displaying the time. These names are a standard set provided by an imported
zoneinfo database. The name can also be specified as an offest (-14:00 hours to +12:00 hours)
from UTC using one of these formats:

2.9 config general trap-throttling
2.9.1 Purpose
This command configures the network element trap throttling related parameters.
Use this command to:
• Configure the trap throttling related parameters on the network element
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
2.9.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Controls how the network element traps towards a management system are throttled.
Access Levels: Administrator
2.9.3 Input Format
config general trap-throttling
detail
status
threshold1
threshold2
threshold3
time-over-threshold
time-under-threshold
2.9.4 Input Parameters
detail
Displays the trap throttling related parameters. See command "show general trap-throttling" for
the output.
status
Syntax
status [<value>]
Values
disabled
enabled
Default
disabled
Disable or enable the trap throttling related parameters (threshold1, threshold2, threshold3,
time-over-threshold, time-under-threshold) on the network element.
General CLI commands
config general trap-throttling
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 195
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
The disabled option disables the trap-throttling functionality on the network element and any
provisioned trap-throttling parameters are ignored on the network element.
The enabled option sets the trap-throttling functionality on the network element and enables the
applicability of the trap-throttling parameters on the network element.
threshold1
Syntax
threshold1 [<threshold1>]
Values
1..150 - value depicting the number of traps for category1 traps
Default
20
Configures the maximum number of category1 traps that can be processed as part of the trap-
throttling functionality (if enabled) on the network element
threshold2
Syntax
threshold2 [<threshold2>]
Values
1..150 - value depicting the number of traps for category2 traps
Default
20
Configures the maximum number of category2 traps that can be processed as part of the trap-
throttling functionality (if enabled) on the network element
threshold3
Syntax
threshold3 [<threshold3>]
Values
1..150 - value depicting the number of traps for category3 traps
Default
20
Configures the maximum number of category3 traps that can be processed as part of the trap-
throttling functionality (if enabled) on the network element
time-over-threshold
Syntax
time-over-threshold [<seconds>]
General CLI commands
config general trap-throttling
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
196 Issue 1
Values
1..600 - value depicting the number of consecutive seconds traps remain over a threshold
after which the trap throttling (if enabled) state is entered on the network element
Default
5
Configures the number of consecutive seconds for which traps are above the threshold (sum of
the set threshold1, threshold2, threshold3 values), after which the network element enters the
trap throttling state, assuming that trap throttling functionality is enabled on the network element
time-under-threshold
Syntax
time-under-threshold [<seconds>]
Values
1..600 - value depicting the number of consecutive seconds traps remain under a threshold
after which the trap throttling (if enabled) state is exited on the network element
Default
20
Configures the number of consecutive seconds for which traps are below the threshold (sum of
the set threshold1, threshold2, threshold3 values), after which the trap throttling state is exited
on the network element assuming that the trap throttling functionality is enabled on the network
element.
2.9.5 Examples

# config general trap-throttling time-over-threshold 8

2.10 config interface
2.10.1 Purpose
This command configures the interface parameters and provide access to sub-commands which
are available at the interface level on the network element.
Use this command to enter the config interface mode.
2.10.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
2.10.3 Input Format

brief
extwavekeys
gmre
<loopback-interface>
powermgmt
topology
<card-name>
<port-aid>
2.10.4 Input Parameters
Sub-command: brief
Displays the properties of the addressed entity and state related parameters of an interface.
See "config interface brief" command.
Sub-command: extwavekeys
Configures the wavekeys on the network element. See "config interface extwavekeys"
command.
Sub-command: gmre
Configures the IP address for GMRE (Generalized MPLS Routing Engine) application. See
"config interface gmre" command.
Sub-command: <loopback-interface>
Configures the primary and secondary loopback address on the network element. See "config
interface <loopback-interface>" command.
Sub-command: powermgmt
Configures the power management options. See "config interface powermgmt" command.

2.14 history
2.14.1 Purpose
This command displays the command history. The command history is a listing of the last 100
commands entered in the current CLI session. You can enter this command at any level in the
hierarchy.
You can use the following commands to recall previous commands:
• !!: Recall the last command
• !n: Recall the command at line n
• !string: Recall the most recent command starting with string
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
2.14.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None

2.14.3 Input Format

2.14.4 Input Parameters

2.16 paging
2.16.1 Purpose
This command configures the paging properties for the CLI display. The paging properties
determine how many records of output are displayed on the screen before you are prompted to
display the next page of information.
A record can contain more than one line. For example, each alarm record uses three lines.
Use this command to:
• Display the current paging settings
• Enable or disable paging
• Set the paging size (number of records displayed) for the current CLI session
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
2.16.2 Command Access Level

Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
2.16.3 Input Format

status

2.16.4 Input Parameters
status
Syntax
status [<value>]
Values

are displayed. You are then prompted to display the next page or quit.
disabled - When paging is disabled, all of the records for the request are displayed in a
scrolling list until complete.
Default
enabled
Enter this keyword followed by an enable/disable value to change the paging status, or enter
this keyword without any parameter to display the current setting.

2.18 session
2.18.1 Purpose
This command configures session related attributes for the current CLI session.
Use this command to:
• Configure the confirmation dialog response
• Configure the command context change
• Configure the paging properties for the CLI display (using a subcommand)
• Display current session settings
2.18.2 Command Access Level
Impact: changes behavior of the current CLI session
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer (unless the parameter specification differs)
2.18.3 Input Format
session
confirmationbypass
detail
fullcontext
paging
2.18.4 Input Parameters
confirmationbypass
Syntax
confirmationbypass [<value>]
Values
yes
no
Default
no
Configures behavior of the user confirmation dialogs for the current CLI session.
If set to no, the user of the current CLI session has to answer user confirmation dialog
questions.
If set to yes, confirmation prompts are bypassed for the user of the current CLI session. This
setting is useful in scripting, so the script does not have to be designed to handle confirmation
prompts. Otherwise, this setting is not recommended as it disables user warning questions.
General CLI commands
session
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 211
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Restrictions
Access Levels: Administrator only
detail
Displays the settings of the current CLI session.
fullcontext
Syntax
fullcontext [<value>]
Values
yes
no
Default
no
Configures command tree context change for the current CLI session.
If set to no, the user of the current CLI session is allowed to switch the context in the command
tree.
If set to yes, the user of the current CLI session is not allowed to switch the context and must
enter the complete command. This setting is useful in scripting so that a partially-entered
command mistakenly included in a script does not cause the script to enter a context which
would then cause the next command in the script to fail. Instead, the script will fail on the
command that causes the failure (that is, the partially-entered command) which is a simpler
scenario to troubleshoot.
Sub-command: paging
Configures the paging properties of the CLI display. See command "paging".
2.18.5 Examples
# session confirmationbypass
# session confirmationbypass yes
# session detail
confirmationbypass : yes
fullcontext : no
paging status : enabled
paging size : 10
# session fullcontext no
# show
(show)# mm

2.20.1 Purpose
This command displays the general parameters for the network element.

network element:
• The name, description, location and contact information

• The network element serial number and system identification information
• The Anti-Theft Protection related settings

240 Issue 1
2.21 show general atp
2.21.1 Purpose
This command displays Anti-Theft Protection parameters.
Use this command to:
• Display the grace period for anti-theft cards.
• Display whether the network element has received anti-theft key.
• Display the time period in days after detecting an NE loss of communication, after which an
alarm is raised.
• Display the time period in days after detecting an NE loss of communication, after which all
supported cards on the NE are shut down.
This command applies to all PSS shelf types.
2.21.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Anti-Theft settings apply to all supported cards.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
2.21.3 Input Format
show general atp
graceperiod
keystatus
mgmt-loss-declaration-period
mgmt-loss-shutdown-period
2.21.4 Input Parameters
keystatus
Displays whether the network element has received anti-theft key. The value is 'keyed' or
'unkeyed'.
graceperiod
Displays the network element grace period for anti-theft supported cards with an ongoing or
expired grace period. The value displayed is the absolute time when the grace period expires
on a card with an ongoing grace period. If the grace period has expired on a card, the value
displayed is 'Expired'.
mgmt-loss-declaration-period
Displays the time period in days after detecting an NE loss of communication, after which an
alarm is raised.
General CLI commands
show general atp
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 241
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
mgmt-loss-shutdown-period
Displays the time period in days after detecting an NE loss of communication, after which all
supported cards on the NE are shut down.
2.21.5 Examples
# show general atp ?
graceperiod Displays the network element grace period for anti-theft
supported cards with an ongoing or expired grace period.
keystatus Displays whether the network element has received anti-theft
key.
mgmt-loss-declaration-period Displays the time period in days after detecting an NE loss
of communication, after which an alarm is raised.
mgmt-loss-shutdown-period Displays the time period in days after detecting an NE loss
of communication, after which all supported cards on the NE are shut down.
# show general atp graceperiod
Anti-Theft Grace Period: 30 days
Location Card Name Grace Period Expiration At
-------- --------- ------------------------------
1/2 S13X100E 15-November-2023 14:47:02 (UTC)

NE ATP Key Status: keyed
# show general atp mgmt-loss-declaration-period
NE ATP Management Loss Declaration Period: 5 days
# show general atp mgmt-loss-shutdown-period
NE ATP Management Loss Shutdown Period: 90 days

2.22 show general performance
2.22.1 Purpose
This command displays performance data for the network element.
Use this command to display a snapshot of the CPU and memory statistics for the active controller.
2.22.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
2.22.3 Input Format
show general performance
2.22.4 Input Parameters
performance
Syntax
performance
Displays the following information about CPU and memory on the active controller of the
system. See table below for details.
2.22.5 Output Parameters
The command returns the following output parameter, as listed in the table below.
Table 2-1 Returned Output Parameter
Label Description
Time Current time in hours, minutes, seconds
Utilization CPU utilization other than time spent in idle task (in percentage)
User CPU time spent in user mode in percentage (in percentage)
System CPU time spent in system mode (in percentage)
Nice CPU time spent in user mode with low priority (in percentage)
I/O Wait CPU time spent for I/O to complete (in percentage)
Irq CPU time spent servicing hardware interrupts (in percentage)
Soft Irq CPU time spent servicing queued work from software interrupts (in percentage)
Idle CPU time spent in idle task (in percentage)
Memory total (MB) Memory available in the system (in MB)
Memory used (MB) Memory used by the system (in MB)
General CLI commands
show general performance

2.23 show interface
2.23.1 Purpose
This command displays the interface parameters and provide access to sub-commands which are
available at the interface level on the network element.
Use this command to enter the show interface mode.
2.23.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
2.23.3 Input Format
show interface
ason
brief
extwavekeys
gmre
inventory
<loopback-interface>
powermgmt
topology
unassigned
wtdomain
<card-name>
<port-aid>
2.23.4 Input Parameters
Sub-command: ason
Displays the ASON OMS line parameters of an interface of a card. See "show interface ason"
command.
Sub-command: brief
Displays the properties of the addressed entity and state related parameters of an interface.
See "show interface brief" command.
Sub-command: extwavekeys
Displays the wavekeys on the network element. See "show interface extwavekeys" command.
General CLI commands
show interface
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 245
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Sub-command: gmre
Displays the IP address for GMRE (Generalized MPLS Routing Engine) application. See "show
interface gmre" command.
Sub-command: inventory
Displays the remote inventory information for a pluggable module in a port. See "show interface
inventory" command.
Sub-command: <loopback-interface>
Displays the primary and secondary loopback address on the network element. See "show
interface <loopback-interface>" command.
Sub-command: powermgmt
Displays the power management options. See "show interface powermgmt" command.
Sub-command: topology
Displays the fiber connectivity on the network element. See "show interface topology"
command.
Sub-command: unassigned
Displays the unassigned interfaces of all cards provisioned in the network element.
Sub-command: wtdomain
Syntax
wtdomain <port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/<port> - addresses a single port.
* - display the list of all ports
Default
Entry required

2.25.1 Purpose
This command displays the logs for the network elements. Use this command to display all of the
logs on the network element or logs for a particular type of event. The log entries are listed in
reverse chronological order, with the most recent log event listed first. Both raised and cleared
events are displayed.

2.30 tools linux
2.30.1 Purpose
This command provides certain users (see 'config admin users edit' command) access to the Linux
operating system for debugging subsystems that are not accessible through the normal user
interfaces. Use this command to submit shell commands to the operating system to be executed
with non-root, but elevated privilege.
There is no default account with this privilege. A user already in the "Administrator" group must
enable the "linuxtools" privilege for any user (including Administrator class users) before the
designated user can execute the 'tools linux' CLI command.
Note: Limits are established for execution (60 seconds) and output (100 KByte). Large output
should be redirected to a file using shell syntax for subsequent retrieval.
Note: Not all combinations of quoted strings act as they would in bash or other Linux shells. This is
a known limitation. Alternate string quoting may be necessary to execute the desired command. For
Example:
SYSTEM# tools linux "echo \"hello\""
Error: too many arguments
SYSTEM#
The same echo command works correctly with single quotes as shown below:
SYSTEM# tools linux 'echo \"hello\"'
"hello"
SYSTEM# tools linux "echo 'hello world'"
hello world
SYSTEM# tools linux "echo 'hello world'; echo 'it is '`date +%r`; echo 'I hope you are well!'"
hello world
it is 06:46:58 PM
I hope you are well!
SYSTEM#
This command applies to all 1830 shelf types.
2.30.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner (when enabled)
2.30.3 Input Format
tools linux <well-formed-bash-command-string>
General CLI commands
tools linux
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 259
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
2.30.4 Input Parameters
<well-formed-bash-command-string>
A bash (Bourne Again SHell) command string to be executed by the Linux shell under the
privilege and environment of a special user.
As explained in Section "Case sensitivity," when the command string contains spaces, the
complete command string must be surrounded by double quotation marks like, "This is a
string". In addition, when the command string itself contains quotation marks, they must be
escaped by backslash like, "The name \"System\" is used here".

3.2 config admin
3.2.1 Purpose
This command configures the administrative options for the network element.
Use this command to:
• Configure the NE Installation
• Access subcommands for configuring local and remote authentication and authorization
properties
• Configure the NE to operate in SONET or SDH mode
• Set any one of the OCS compounds (OCS1 or OCS2 or OCS3) with its associated IP address
for uplink communication.
• Restart the network element software
• Set up session options
• Access subcommands for configuring the syslog parameters
• Set the units used to display temperature
• Access subcommands for user login management
• Configure the NE for secure/unsecure mode
• Access subcommands for configuring the clusterip parameter
• Access subcommands for configuring flexible grid channel add/drop for OCS and cluster
associated network elements
• Set the source IP interface for packets the NE transmits for a given protocol
• Disable or enable ZTP
• Configure the security settings for SSH and TLS
• Configure a delay before NE cold reset during which the reset will be announced by raising a
transient condition
• Configure the network management system (NMS) user and IP address access
• Switch Delaymode on or off
• reset the NE configuration to factory default
• clear Ne configuration and software for decommissioning
• Specify a pre-login and post-login banner
• Access subcommands for the storage device
• Configure the CLI Terminal
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.

3.2.4 Input Parameters
Sub-command: aaa-servers
Configures the servers used for authentication, authorization, and accounting (AAA). See
"config admin aaa-servers".
Sub-command: aaa-server-group
Configures a server group to be used for authentication, authorization, and accounting (AAA).
See "config admin aaa-server-group".
Sub-command: authentication
Configures user login and password authentication properties so that the NE is secured by a
trusted path. User identification and authentication are based upon Local, RADIUS (Remote
Authentication Dial In User Service) or TACACS+ (Terminal Access Controller Access-Control
System Plus)
See "config admin authentication".
Sub-command: authorization
Configures authorization information. See "config admin authorization".
Sub-command: cli-terminal
Configure the remote CLI terminal access. See "config admin cli-terminal".
Sub-command: clusterip
Configure the unique user-assigned (TIDs) NE Names with its associated IP address for remote
cluster NEs. The IP address is been changed centrally in one place, rather than changing every
remote connected port (rmconport) parameter for add/drop nodes or oconn parameter for
optical line nodes. See "config admin clusterip".

<string> - NE name (TID), 1 to 20 characters

Commands addressing multiple areas
config admin
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 279
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Default
Entry required
Values
For delaymode:
off - delaymode switch to off
on - delaymode switch to on
Default
off - if TID is set
on - if TID is not set
Supports the NE installation through standalone CLI interface.
The config admin commission command allows an operator to initialize an NE's Name (TID)
and NE database from the CLI interface. When connecting to a new NE for the first time, the
system typically has no NE-Name (no TID) and an invalid Database. After initializing the
database and name of a newly installed NE, the operator is typically recommended to initialize
the NE's IP address(es) (See "config interface loopback" and "config interface panel-card").
With "config admin commission delaymode on" NE warm resets during initialization can be hold
back until the initialization data is applied over a single NE warm reboot.
When delaymode is on, as a consequence the CLI prompt will not be changed on the CLI
session prior to the delayed reboot is completed.
Note: Avoid using a forward slash ("/") in the NE name (TID). This will allow automatic backup
file name generation. See command "config database".
When the optional initial keyword is included, then this keyword must be followed by a string
that will be the NE Name (TID). The initial keyword suppresses all prompts for input that occur
during the commission process. If the NE Name has never been set, the commission
command with the initial keyword triggers an immediate reboot.
With the initial keyword, the commission command is re-issue safe in that repeating the
command with the NE Name that has already been set will not be flagged as an error nor
trigger a reboot. That is, the NE will not return an error message in this scenario and will not
change any parameter values nor trigger a reboot. If the commission command with the initial
keyword is repeated with a different NE Name, the NE will not return an error, will change the
NE Name, and will not trigger a reboot. Note that config general name <string> also can be
used to change the NE Name.
The initial keyword may be used in scripting to suppress prompts for input that would otherwise
occur during the commission process.
Enter delaymode without parameter to see the current setting.
delay-resetne
Syntax
delay-resetne [<value>]

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12

280 Issue 1
Values
0..50000 - time in milliseconds
Default
0 (unset)
Specifies the delay in milliseconds between the assertion of the transient condition USER-NE-
COLD-RESET-PENDING and the execution of the cold reboot of the NE (see "resetne cold").
At the start of this delay timer the system asserts the transient condition USER-NE-COLD-
RESET-PENDING to inform other network elements and network management systems which
about the upcoming cold reboot. This shall give them enough time to react proactively to this
service affecting reboot.
The delay timer does not apply to the warm reboot of the NE (see "resetne warm").
The default value "unset" acts like, and is displayed as a value of 0 ms.
factory-reset
Deletes all data from the network element and replaces it with default values where necessary.
The installed software release will not be changed.
The command includes a cold reset of the network element to clear volatile memory.
The following actions are performed during the reset to factory configuration:
• Clears the database.
• Clears the TID and OAMP port administrative state.
• Clears the IP values kept in the SEEP (Serial EEPROM), which are the IPv4 and IPv6
addresses of the OAMP, Loopback and Default Route (equivalent to 'config database
clear ipclear').
• Clears the currently provisioned trust anchor list
• Clears User Authentication data (e.g. ssh keys)
• Clears ZTP provisioning
• Clears logfiles.
• Network element cold reset
Please consult the Installation and System Turnup Guide for instructions on how to reconfigure
the system.

associated network element capabilities. See "config admin flexgrid".

communicates to manage uplink services. Enter this keyword to display the current value. Enter
this keyword followed by 0.0.0.0 to terminate the uplink management relationship. If the

the password for login to the OCS1/OCS2/OCS3 NE.
The password must be compliant to the OCS password format. Please refer the related OCS
documentation.
When the command is issued without passwd parameter, a warning and confirmation request
will be prompted:
WARNING: You are about to change the OCS1/OCS2/OCS3 IP Settings. This may be
disruptive to the configured traffic. Please make sure that you follow the proper procedure for

Sub-command: protocol
Configures the source IP address the NE uses for packets it transmits for a given service or
protocol. See "config admin protocol".
resetne
Syntax
resetne <value>
Values
warm - re-initializes the network element software only and is not service affecting.
cold - re-initializes the hardware and software of the network element and is service
affecting.
Default
Entry required
Restarts the software on the network element. Enter the keyword resetne followed by warm or
cold.
You will be prompted with a warning and need to confirm before the command is executed.
Note: If delay-resetne is provisioned, a short delay (up to 50 sec) is inserted before the resetne
is executed and a condition is raised. The parameter delay-resetne has impact on service
affecting resets only.
Note: Executing "resetne warm" will reboot all line cards in a node too. This includes all L2 SR
OS packets cards, which suffer a several minute traffic hit during a warm reset.
return-to-factory
Purges all data from the network element's memory drives and applies measures to prevent the
recovery of that data. After that, the system performs a cold reset to clear all volatile memory.
After this command is complete, all affected controllers will be unusable as they will no
longer have any release software to be executed.
This command is only intended for the secure decommissioning of a network element from
security sensitive networks.
Considerable manual effort is required if the controllers are to be reused.
To make the controllers operational again a USBkey scratch installation needs to be performed
by Nokia personnel on each affected controller.
Sub-command: security
Configures the security settings of the network element for SSH, TLS. See "config admin
security".
Sub-command: session
Configures the session parameters: maximum number of failed login attempts, timeout. See
"config admin session".

3.3 config admin storage
3.3.1 Purpose
The auto-recovery feature provides a means to recover the active software and configuration when
a simplex controller is replaced. When the optional storage device is present, the network element
maintains on the device a copy of the active software on the controller and an updated copy of the
controller's configuration. When a controller is replaced with a new one, the new controller
automatically installs the software and the configuration from the storage device and returns the
network element to the same operation as before the controller was replaced. When the network
element cannot determine whether it should recover automatically, no recovery occurs and the
operator has the option to choose the next step.
The contents of the storage device are encrypted. Therefore, a device used on one network
element becomes associated with that network element. If such a device is moved to another
network element, the other network element cannot read from, or write content to, that device. In
addition, the content of such a storage device cannot be read or written by a different piece of
equipment like a Windows-based PC. The only operation that can be done with a storage device by
a system other than the network element with which the storage device is associated is to remove
the content by using a network element's format directive or, for example, by using the format
command in a Windows-based PC.
Use this command to configure the auto-recovery feature and to manage the storage device, as
follows:
• Enable or disable software and database auto-recovery from the storage device
• Prepare the storage device for safe removal
• Cause the controller to overwrite the software image and the database on the storage device
• Cause the controller to recover the software image and the database from the storage device
• Format the storage device
Use show admin storage to display status parameters related to the auto-recovery feature. Many
of the status parameters are referenced below in the input parameter descriptions for config admin
storage.
This command applies only to the 1830 PSS-4II.
3.3.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator only

3.3.4 Input Parameters
auto-recovery-enabled
Syntax
auto-recovery-enabled [<value>]
Values
true - Enables software and database auto-recovery
false - Disables software and database auto-recovery
Default
true
Enables and disables the feature for automatically recovering software and database from the
storage device.
If you do not plan to use this feature, then:
• Set auto-recovery-enabled to false
• Do not install a storage device
• Use the eject option to remove a storage device if one is already installed
For any of the activities of the auto-recovery feature to work, a storage device must be installed
in the network element and the format option must have been used on that device while
installed in that network element. This description assumes that action has been taken, unless
otherwise stated. See the description of format below for more detail.
A controller automatically attempts to recover from the storage device if its database becomes
invalid (Controller Database Valid is false) and if the following conditions exist before and
while the controller's database is invalid:
• Storage device Operational Status is up (this status means a storage device is present
and that auto-recovery-enabled set to true)
• AND storage device Equipment Device Status is normal
• AND Storage Device Ready To Protect is true
On the other hand, a controller will not automatically attempt to recover from the storage device
if the controller is already running with an invalid database and a storage device is inserted that
had last been formatted in this network element and was in the conditions listed above before it
was removed from this network element. You can start a recovery operation using config
admin storage recover-controller-from-storage or by restarting the controller without
removing the storage device. In this scenario, you are recommended to be sure you have
inserted the device you intend to recover from before starting a recovery operation.
For the cases of a controller starting up on installation, the controller may be replacing a faulty
controller. In that case, the newly-installed controller might be one that has:
• Never been used before

After a successful recovery, the controller's active software version and its database will be the
same as that on the storage device. This result occurs regardless of whether the software
version on the storage device was older than, newer than, or the same as the one that was on
the controller before the recovery.
Under other conditions, the controller will not automatically recover from the storage device nor
will it automatically overwrite the software image and the database on the device. For details of
various scenarios, see the User Provisioning Guide.
Changing auto-recovery-enabled from true to false:
If the controller has taken over the storage device, Equipment Device Status becomes safe-
removal-preparing and then it prepares the device for safe removal by performing a final
recovery database update or by terminating an in-progress initial recovery software and/or
recovery database synchronization. Equipment Device Status becomes present after the
change completes successfully. The value of present indicates that a storage device is
installed but auto-recovery-enabled is false. This process is similar to the eject directive. If
the controller has not taken over the storage device, then no storage device updates are done
before Equipment Device Status becomes present. See show admin storage for a
description of how the Storage Device Record status parameter behaves in this scenario.
Changing auto-recovery-enabled from false to true:
Does not trigger a recovery.
If no storage device is installed, or if one is installed that is not properly formatted, the setting is
allowed but the following status values and alarm will be set:
- Recovery Software Release is none
- Recovery Database is none
- Storage Device Ready To Protect is false
- An alarm will be issued
If a storage device is installed after auto-recovery-enabled is set to true, then the controller
automatically overwrites the software image and the database on the storge device, or "takes
over" the device, if the device's conditions are suitable. That is, the controller will write its
software image and its latest database to the device. After this initial synchronization, the
controller will apply database updates to the storage device. The conditions that need to exist
for the controller to take over the storage device are:
- auto-recovery-enabled is true
- Storage Device Record is true
- Device is properly formatted
- The software version on the controller is committed (see additional details a few paragraphs
below)
- Controller Database Valid is true
• If the Storage Device Record of an already-installed device is false after auto-

recovers from that storage device, the result will be that the software version on the controller

activated, and the database will contain only the settings that were made before the upgrade.

copy-controller-to-storage
Syntax
copy-controller-to-storage
Causes the controller to overwrite the software image and the database on the storage device.
After this initial synchronization, the controller will apply database updates to the storage
device. And, when an in-service software upgrade occurs from a remote file server, the
controller will copy the new software version to the storage device when the new version is
committed. That is, Storage Device Ready To Protect will become true. The result is that the
controller has "taken over" the storage device. The status values are displayed by show admin
storage and can be used to follow the progress of copy-controller-to-storage.
For a copy-controller-to-storage operation to work, a storage device must be installed in the
network element and the format option must have been used on that device while installed in
that network element. Otherwise, the command is rejected. This description assumes that the
actions have been taken so that the operation will work, unless otherwise stated. See the
description of format below for more detail.
The controller attempts an automatic takeover operation (that is, an automatic copy-controller-
to-storage operation) under the following conditions:
• Storage device Operational Status is up
• AND storage device Equipment Device Status is normal
• AND Storage Device Record - Is true AND Recovery Database is present OR - Is
no-record AND Recovery Database is none

• AND auto-recovery-enabled is true

Under other conditions, the controller will not automatically overwrite the storage device, nor will
it automatically recover from it. Under these other conditions, the storage device will not be
ready to provide software or database recovery; that is, it will not be ready to protect. If you
want the controller to take over the device, use the copy-controller-to-storage directive. An

• Enter yes to copy the software and database onto the storage device
• Enter no to cancel the command without taking any action
You can bypass the confirmation prompt by including yes at the end of the command line.

device will be kept ready to protect.
If the controller has already taken over the storage device, for example, when the copy-
controller-to-storage directive had already been used, the copy-controller-to-storage
directive will not cause any change of behavior or status of the auto-recovery function.
Restrictions

• auto-recovery-enabled is false

network element
• OR the last time the format command was run on the storage device was while it was
installed in a different network element
• OR the software version running on the controller has been activated but not committed

• eject
• format

eject
Syntax
eject
The controller prepares the storage device for safe removal by terminating any in-progress
config admin storage operation and then stopping all activities on the device such as updating
the recovery software and recovery database. For example, if the controller has taken over the
storage device, then it prepares the storage device for safe removal by performing a final
recovery database update or by terminating an in-progress initial recovery software and/or
recovery database synchronization and then stopping all activities on the device. While the
controller prepares the storage device for safe removal, Equipment Device Status displays
safe-removal-preparing. After the activities complete successfully, the Storage Device
Record status parameter changes to no-record and Equipment Device Status becomes
safe-removal-ready. If the controller has not taken over the storage device, then there are no
synchronization activities to terminate and no storage device updates are made before
Equipment Device Status becomes safe-removal-ready. In that case, the Storage Device
Record also changes to no-record.
Note: The eject command takes action only if the controller's auto-recovery-enabled setting is
true. If the controller's auto-recovery-enabled setting is false, then Equipment Device
Status is already safe-removal-ready and the eject command will have no effect. The storage
device can be safely removed. In addition, the storage device can be safely removed when
Equipment Device Status is present.
Note: If you execute the eject command inadvertently when it was operating normally
(Equipment Device Status is normal), you can put the storage device back into normal
operation by following either of these steps:
- If you are located at the network element, then remove the device and plug it back in.
OR
- If you executed the eject command remotely, then set-auto-recovery-enabled to false and
then back to true again.
The status values are displayed by the detail option or by show admin storage.
format
Syntax
format [eject]
Causes the controller to format the storage device such that it is ready to use but with no
software or database files on it. All content on the device is removed.
Due to the encryption function, a storage device must have the format option run on it in a
network element before it will function as a storage device in that network element. After the
format operation is complete, the storage device will be associated with the network element in
which it was installed when the format option was run. If the device previously had the format
option run on it in a different network element, that device no longer has an association with the
other network element. A storage device will accommodate the auto-recovery feature only in the
network element with which it is associated.

Note that the format option can be used to associate any number of storage devices with the
same network element. If you want to swap among multiple storage devices on the same
network element, it is recommended that you track the content of each device carefully so you
will know what to expect when you install the device. For example, the network element might

command displays the Recovery Software Release on the device and also the auto-recovery

A few scenarios where you might use the format option are:
• If you install a device that is not properly formatted, use the format option to make the
device ready to use with the auto-recovery feature.
• If you want to start using a device in a network element that was previously used in
another network element, install the device in the network element and use the format
option. Such a device will become usable for the auto-recovery feature in that network
element but all prior content will be removed.
If you no longer want to use a storage device for the auto-recovery feature, you may use
commands such as the Microsoft Windows format command to change the file format of the
device and even zeroize the sectors on the device.
Use the eject option to format the device and make it ready for safe removal. If the eject option
is not used, after formatting is complete, the controller will write the software image and the
database to the device and then begin applying incremental, periodic updates. That is, Storage
Device Ready To Protect will become true.

• Enter no to cancel the command without formatting the device

Causes the controller to recover from the storage device. As a result of a successful recover-
controller-from-storage operation, Software Release On Controller will be the same as
Recovery Software Release. And, the database on the storage device will be applied to the
controller. After recovery, whether the controller takes over the storage device depends on the
Storage Device Record; that is, on the administrative state stored on the device for software
and database auto-recovery. The dependency on Storage Device Record is as follows:
• true - After the controller recovers the software image and the database, it applies
database updates to the storage device. And, when an in-service software upgrade
occurs from a remote file server, the controller will copy the new software image to the
storage device. That is, Storage Device Ready To Protect will be true. The end result
is that the controller has recovered from the storage device and has taken it over.
• false - The controller does not take over the storage device after it recovers the software
image and the database. The end result is a one-time recovery from the device and the
auto-recovery-enabled setting will change from true to false. Storage Device Ready
To Protect will be false.
See show admin storage for more details of Storage Device Record. The status values
displayed by show admin storage can be used to follow the progress of recover-controller-
from-storage.
For a recover-controller-from-storage operation to work, a storage device must be installed
in the network element and the format option must have been used on that device while
installed in that network element. This description assumes that action has been taken, unless
otherwise stated. See the description of format for more detail.
Under conditions when the controller will not automatically recover from the storge device, if
you want the controller to recover from the device anyway, use the recover-controller-from-
storage directive.
One example of when you might use recover-controller-from-storage is when Storage
Device Record is false but you want to do a one-time recovery as described above. As a result
of a successful recover-controller-from-storage operation, Software Release On Controller
will be the same as Recovery Software Release. And, the database on the storage device will
be applied to the controller. But, the controller will not take over the device and Storage Device
Ready To Protect will be false.
When you use the recover-controller-from-storage directive, you are prompted to confirm the
request:
• Enter yes to recover from the storage device
• Enter no to cancel the command without taking any action
You can bypass the confirmation prompt by including yes at the end of the command line.
Note: If recover-controller-from-storage is run when a new software version on the controller
has been activated but not yet committed, the result will be that the software version on the
controller will be the one running before the upgrade and that software version will be
committed, not activated. The database on the controller will contain only the settings that were
made before the upgrade.

3.4 config admin ztp
3.4.1 Purpose
This command configures the zero touch provisioning (ztp) options for the network element.
Use this command to:
• Disable or enable ZTP
• Bring NE into ZTP initial default state for the currently installed SW load (clear)
When ZTP is enabled the following occurs:
• On any LAN interface (typically OAMP) with dhcp_client or ipv6_autoconfig enabled, the DHCP
or DHCPv6 message will include a bootfile request.
• The NE can then receive a bootfile URL from the DHCP server, and that bootfile is then
downloaded.
• The bootfile is then executed to configure the system.
The following actions are performed during reset to initial default state:
• Clear the database,
• Clear TID and OAMP port administrative state, the OAMP-, Gateway- and default route-IPv4 and
-IPv6 and the IPv6 loopback data kept in system SEEP
• Clear the loopback IPv4 data kept in system SEEP - optionally with ipclear keyword
• Clear the currently provisioned trust anchor list - optionally with trustanchorclear keyword
• Clear ZTP provisioning and
• Clear logfiles.
This command applies to 1830 PSS shelf types except PSS-16 and PSS-4.
3.4.2 Command Access Level
Impact: enable or disables ZTP turn-up operations. Separately it can clear ZTP configuration back
to start, including database clearing and clearing IP data stored in system remote inventory, NE will
be restarting, and ZTP starts from scratch. A DBINBVALID alarm will be active after clearing.
Access Levels: Administrator
3.4.3 Input Format
config admin ztp
{enable | disable}
clear
3.4.4 Input Parameters
{enable | disable}
Syntax
{enable | disable}
System administration commands
Commands addressing multiple areas

Values

disable - ZTP function for NE turn-up not activated

enable
Enable / disable NE turn-up via ZTP. Enter "config admin ztp" without value to display the
current mode.

Syntax
clear [ipclear] [trustanchorclear]
Values
ipclear - clears the current loopback IP configuration in addition.
trustanchorclear - clears the currently provisioned ZTP trust anchor list in addition.
Clears ZTP related configuration including the database, the TID and OAMP port administrative
state, the OAMP-, Gateway- and default route-IPv4 and -IPv6 and the IPv6 loopback data kept
in system SEEP and system log files.
Follow this keyword with ipclear to also clear the current loopback IPv4 configuration kept in
system SEEP. Follow the keyword trustanchorclear to also clear the currently provisioned trust
anchor configuration.
Restarts the NE, which will come up in DBINVALID state and default TID, and optionally apply
the default IP configuration and apply optionally the default trust anchor list of the active SW
load. Before ZTP configuration is cleared, you are prompted to confirm the request:
• Enter yes to reset ZTP configuration
• Enter no to cancel the command without touching ZTP configuration.
Requires administrator level user privilege.
Restrictions

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Table 3-2 Storage Device Information Parameters: (continued)
Parameters Description
Equipment Device Status The physical condition of the storage device.
• normal - auto-recovery-enabled is true and the device has no alarm against it that
prevents it from performing its functions. Operational Status is up.
• failed - The storage device has an alarm against it that prevents it from performing its
functions. Operational status is down. Here are scenarios to reach this status:
- auto-recovery-enabled is true and the device has such an alarm.
- auto-recovery-enabled was changed from true to false while the device has such an
alarm. Equipment Device Status transitions to present when the device can be safely
removed.
• empty - Device is physically absent. Operational Status is down or disabled. Alarm
behavior depends on the setting of auto-recovery-enabled:
- true - The storage device is expected so an alarm also is raised indicating that the
storage device is missing. Equipment Device Status remains empty, not failed.
- false - The storage device is not expected so no alarm is raised.
• present - Device can be safely removed. Here are scenarios to reach this status:
- When a storage device is already installed and the device has no alarms against it
and auto-recovery-enabled is changed from true to false, the status transitions to
safe-removal-preparing and then to present.
- When a storage device is already installed and the device already has an alarm
against it that prevents it from performing its functions and then auto-recovery-
enabled is changed from true to false, the status remains failed and then transitions
to present when the device can be safely removed.
- When a storage device is inserted while auto-recovery-enabled is false, the status
transitions from empty to present.
For any of these scenarios, the device can be safely removed. Operational Status is
disabled.
• safe-removal-preparing - The eject or auto-recovery-enabled false command was
issued. Activities related to the device are being terminated but the device is not yet
ready to be removed safely.
• safe-removal-ready - The auto-recovery-enabled parameter is true and the eject
command was successfully processed and the device is ready to be removed safely
but has not yet been removed. Operational status is down.
For empty and safe-removal-preparing, the Operational Status depends on the setting
of auto-recovery-enabled, as follows:
• auto-recovery-enabled true - Operational Status down
• auto-recovery-enabled false - Operational Status disabled
See the description of config admin storage for more details of the format option.
Encryption Status Details about the encryption status on the storage device.
• match - The network element and the storage device are associated with one
another. This status is necessary for Equipment Device Status to be normal.
• no-match - The network element and the storage device are not associated with one
another. Equipment Device Status will be failed. In this case, consider using the
format directive on this network element with this device.
• not-reported - Equipment Device Status for the storage device is present or empty.
In the description of config admin storage, see the format option for more details about
the association between a storage device and a network element.
