3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Table 3-3 Auto-Recovery Enabled Parameters: (continued)
Parameters Description
Storage Device Record The administrative state stored on the storage device for software and database auto-recovery.
• true - Software and database auto-recovery features are enabled on the device
• false - Software and database auto-recovery features are disabled on the device
• no-record - Some of the conditions that cause this status are:
- No database is present on the storage device.
- Recovery Database Update Status is recovery-database-initializing.
- Equipment Device Status is empty, failed, present, safe-removal-preparing, or
safe-removal-ready.
When the controller is keeping the software and database up-to-date on the storage device, this
parameter will have the same value as the Controller value. However, under certain
circumstances, this parameter might be different from the Controller value. In that case, the
controller will not automatically update the device nor will it ever automatically recover from it.
Here are two examples when the Controller value is true and the Storage Device Record is false:
• Controller value is true. Then a device is inserted that was used on that same network element
and Storage Device Record for that device is false.
• If auto-recovery-enabled is changed from true to false, this setting on the storage device is
changed to false but Storage Device Record becomes no-record because the device is made
ready for safe removal. If auto-recovery-enabled is set back to true, then Storage Device
Record becomes false and no automatic recovery or takeover occurs. Note that if you
inadvertently set auto-recovery-enabled to false, you will need to set it back to true AND
execute copy-controller-to-storage to resume periodic, incremental updates.
For both cases, you will need to decide what to do:
• recover-controller-from-storage - One time recovery from the device and the controller does
not take over the device. The result will be auto-recovery-enabled and the Controller value will
become false and the Storage Device Record will become no-record. The device will be made
ready for safe removal.
• copy-controller-to-storage - Controller takes over the device. Storage Device Record becomes
true. After synchronization, periodic, incremental updates will occur from the controller to the
device.

• recovery-database-initializing - The controller is copying its entire database onto the
device after taking over the device. Recovery Database Ready To Protect will be false
until this operation is complete.
• functioning - The process is functioning by which a controller executes a periodic,
incremental update of the recovery database. This value applies when an update is
occurring or between updates. Recovery Database Ready To Protect will be true while
this status is in effect.
• stopped - Some of the conditions that cause this status are:
- No recovery database is present
- Controller Database Valid is false
- Controller is recovering from the device
- Equipment Device Status is not normal
- Storage Device Record is false
Recovery Database Last Update Indicates how up-to-date the recovery database is.
• <yyyy/mm/dd hh:mm:ss> - The date and time for which the database on the controller will
be up-to-date if an automatic recovery occurs or if a recover-controller-from-storage
operation is executed.
• no-record - Some of the conditions that cause this status are:
- No database is present on the storage device
- Recovery Database Update Status is recovery-database-initializing
- Equipment Device Status is empty, failed, present, safe-removal-preparing, or
safe-removal-ready
Recovery In Progress Indicates if a recovery operation (automatic or recover-controller-from-storage) is in
progress.
• true - Recovery is in progress.
• false - No recovery in progress.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
The timeout for accessing this TACACS+ server.
single-connect
Syntax
single-connect <value>
Values
enabled - will attempt to keep a single connection to the TACACS+ server
disabled - will not keep a single connection to the TACACS+ server
Default
disabled
Specifies to enable or disable the single connection option. Rather than have the NE open and
close a TCP connection to the server with each communication, enabling single-connect means
that NE maintains a single open connection between itself and the server. The single
connection is more efficient because it allows the server to handle a higher number of TACACS
operations.
<shared-secret>
Values
<string> - shared secret key is an ASCII string between 5 to 63 characters
Default
Entry required
Do not include the shared-secret on the command line.
After entering the above parameters, the shared secret key between the NE and the target
TACACS+ server is requested to be entered and verified. The secret key is encrypted on the
NE using AES.
Note: the shared-secret is used to encrypt TACACS+ messages, which recipient (e.g., server)
uses to decrypt the message. If the NE and Server's secrets do not match, any TACACS+
message will be ill-formed, and there will be an error response from the server.
Restrictions
The <shared-secret> cannot contain a '?' or start with a '#' character.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
336 Issue 1
Values
8..32
Default
8
Specifies the minimum length for user passwords accepted by the NE.
Changes in this setting affect passwords created or edited after the value is changed.
Passwords created or edited before the value is changed are not affected.
Enter the keyword without a value to display the current value.
local password history-size
Syntax
local password history-size [<value>]
Values
0..24
Default
10
Specifies the password history size. This value is used system-wide with the same value
applying to each user. This value is the maximum number of previously-used passwords stored
for each user. The user cannot reuse a password that is on this list. When a user's password is
changed, their previous password is placed in the password history list. If the history already
contains the maximum number of entries, then if the user changes password again, the oldest
password rotates off the list. Therefore, any password that is not on the password history list
can be reused at any time even if it has been used before.
Entries also are removed (that is, "aged out") from the password history list after the time
interval set by local password obsolescence. For example, if obsolescence is 30 days, then
any previous password used over 30 days ago is removed from the list, regardless of history-
size and regardless of how many passwords are in the history list.
Note that a password may rotate off the password history list before the obsolescence interval
passes for that password. To use history-size alone, disable the "aging out" effect by setting
local password obsolescence to 0.
Values of local password history-size are:
1..24 - Maximum number of entries in the local password history list.
0 - No local password history is kept. Any previously-used password can be reused at any time
regardless of the setting of local password obsolescence.
Enter the keyword without a value to display the current value.
local password obsolescence
Syntax
local password obsolescence [<value>]
System administration commands
Security commands
config admin authentication
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 337
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
0..999
Default
0
Specifies the password obsolescence Interval. This value is the time interval in days after a
user's password is changed when the previously-used password is removed from the local
password history list for that user. A password that is not on the local password history list can
be reused at any time. The size of the local password history list is set by the local password
history-size parameter. Values of local password obsolescence are:
1..999 - Number of days before a previously-used password is removed from the password
history list.
0 - Disables password obsolescence. A password can be reused only after it rotates off the
password history list.
Enter the keyword without a value to display the current value.

grace period or after the number of allowed logins has occurred (whichever happens later). Also

Sets whether the system prompts a user to change their password when they log in the first

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
For <reject-option> the value can be:
exit-on-reject
no-exit-on-reject
Default
exit-on-reject
Restrictions
In ANSSI mode, only the value "local" is allowed.
The "tacplus" option is not available on the 1830 PSS-4 shelf type.
Specifies which authentication method(s) to use for network element users. Specify up to three
different authentication methods:
• local - authentication is based on the local network element's user database. If
successful, the user is logged in with a defined local privilege level; otherwise an
access-reject occurs.
• radius - authentication is based on the RADIUS servers' database. A RADIUS server
will return an access-accept, in which case the user is logged in with an authorization
level, an access-reject, or not respond.
• tacplus - authentication is based on the TACACS+ servers' database. A TACACS+ will
return an access-accept, in which case the user is logged in and authorized separately
(local or TACACS+), an access-reject, or not respond.
If a RADIUS server does not respond, then authentication is tried with the next RADIUS server,
until all servers are checked. The NE will then retry all RADIUS servers again depending on
retry value (see 'config admin authentication radius retry'). This is similar for TACACS servers
except that there is no retry. In addition, the optional <reject-option> determines the action on
an access-reject:
• exit-on-reject - a reject from an authentication method will immediately deny login
without trying other methods. This is the default setting if <reject-option> is not provided.
• no-exit-on-reject - on reject from an authentication method, the NE will try the next
login method in the list. A login deny occurs only after all methods return an access-
reject, or none of the methods respond.
Authentication will be attempted in the specified order. If an authentication returns success
(e.g., RADIUS returns access-accept) the user is immediately logged in. If none of the servers
in authentication method (RADIUS or TACACS+) respond, then the next authentication method
in the list will be used. If an authentication method denies access (e.g., access-reject) then the
user is immediately denied access or the next method is tried, depending on the <reject-option>
setting. A method cannot be listed twice.
Enter the 'order' keyword alone to display the current value(s).
Note: if network-only authentication is used (i.e., radius, tacplus, radius tacplus, tacplus radius)
and the network authentication server(s) are not available, e.g., because of network issues,
then a login will not be possible except via the service user.

For a user that is authenticated with TACACS+, this defines the type of authorization that will be
used:
• priv-lvl - the TACACS+ server will return a privilege level which will be mapped to one of

defined for authorization, or no response is received from the servers, then login will fail.
• cmd-by-cmd - this authorization option means that every command that is entered will
be authorized by a TACACS+ server before being executed. If there are no TACACS+
servers defined for authorization, or no response is received from the servers, then the
specific command will fail.
• local - the privilege level of a matching local user is used. If the local user account does
not exist or is not enabled, authorization will fail and hence authentication will fail, i.e.,
the user will not be logged in.
If type is given without a value, then the current value is displayed.
Note: cmd-by-cmd authorization applies to CLI and TL1. Note: WebUI cannot utilize cmd-by-
cmd, and if type is cmd-by-cmd, WebUI will use priv-lvl. If the server does not return a privilege
level, then WebUI login will fail. If type is priv-lvl or local, WebUI will use the same.

3.19.4 Input Parameters
ssh login-mode
Syntax
ssh login-mode [<value>]
Values
cli-authentication - Login using the CLI shell authentication.
ssh-authentication - Login using the SSH authentication.
Default
ssh-authentication
Configures the authentication mode for the remote CLI terminal SSH login. Enter the parameter
without value to display the current setting.
cli-authentication:
Login using the CLI shell authentication. At the "login as" prompt, respond with "cli." Then the
SSH session is set up and the CLI console opens requiring the user authentication by entering
username and password before CLI commands can be issued.
ssh-authentication:
Login using the SSH authentication protocol. At the "login as" prompt, respond with the
username and then with the password. After establishing the SSH session, the user ends up at
the CLI prompt, is authenticated, and can proceed with CLI commands. Alternatively, if a public
key is configured then a local can proceed directly with CLI commands after typing the
username without entering a password.

compmode - backward compatibility mode, to be used while secure Network Trace
communication is not available on all network elements.
maintenance - maintenance mode, to be used during Network Trace communication
maintenance
securemode - secure mode, recommended mode during normal operation.
Note: The compmode is an insecure mode to be used only during upgrade, while not all
network elements are upgraded to a version supporting Network Trace security. After the
upgrade of the network is complete, it is recommended to switch to maintenance mode. The
maintenance mode ensures Network Trace communication on moderate security level. While
all network elements are in maintenance mode, security credentials for Network Trace can be
set on all network elements without communication impairment. When all network elements are
set to the same security credentials, it is recommended to switch to secure mode on all network
elements.

3.25 config admin powerman
3.25.1 Purpose
This command configures the security mode of the Power Management NE to NE communication.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.25.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Security of NE to NE communication
Access Levels: Administrator
3.25.3 Input Format
config admin powerman
security
3.25.4 Input Parameters
security
Syntax
security [<value>]
Values
maintenance - maintenance mode
securemode - secure mode
Default
maintenance
Sets the Power Management communication security mode:
maintenance - maintenance mode, to be used during Power Management communication
maintenance
securemode - secure mode, recommended mode during normal operation.
Note: In maintenance mode, the network element detects the Power Management
communication security capabilities of the NEs in the network and chooses the highest possible
security level in the network. While all network elements are in maintenance mode, security
credentials for Power Management can be set on all network elements without communication
impairment. When all network elements are set to the same security credentials, it is
recommended to switch to secure mode on all network elements. While in secure mode, the
mode is fixed. This ensures that a newly added network element does not enforce a switch to a
lower security level.

3.26 config admin protocol
3.26.1 Purpose
This command is used to configure the Loopback For All IP Services (LFAIS) as described in the
DCN Guide. This command configures the source IP address the NE uses for IP packets it
transmits for a given protocol. The user can choose the source IP address as follows:
• The IP address of the egress interface (any interface)
• The IP address of the loopback interface
The user can set the source IP address for a specific protocol or apply it to all protocols.
The initial state of the system is for all protocols to use the any interface. If the user changes the
source IP for one protocol, the source IP for the other protocols remain unchanged.
The user can set the source IP address for a specific protocol or apply it to all protocols.
The initial state of the system is for all protocols to use the any interface. If the user changes the
source IP for one protocol, the source IP for the other protocols remain unchanged.
Note: this command should be run only after the IP addresses of the loopback(s) and egress
interfaces (e.g., oamp) has been configured. If a protocol set to use the IP address of the loopback
interface and the IP address of the loopback is changed, this command should be run again.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.26.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

mutualauth
Syntax
mutualauth [<value>]
Values
enabled - enables the mutual authentication
disabled - disables the mutual authentication
Default
disabled
Enables or disables the mutual authentication. Enter this keyword without option to display the
current setting. If mutual authentication is enabled:
• A client certificate will be requested by the NE for the WebUI.
• The NE will perform certificate validation on all presented certificates for the WebUI,
Syslog over TLS, and RADSec. If the certificate validation fails, then the TLS connection
will be cancelled.
Note: san-authentication must be enabled for the verification of the FQDN or IP address in the
Subject Alternative Name extension of a received X.509v3 certificate. Mutual authentication is a
prerequisite for san-authentication (see "config admin security san-authentication").
Note: OCSP must be enabled for the verification of the revocation status of a received X.509v3
certificate (see "config admin pki ca <ca-profile> ocsp").
Note: If mutual authentication will be enabled, all TLS services supporting certificate
authentication will be affected immediately. Make sure that the trust anchor (see "config
keystore system trustanchor") contains all X.509v3 CA certificates (root and intermediate if
needed) for certificate chain resolution. This must be done before enabling mutual
authentication!
Note: If mutual authentication is disabled, then only a TLS channel without certificate
verification will be established for WebUI, Syslog over TLS, and RADSec.

3.31 config admin session
3.31.1 Purpose
This command configures the following user security parameters:
• Maximum number of consecutive failed login attempts, regardless of time interval or number of
sessions.
• Time that a session is allowed to remain inactive before the user is logged out and the user
session closed.
• Waiting time after a failed login until logins are allowed again
• Number of allowed simultaneous sessions per user
• Number of allowed logins per user
Note: Upon a failed login of a local NE user either after consecutive invalid login attempts
exceeding the Maximum of Invalid Login Attempts or two invalid login attempts during the Minimum
Wait Time after Invalid Login then the system changes the status of this user profile to disabled (the
user is locked out of the system). The last local Administrator privilege user will not be disabled.
This command affects sessions for CLI, WEBUI, TL1.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.31.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Specifies the maximum number of consecutive failed login attempts, regardless of time
interval or number of sessions. Specifies the time that a session is allowed to remain inactive
before the user will be logged out and the user session closed.

3.35 config admin snmpusers cert-fingerprint
3.35.1 Purpose
This command sets the X.509v3 certificate fingerprints together with the related snmpv3 users.
These fingerprints will be used for authentication of received X.509v3 certificates and their mapping
to the snmpv3 users for SNMP over TLS.
SNMP over TLS can be used for SNMPv3 users only which have a certificate configured. SNMP
over TLS authenticates the client automatically using the sent X.509v3 certificate. (Mutual
authentication must not be enabled for this (see "config admin security tls")).
If server certificate revocation status shall be verified, then the OCSP service must be enabled (see
"config admin pki ca <ca-profile> ocsp").
Note: A fingerprint for a certificate must be provisioned once only.
This command does not apply to the PSS-4 or to a PSS-16 or PSS-32 shelf with equipment
controller type "EC", i.e., classic EC, in the main shelf.
3.35.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Modifies the snmpuserv3 - X.509v3 certificate fingerprint mapping table.
Access Levels: Administrator
3.35.3 Input Format

Default

<fingerprint>

<fingerprint> - fingerprint as string in hex format, with or without colons.

3.36 config admin syslog
3.36.1 Purpose
This command configures the syslog options on the network element.
The configuration will be for each remote syslog server separately.
Use this command to:
• Display the current syslog configuration
• enable or disable system logging
• specify the IP address of the remote syslog server
• specify the port on the remote syslog server used for system logging
• specify the protocol used for transmission
• specify the minimum priority level of the messages to send through syslog
This command conforms with the BSD Syslog Protocol as defined in RFC 3164.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.36.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Specifies which log messages are sent through Syslog, and the location they are sent to.

410 Issue 1
If TLS is provisioned, then a TLS channel without certificate verification will be established
without doing the following configuration settings:
Syslog server certificate validation requires that mutual authentication is enabled (see "config
admin security tls"). A precondition for syslog server TLS authentication is that the trust anchor
(see "config keystore system trustanchor") contains all syslog server X.509v3 CA certificates
(root and intermediate if needed) for certificate chain resolution.

anchor configuration must be completed before enabling syslog!

extension shall be verified, then the san-authentication must be enabled and the FQDN or IP
address presented in the syslog server certificate must be contained in the SAN list (see "config

authentication must be properly configured with the syslog server FQDN or IP address before
enabling syslog!
If server certificate revocation status shall be verified, then the OCSP service must be enabled
(see "config admin pki ca <ca-profile> ocsp").
Note:When a TCP or TLS connection carrying syslog messages is reopened (e.g., due to
network element reset) and syslog messages can then be sent, a message is written into
syslog stating that syslog transmission has restarted and that messages may have been lost.
Any category of syslog message may have been lost, e.g., alarm, security event, configuration
change, status message, etc.

equipment controller type "EC", i.e., classic EC, in the main shelf.

3.37 config admin system
3.37.1 Purpose
This command configures the operations NOKIA maintenance and system user options for the
network element. Use this command to modify settings on operations system users and Security
Database for one of the NOKIA system users and to retrieve the statuses, e.g., the password
status, remote login status, local maintenance access or inactivity timeout. These users are not
administrative for the NE. They shall be enabled only as needed for the intended purpose and then
disabled.

sshkey
Syntax
sshkey <keyindex> <keystring>
Values
<keyindex> - 1,2 Index of the ssh key to be provisioned
<keystring> - "SSH key string" or empty string: ""
Default
empty string ""
The sshkey parameter provisions the user public keys used for user authentication. The
number of keys configurable per user is defined by the available key indices.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings - no public user key authentication will be applied.
If at least one key is provisioned, all provisioned keys can be used for user authentication.
The format of the string of the ssh key supported is the OpenSSH key format which can be
generated by the ssh-keygen command - "<type name> <base64 coded key string>
[<comment>]" (Ref RFC 4253). The content of the ".pub" file can be directly copied.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
Note: Only key types shall be provisioned, which are supported by the NE.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring>) deletes the provisioned key and removes it
from the system.
This command does not apply to the PSS-4 or to a PSS-16 or PSS-32 shelf with equipment
controller type "EC", i.e., classic EC, in the main shelf.

changed.

actual provisioned inactivity timer for the NOKIA maintenance users will be shown too.
It displays the SSH user public keys and snmp_sms user status for Equipment Controllers for
those this functionality is supported only.

3.39 config admin transfersyslog server
3.39.1 Purpose
This command sets the attributes for the server which shall upload NE syslog messages, which are
collected inside the NE.
The content of the transferred syslog messages is the same as done with the NE syslog streaming
functionally. It is just like another syslog stream.
Use this command to set:
• IP address and root directory of the log server
• Protocol and TCP port used to access the log server
• User identifier and password used to log in to the log server
• User private key for user key based authentication
• Host public key for host authentication
• period of automatic file transfer
Note: The command collects and transfers all messages which corresponds to a priority setting of
"debug" (minimum level / all messages) of the syslog settings. (see "config admin syslog")
This command does not apply to the PSS-4 or to a PSS-16 or PSS-32 shelf with equipment
controller type "EC", i.e., classic EC, in the main shelf.
3.39.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Specifies the location for syslog server for syslog file transfer and properties of the syslog
file transfer.
Access Levels: Administrator
3.39.3 Input Format

3.39.4 Input Parameters
hostkey
Syntax

Values

{1,2} - index of the public host key

The hostkey parameter provisions the host public keys used for host authentication. The
number of keys configurable per host is defined by the available key indices.
If no keys are provisioned -- empty strings or spaces only for all key entries -- no host key
authentication will be applied.
If at least one key is provisioned, all provisioned keys can be used for user authentication.
Provisioning a second key allows key rotation without service interruption. After a new key is
deployed on server side the old one should be removed. A normal secure configuration applies
one key only.
The format of the string of the ssh key supported is the OpenSSH key format which can be
generated by the ssh-keygen command - "<type name> <base64 coded key string>
[<comment>]" (Ref RFC 4253). The content of the ".pub" file can be directly copied.
The host name, ip address and port, will be taken from the provisioned ip address and port
number.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring>) deletes the provisioned key and removes it
from the system.
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin
security ssh" command.
Note: The hostkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.

sshprivkey
Syntax
sshprivkey <keystring> [<password>]
Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 character SSH key string.
"" - to clear the string.
Default
Entry required
Values
For <password>:
<string> - UTF-8 string, 1..64 characters in double quotes.
"" - empty string for no password.
Default
""
The sshprivkey parameter provisions the user private keys used for user authentication on
server side. If no keys are provisioned -- empty strings -- no public user key authentication will
be applied.
The format of the string of the SSH key supported is the OpenSSH private key PEM file format
which can be generated by the ssh-keygen command
The format looks like:
"-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----b3BlbnNzaC1rZXktdjEAAA ...
RAQ0VDMi04MS0yAQIDBA==-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----"
The key must be surrounded by quotation marks.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring> = "") deletes the provisioned key and
removes it from the system.
The private key can be protected by a password, which is needed by the system for decryption.
Following behavior of this parameter applies:
• If a password is provided, the key is password or pass phrase protected. If a pass
phrase contains spaces, it must be surrounded by quotation marks.
• If an empty string is provided, the key is not password protected. Empty string means: ""
is provided.
• If no password string is provided, the system asks for a password. If in this case ENTER
is typed without typing a password or pass phrase the key is not password protected.

3.40 config admin ui
3.40.1 Purpose
This command configures the user interface security mode on the network element.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.40.2 Command Access Level
Impact: The NE is set to secure or non-secure mode
Access Levels: Administrator
3.40.3 Input Format
config admin ui
brief
mode
3.40.4 Input Parameters
brief
Displays the current security mode:
encrypted - only allows UDP/TCP Network ports with encrypted protocols including SSHv2,
HTTPS, TLS, SFTP and SNMPv3
normal - allows Telnet, HTTP and SNMPv1/v2 in addition to the access protocols allowed in
encrypted mode.
fips - legacy mode for use with R7 FIPS for use with Key Management Tool(KMT) and Photonic
Manager(PhM) - fixed use of SNMPv3 aes256/sha1 for all SNMP connections
anssi - only allows UDP/TCP Network ports with encrypted protocols including SSH and TLS
and SNMPv3 specific for ANSSI configurations
mode
Syntax
mode [<value>] [force]
Values
encrypted - only allows UDP/TCP Network ports with encrypted protocols including SSHv2,
HTTPS, TLS, SFTP and SNMPv3- defaults to using AES128/MD5 for SNMPv3 but allows
different provisioning of SNMP encrypted choices for different SNMP users.
normal - allows unsecure protocols including, but not limited to, Telnet, HTTP, FTP,
SNMPv1/v2 addition to the access protocols allowed in encrypted mode.
fips - legacy mode for use with R7 FIPS for use with Key Management Tool(KMT) and
Photonic Manager(PhM) - fixed use of SNMPv3 aes256/sha1 for all SNMP connections
System administration commands
Security commands
config admin ui

Release 24.12

Issue 1 429
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Default
normal
Sets the user interface secure mode.
Note: Changing the User Interface mode will cause the Network Element to reset, which will
reboot all line cards in a node too. This includes all L2 SR OS packets cards, which suffer a
several minute traffic hit during a warm reset.
Note: Changing the UI mode will also reset the Access Control List to the system default
setting. See the command 'config acl_default restore-default' for details.
The force directive at the end of the line makes this command re-issue safe in that a repeat of
the same setting (setting is the same as already configured) will not be flagged as an error.
That is, the NE will not return an error message in this scenario and will not change any
parameter values.
The force directive also bypasses the confirmation prompt as though the operator had included
the yes directive at the end of the command line. That is, when the force directive is used, there
is no need to say force yes at the end of the command.
Restrictions
In ANSSI mode, the parameter is not allowed.

normal Configure node to normal mode
fips Configure node to fips mode

3.45 config admin users logging {cli | snmp}
3.45.1 Purpose
This command configures the options for logging user activity on the network element:
• For users accessing the network element through CLI, the 'cli' option applies to all (UI) user
interfaces (CLI, TL1 or WEBUI).
• For users accessing the network element through SNMP, the 'snmp' option applies.
Use this command to:
• Display which operations (read or write) are currently logged for users accessing the network
element through UI or SNMP
• Enable or disable logging for all users accessing the network element through UI or SNMP
• Define whether write operations are logged for the CLI or SNMP userids
Note: Although read operations appear in the syntax display in the CLI or SNMP, read operation
logging is not supported.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.

detail
This parameter shall give the administrator detailed information about:
• The installed certificates in the Trust Anchor.
• The status of the download and installation process.
• The content of the downloaded and not yet installed new Trust Anchor certificates.
download
Syntax
download
Downloads the certificates of the Trust Anchor.
The result of the operation can be retrieved by the status or detailed parameter.
The download request will be rejected if the current status is dwdlinprogress because of a
previously download.
The download will be rejected if basic parameters required are not provided. This are the
protocol, host, file name in location.
default
Syntax
default
Sets the Trust Anchor back to the default Trust Anchor value provided by NOKIA for this
release.
Note: Each new software load may contain a new default Trust Anchor.

Syntax

Installs a previously downloaded new Trust Anchor. The installation succeeds if the status has
the value: downloaded. In all other cases the command will be rejected. That means there must
be a valid new Trust Anchor downloaded first.

Release 24.12
December 2024
454 Issue 1
server location
Syntax
server location [<location>]
Values
<location> - file location on the server including path and file name.
Default
""
Specifies the location (path) where the file is located on the server. The path must start always
with the leading "/".
The file extension of the file containing the certificates must be ".pem".
The file must follow these rules:
• The file is in PEM format
• The file contains X.509v3 certificates only and they are readable.
• The sequence of the certificates is according the chain of trust. The certificate which is
needed for verification must be contained before.
• The base64 string length of a certificate must not exceed 4096 characters.
• A maximum of 256 certificates will be supported in one file.
server port
Syntax
server port [<port>]
Values
<port> - port value. This is an numerical value between 1 .. 65535
Default
443 for https
Specifies the host port where the service is offered. If the port is empty the default port for the
specified protocol will be used.
server protocol
Syntax
server protocol [https]
Values
https - https / TLS protocol
Default
https
Specifies the type of protocol used.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
server uri
Syntax
server uri [<uri>]
Values
<uri> - URI/URL of the file containing the certificates of the Trust Anchor.
Default
"https://"
Specifies the server parameters in the URI form. It replaces all server parameters (host,
location, port, protocol) with the provided values. If some parameters are not contained in the
provided URI, the default ones will be taken. Example: if the port is not specified, then the
default port value 443 is used for the https protocol.
The URI contains the used protocol, the location of the file on the server and the file name as
well.
For the path part of the URI please refer the location parameter.
If the URI configuration is accepted, all the parameters will be updated (ip, port, location ... )
acc. the URI specification.
Restrictions
The host name provided in the URI can be an IPv4 or IPv6 address only. (see host
parameter)
The supported protocol is https only. No URI parameters and user specification are
supported.

detail
This parameter shall give the administrator detailed information about:
• The installed certificates in the Trust Anchor.

• The content of the downloaded and not yet installed new Trust Anchor certificates.
download
Syntax
download
Downloads the certificates of the Trust Anchor. A downloaded Trust Anchor but not yet installed
one can be overwritten and replaced by reissuing the "config keystore system trustanchor
download" command.
The result of the operation can be retrieved by the status or detail parameter.
The download request will be rejected if the current status is dwdlinprogress because of a
previous download.
The download will be rejected if basic parameters required are not provided. These are the
protocol, host, file name, and location.
expiration-warning
Syntax
expiration-warning [<value>]
Values
0..255 - Number of days before a certificate expires to send an initial certificate expiration
warning alarm for trustanchor certificates.
Default
30
Configures the certificate expiration warning period for trustanchor certificates. Setting to 0
disables sending of warning.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
Note: Certificate expiration is audited daily. After the initial alarm, subsequent alarms are issued
once in a day until the certificate expiry date. The certificate must be changed before expiration
to avoid any potential service interruption.
install
Syntax
install
Installs a previously downloaded new Trust Anchor. The installation succeeds if the status has
the value: downloaded. In all other cases the command will be rejected. That means there must
be a valid new Trust Anchor downloaded first. The Trust Anchor becomes active immediately
after installation.

3.49 config keystore system trustanchor server
3.49.1 Purpose
The command sets the attributes for the management of certificates installed in the system Trust
Anchor server.
Use this command to set:
• IP address of the server.
• Path location on the server.
• Type of protocol.
• Host port.
• User credentials.
• ssh key for host and user authentication.
This command does not apply to the PSS-4 or to a PSS-16 or PSS-32 shelf with equipment
controller type "EC", i.e., classic EC, in the main shelf.
3.49.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Modifies certificates installed in the System Trust Anchor. These certificates are used for
authentication. A misconfiguration may result in a behavior that the server which shall be contacted
by the Network Element will be not accepted any more.
Access Levels: Administrator
3.49.3 Input Format
config keystore system trustanchor server
host
hostkey
location
port
protocol
sshprivkey
userid
3.49.4 Input Parameters
hostkey
Syntax
hostkey [<keyindex> <keystring>]
System administration commands
Security commands
config keystore system trustanchor server
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 471
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
For <keyindex>:
{1,2} - index of the public host key
Default
Entry required
Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 characters containing the SSH key string in OpenSSH format.
"" - to clear the string.
Default
Entry required
Provisions the host keys used for host authentication. The number of keys configurable per
host is defined by the available key indices.
If no keys are provisioned, then no host key authentication will be applied.
If at least one key is provisioned, all provisioned keys can be used for user authentication.
Provisioning a second key allows key rotation without service interruption. After a new key is
deployed on server side the old one should be removed by setting an empty string "" for the
keyindex which holds the old key. A normal secure configuration applies one key only.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
The supported format of the ssh key is the OpenSSH key format which can be generated by the
ssh-keygen command - "<type name> <base64 coded key string> [<comment>]" (Ref RFC
4253). The content of the ".pub" file can be directly copied.
The host name, ip address and port, will be taken from the provisioned IP address and port
number.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring>) deletes the provisioned key and removes it
from the system.
Note: Only key types can be provisioned, which are supported by the NE. See "config admin
security ssh" command.
Restrictions
The hostkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.

The supported format of the SSH key is the OpenSSH private key PEM file format which can be
generated by the ssh-keygen command
The format looks like:
"-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----b3BlbnNzaC1rZXktdjEAAA ...
RAQ0VDMi04MS0yAQIDBA==-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----"
The key must be surrounded by quotation marks.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring> = "") deletes the provisioned key and
removes it from the system.
The private key can be protected by a password, which is used by the system for decryption.
The following behavior applies:
• If a password is provided, the key is password or pass phrase protected. If a pass
phrase contains spaces, it must be surrounded by quotation marks.
• If an empty string ("") is provided, the key is not password protected.
• If no password string is provided, the system asks for a password. If in this case ENTER
is typed without typing a password or pass phrase the key is not password protected.
If the sshprivkey parameter will be typed in without a value, then the fingerprint of the currently
provisioned key will be shown.
Note: Only key types can be provisioned, which are supported by the NE. See "config admin
security ssh" command.
Restrictions
The sshprivkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.

Default
""
Specifies the userid for accessing the log server. After the userid is entered, you will be
prompted to enter a password value. Enter <cr> for no password value.
The maximum supported username length is 32 characters. The maximum password length
supported is 256 characters.

3.50 config sslcert
3.50.1 Purpose
Use this command to install a X.509v3 NE certificate used for TLS / HTTPS connections.
Before certificate installation the X.509v3 certificate will be verified for:
• validity
• chain of trust (issuer of certificate)
• trust bits
• (extended) key purpose
• revocation status
End Entity or self-signed certificates will be accepted.
If the verification fails, the command will be rejected.
Note: Installing the X.509v3 certificate may cause a NE warm reboot.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.50.2 Command Access Level
Impact: The SSL certificate required for secure/encrypted mode; Network Element will be rebooted.
Access Levels: Administrator
3.50.3 Input Format
config sslcert [certverification]
config sslcert
certverification
expiration-warning
3.50.4 Input Parameters
certverification
Specifies that the X.509v3 certificate will be verified before installation. This means verification
of:
• validity
• chain of trust (issuer of certificate)
• basicConstraints
• (extended) key purpose
• revocation status
System administration commands
Security commands
config sslcert
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 477
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
expiration-warning
Syntax
expiration-warning [<value>]
Values
0..255 - Number of days before a certificate expires to send an initial certificate expiration
warning alarm for NE certificates.
Default
30
Configures the certificate expiration warning period for NE certificate. Setting to 0 disables
sending of warning.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
Note: Certificate expiration is audited daily. After the initial alarm, subsequent alarms are issued
once in a day until the certificate expiry date. The certificate must be changed before expiration
to avoid any potential service interruption.
3.50.5 Examples
The following example shows the installation of the NE certificate without verification:

The following example shows the installation of the NE certificate with verification of the
certificate:
# config sslcert certverification
WARNING: You are about to install the SSL certificate. This will cause a warm
reboot of the Network Element.
Enter 'yes' to confirm, 'no' to cancel: no
The following example provisions an expiration warning for the certificates:
# config sslcert expiration-warning 5

3.51 config sslcsr
3.51.1 Purpose
This command is used to provision ssl certificate parameters in order to send to NMS for signing
request
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.51.2 Command Access Level
Impact: The SSL certificate required for secure/encrypted mode
Access Levels: Administrator

config sslcsr
details
country
state
loc
org
orguni
cn

san

3.51.4 Input Parameters
details
Display the SSL certificate configuration parameters and certificate status.
The SSL CSR status can be 'editing', 'completed', 'inProgress', 'failed' or 'none'.
1. Changing any parameter of CSR, NE will set the CSR status to 'editing'.
2. After users issue a "generate", the NE will set the CSR status to 'inProgress', then to
'completed' or 'failed'.
3. The CSR status must be 'completed' before users try to upload the CSR to NMS.
4. Finishing installation of CERT, NE will change the status from 'completed' to 'none'.

Country name.

3.52 crypto key
3.52.1 Purpose
Configure the network element to set to secure mode.
Use this command to:
• Generate RSA, ECDSA, ED25519 SSH keys to be used in secure mode
• Display SSH key information
• Zeroize the SSH key
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.52.2 Command Access Level
Impact: The RSA, ECDSA, ED25519 keys are available for SSH to use.
Access Levels: Administrator
3.52.3 Input Format
crypto key
detail
generate all [<rsa-length> <ecdsa-length>]
generate rsa [<rsa-length>]
generate ecdsa [<ecdsa-length>]
generate ed25519
zeroize
3.52.4 Input Parameters
detail
Displays the SSH key information
The command displays the RSA, ECDSA and ED255519 SSH public keys in OpenSSH file
format according to RFC4716 as Base64 coded ASCII string. The ASCII characters are
represented as hexadecimal bytes.
The length indicates the length of the ASCII string.
While an SSH key generation is in progress, the command does not display the SSH keys. A
message is displayed indicating that a key generation is in progress.
Sub-command: generate all
Syntax
generate all [<rsa-length> <ecdsa-length>]
Generates all SSH keys
System administration commands
Security commands
crypto key
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 483
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
The optional length values indicate the length of the RSA and ECDSA key. If the length is
omitted, then the RSA and ECDSA key is generated with their default key length.
Note: The length of the ED25519 key is fixed to 256 bits.
If the key generation request can be fulfilled immediately, then the command displays the newly
generated keys. In the case, the key generation takes longer time, the command returns a
message indicating the key generation in progress.
If the ed25519 public key algorithm for host keys is not enabled (see "config admin security ssh
<ssh-profile> hostkeyalgorithms") then the ed25519 key type will be not generated.
Sub-command: generate rsa
Syntax
generate rsa [<rsa-length>]
Generates the RSA type SSH key only.
The optional length values indicate the length of the RSA key. If the length is omitted, then the
RSA key is generated with the default key length.
If the key generation request can be fulfilled immediately, then the command displays the newly
generated key. In the case, the key generation takes longer time, the command returns a
message indicating the key generation in progress.
Sub-command: generate ecdsa
Syntax
generate ecdsa [<ecsda-length>]
Generates the ECDSA type SSH key only.
The optional length values indicate the length of the ECDSA key. If the length is omitted, then
the ECDSA key is generated with the default key length.
If the key generation request can be fulfilled immediately, then the command displays the newly
generated key. In the case, the key generation takes longer time, the command returns a
message indicating the key generation in progress.
Sub-command: generate ed25519
Syntax
generate ed25519
Generates the ED25519 type SSH key only.
The ED25519 key type does not need a length specified, because all keys have a length of 256
bit.
If the key generation request can be fulfilled immediately, then the command displays the newly
generated key. In the case, the key generation takes longer time, the command returns a
message indicating the key generation in progress.
Note:When generating the ed25519 key type, the ssh-ed25519 public key algorithm for host
keys must be enabled for making them operationable (see "config admin security ssh <ssh-
profile> hostkeyalgorithms").

502 Issue 1
connection-state
Displays the state of the connection to the OCSP responder.
Returned Values:
• OCSP responder not enabled
• OCSP responder not recognized
• OCSP responder unreachable
• OCSP connection good
OCSP responder not enabled - Indicates that the OCSP responder has not been enabled.
OCSP responder not recognized - Indicates the NE is not able to verify the digital signatures of
the OCSP responses. Check the OSCP responder configuration and install new certificates on
the OCSP responder or NE as needed.
OCSP responder unreachable - Indicates the NE received an internal error code back from the
OCSP responder, which may be due to a potential network error. Check the configured IP
address of the OCSP responder or the network connection to the OCSP responder.
OCSP connection good - Indicates the connection to the OCSP responder is good.
3.61.5 Examples
# show admin pki ca ca-system ocsp
server
======
url : http://ocsp.exampleca.com
connection-state : OCSP connection good
status : enabled
timeout : 10 seconds
retry : 1
# show admin pki ca ca-system ocsp connection-state
connection-state : OCSP connection good

3.63.5 Output Parameters
Output Parameter Description
Protocol The protocol which uses the listed Source IP Address. The entry for Protocol all indicates the steps
used for configuring the Source IP Address. See definition of "Source IP Address" below.
Source IP Address The source IP address used by the listed Protocol. The possible values are:
• any - Uses the address of the egress interface
• loopback - Uses the loopback address
• N/A - Applies only to a Protocol value of all. Indicates that the Source IP Address settings have
been configured individually to each Protocol. If Protocol all displays one of the other values, then
the Source IP Setting was configured using one command applied to all the Protocols.

3.74 show sslcert
3.74.1 Purpose
This command is used to display the status of SSL certificate installation.
The following certificate details are displayed:
• Country
• State
• Locality
• Organisation
• Organization Unit
• Host Name
• Email Address
• Subject Alternative Name
• Signature Algorithm
• Validity
• Expiration Warning
Note: The attributes Country, State, Locality, Organization, Organization Unit, Host Name, Email
Address and Subject Alternative Name are taken over from the certificate signing request (CSR). If
the CSR has been modified since the last certificate generation, then the displayed certificate
details do no longer match the attributes of the installed certificate. Whether the CSR has been
modified is indicated in the CSR status, which can be retrieved using "config sslcsr details".
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.

3.80 config acl_pattern
3.80.1 Purpose
The command can be used to define a new pattern on the system to be used for IPv4 Access
Control.
An ACL Pattern is a set of packet field descriptors that can be tested against an IPv4 packet. For a
pattern to match, each of its field descriptors must fit the data in the packet. The fields that may be
tested are:
• Source IPv4 address (or range)
• Destination IPv4 address (or range)
• TCP/UDP destination port
• IP protocol
• IP fragmentation
• ICMP type and code
• Whether or not a TCP packet belongs to an established connection
Each field test is optional: a pattern may specify only some (or no) fields to test. Each pattern also
has an associated action to take when the pattern matches: block, pass or log. Regardless of the
associated action, when a match occurs the match count (statCount) will be incremented for the
pattern within the filter. If a pattern specifies a block action, it may also have an ICMP error
reporting behavior, which affects generation of ICMP 3 (Destination Unreachable) / 13
(Communication Administratively Prohibited) errors for forwarded packets that are blocked. The
total combination of <filter-id> and <pattern-id> cannot exceed 4000.
By using the command on a pattern already created, the system will overwrite the old pattern with
the new settings. System default patterns, however, cannot be modified.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.80.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator
3.80.3 Input Format
config acl_pattern <pattern-id>
action
delete
detail

dstPort

Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
pass - action is to pass the packet
block - action is to block, i.e., drop the packet
log - action is to log the packet
Default
pass
Action to take on packets matching the ACL pattern. With the 'pass' and the 'block' (i.e., drop)
action, ACL processing will cease upon match.
With the 'log' action, a summary of the matched packet will be recorded (logged) and sent to
syslog, and ACL processing will continue to the next pattern. Hence, in order to log and then
block a packet, there would need to be two identical patterns varying only by action: the first
pattern would be action 'log' and the second pattern would be action 'block'. Note that logging of
packets is rate limited and hence not all packets in a stream may be logged. Also note that
priority of logged packet summary is DEBUG(7), which is the default priority for syslog
messages (see 'config admin syslog priority').
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.

Release 24.12
December 2024
550 Issue 1
• Enabled (true): Will match a packet if the TCP flags in the IP header correspond to the
"established" state.
• Local:Will only attempt to match packets that are destined for this NE, in which case
tcpESTABLISHED=Enabled will be applied to the packet. Packets that are going through
the NE will have tcpESTABLISHED=Disabled applied to the packet.
The local value is commonly used if there is asymmetric routing on the node, i.e., a connection
request egress one GNE, and the response or ACK (established) ingresses through a different
GNE.
The true/false values are accepted for compatibility with previous releases. The parameter is
only applicable when IP Protocol is TCP.

3.80.5 Examples

will only log the packet, but not drop it. A separate pattern must be created to block the packet.

# config acl_pattern LogTelnet102 action log
# config acl_pattern LogTelnet102 ipproto TCP
# config acl_pattern LogTelnet102 dstport 23
# config acl_pattern LogTelnet102 srcipaddr 102.33.5.0
# config acl_pattern LogTelnet102 srcipprefix 0.0.0.255
Create a pattern to block telnet to from a subnet 102.33.5.0/24

# config acl_pattern BlockTelnet102 action block
# config acl_pattern BlockTelnet102 ipproto TCP
# config acl_pattern BlockTelnet102 dstport 23
# config acl_pattern BlockTelnet102 srcipaddr 102.33.5.0

3.81 config acl_port
3.81.1 Purpose
This command is used to associate (or disassociate) an IPv4 access control list (ACL) filter with a
physical interface or logical sub-interface, enable (or disable) a filter, or set logging on an interface.
The physical interfaces are:
• LAN ports,
• OSC ports,
• GCCs (for example, NETIF-23),
• Ethernet In-band Management interfaces (for example, ETHIF-5)
The logical sub-interfaces are:
• LAN-PPP, which represents all GCC and OSC interfaces, and
• LAN-ETH, which represents all ETHIF interfaces.
Two filters may be associated with each interface, one receives, and one transmit. The receive and
transmit filters on an interface may be independently enabled and disabled. Once a filter is
associated to an interface, the filter cannot be associated to other interfaces.
The physical LAN interfaces depend on the main shelf type, user panel, shelf panel, and/or the
related EC/MFC.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables”, User service interfaces for the LAN interfaces on each of the
supported shelf types.
3.81.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Limited communication towards/ from different IPs
Access Levels: Administrator
3.81.3 Input Format
config acl_port <acl-port-aid> <direction>
add filter
modify status
modify log
remove

default action in the Rx direction must be 'block' in order to enable logging.

Received packet action : block
Transmitted packet action : pass
SNMP Configuration Access : Enabled

3.84 config acl_pattern6
3.84.1 Purpose
The command can be used to define a new pattern on the system to be used for IPv6 Access
Control.
An ACL Pattern6 is a set of packet field descriptors that can be tested against an IPv6 packet. For a
pattern to match, each of its field descriptors must fit the data in the packet. The fields that may be
tested are:
• Source IPv6 address and prefix-len
• Destination IPv6 address and prefix-len
• TCP/UDP destination port
• IP protocol
• ICMP type and code
• Whether or not a TCP packet belongs to an established connection
Each field test is optional: a pattern may specify only some (or no) fields to test. Each pattern also
has an associated action to take when the pattern matches: block, pass or log. Regardless of the
associated action, when a match occurs, the match count (statCount) is incremented for the pattern
within the filter. If a pattern specifies a block action, it may also specify an ICMP error reporting
behavior, which affects generation of ICMP 3 (Destination Unreachable) / 13 (Communication
Administratively Prohibited) errors for forwarded packets that are blocked. Total combination of
<filter-id> and <pattern-id> shall not exceed 4000.
By using the command on a pattern already created, the system will overwrite the old pattern with
the new settings.
This command applies to most 1830 PSS shelf types.
Note: This command does not apply to the PSS-4 or to the PSS-16 or PSS-32 shelf with equipment
controller type "EC", i.e., classic EC. These shelves do not support IPv6."
3.84.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None

566 Issue 1
Default
pass
Action to take on packets matching the ACL pattern. With the 'pass' and the 'block' (i.e., drop)
action, ACL processing will cease upon match.
With the 'log' action, a summary of the matched packet will be recorded (logged) and sent to
syslog, and ACL processing will continue to the next pattern. Hence, in order to log and then
block a packet, there would need to be two identical patterns varying only by action: the first
pattern would be action 'log' and the second pattern would be action 'block'. Note that logging of
packets is rate limited and hence not all packets in a stream may be logged. Also note that
priority of logged packet summary is DEBUG(7), which is the default priority for syslog
messages (see 'config admin syslog priority').

tcpestablished
Syntax
tcpestablished [<value>]
Values
{enabled, disabled, local}
{true, false}
Default
disabled
The TCP Established flag matches a packet depending on whether the TCP flags in the IP
header correspond to the "established" state. The packet must be associated with a connection
attempt in the opposite direction. The flag can have the following values:
• Disabled (false): Will match a packet without considering the TCP flags in the IP header.
• Enabled (true): Will match a packet if the TCP flags in the IP header correspond to the
"established" state, meaning that the packet is associated with a connection which has
seen packets in both directions.
• Local:Will only attempt to match packets that are destined for this NE, in which case
tcpESTABLISHED=Enabled will be applied to the packet. Packets that are going through
the NE will have tcpESTABLISHED=Disabled applied to the packet.
The true/false values are accepted for compatibility with previous releases. The parameter is
only applicable when IP Protocol is TCP.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.

3.85 config acl_port6
3.85.1 Purpose
This command is used to associate (or disassociate) an IPv6 access control list (ACL) filter with a
physical interface or logical sub-interface, enable (or disable) a filter, or set logging on an interface.
The physical interfaces are:
• LAN ports,
• OSC ports,
• GCCs (for example, NETIF-23),
• Ethernet In-band Management interfaces (for example, ETHIF-5)
The logical sub-interfaces are:
• LAN-PPP, which represents all GCC and OSC interfaces, and
• LAN-ETH, which represents all ETHIF interfaces.
Two filters may be associated with each interface, one receives, and one transmit. The receive and
transmit filters on an interface may be independently enabled and disabled. Once a filter is
associated to an interface, the filter cannot be associated to other interfaces.
The physical LAN interfaces depend on the main shelf type, user panel, shelf panel, and/or the
related EC/MFC.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables”, User service interfaces for the LAN interfaces on each of the
supported shelf types.
This command applies to most PSS shelf types.
Note: This command does not apply to the PSS-4 or to the PSS-16 or PSS-32 shelf with equipment
controller type "EC", i.e., classic EC. These shelves do not support IPv6."
3.85.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Limit IPv6 communication into and out of different interfaces
Access Levels: Administrator

3.87 config cn bgp
3.87.1 Purpose
This command is used to configure BGP the NE.
Restrictions: The BGP feature is not available on the PSS-4, or the PSS-16 and PSS-32 shelves
with equipment controller 'EC'. See Appendix A, “Reference tables”, User service interfaces table.
3.87.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Specifies BGP for the network element.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.87.3 Input Format
config cn bgp
asn
distance
neighbor
3.87.4 Input Parameters
asn
Syntax
asn [<as-number>]
Values
0..4294967295
Default
0
Set the Autonomous System Number (ASN), which will enable BGP on the NE. Setting the ASN
to 0 will disable BGP on the NE. Any ASN can be used, though guidelines should be followed to
avoid a specialty ASN or an ASN owned by some other organization.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables”, Autonomous System Number Definition. Enter this
keyword without a value to display the current ASN.
Note: the NE can only have one ASN.
Note: the BGP router ID will be the same as the (IPv4) loopback address.
distance
Syntax
distance [<value>]
System administration commands
Data communication network commands
config cn bgp
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
580 Issue 1
Values
1..255
Default
20
Set the administrative distance of BGP protocol. The distance value is used to determine which
route to be entered in the NE routing table when there are multiple identical routes discovered
through different routing protocols. Lower values have higher precedence.
Enter this keyword without a value to display the current administrative distance.
BGP distance can be used to give one GNE preference over another GNE. BGP has a default
distance value of 20, and hence is preferred over OSPF routes which has a distance of 110. If
the BGP distance is set to a value greater than 110 then the same route in OSPF will take
precedence and be installed in the NE routing table. In this case, using the default route
redistributed into OSPF as an example, GNE1 has BGP distance 20 and GNE2 has BGP
distance 120. The network will accept the default route on GNE1 from BGP, but not accept the
default route on GNE2 from BGP. GNE2 will instead use the default route from OSPF (distance
110, originally from GNE1), unless the route is lost at GNE1 due to lost connection.
If a distance value of 255 is entered, the route will NOT be installed in the routing table. A
distance value of 255 is used to indicate an Unknown route.
Sub-command: neighbor
Configure a BGP peer on the NE. See subcommand "config cn bgp neighbor".
3.87.5 Examples
Set the BGP Autonomous System Number (ASN) on the NE to 64555
# config cn bgp asn 64555
Disable BGP on the local host by setting the Autonomous System Number (ASN) to 0.
# config cn bgp asn 0
Set the BGP administrative distance to 120, which is a lower precedence than OSPF
(distance 110)
# config cn bgp distance 120

Modify any or all of the parameter values for BGP IPv4 prefix-limits, including:

3.91 config cn dhcp_relay
3.91.1 Purpose
This command configures DHCP relay on the system, specifying two ports which the relay will
transit, and the DHCP server where the requests will be sent.
Note that this command can be used to configure the relaying of DHCPv4 or DHCPv6 messages.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.91.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.91.3 Input Format
config cn dhcp_relay
detail
add <port-aid1> <port-aid2> <DHCP-Server-IP> [rail-id]
delete
3.91.4 Input Parameters
Sub-command: detail
List details of the DHCP Relay services.
Sub-command: add
Syntax
add <port-aid1> <port-aid2> <DHCP-Server-IP> [rail-id] [force]
Add a DHCP Relay service, with two interfaces (<port-aid1> & <port-aid2>) which can receive
and forward DHCP requests to a DHCP Server (<DHCP-Server-IP>). The optional <rail-id> will
further identify service.
The force directive at the end of the line makes the add subcommand re-issue safe in that a
repeat adding of the same DHCP Relay service (all settings the same as already configured)
will not be flagged as an error. That is, the NE will not return an error message in this scenario
and will not change any parameter values.
The force directive at the end of the line allows the add sub-command to be used to modify the
rail-id parameter. When the add sub-command is used in this way, the combination of port-
aid1, port-aid2, and DHCP-Server-IP must be a combination that is already provisioned. If the
combination of port-aid1, port-aid2, and DHCP-Server-IP does not match a combination
already configured, then the NE will create a new DHCP Relay service just as it would if the
force directive was omitted. Note that one, two, or three of these parameters being different
from an existing combination triggers the NE to create a new service.
The force directive may be used in scripting to suppress unnecessary error messages.

Data communication network commands

Restrictions
This parameter has no meaning unless dhcp_client is enabled.
If there is more than one dhcp client port, only one of the ports can have dhcp_client_

Syntax
ipv6_autoconfig [<value>]
Values
enabled - enable IPv6 AutoConfig on the port
disabled - disable IPv6 AutoConfig on the port
Default
disabled
Enable or disable IPv6 automatic configuration on the port. If enabled, the port will be assigned
an address via StateLess Address AutoConfig (SLAAC) or stateful DHCPv6, depending on the
Router Advertisement received from the attached router. For SLAAC, the port will receive an
advertised network of 64 bits (i.e., /64 prefix length); the port will then dynamically form a 64 bit
host identifier using modified EUI-64 rules, thus creating a full IPv6 address. For DHCPv6 a full
IPv6 address, with /128 prefix length, will be assigned.

routestate
Syntax
routestate [disabled | enabled | redistribute]
Values
disabled - Disable OSPF routing.
enabled - Enable OSPF routing.
redistribute - Redistribute the interface's subnet in OSPF, but do not participate in OSPF.
Default
disabled
Set the OSPF routing state of the ETHIF interface. Enter this keyword without a parameter to
display the current OSPF routing state.
When set to enabled, OSPF attempts to form adjacencies with other devices on the ETHIF
interface, and distribute routes.
When set to disabled, the subnet on the ETHIF interface is not distributed to OSPF.
When set to redistribute, the NE treats the ETHIF interface as a network outside its
autonomous system, and distributes this interface's address through OSPF. The interface,
however, does not participate in OSPF.

helloint
Syntax
helloint [<value>]
Values
1..65534 - time in seconds
Default
10 seconds
Specifies the Hello interval for the link. The Hello interval specifies how often (in seconds) a
hello packet is sent out on the interface. Hello packets are used to establish and maintain
relationships with neighboring network elements.
Note: The helloint must be set to identical values on all OSPF routers/NEs connected to same
LAN segment.
Enter this keyword followed by an integer value to set the Hello interval.
Enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current value for the Hello interval.
metric
Syntax
metric [<value>]
Values
1..65535
Default
16
Specifies the traffic engineering metric or cost for the control network link. The metric is an
integer value that specifies the cost of sending traffic over the link. The lower the cost, the more
preferred the interface is for the routing of packets. OSPF always detects the lowest cost route
for the given prefix in the IP forwarding table. Enter this keyword followed by an integer value
for the traffic engineering metric. Enter this keyword without any parameters to display the
current value of metric.

Default

Configures the OSPF time between LSA transmissions. The option specifies the length of time,

Default
40 seconds
OSPF Router Dead Interval of the interface. This is the time elapsed between not hearing a
router's Hello PDU before the interface OSPF state is declared down. The dead interval is a
timer used to timeout inactive adjacencies. The dead interval value must be greater than the
hello interval value. By default, the interface shall be set to four times the value of the
HELLOINT, so the default is 40 seconds. Enter the keyword without any value to display the
current setting.
Enter this keyword followed by an integer value for the dead interval, in seconds. Enter this
keyword without any parameters to display the current value of dead interval.

the same LAN segment.

3.101 config cn netif add
3.101.1 Purpose
This command allows the operator to create a network interface (NETIF) instance over an
embedded communication channel (ECC). The only type of ECC currently supported for this
command is GCC.
There are limits on the number of NETIFs that can be provisioned on an NE and on a shelf. An NE
supports up to 512 NETIFs, except when the main shelf has an EC or an 8EC2 in which case the
limit is 128 NETIFs. The following shelves, PSS-8x, PSS-12x, PSS-24x, PSS-8 (with a 8EC3), and
PSS-16/16-II/32 (with 32EC2 or 32EC3), and PSS-4II (with 4EC3) support up to 512 NETIFs. All
other shelves support up to 64 NETIFs. Note that in a multi-shelf NE, the per-shelf limit still applies
even if the total NETIFs supported on the NE is higher. For further details see 1830 Photonic
Service Switch (PSS) DCN Network Dimensioning Guide.
Only one GCC Type (GCC0, GCC1 or GCC2) may be terminated on any given facility instance.
Refer to the ECC Slot Ranges table in Appendix A, “Reference tables” Reference tables for valid
values of facility and shelf and slot and port ranges for each supported circuit pack type. This table
also indicates valid combinations of facility type and GCC type.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.101.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.101.3 Input Format
config cn netif add
<index> <facility-port-aid> eccchnl
3.101.4 Input Parameters
<index>
Values
1..512
Access identifier for the NETIF.
Note: The recommended value range is {1..128} for EC and 8EC2 equipment controller card
types in main shelf.
<facility-port-aid>
The facility carrying the ECC.
Refer to the ECC Slot Ranges table in Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid values of facility
and shelf and slot and port ranges for each supported circuit pack type.
System administration commands
Data communication network commands

Restrictions
The following restriction applies to D5X500/D5X500L/D5X500Q cards:
• To provision the <facility-port-aid>, the Operation Mode must be set adddrop
(oprmode=adddrop). See 'config interface <d5x500-card> <port-aid> <otun>'.
Refer to the ECC Slot Ranges table in Appendix A, “Reference tables”, "Reference tables"
for cards that use the OTSIG model and for valid values of facility and shelf and slot and
port ranges, and also for which equipment controllers must be used when GCCs are to be
supported on the card.
The OTSIG model allows flexible mapping of OTU/ODU facilities to uplink ports. For
example, with the 8UC1T this model allows flexible mapping to 100G or 200G uplink ports.
For cards supporting the OTSIG model, this mapping is created with the CLI command
'config otsig', using the OTUSTRUCT and OTSILIST options and depends on port
configuration. For example, with the 8UC1T the following command creates an otsig (1/3/1
- 1 is otsig-id) on port 2 (otsilist 2) as a 1x200G OTSi, with OTU id 3 & 4 (otustruct
otu4#3&otu4#4):
config otsig 1/3/1 create otustruct otu4#3&otu4#4 otsilist 2
Given that the facility has been created, the following restrictions apply to cards that
support the OTSIG model when creating a netif:
• For GCC0, only the first OTU within OTUSTRUCT of one OTSiG can be used in the
netif. Thus, in the above example, only OTU #3 can be used for the netif, but OTU #4
can not.
• For GCC1/GCC2, only the ODUNIM associated with the first OTU within OTUSTRUCT
of one OTSiG can be used in the netif. Thus, in the above example, only ODUNIM #3
will be used for the netif.
• Only one GCC channel (GCC0, GCC1, GCC2) can be selected for one OTSiG.
eccchnl
Syntax
eccchnl <value> [force]
Values
gcc0 - the referred ECC is a GCC0
gcc1 - the referred ECC is a GCC1
gcc2 - the referred ECC is a GCC2
Specifies the ECC type of the referred ECC channel.
See ECC Slot Ranges table in Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid values of eccchnl
supported on facility and shelf and slot and port ranges for each supported circuit pack type.
The force directive at the end of the line makes the command re-issue safe in that a repeat
adding of the same NETIF (all settings the same as already configured) will not be flagged as
an error. That is, the NE will not return an error message in this scenario and will not change
any parameter values.
The force directive at the end of the line allows the command to be used to modify the eccchnl

parameter. When the command is used in this way, the command is equivalent to config cn

3.101.5 Examples
Add multiple NETIFs.
# config cn netif add 1 OTU-1/2/L1 eccchnl gcc0
# config cn netif add 2 OTUODU2-2/7/3 eccchnl gcc1
Add a NETIF for an 8UC1T card based on the example for otsig 1/3/1 above
config otsig 1/3/1 create otustruct otu4#3&otu4#4 otsilist 2
config cn netif add 10 OTU-1/3/3 eccchnl gcc0
Change the "eccchnl" using the "force" directive.
# config cn netif add 1 OTU-1/2/L1 eccchnl gcc0
# config cn netif add 1 OTU-1/2/L1 eccchnl gcc1
Unable to complete request.
Error: NETIF Id already exists.
# config cn netif add 1 OTU-1/2/L1 eccchnl gcc1 force
#
Use the "force" directive to suppress the error message when repeating an operation.
# config cn netif add 1 OTU-1/2/L1 eccchnl gcc0
# config cn netif add 1 OTU-1/2/L1 eccchnl gcc0
Unable to complete request.
Error: NETIF Id already exists.
# config cn netif add 1 OTU-1/2/L1 eccchnl gcc0 force
#

lcp-echo-failure
Syntax
lcp-echo-failure [<value>]
Values
1..600
Default
20
This parameter specifies the number of times an NE repeats an LCP echo request to its peer
on the PPP link. The definition below for "lcp-echo-interval" describes how an NE uses these
two "lcp-echo" parameters to determine that the PPP link on the ECC has failed.
lcp-echo-interval
Syntax
lcp-echo-interval [<value>]
Values
1..600 - time in seconds
Default
3 seconds
This parameter specifies the number of seconds a Network Element (NE) waits to receive an
echo response. The NE sends an LCP echo request to its peer on the PPP link every "lcp-
echo-interval" seconds. Whenever the NE does not receive a response within this time, the NE
increments a counter. If the counter reaches the value specified by "lcp-echo-failure" (see
format of this parameter above), then the PPP protocol terminates the connection and attempts
to establish a new connection.
Note that the counter is reset to zero whenever a response is received.

pkttype
Syntax
pkttype [nonstd | std]
Values
std - standard MTU packet size can be configured
nonstd - fixed non-standard MTU packet size
Default
std
Restrictions
Parameter only provisionable for 4DPA4, 11DPE12, 11STAR1, and 11STMM10 pack
related NETIFs.
GCC Packet type. This parameter indicates if the NETIF packet type is standard (std) or non-
standard (nonstd). Enter the keyword without any value to display the current setting.
If the PKTTYPE=STD the MTU size parameter can be changed. If the PKTTYPE=NONSTD the
MTU size parameter is always 1473 bytes and cannot be changed.
Changing PKTTYPE from STD to NONSTD results in the MTU value of the NETIF changing to
1473 bytes.
Changing PKTTYPE from NONSTD to STD results in the MTU value of the NETIF changing to
1500 bytes.
The default GCC Packet type has changed in R7 from previous releases to "standard" for ALL
facility packs/ports. Any new GCC connection added between 2 NEs running R7 or greater and
an earlier release will not automatically come up unless the user ensures the provisioned GCC
packet type value matches on both sides of the connection.

routestate
Syntax
routestate [<value>]
Values
disabled
enabled
redistribute
Default
enabled
Set the OSPF routing state of the NETIF interface. Enter this keyword without a parameter to
display the current OSPF routing state.
• Set to enabled to enable OSPF routing on the NETIF. OSPF attempts to form
adjacencies with other devices and distributes the neighbor IP address and mask into
OSPF.
• Set to disabled to disable OSPF routing on the NETIF. The neighbor IP address and
mask are not distributed into OSPF.
• Set to redistribute to distribute the neighbor IP address and mask into OSPF, but do not
form an adjacency. Also called Passive mode, the NE treats the interface as a network
outside its autonomous system.
Note: there is no reason to disable OSPF on a NETIF (GCC) except for the case where the
neighbor does not support OSPF, e.g., neighbor is a PSD. In such a case, set routestate to
disabled to suppress OSPF_ADJ alarms, or to redistribute to suppress alarms yet still distribute
the neighbor IP into OSPF.

disabled

enabled if the IPv6 address of the primary loopback is zero (i.e., ::/0)
Specifies the OSPFv3 routing state of the port. Enter this keyword without any parameters to
display the current OSPFv3 routing state.
• Set to enabled to enable OSPFv3 routing. OSPFv3 attempts to form adjacencies with
