retransint
Syntax
retransint [<value>]
Values
1..65535 - time in seconds
Default
5 seconds
Configures the OSPF time between LSA transmissions. The option specifies the length of time,
in seconds, that OSPF will wait before retransmitting an unacknowledged link state
advertisement (LSA) to an OSPF neighbor. Specify a value that is longer than the expected
round trip delay between any two NEs on the network. Once the retransmit-interval expires and
no acknowledgement has been received, the LSA will be retransmitted.
Enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current value of retransmit interval.
rtrdeadint
Syntax
rtrdeadint [<value>]
Values
2..65535 - time in seconds
Default
40 seconds
OSPF Router Dead Interval of the interface. This is the time elapsed between not hearing a
router's Hello PDU before the interface OSPF state is declared down. The dead interval is a
timer used to timeout inactive adjacencies. The dead interval value must be greater than the
hello interval value. By default, the interface shall be set to four times the value of the
HELLOINT, so the default is 40 seconds. Enter the keyword without any value to display the
current setting.
Enter this keyword followed by an integer value for the dead interval, in seconds. Enter this
keyword without any parameters to display the current value of dead interval.
Note: The rtrdeadint must be set to identical values on all the OSPF routers/NEs connected to
the same LAN segment.

to the same LAN segment.

3.107 config cn ospf area add
3.107.1 Purpose
This command creates a new OSPF area definition on the network element.
Use this command to set:
• The OSPF area type
• Opaque LSAs distribution into the area
• Default cost of the area
• Additional properties of an NSSA area
There are five types of OSPF areas:
• normal areas are defined as areas that can accept intra-area, inter-area, and external routes.
• stub areas do not accept routes belonging to external autonomous systems (AS), however,
these areas have inter-area and intra-area routes. This reduces the size of the routing databases
for the areas internal routers. Routers in the stub area also contain a default route which is
advertised to the area by the Area Border Router (ABR).
• totally_stub areas do not allow routes other than intra-area and the default route to be
propagated within this area. This further reduces the size of the routing databases for the area's
internal routers. The ABR advertises a default route into the area and all the routers belonging to
this area use the default route to send any traffic outside the area.
• nssa (Not So Stubby Areas): can import AS external routes from within the area and send them
to other areas, but cannot receive AS external routes from other areas. Inter-area and intra-area
routes are allowed along with a default route which is advertised to the area by the ABR.
• nssa_totally_stub areas are similar to nssa with the added restriction that inter-area routes are
not allowed.
Note that OSPF area properties in this command apply to OSPFv2 only.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.107.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.107.3 Input Format
config cn ospf area add <area-index> <area-id>
type <normal-value> dns_opaque_lsa wavekey_opaque_lsa virtual_link
[force]
type <nssa-value> dns_opaque_lsa wavekey_opaque_lsa nssa_translate
default_cost [force]
type <stub-value> dns_opaque_lsa wavekey_opaque_lsa default_cost [force]

Data communication network commands

3.107.4 Input Parameters
<area-index>
Values
1..3
Default
Entry required
Specifies the access identifier of the OSPF areas.
<area-id>
Values
{0..255}.{0..255}.{0..255}.{0..255}
Default
Entry required
Specifies the area identifier of the OSPF area. This ID has the format of an IP address that
uniquely identifies the OSPF area. A valid <area-id> consists of four integer values separated
by periods.
Restrictions
The <area-id> cannot be 0.0.0.0 since it is already defined by <area-index> 0 and it cannot
be an already defined <area-id>.
force
The force directive at the end of the line makes the add subcommand re-issue safe in that a
repeat adding of the same OSPF Area (all settings the same as already configured) will not be
flagged as an error. That is, the NE will not return an error message in this scenario and will not
change any parameter values.
The force directive at the end of the line also allows the add sub-command to be used to
modify settings for an existing OSPF Area. There is no need to delete the area and build it back
again. When issued with the force directive, the command is equivalent to config cn ospf area
modify.
When using the command with the force directive to modify parameters, the area-id must
match the value already provisioned for the given area-index; that is, area-id cannot be
modified. If they do not match, the NE will issue an error message.
The force directive may be used in scripting to suppress unnecessary error messages.

virtual_link
Syntax
virtual_link <ip-address>
Values
<ipv4-address> - Appendix A, “Reference tables”, IPv4 address character (IPv4) definition.
Default
Entry required
Allows for the creation of a virtual link for this area. OSPF requires that all areas attach directly
to Area 0.0.0.0, but the attachment need not be physical. One can take any physical
arrangement of areas and attach them logically through OSPF virtual links.
Specify the Loopback interface IP Address of the network element to terminate the virtual link.
Set to 0.0.0.0 for no Virtual Link. This network element must be an ABR (Area Border Router),
i.e., have an interface that is connected to Area 0.0.0.0 and another interface connected to a
non-0.0.0.0 Area.
Note: A virtual link must be configured on both network elements. When virtual link is created
across an OSC/GCC path, the MTU size must be set to 1500 bytes for the OSC/GCC
interfaces on that path.
Restrictions
Applicable only if area type is 'normal'. Virtual Links cannot be established through Area
0.0.0.0, 'stub', 'totally_stub', 'nssa' or 'nssa_totally_stub' type areas.

3.109 config cn ospf iprange
3.109.1 Purpose
This command creates or deletes an IP address range for a given OSPF area.
Use this command to:
1. Summarize into one Type-3 summary-LSA and announce to other OSPF areas
2. Filter intra area paths from the specified IP range that are not advertised into other OSPF areas
3. The IP address range that is specified must exist within the OSPF area index specified
Up to 16 IP address ranges can be configured on the NE. This command makes sense in an ABR
only. In order to take advantage of OSPF IP address range summarization, network numbers in
OSPF areas must be assigned in a continuous way to be able to lump these addresses into one
range.
Note that this command only applies to IPv4 and OSPFv2. Currently, IPv6 ranges cannot be set for
OSPFv3.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.109.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Specifies the OSPF IP ranges summarized/filtered for the network element.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.109.3 Input Format
config cn ospf iprange
add <areaindex> <iprange> <advertise>
del <areaindex> <iprange>
detail
3.109.4 Input Parameters
Sub-command: add
Syntax
add <areaindex> <iprange> <advertise> [force]
Creates an IP address range for the OSPF area specified.
The force directive at the end of the line makes the add subcommand re-issue safe in that a
repeat adding of the same IP address range (all settings the same as already configured) will
not be flagged as an error. That is, the NE will not return an error message in this scenario and
will not change any parameter values.
The force directive at the end of the line also allows the add subcommand to be used to modify
the advertise parameter for an existing IP address range. There is no need to delete the range

3.112 config cn ospf3 area add
3.112.1 Purpose
This command creates a new OSPFv3 area definition on the network element.
Use this command to set:
• The OSPFv3 area type
• opaque LSAs distribution into the area
• Default cost of the area
• Additional properties of an NSSA area
There are five types of OSPFv3 areas:
• normal areas are defined as areas that can accept intra-area, inter-area, and external routes.
• stub areas do not accept routes belonging to external autonomous systems (AS), however,
these areas have inter-area and intra-area routes. This reduces the size of the routing databases
for the areas internal routers. Routers in the stub area also contain a default route which is
advertised to the area by the Area Border Router (ABR).
• totally_stub areas do not allow routes other than intra-area and the default route to be
propagated within this area. This further reduces the size of the routing databases for the area's
internal routers. The ABR advertises a default route into the area and all the routers belonging to
this area use the default route to send any traffic outside the area.
• nssa (Not So Stubby Areas): can import AS external routes from within the area and send them
to other areas, but cannot receive AS external routes from other areas. Inter-area and intra-area
routes are allowed along with a default route which is advertised to the area by the ABR.
• nssa_totally_stub areas are similar to nssa with the added restriction that inter-area routes are
not allowed.
Note: OSPFv3 does not support opaque LSA distribution and Virtual Links.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.112.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.112.3 Input Format
config cn ospf3 area add <area-index> <area-id>
type <normal-value> dns_opaque_lsa wavekey_opaque_lsa [force]
type <nssa-value> dns_opaque_lsa wavekey_opaque_lsa nssa_translate
default_cost [force]
type <stub-value> dns_opaque_lsa wavekey_opaque_lsa default_cost [force]

Default
Entry required
Specifies the area identifier of the OSPFv3 area. This ID has the format of an IP address that

Restrictions

force
The force directive at the end of the line makes the add sub-command re-issue safe in that a
repeat adding of the same OSPFv3 Area (all settings the same as already configured) will not
be flagged as an error. That is, the NE will not return an error message in this scenario and will
not change any parameter values.
The force directive at the end of the line also allows the add sub-command to be used to
modify settings for an existing OSPFv3 Area. There is no need to delete the area and build it
back again. When issued with the force directive, the command is equivalent to "config cn
ospf3 area modify".
When using the command with the force directive to modify parameters, the area-id must
match the value already provisioned for the given area-index; that is, area-id cannot be
modified. If they do not match, the NE will issue an error message.
The force directive may be used in scripting to suppress unnecessary error messages.

3.114 config cn routes
3.114.1 Purpose
This command configures the default and static routes in the control network routing table. It also is
used to define metrics for redistribution of routes to OSPF.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.114.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Deleting a default route can affect routing in the control network.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.114.3 Input Format
config cn routes
default
default6
static
redistribute
3.114.4 Input Parameters
Sub-command: default
Use this subcommand to configure the IPv4 default route in the control network routing table.
See "config cn routes default".
Sub-command: default6
Use this subcommand to configure the IPv6 default route in the control network routing table.
See "config cn routes default6".
Sub-command: static
Use this subcommand to configure the IPv4 and IPv6 static routes in the control network
routing table. See "config cn routes static".
Sub-command: redistribute
Use this subcommand to configure the global redistribute setting and metrics for default routes,

3.115 config cn routes default
3.115.1 Purpose
This command configures the IPv4 default route in the control network routing table. The default
route is the route that defines the packet forwarding rule when no specific route can be determined
for a given IP address.
Use this command to:
• Access a subcommand for adding a default route to the control network routing table
• Change the gateway of the default route
• Change the OSPF distribution of the default route
• Change the distance of the default route
• Delete a default route from the control network routing table
Use the 'add' option to create the default route. This will ensure that the route is inserted in one step
to avoid disconnect. Once the route is created, any part of the default route can be modified with
the 'gateway', 'ospf-distribution' and 'distance' options.
This command applies to all 1830 shelf types.
3.115.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Deleting a default route can affect routing in the control network.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.115.3 Input Format
config cn routes default
add
delete
distance
ospf-distribution
gateway
3.115.4 Input Parameters
Sub-command: add
Add a default route to the routing table. See "config cn routes default add".
Sub-command: delete
Deletes the default route from the routing table. See "config cn routes default delete".
distance
Syntax
distance [<value>]

Data communication network commands

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
1..255
Default
1
The distance value is used to determine which route to be entered in the NE routing table when
there are multiple identical routes discovered through different routing protocols.
Lower values have higher precedence.
The OSPF routing protocol has a fixed distance value of 110, while static and default routes
have a default distance value of 1. If the default route is entered with a distance value less than
110, then the default route is installed in the NE routing table, even if the same route with a
different next hop is discovered through OSPF. If the default route has a distance value greater
than 110, then same route in OSPF will take precedence and be installed in the NE routing
table. A distance value of 255 is used to indicate an Unknown route, and the route will NOT be
installed in the routing table.
Setting the distance value to greater than 110 is used, for example, to create a backup gateway
(GNE) that is used only if the primary gateway (a different GNE) fails. When the primary
gateway fails, its default route will no longer be advertised in OSPF, and hence the backup
gateway's default route (with distance greater than 110) will be advertised.
Enter this keyword without a value to display the current value for distance.

nonredist

one of the allowed values.
If the value is omitted, the current setting for the ospf-distribution parameter is displayed.

Default
Entry required

change any parameter values.

3.117 config cn routes default delete
3.117.1 Purpose
This command deletes a default route from the control network routing table.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.117.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Deleting a default route can affect routing in the control network.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.117.3 Input Format
config cn routes default delete <gateway>
3.117.4 Input Parameters
<gateway>
Syntax
<gateway> [force]
Values
<ip-address> - specifies the IP address of the gateway.
NETIF-{1..512} - identifies an outgoing NETIF
<shelf>/<slot>/{OSC, OSCSFP} - identifies an outgoing OSC or OSCSFP port, see
Appendix A, “Reference tables” (refer to "Port name to port number mappings") for valid
amplifier cards which support an OSC or OSCSFP port.
Default
Entry required
Deletes the default route from the routing table.
The force directive at the end of the line makes the delete subcommand re-issue safe in that
attempts to delete a non-existent route (e.g., attempting to delete a route that has already been
deleted) will not be flagged as an error. That is, the NE will not return an error message in this
scenario and will not change any parameter values.
This command requests a yes/no confirmation after pressing the Enter key. The confirmation
prompt can be bypassed by giving the yes directive at the end the command line (see Chapter
1, “Introduction to 1830 CLI”, "CLI Navigation"). The force directive also bypasses the
confirmation prompt as though the operator had included the yes directive at the end of the
command line. That is, when the force directive is used, there is no need to say force yes at
the end of the command.
If you are using scripting to delete a route, and if you want to suppress the error message and
to bypass the confirmation prompt, include force at the end of the command line.

3.123 config cn routes redistribute
3.123.1 Purpose
This command is used to control and set the metric type and metric value when redistributing
various default and static routes into the BGP or OSPF. It is also used to set rules for select
redistribution and route tagging between BGP and OSPF. This command is used for the following
redistribution:
Distribution into OSPF
• Default routes set by user
• Default routes from DHCP and IPv6 Router Advertisements
• Default routes from BGP
• Static routes
• Select BGP routes to be tagged in OSPF
Distribution into BGP
• Static routes
• Select tagged OSPF routes to be tagged with a BGP community
Note: if OSPF and BGP are configured, then all OSPF routes are automatically redistributed to
BGP except for the default route. There is an option to also redistribute the default route.
Both the IPv4 (and IPv6) default and static route will be redistributed into OSPF (and OSPFv3). If
the system if not running OSPFv3, this will have no effect on IPv6 routing.
This command applies to all 1830 shelf types.

Impact: Adding a default route affects control network behavior.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

This command is used to control and set the metric type and metric value when redistributing
various default routes into the routing table. This command includes distribution into OSPF the
default route which can come from:
• Default route set by user (static or user defined route)

BGP, except for the default route. There is an option in this command to also include the default
route in such redistribution.
Both the IPv4 (and IPv6) default route will be redistributed into OSPF (and OSPFv3). If the system
if not running OSPFv3, this will have no effect on IPv6 routing.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
For <mode-value>:
disabled - Disable the redistribution the BGP default route to OSPF
use_bgp_med - Enable the redistribution of BGP default route to OSPF, using the BGP
MED value
user_defined - Enable the redistribution of BGP default route to OSPF, using the configured
OSPF metric
Default
disabled
Use this command to configure the OSPF redistribution metric_type and metric for BGP
default route. Also use this command to set the redistribution mode for the BGP default route
into OSPF. The metric_type specifies the handling of internal OSPF cost when a route is
redistributed. The metric is the OSPF cost to assign to the route, which is the value used within
the OSPF routing protocol to determine which route to be entered when there are multiple
identical routes. Precedence is given to the route with a lower metric. The mode option
specifies whether the BGP default route will be distributed to OSPF and if redistribute, the
OSPF cost assigned to route. If disabled then the BGP default will not be redistributed into
OSPF. If use_bgp_med then redistribution is enabled and the BGP MED (Multi Exit
Discriminator) value from the BGP received default route will be used as the OSPF cost. If
user_defined then redistribution is enabled and the cost will be the defined OSPF metric (from
'metric [<value>]').
If no value is specified, the current setting of the status parameter is output.
Note that BGP MED, also called the BGP metric, can have a range of 0..4,294,967,294. The
range of OSPF metric, however, is 0..16,777,214. Any MED value greater than the maximum
OSPF metric (16,777,214) will be assigned the OSPF maximum.
These parameters will apply to both OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 (if running).

Restrictions
Note that there are restrictions on dhcp_ra_to_ospf status.
The dhcp_ra_to_ospf status only applies if DHCP Client and Client gateway are enabled, or
ipv6_autoconfig is enabled on any interfaces. If these are enabled, then the following
conditions apply:
• When a static default route is configured with OSPF redistribute, then:
dhcp_ra_to_ospf status must be disabled and
dhcp_ra_to_ospf status cannot be set to enabled
• If dhcp_ra_to_ospf status is enabled, then adding or modifying a static default route to
have OSPF redistribute will be denied, i.e., the following will be denied:
config cn routes default[6] add <gateway> <distance> redist and config cn routes
default[6] ospf-distribution redist
These restrictions apply to both default and default6.

Use this command to allow the redistribution of the OSPF default route into BGP and set the
metric to assign to the BGP MED (Multi Exit Discriminator) for such redistribution. If mode is
disabled, then the OSPF default route is not redistributed into OSPF (metric parameter will be
ignored). If mode is use_ospf_metric then redistribution is enabled and the BGP MED will be
assigned the OSPF metric of the route (metric parameter will be ignored). If mode is user_

<metric>. Enter the keyword without a value to display the current value.
3.124.5 Examples
Set OSPF metric rules for the redistribution of the user defined default route
# config cn routes redistribute default user_defined_to_ospf metric 18
# config cn routes redistribute default user_defined_to_ospf metric_type 1
Enable the redistribution of the default route from BGP to OSPF to use the defined metric, and set
the metric values.
# config cn routes redistribute default bgp_to_ospf metric 18
# config cn routes redistribute default bgp_to_ospf metric_type 1
# config cn routes redistribute default bgp_to_ospf mode user_defined
Here are two examples of enabling the redistribution of the default route in OSPF into BGP. The
metric is set on the second example.
The setting "mode use_ospf_metric" will assign the BGP MED based on the OSPF metric of the
route; the metric value will be ignored The setting "mode user_defined" will assign the BGP MED
based presented metric (100 in this case).
# ### Example 1
# config cn routes redistribute default ospf_to_bgp mode use_ospf_metric

3.125 config cn routes redistribute non_default
3.125.1 Purpose
This command is used to configure the redistribution of specific non-default routes from BGP into
OSPF, and from OSPF into BGP.
• For the BGP into OSPF case, this redistribution will be performed on specific BGP routes and
optionally apply an OSPF tag and set a metric on the route.
• For the OSPF into BGP case, the redistribution will be performed on specific tagged OSPF and
will be re-tagged with BGP community.
Note: Redistribution tagging rules cannot be configured for the default route.
Note: If OSPF and BGP are configured, then all OSPF routes are automatically redistributed to
BGP, except for the default route. OSPF to BGP redistribution rules set with this command will add
a community tag to the route.
Note: This tagging feature only applies to IPv4 routes.
This command applies to all 1830 shelf types.
Restrictions: Features of this command related to redistribution to and from BGP are not available
on the PSS-4, or the PSS-16 and PSS-32 shelves with equipment controller 'EC'. See Appendix A,
“Reference tables”, User service interfaces table.

3.127 config cn routes static
3.127.1 Purpose
This command configures the static routes in the control network routing table. A static route is a
manually configured route that defines the path to a specific destination IP address or network.
Use this command to:
• Display the currently configured static routes in the control network
• Access a subcommand that allows you to add a static route to the control network routing table
• Access a subcommand that allows you to delete a static route from the control network routing
table
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.127.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Adding/deleting a static route can affect routing in the control network.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.127.3 Input Format
config cn routes static
brief
add
delete
3.127.4 Input Parameters
brief
Displays the current control network routing table.
Sub-command: add
Add a static route to the routing table. The NE can support and redistribute up to 512 static
routes. See "config cn routes static add" and "config cn routes redistribute".
Sub-command: delete
Deletes a static route from the routing table. See "config cn routes static delete".
3.127.5 Examples
The following will display all configured static routes, including the default route (0.0.0.0/)
and is equivalent to 'show cn routes static'. See that command for more sample output.
# config cn routes static brief
IP Static Route Table

3.128.1 Purpose
This command adds a static route to the control network routing table. This command is used for
both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
<gateway>
Syntax
<gateway> [force]
Values
<ipv4-address> - IPv4 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”
<ipv6-address> - IPv6 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”
NETIF-{1..512} - identifies an outgoing NETIF
<shelf>/<slot>/{OSC, OSCSFP} - identifies an outgoing OSC or OSCSFP port, see
Appendix A, “Reference tables” (refer to "Port name to port number mappings") for valid
amplifier cards which support an OSC or OSCSFP port.
Default
Entry required
The gateway specifies either the IP address of a gateway or an unnumbered outgoing interface
for the static route.
Note: A NETIF or {OSC,OSCSFP} interface can be used as the <gateway> for an IPv4 or IPv6
<destination-prefix>.
The force directive at the end of the line makes the add subcommand re-issue safe in that a
repeat adding of the same <gateway> (all settings the same as already configured) will not be
flagged as a duplicate route error. That is, the NE will not return an error message in this
scenario and will not change any parameter values.
The force directive allows the add subcommand to be used to modify settings for an existing
route for <gateway>, <distance>, and <ospf-distribution>. There is no need to delete the route
and build it back again. Other characteristics of using the add sub-command in this way are:
• You must include the <destination-prefix> and <gateway> parameters even if you are
not changing them
• You must include <distance> if you want to change <ospf-distribution> (if you do not
want to change <distance>, then set it to the same value it already has)
• Omitting <ospf-distribution>, or <ospf-distribution> and <distance>, changes the value(s)
of the omitted parameter(s) to the default value(s)
• If you enter a combination of <destination-prefix> and <gateway> that has not already
been configured, then the NE will create another static route using those values.
The force directive may be used in scripting to suppress unnecessary error messages.
Restrictions
Use only an IPv4 <gateway> for an IPv4 <destination-prefix>, and only an IPv6 <gateway>
with an IPv6 <destination-prefix>.
<distance>
Syntax
<distance> [force]

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12

724 Issue 1
Values
1..255
Default
1
The distance value is used to determine which route to be entered in the NE routing table when
there are multiple identical routes discovered through different routing protocols.
Lower values have higher precedence.
The OSPF routing protocol has a fixed distance value of 110, while static routes have a default
distance value of 1. If a static route is entered with a distance value less than 110, and the
same route with a different next hop is discovered through OSPF, the static route is installed in
the NE routing table. If the static route has a distance value greater than 110, the same route in
OSPF will take precedence and be installed in the NE routing table. If a distance value of 255 is
entered, the route will NOT be installed in the routing table. A distance value of 255 is used to
indicate an Unknown route.
For a description of the force directive, see the description of the gateway parameter above.
<ospf-distribution>
Syntax
<ospf-distribution> [force]
Values
redist
nonredist
Default
nonredist
Specifies whether or not to distribute the static route onto OSPF.
If distribution is set, then an IPv4 route will be distributed into OSPFv2, and an IPv6 route will
be distributed into OSPFv3.
For a description of the force directive, see the description of the gateway parameter above.
<bgp-distribution>
Syntax
<bpg-distribution> [force]
Values
redist
nonredist
Default
nonredist

The following is the display from the help option
# config cn routes static add help
SYNTAX FORMAT :
add <dest-ipv4/cidr-mask> <gateway> [<distance> [<ospf-distr> [<bgp-distr>]]] [force]
add <dest-ipv4> <subnet-mask> <gateway> [<distance> [<ospf-distr> [<bgp-distr>]]] [force]
add <dest-ipv6/prefix-length> <gateway> [<distance> [<ospf-distr> [<bgp-distr>]]] [force]
INPUT PARAMETERS :
Dest-ip : IPv4 or IPv6 address
Cidr-mask : IPv4 CIDR mask {1..32}
Subnet-mask : Dot-notation mask {aaa.bbb.ccc.ddd}
Prefix length: Range {1-128}
Gateway : IPv4 or IPv6 address or NETIF-{1..512} or shelf/slot/{OSC,OSCSFP,OSCSFP
{1-2}}
Distance : Range {1-255 } Default value: 1
OSPF-Distr : redist or nonredist route into OSPF Default value: nonredist
BGP-Distr : redist or nonredist route into BGP Default value: nonredist
Force : Use the force directive to suppress the error message when repeating an
operation.
Add a static route.
# config cn routes static add 10.1.30.0/24 10.1.20.1 1 nonredist
# config cn routes static add 10.20.30.16 255.255.255.248 192.168.15.1 20 redist
# config cn routes static add 2001:db8:0:21::/64 2001:db8:0:22::3f:2 100
Two examples of static routes redistribute into OSPF, and OSPF and BGP In the first
example, the route is the /32 address of a LAN interface (E1=10.10.30.5) with next-hop as
loopback address (10.1.20.5). This is to force the specific /32 address of E1 to be advertised
into OSPF.
# config cn routes static add 10.10.30.5/32 10.1.20.5 1 redist
# config cn routes static add 10.1.30.0/24 10.1.20.4 20 redist redist
Use the "force" directive to suppress the error message when repeating an operation: IPv4
example.

This command requests a yes/no confirmation after pressing the Enter key. The confirmation
prompt can be bypassed by giving the yes directive at the end the command line (see Chapter
1, “Introduction to 1830 CLI”, "CLI Navigation"). The force directive also bypasses the
confirmation prompt as though the operator had included the yes directive at the end of the
command line. That is, when the force directive is used, there is no need to say force yes at
the end of the command.

to bypass the confirmation prompt, include force at the end of the command line.

Values

OSPF Metric or Cost of the interface. The lower the cost, the more preferred the interface is for

Syntax
retransint [<value>]
Values
1..65535 - time in seconds
Default
5 seconds
Configures the OSPF time between LSA transmissions. The option specifies the length of time,
in seconds, that OSPF will wait before retransmitting an unacknowledged link state
advertisement (LSA) to an OSPF neighbor. Specify a value that is longer than the expected
round trip delay between any two NEs on the network. Once the retransmit-interval expires and
no acknowledgement has been received, the LSA will be retransmitted.
rtrdeadint
Syntax
rtrdeadint [<value>]
Values
2..65535 - time in seconds
Default
40 seconds
OSPF Router Dead Interval of the interface. This is the time elapsed between not hearing a
router's Hello PDU before the interface OSPF state is declared down. The dead interval is a
timer used to timeout inactive adjacencies. The dead interval value shall always be greater than
the hello interval value. By default, the interface shall be set to four times the value of the
helloint parameter, so the default is 40 seconds.
Note: Any 1830 OSC interfaces being used to connect to a 1696R must have their OSPF Hello
value configured as 1 second and their OSPF Router Dead Interval value provisioned to 5
seconds. If this is not done, there will be a Data Link Failure on the OSC and loss of
communication until it is done.
Enter the keyword without a parameter to display the current setting.

retransint
Syntax
retransint [<value>]
Values
1..65535 - time in seconds
Default
5 seconds
Configures the OSPFv3 time between LSA transmissions. The option specifies the length of
time, in seconds, that OSPFv3 will wait before retransmitting an unacknowledged link state
advertisement (LSA) to an OSPFv3 neighbor. Specify a value that is longer than the expected
round trip delay between any two NEs on the network. Once the retransmit-interval expires and
no acknowledgement has been received, the LSA will be retransmitted.
rtrdeadint
Syntax
rtrdeadint [<value>]
Values
2..65535 - time in seconds
Default
40 seconds
Specifies the Router Dead Interval for the link. This is the time elapsed between not hearing a
router's Hello PDU before the interface OSPFv3 state is declared down. The dead interval is a
timer used to timeout inactive adjacencies. The dead interval value must be greater than the
hello interval value. By default, the interface shall be set to four times the value of the
HELLOINT, so the default is 40 seconds. Enter this keyword followed by an integer value for the
dead interval, in seconds. Enter this keyword without a value to display the current value.
Note: The rtrdeadint must be set to identical values on all OSPFv3 routers/NEs connected to
the same LAN segment.
Enter the keyword without a parameter to display the current setting.

# config interface IRDM32 1/1/OSCSFP ospf3 metric 13

3.132 config interface <card> <custlan-port>
3.132.1 Purpose
This command configures the Customer LAN (CUSTLAN) port on any of the various cards that
support OSC and have a Customer LAN port. This port is a 10/100BASE-T or 10/100/1000BASE-T
card LAN port which can transport customer Layer 2 traffic over the OSC to the peer Customer LAN
port on the remote card.
For a card with two OSC ports (OMDCL, EILA and EILAL) the CUSTLAN will be a Layer 2 port
through both OSCSFP1 and OSCSFP2.
Use this command to
• Enable or disable the Customer LAN port.
• Set Duplex and Speed negotiation.
• Set port description.
• Set the ingress traffic rate limit.
• Set the option to tie link integrity to the OSC state.
• Display the current port configuration.
Note: The customer LAN is only supported when the OSC mode is OC2/STM1. If mode is
100BASEFX the customer LAN will remain down. See 'config interface <card> <oscsfp-port-aid>'.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
3.132.2 Command Access Level
Impact: The Customer LAN port provides point to point Layer 2 connectivity between cards over the
OSC.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

Enable or disable IPv6 automatic configuration on the port. If enabled, the port will be assigned

advertised network of 64 bits (i.e., /64 prefix length); the port will then dynamically form a 64 bit

router(s) will be the gateway. For DHCPv6 a full IPv6 address, with /128 prefix length, will be
assigned.

Default

Specifies the OSPF routing state of the port. Enter this keyword without any parameters to
display the current OSPF routing state.
• Set to enabled to enable OSPF routing. OSPF attempts to form adjacencies with other
routers on the LAN, and the LAN network (or subnet) is distributed to other network
elements via OSPF.
• Set to disabled to disable OSPF routing. The network (or subnet) that the port is on is
not distributed to other network elements via OSPF.
• Set to redistribute to redistribute this LAN network (or subnet) into OSPF, but do not form
adjacencies with other routers on the LAN. Also called Passive mode, the NE treats the
port as a network outside its autonomous system, and distributes this network to other
network elements via OSPF.

3.134.5 Examples
The following examples set the IPv4 address:
# config interface mfc 1/10/oamp ip 135.17.22.5/24

# config interface mfc 1/10/lan3 ip 2001:db8:0:23::3fe:1/64

The following example sets the moduletype for a LAN3 port to a specific module.
# config interface mfc 1/10/lan3 state down
# config interface mfc 1/10/lan3 moduletype 1000B-T
# config interface mfc 1/10/lan3 state up
For examples of "detail" output, please see command "show interface <card-type> <lan-port-aid>"
as the outputs of both commands are identical.

NE-initiated - The NE confirms communication by sending ICMP ping to the configured auto_
state_ip address. The timeout period with unsuccessful pings before the NE enables local
access is auto_state_interval * auto_state_count.
NMS-initiated - The Network Management System (NMS) sends to the NE SNMP GET
messages for sysUpTime. The NE expects the NMS to authenticate according to how SNMP is
configured on the NE (SNMPv2 or SNMPv3). The timeout period without receiving this SNMP
GET before the NE enables local access is auto_state_interval. This method for monitoring
requires that the NMS send these periodic SNMP GET messages to the NE. For the purpose of
NMS-initiated monitoring, the NE considers SNMP GET for sysUpTime from:
• Any IP source address (auto_state_ip is not used with NMS-initiated confirmation)
• Any device
• Any management interface (e.g., OAMP) except the CIT port
Enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current value.

dhcp_range
Syntax
dhcp_range [<value>]
Values
1..10
Default
1
This is the range of the IP pool for the DHCP server. The port can dole out from 1 to up to 10 IP
addresses, beginning with the CIT IP address. This parameter is valid only when dhcp is
enabled. If entered without a value, will display the current value.
For the CIT port, the default value is 1, and thus the assigned IP address will be the next
address after the CIT port's address. For example, if the CIT port is 172.16.0.1 (default value),
then the assigned IP address for the laptop will be 172.16.0.2.

3.137 config interface <eqm-ctrl>
3.137.1 Purpose
This command configures the interface ports on an Equipment Controller card.
Use this command to:
• Display the list of all equipment controller ports on network element: ES1 and ES2 for main and
extension shelves, other ports for main shelf only.
• Access a subcommand that allows you to configure the OAMP, AUX, or E1 port for a main shelf.
• Access a subcommand that allows you to configure the CIT port for a main shelf.
• Access a subcommand that allows you to configure the ES1 and ES2 ports for main and
extension shelves.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types. Supported interfaces depend on specific
equipment controller type.
For shelf type applicability and port to card association, see table "User Service Interfaces" in
Appendix A, “Reference tables”.

3.138 config interface <eqm-ctrl> <port-aid>
3.138.1 Purpose
This command configures the LAN ports on the equipment controller of the main shelf.
Use this command to:
• Display the current LAN port configuration.
• Enable or disable the port.
• Set the port IPv4 or IPv6 address.
• Set physical LAN attributes.
• Enable or disable routing on the port.
• Access a subcommand that allows configuration of OSPF and OSPFv3 options on the port.
• Configure DHCP client parameters for the port.
• Configure IPv6 Autoconfig Client for the port.
• Configure DHCP or DHCPv6 server for the port.
• Access sub-command to configure IPv6 Router Advertisement on the port.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.138.2 Command Access Level
Impact: The ports provide network management communication, inter-compound NEs and optical
extension shelves or routers (UNI).
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

disabled
Specifies the OSPF routing state of the port. Enter this keyword without any parameters to

LAN, and distribute routes.
• When set to disabled, the network (or subnet) on the port is not distributed to OSPF.
• When set to redistribute, the NE treats the LAN as a network outside its autonomous

• Set to enabled to enable OSPFv3 routing. OSPFv3 attempts to form adjacencies with

3.138.5 Examples
The following examples set the IPv4 address.
# config interface ec 1/1/aux ip 135.17.22.5/24
# config interface ec 1/1/aux ip 135.17.22.5 255.255.255.0
# config interface cec2 1/16/e1 ip 135.17.22.5/24
# config interface cec2 1/16/e1 ip 135.17.22.5 255.255.255.0
# config interface cec1 1/16/oamp ip 135.17.22.5/30
# config interface cec1 1/16/oamp ip 135.17.22.5 255.255.255.240
The following examples set the IPv6 address.
# config interface 32ec2 1/1/aux ip 2001:db8:0:23::3fe:1/64
# config interface cec2 1/16/e1 ip 2001:db8:0:23::3fe:1/64
# config interface cec1 1/16/oamp ip 2001:db8:0:23::3fe:1/64
For examples of "detail" output, please see command "show interface <card-type> <lan-port-aid>"
as the outputs of both commands are identical.
The following example set the dhcprange.
# config interface 32ec3 1/1/aux dhcp_range 5
The following example set the duplex.
# config interface 8xcec2II 1/2/aux duplex half
The following example set the IPv6 automatic configuration.
# config interface CEC2II 1/2/oamp ipv6_autoconfig enabled

3.139 config interface <eqm-ctrl> <cit-port>
3.139.1 Purpose
This command configures the CIT port on an Equipment Controller card on the main shelf. If the
network element is equipped with redundant control cards, setting a parameter on the port of one
card will set the same parameter of the port on the other card. The exception is the description field
which is independent on each port.
Use this command to:
• Display the current CIT port configuration.
• Set the port IPv4 or IPv6 address.
• Enable or disable the proxy ARP on the port.
• Configure DHCP and DHCPv6 Server on the CIT port.
• Access subcommand to configure IPv6 Router Advertisement on the port.
• Set physical LAN attributes.
• Set state of the CIT port.
• Enable or disable the auto-state feature.
• Set the parameters for the auto-state feature.
• Set the routing state.
• Set area index.
For shelf type applicability and port to card association, see table "User Service Interfaces" in
Appendix A, “Reference tables”.
3.139.2 Command Access Level
Impact: The CIT port provides network management communications.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

Specifies the shelf, slot and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot

auto_state
Syntax
auto_state [<value>]
Values
enable
disable
Default
disable
Enables or Disables the auto-state feature. The auto-state feature prohibits connections to the
local access interfaces on the network element, while the NE is in contact with a Network
Management System (NMS).
The local access interfaces are:
• CIT port
• serial craft port
• USB craft port
If auto_state = enable:
The CIT port's admin state will be either up (enabled) or down (disabled) autonomously on
different conditions as described below (also see the auto_state_initiatedby parameter for this
command).
1. The CIT port's admin state will be set to down autonomously when the NE is in
contact with the NMS.
2. The CIT port's admin state will be set to up autonomously when the NE is not in
contact with the NMS.
If auto_state = disable:
The CIT port's admin state cannot be set up or down autonomously.
Enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current setting.
System administration commands
Data communication network commands
config interface <eqm-ctrl> <cit-port>
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
788 Issue 1
Restrictions
The auto_state parameter can be set to enabled under either of the following conditions:
• auto_state_initiatedby set to ne AND auto_state_ip address configured
OR
• auto_state_initiatedby set to nms (auto_state_ip can be configured or not configured)
The auto-state feature will be disabled when a user manually sets the admin state of the
CIT port to up.
The admin state of the CIT port will autonomously be set to up when a user manually
disables the auto-state feature.
auto_state_initiatedby
Syntax
auto_state_initiatedby [<value>]
Values
ne - NE-initiated communication
nms - NMS-initiated communication
Default
ne
The 1830 supports two methods for monitoring communication with the network management
system:
NE-initiated - The NE confirms communication by sending ICMP ping to the configured auto_
state_ip address. The timeout period with unsuccessful pings before the NE enables local
access is auto_state_interval * auto_state_count.
NMS-initiated - The Network Management System (NMS) sends to the NE SNMP GET
messages for sysUpTime. The NE expects the NMS to authenticate according to how SNMP is
configured on the NE (SNMPv2 or SNMPv3). The timeout period without receiving this SNMP
GET before the NE enables local access is auto_state_interval. This method for monitoring
requires that the NMS send these periodic SNMP GET messages to the NE. For the purpose of
NMS-initiated monitoring, the NE considers SNMP GET for sysUpTime from:
• Any IP source address (auto_state_ip is not used with NMS-initiated confirmation)
• Any device
• Any management interface (e.g., OAMP or OSC) except the CIT port
Enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current value.

3.143 config interface <loopback-interface>
3.143.1 Purpose
This command configures the primary and secondary loopback address on the network element
and sets the OSPF or OSPFv3 area index for the loopbacks.
Use this command to configure the IPv4 or IPv6 address and subnet mask (prefix length) of the
primary loopback. The primary loopback is also known as the IP address, or SYSTEM IP address,
of the network element. The user can log into network element using the loopback address or a
management interface (e.g., OAMP).
Also use this command to configure the IPv4 address and subnet mask of the secondary loopback
(loopback1) on the network element. The ospfareaindex and ospf3areaindex cannot be set
separately for this address, but is inherited from the primary loopback.
Note: Set the primary loopback only when commissioning a network element. You should not need
to set the primary loopback with this command during normal operation.
This command applies to all 1830 shelf types.
3.143.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Specifies the network element IP address.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.143.3 Input Format
config interface <loopback-interface>
ip
ospfareaindex
ospf3areaindex
3.143.4 Input Parameters
<loopback-interface>
Values
loopback - Specify the primary loopback
loopback1 - Specify the secondary loopback
Default
Entry required
The name of the loopback address which will be configured.

Set the IPv4 and/or IPv6 address and subnet mask (or prefix length) of the loopback/loopback1

For the loopback interface, the user can optionally set both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. If setting

IPv6 address. If setting only one address, an IPv4 or IPv6 address can specified. For IPv4, both
CIDR mask (e.g., /32) and dot-notation mask (e.g., 255.255.255.255) are accepted. For IPv6,
use the prefix length (/1 - /128). For format and allowable addresses, see "IPv4 address
character (IPv4) definition" and "IPv6 address character (IPv6) definition" in Appendix A,
“Reference tables”.
Enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current IP address settings.

warm reset.

/128 prefix length (IPv6).
Note: On loopback, there can be an IPv4 address or IPv6 address, or both.

loopback1, set it to 0.0.0.0/0. The IPv4 address cannot be removed from the primary loopback.
Note: Do not use a link local address (i.e., from FE80:/10) for IPv6 loopback; the loopback will
be inaccessible with such an address.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
806 Issue 1
Restrictions
The loopback address cannot be contained in any of the LAN subnets of this or any other
NE. The exception to this is ProxyARP.
When ProxyARP is configured on a LAN interface (e.g., OAMP) in the network, loopbacks
of participating GNEs and RNEs should be in the IP subnetwork of the LAN interface with
ProxyARP enabled.
IPv6 loopback address cannot be the same value as any of the LAN interface IPv6
addresses.
On loopback1, there can only be an IPv4 address, i.e., IPv6 is not allowed on loopback1.
If loopback1 is used it should be set after primary loopback is defined and it should be in a
different subnet than the primary loopback IP address.
An IPv6 address cannot be provisioned on the loopback if there is an OSC set to

3.143.5 Examples
The following are several examples of configuring the IPv4 address.
# config interface loopback ip 192.168.3.1/32
# config interface loopback ip 192.168.3.1 255.255.255.255
# config interface loopback ip 10.10.40.9/29
The following are three examples of setting the IPv6 address.
# config interface loopback ip 2001:db8:0:ac:10:20:122:202/128
# config interface loopback ip 2001:db8:0:24::172.16.0.1/128
# config interface loopback ip 2001:DB8:0:24::2/128
The following is an example of setting the both the IPv4 and IPv6 address. Note that the IPv4
address must be given first.
# config interface loopback ip 192.168.3.1/32 2001:db8:0:ac:10:20:122:202/128
# config interface loopback ip 172.16.0.1 255.255.255.255 2001:db8:0:24::172.16.0.1/128
The following are examples of setting the secondary loopback address.
# config interface loopback1 ip 172.16.3.1/32
# config interface loopback1 ip 10.10.248.21 255.255.255.255
The following is an example of changing the OSPF area index of the loopback.
# config interface loopback ospfareaindex 3
# config interface loopback ospf3areaindex 1

3.144 config interface <panel-card> <port-aid>
3.144.1 Purpose
This command configures the OAMP, VOIP, E1 or E2 port on the user panel or shelf panel of the
main shelf.
Use this command to:
• Display the current OAMP, VOIP, E1 or, E2 port configuration.
• Enable or disable the port.
• Set the port IP address.
• Set physical LAN attributes.
• Access subcommand that allows configuration of OSPF options on the port.
• Configure DHCP client parameters on the port.
• Configure IPv6 Autoconfig client on the port.
• Configure DHCP and DHCPv6 server on the VoIP, E1 or E2 port.
• Access subcommand to configure IPv6 Router Advertisement on the port.
For shelf type applicability and port to card association, see table "User Service Interfaces" in
Appendix A, “Reference tables”.

Enable or disable IPv6 automatic configuration on the port. If enabled, the port will be assigned
an address via StateLess Address AutoConfig (SLAAC) or stateful DHCPv6, depending on the
Router Advertisement received from the attached router(s). For SLAAC, the port will receive an
advertised network of 64 bits (i.e., /64 prefix length); the port will then dynamically form a 64 bit
host identifier using modified EUI-64 rules, thus creating a full IPv6 address. The advertising
router(s) will be the gateway. For DHCPv6 a full IPv6 address, with /128 prefix length, will be
assigned.

address will be removed, i.e., set to ::/0.

type "EC", i.e., classic EC.

Specifies the OSPF routing state of the port. Enter this keyword without any parameters to

routers on the LAN, and the LAN network (or subnet) is distributed to other network
elements via OSPF.
• Set to disabled to disable OSPF routing. The network (or subnet) that the port is on is
not distributed to other network elements via OSPF.
• Set to redistribute to redistribute this LAN network (or subnet) into OSPF, but do not
form adjacencies with other routers on the LAN. Also called Passive mode, the NE treats
the port as a network outside its autonomous system, and distributes this network to
other network elements via OSPF.

helloint
Syntax
helloint [<value>]
Values
1..65534 - time in seconds
Default
10 seconds
Specifies the Hello interval for the link. The Hello interval specifies how often (in seconds) a
Hello packet is sent out on the interface. Hello packets are used to establish and maintain
relationships with neighboring network elements. Enter this keyword without any parameters to
display the current value for the Hello interval.
Note: The helloint must be set to identical values on all OSPF routers/NEs connected to same
LAN segment.
metric
Syntax
metric [<value>]
Values
1..65535
Default
10
Specifies the traffic engineering metric for the control network link. The metric is an integer
value that specifies the cost of sending traffic over the link. OSPF always detects the lowest
cost route for the given prefix in the IP forwarding table. Enter this keyword without any
parameters to display the current value of metric.
retransint
Syntax
retransint [<value>]
Values
1..65535 - time in seconds
Default
5 seconds
Configures the OSPF time between LSA transmissions. The option specifies the length of time,
in seconds, that OSPF will wait before retransmitting an unacknowledged link state
advertisement (LSA) to an OSPF neighbor. Specify a value that is longer than the expected
round trip delay between any two NEs on the network. Once the retransmit-interval expires and
no acknowledgement has been received, the LSA will be retransmitted. Enter this keyword
without any parameters to display the current value of retransmit interval.

rtrdeadint
Syntax
rtrdeadint [<value>]
Values
2..65535 - time in seconds
Default
40 seconds
OSPF Router Dead Interval of the interface. This is the time elapsed between not hearing a
router's Hello PDU before the interface OSPF state is declared down. The dead interval is a
timer used to timeout inactive adjacencies. The dead interval value must be greater than the
hello interval value. By default, the interface shall be set to four times the value of the
HELLOINT, so the default is 40 seconds. Enter this keyword followed by an integer value for the
dead interval, in seconds. Enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current
value of dead interval.
Note: The rtrdeadint must be set to identical values on all the OSPF routers/NEs connected to
the same LAN segment.
rtrpriority
Syntax
rtrpriority [<value>]
Values
0..255
Default
1
Specifies the router priority. The router priority is used to determine which network elements on
a broadband network are the designated router (DR) and backup designated router (BDR). The
network element with the highest router priority value is the DR. The network element with the
second highest router priority is the BDR. In the event that two network elements have the
same router priority, the DR/BDR selection is resolved based on their loopback addresses (see
"config interface <loopback-interface>"): the network element with the highest loopback
address is the DR. Set the router priority to 0 to prevent the network element from becoming a
DR or BDR on this interface. Enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current
value of router priority.

Values
<string> - 1 to 16 alphanumerical ASCII characters
"" - to clear / set it to empty

helloint
Syntax
helloint [<value>]
Values
1..65534 - time in seconds
Default
10 seconds
Specifies the Hello interval for the link. The Hello interval specifies how often (in seconds) a
Hello packet is sent out on the interface. Hello packets are used to establish and maintain
relationships with neighboring network elements. Enter this keyword without any parameters to
display the current value for the Hello interval.
Note: The helloint must be set to identical values on all OSPF routers/NEs connected to same
LAN segment.
metric
Syntax
metric [<value>]
Values
1..65535
Default
10
Specifies the traffic engineering metric for the control network link. The metric is an integer
value that specifies the cost of sending traffic over the link. OSPF always detects the lowest
cost route for the given prefix in the IP forwarding table. Enter this keyword without any
parameters to display the current value of metric.
retransint
Syntax
retransint [<value>]
Values
1..65535 - time in seconds
Default
5 seconds
Configures the OSPF time between LSA transmissions. The option specifies the length of time,
in seconds, that OSPF will wait before retransmitting an unacknowledged link state
advertisement (LSA) to an OSPF neighbor. Specify a value that is longer than the expected
round trip delay between any two NEs on the network. Once the retransmit-interval expires and
no acknowledgement has been received, the LSA will be retransmitted. Enter this keyword
without any parameters to display the current value of retransmit interval.

rtrdeadint
Syntax
rtrdeadint [<value>]
Values
2..65535 - time in seconds
Default
40 seconds
OSPF Router Dead Interval of the interface. This is the time elapsed between not hearing a
router's Hello PDU before the interface OSPF state is declared down. The dead interval is a
timer used to timeout inactive adjacencies. The dead interval value must be greater than the
hello interval value. By default, the interface shall be set to four times the value of the
HELLOINT, so the default is 40 seconds. Enter this keyword followed by an integer value for the
dead interval, in seconds. Enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current
value of dead interval.
Note: The rtrdeadint must be set to identical values on all the OSPF routers/NEs connected to
the same LAN segment.
rtrpriority
Syntax
rtrpriority [<value>]
Values
0..255
Default
1
Specifies the router priority. The router priority is used to determine which network elements on
a broadband network are the designated router (DR) and backup designated router (BDR). The
network element with the highest router priority value is the DR. The network element with the
second highest router priority is the BDR. In the event that two network elements have the
same router priority, the DR/BDR selection is resolved based on their loopback addresses (see
"config interface <loopback-interface>"): the network element with the highest loopback
address is the DR. Set the router priority to 0 to prevent the network element from becoming a
DR or BDR on this interface. Enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current
value of router priority.

Configure IPv6 Router Advertisements on a LAN interface.

3.149 config snmpserver community
3.149.1 Purpose
This command configures the SNMP server community strings. The SNMP community strings
function as passwords that are embedded in every SNMP packet to authenticate access to the
Management Information Base (MIB) on the network element. Use this command to set the
community string for the various SNMP communities.
Note: The community strings must match those defined on the Management System configured as
the SNMP trap destinations for the network element. See "config snmpserver trapdest".
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.149.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Changes the community strings. The correct community string is required to access the
MIBs.

Syntax

Deletes an SNMP trap destination. Enter this keyword followed by the destination identifier of
the trap destination you want to delete.
If the destination identifier is surrounded by angle brackets < >, on output displayed, it means
that the identifier contains non-printable characters, and is displayed in dotted decimal notation.
Use the optional octets keyword to specify that the destination_ID value is in dotted decimal
notation, on input.
If the destination identifier contains spaces (for example: Service Provider West), you must
enclose the destination identifier in double quotation marks ("Service Provider West").

3.151 config snmpserver trapdest add
3.151.1 Purpose
This command adds an SNMP trap destination and specifies whether the trap is formatted using
SNMP version 1 (v1) or version 2c (v2c) or version 3 (v3). A trap destination is usually a network
management workstation. You can add up to a maximum of 10 trap destinations per network
element.
This command is accepted and no error is raised when it is issued using the same settings that are
already configured. That is, the NE will not return an error message in this scenario and will not
change any parameter values. This behavior is useful in scripting where the same command line
may be repeated with the expectation that the script executes to completion with no errors.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.151.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Traps are sent to the destination immediately after it is added.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

3.154 show acl_pattern
3.154.1 Purpose
The command can be used to retrieve an IP ACL pattern, or a list of patterns that have been
defined on the system.
An ACL Pattern is a set of packet field descriptors that can be tested against a packet. For a pattern
to match, each of its field descriptors must fit the data in the packet. The fields that may be tested
are:
• Source IP address (or range)
• Destination IP address (or range)
• TCP/UDP destination port
• IP protocol
• IP fragmentation
• ICMP type and code
• Whether or not a TCP packet belongs to an established connection
• Whether the pattern is set by NE or configured by users.
Each field test is optional: a pattern may specify only some (or no) fields to test. Each pattern also
has an associated action to take when the pattern matches: pass, block (i.e., drop) or log.
Regardless of the specified action, a match count associated with the pattern within the filter is
incremented whenever a match occurs. If a pattern specifies a block action, it may also specify an
ICMP error reporting behavior, which affects generation of ICMP 3/13 errors for forwarded packets
that are blocked. Total combination of filterID and patternID shall not exceed 4000.
Note: This command applies to 1830 PSS.
3.154.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
3.154.3 Input Format
show acl_pattern <pattern-id>
3.154.4 Input Parameters
<pattern-id>
Values
1..512 - arbitrary integer
<string> - up to 30 case-sensitive alphanumeric characters
* - to display all pattern in the system.
The unique pattern identifier that belongs to the filter. This can be an arbitrary integer, 1 - 512,
or a string of up to 30 case-sensitive alphanumeric characters, which is selected by the user to

Data communication network commands

Pack action
[action]
Pass, Block or Log
Action to take on packets matching the ACL pattern
With the 'pass' and the 'block' (i.e., drop) action, ACL processing will cease upon match.
With the 'log' action, a summary of the matched packet will be recorded (logged) and sent
to syslog, and ACL processing will continue to the next pattern.
ICMP Error
[icmpError]
True or False
ICMP Error behavior when Pack Action is block. If True, then an ICMP Error will be
returned to the sender if this ACL pattern matches. If False, an ICMP Error is not returned.
Defaults to False.
Source IP
[srcIpAddr]
Source IP Address. Can be specified explicitly to match only packets that originate from a
particular address, or can be used along with the srcIpPrefix parameter to specify a range
of supported originating IP addresses.
Source wildcard
[srcIpPrefix]
Wildcard Mask for the Source IP. String xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx format. The Wildcard Mask, also
called the Wildcard (Inverse) Subnet Mask, is the inverse of the subnet mask and consists
of an uninterrupted series of 0 bits followed by uninterrupted series of 1 bits. For example,
the wildcard mask for /24 is 0.0.0.255, while the wildcard mask for /28 is 0.0.0.15. When
srcIpAddr and srcIpPrefix are both specified, the pattern will match packets whose
originating IP is within the range defined by the source IP and the wildcard mask. If the
srcIpPrefix is unspecified, or 0.0.0.0, the originating IP address of the packet must match
the srcIpAddr exactly.
Destination IP
[dstIpAddr]
Destination IP Address. Can be specified explicitly to match only packets that are destined
for a particular address, or can be used along with the dstIpPrefix parameter to specify a
range of supported destination IP addresses.
Destination wildcard
[dstIpPrefix ]
Wildcard Mask for the Destination IP. String xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx format. See above "Source
wildcard" for an explanation. If the dstIpPrefix is unspecified, or 0.0.0.0, the target IP
address of the packet must match the dstIpAddr exactly.
Source Port
[srcPort]
{0..65535}[:{2-65535}]
TCP/UDP Source Port or port range. Applicable only when IP Protocol is TCP or UDP.
Destination Port
[dstPort]
{0..65535}[:{2-65535}]
TCP/UDP Destination Port or port range. Applicable only when IP Protocol is TCP or UDP.
Protocol
[ipProto]
ICMP, TCP, UDP, RSVP, GRE, OSPF or {0..255}
IP Protocol. Can be specified by explicit protocol number or by common protocol types.
ICMP Type
[icmpType]
{0..255}
ICMP Type identifier. Applicable only when IP Protocol is ICMP. If specified, the pattern will
only match packets with this exact ICMP type. A value of 255 means to match any ICMP
type.

3.158 show acl_pattern6
3.158.1 Purpose
The command can be used to retrieve an IPv6 ACL pattern, or a list of patterns that have been
defined on the system.
An IPv6 ACL Pattern is a set of packet field descriptors that can be tested against a packet. For a
pattern to match, each of its field descriptors must fit the data in the packet.
• Source IPv6 address and prefix-length
• Destination IPv6 address and prefix-length
• TCP/UDP destination port
• IP protocol
• ICMPv6 type and code
• Whether or not a TCP packet belongs to an established connection
• Whether the pattern is set by NE or configured by users.
Each field test is optional: a pattern may specify only some (or no) fields to test. Each pattern also
has an associated action to take when the pattern matches: pass, block (i.e., drop) or log.
Regardless of the specified action, a match count associated with the pattern within the filter is
incremented whenever a match occurs. If a pattern specifies a block action, it may also specify an
ICMP error reporting behavior, which affects generation of ICMP 3/13 errors for forwarded packets
that are blocked. Total combination of filterID and patternID shall not exceed 4000.
Note: This command applies to most 1830 PSS shelf types.
Note: This command does not apply to the PSS-4 or to the PSS-16 or PSS-32 shelf with equipment
controller type "EC", i.e., classic EC. These shelves do not support IPv6."
3.158.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
3.158.3 Input Format
show acl_pattern6 <pattern-id>
3.158.4 Input Parameters
<pattern-id>
Syntax
{<string> | <number> | *}
System administration commands
Data communication network commands

[srcIpPrefix]

{0..128}

(::/0) is no address. If both specified, the pattern will match packets whose originating IPv6
address is within the subnet defined by the destination IP and the prefix-len. A prefix length of
128 means the packet must match the dstIpAddr exactly.

[icmpCode]

will match any ICMP code.
TCP Established Flag
[tcpEstablished]
Enabled, Disabled or Local
TCP Established flag. Matches a packet depending on whether the TCP flags in the IP header
correspond to the "established" state. Applicable only when IP Protocol is TCP.
• Disabled (false): TCP flags in the IP header will not be considered in the match.
• Enabled (true): Will match a packet if the TCP flags in the IP header correspond to the
"established" state.
• Local:Will only attempt to match packets that are destined for this NE, in which case
tcpESTABLISHED=Enabled will be applied to the packet. Packets that are going through the
NE will have tcpESTABLISHED=Disabled applied to the packet.
SystemDefaultPattern True or False
Read-only attribute. If True, then the pattern is a default pattern provided by the system. If
False, then the pattern is not provided by the system. System default patterns may not be
modified or deleted.

The command can be used to retrieve IPv6 filter associations for a particular IPv6 network
interface, or a list of all interface/filter associations provisioned on the NE.
The physical LAN interfaces depend on the main shelf type, user panel, shelf panel, and/or the
related EC/MFC. See Appendix A, “Reference tables”, User service interfaces for the LAN
interfaces available on each shelf type.
Note: This command applies to most 1830 PSS shelf types.
Note: This command does not apply to the PSS-4 or to the PSS-16 or PSS-32 shelf with equipment
controller type "EC", i.e., classic EC. These shelves do not support IPv6."

• Display the configured BGP
• Display the configured DHCP relay services
• Display the DNS (Domain Name Services) configuration

• Display the summary of the OSC and OSCSFP interfaces

3.164.1 Purpose
This command displays the Ethernet Interfaces (ETHIF) associated with an In-Band Management
(IBM) channel. It also displays the parameters associated with the Ethernet Interface.
This command supports different levels of detail for the output, as follows:
• A table with one row for each of the provisioned ETHIF instances with two choices of the number
and content of the columns in the table
• A list of parameters for one specific ETHIF instance
The methods for obtaining the different levels of detail are described below.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
Note: IPv6 and OSPFv3 are not available on PSS-4 shelf.
IPv6 and OSPFv3 are not available on the PSS-16 and PSS-32 shelf with equipment controller type
"EC", i.e., classic EC.
3.164.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.164.3 Input Format
show cn ethif
<index>
full

1..64
Default
Entry required
When the ETHIF index is provided, the command displays all the network interface parameters
for that ETHIF index.
full
Syntax
full [<ipversion>]

Parameters Description
OSPF Adj State The OSPF Adjacency state: Full or Down
In rare instances, an intermediate state may be observed, e.g., 2Way, Exchange,
ExchangeStart, or Init. Persistent display of an intermediate state may indicate problems with
OSPF convergence.
OSPFv3 Adj State The OSPFv3 Adjacency state: Full or Down
In rare instances, an intermediate state may be observed, e.g., 2Way, Exchange,
ExchangeStart, or Init. Persistent display of an intermediate state may indicate problems with
OSPF convergence.
OSPF Area Index The OSPF Area Index
OSPF Area ID The OSPF Area ID associated with the OSPF Area Index
OSPF Routing Administrative state of OSPF Routing; Enabled, Disabled, or Redistribute.
Redistribute (or passive) means that the IP address is redistributed into OSPF, but the interface
does not participate in OSPF.
OSPF Hello Interval The OSPF Hello Interval specifies how often (in seconds) a Hello packet is sent out on the
interface. Hello packets are used to establish and maintain relationships with the neighboring
networking elements.
OSPF Router Priority The OSPF Router Priority, which is used to determine which network elements on a broadcast
interface will be the designated router (DR) and backup designated router (BDR). The network
element with the higher priority value is the DR. If set to zero, this network element cannot be
the DR/BDR on this interface.
OSPF Router Dead Int The OSPF Router Dead Interval Router Interface. This is the time elapsed between not hearing
a router's Hello PDU before the interface OSPF state is declared down. The dead interval is a
timer used to timeout inactive adjacencies.
OSPF Metric The OSPF Metric or Cost of the interface. The lower the cost, the more preferred the interface is
for the routing of packets.
OSPF Retransmit Int The OSPF Retransmit Interval. The length of time, in seconds, that OSPF will wait before
retransmitting an unacknowledged link state advertisement (LSA) to an OSPF neighbor.
OSPF MD5 Status Specifies if OSPF MD5 authentication is enabled or disabled on the interface.
OSPF MD5 Key The MD5 Key used for OSPF MD5 128 bit hash value key calculation on the interface.
OSPF MD5 KeyId The MD5 Key ID used for OSPF MD5 128 bit hash value key calculation on the interface.
Proxy Arp Specifies if Proxy ARP is enabled or disabled. When enabled, the port shall reply back to ARP
request from remote server for all NEs within the internal network, using its own MAC address
for the response.
DHCP Specifies if Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) server is enabled or disabled on this
interface, If enabled this interface will respond to DHCP response from clients to allocate an IP
address.
DHCP_range This is the range of IP pool for the DHCP server. The port can dole out from 1 to up 10 IP
addresses. This parameter is valid only when DHCP is enabled.
DHCP Def Gateway Specifies that this interface's IP address is distributed as the Default Gateway via DHCP. If not
enabled, no Default Gateway IP address is distributed through DHCP on this interface. This
parameter is valid when DHCP is enabled.
DHCPv6 Specifies id Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol Version 6 (DHCPv6) server is enabled or
disabled. If enabled this interface will respond to DHCPv6 client request for an IPv6 address.

Parameters Description
DHCPv6_range This is the range of IP pool for the DHCPv6 server. The port can dole up to 10 IPv6 addresses.
This parameter is valid only when DHCPv6 is enabled.
DHCP Client If enabled the interface will receive its IP address from the network.
DHCP Client Gateway Specifies if Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol Client Gateway is enabled or disabled. If
enabled, the port will request a gateway route in addition to its IP address, from the network. If
disabled, will remove gateway route received from this port.
IPv6 AutoConfig Specifies if IPv6 AutoConfig is enabled. If enabled, the port will be assigned an address via
StateLess Address AutoConfig (SLAAC) or stateful DHCPv6, depending on the Router
Advertisement received from the attached router. For SLAAC, the port will receive an advertised
network of 64 bits (i.e., /64 prefix length); the port will then dynamically form a 64 bit host
identifier using modified EUI-64 rules, thus creating a full IPv6 address. For DHCPv6 a full IPv6
address, with /128 prefix length, will be assigned.
Table 3-26 Router Advertisement Parameters
Parameters Description
Status Displays the Router Advertisement state.
Maximum Advert Interval Displays the maximum time allowed between sending unsolicited multicast Router
Advertisements.
Preferred Lifetime Displays the length of time in seconds (relative to the time the packet is sent) that
addresses generated from the prefix via stateless address auto configuration remain
preferred.
Managed Config (M-Flag) Specifies the value to be placed in the "Managed address configuration" M-flag field in
the Router Advertisement. When enabled, hosts use the administered (stateful) protocol
for address auto configuration in addition to any addresses autoconfigured using
stateless address autoconfiguration
Autonomous Flag Specifies the value to be placed in the "Address Configuration" A-flag field in the Router
Advertisement. When enabled, indicates that the interface prefix can be used for
autonomous stateless address configuration.
Default Preference Displays the preference associated with the default router, as either "low", "medium", or
"high".
Default Lifetime Displays the lifetime associated with the default router. A value of 0 indicates that the
router is not a default router and should not appear on the default router list. The router
lifetime applies only to the router's usefulness as a default router.
Valid Lifetime Displays the length of time in seconds (relative to the time the packet is sent) that the
interface prefix is valid for the purpose of on-link determination.
Other Config(O-Flag) Specifies the value to be placed in the "Other configuration" O-flag field in the Router
Advertisement. When enabled, hosts use the administered (stateful) protocol for auto
configuration of other (non-address) information.

This command displays the network interfaces (NETIF) associated with an embedded
communication channel (ECC) and the facility or OT circuit pack port carrying the ECC. It also
displays the parameters associated with the network interface.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
This command supports different levels of detail for the output, as follows:
• A table with one row for each of the provisioned NETIF instances with two choices of the number
and content of the columns in the table
• A list of parameters for one specific NETIF instance

obtain these different levels of detail.

IPv6 and OSPFv3 are not available on the PSS-16 and PSS-32 shelf with equipment controller type
"EC", i.e., classic EC.

LCP echo failure This parameter specifies the number of times an NE repeats an LCP echo request to its
peer on the PPP link. The definition below for "LCP echo interval" describes how an NE
uses these two "LCP echo" parameters to determine that the PPP link on the ECC has
failed.
LCP echo interval This parameter specifies the number of seconds a Network Element (NE) waits to
receive an echo response. The NE sends an LCP echo request to its peer on the PPP
link every "LCP echo interval" seconds. Whenever the NE does not receive a response
within this time, the NE increments a counter. If the counter reaches the value specified
by "LCP echo failure", then the PPP protocol terminates the connection and attempts to
establish a new connection.
Note that the counter is reset to zero whenever a response is received.
Packet Type GCC Packet type. This parameter indicates if the NETIF packet type is standard or
non-standard

3.166 show cn networkmap
3.166.1 Purpose
This command lists the mapping from network element names to network element IP addresses,
router IDs, and network element SW releases.
Note: All information in the network map is distributed via DNS Opaque LSAs in OSPF and/or
OSPFv3.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.166.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
3.166.3 Input Format
show cn networkmap
full
3.166.4 Input Parameters
full
Syntax
full
Without the full optional parameter, the output is a short, three-column display of NE Name,
IPv4 Address, and SW Release of the NEs.
When the full optional parameter is included, the output is a long, five-column display of NE
Name, Router ID, IPv4 Address, IPv6 Address, and SW Release.
3.166.5 Output Parameters
Parameter Description
NE Name The name configured using config general name.
Router ID Unique identifier of the NE's Router ID. Router ID is a four-byte parameter expressed
using the same dotted decimal format as an IPv4 address.
Displayed only with the full option.
IP Address
IPv4 Address (when full option is used)
The IPv4 primary loopback address of the NE.
IPv6 Address The IPv6 primary loopback address of the NE.
Displayed only with the full option.
Displays "::" if an IPv6 primary loopback address has not been provisioned on the NE.
An NE operating on an older software release will not report its IPv6 primary loopback
address. Dashes are displayed for the IPv6 Address of such an NE.
System administration commands
Data communication network commands
