3.167 show cn osc
3.167.1 Purpose
This command displays a summary of the OSC and OSCSFP interfaces on the Network Element
that are part of the DCN network.
When used with certain options, the command shows the details of an individual OSC or OSCSFP
interface, displaying the same information as: "show interface <card> <osc-port-aid> detail"
See Chapter 5, “Core optics management commands” for cards that support OSC interfaces.
Note: IPv6 and OSPFv3 are not available on PSS-4 shelf.
IPv6 and OSPFv3 are not available on the PSS-16 and PSS-32 shelf with equipment controller type
"EC", i.e., classic EC.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.167.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
3.167.3 Input Format
show cn osc
<slot-aid> [<ipversion>]
<osc-port-aid>
3.167.4 Input Parameters
<slot-aid>
Values
* - for all OSC ports on the network element
<shelf>/* - for all OSC ports in the addressed shelf
<shelf>/<slot> - for all OSC ports of the slot
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf, and slot of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot number, or
* to list all ports on an addressed shelf or on the network element.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
System administration commands
Data communication network commands
show cn osc

© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.

898 Issue 1
<ipversion>
Values
ipv4 - Displays IPv4 information
ipv6 - Displays IPv6 information
Default
ipv4
The <ipversion> option is used when the output will display multiple interfaces. The columns
labeled "OSPF" are affected as follows:
When set to ipv4 or when omitted, IPv4 and OSPFv2 information is displayed.
When set to ipv6, IPv6 and OSPFv3 information is displayed.
<osc-port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/OSC - optical supervisory channel port
<shelf>/<slot>/OSCSFP - optical supervisory channel port
<shelf>/<slot>/OSCSFP{1..2} - optical supervisory channel port
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Note that the OMDCL has two oscsfp
interfaces: oscsfp1 and oscsfp2.
With this option, the command displays the same information as: "show interface <card> <osc-
port-aid> detail"
3.167.5 Output Parameters

column for each parameter listed in the table below.
Parameters Description
Location AID of the OSC
Card Provisioned card type
Admin State Administrative state of the interface: Up or Down
Oper State Operational state of the interface: Up or Down
OSPF[v3] Routing The setting of the routing: Enabled, Disabled or Redistr(ibuted)

Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 899
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Parameters Description
OSPF[v3] Neighbor Address Address of neighboring Network Element.
Display depends on <ipversion> input parameter:
• If ipv4 or omitted, displays the IPv4 loopback address of the neighboring Network
Element
• If ipv6, displays the IPv6 link local address of the OSC on the neighboring Network
Element
Dependency on link conditions:
• Displays current neighbor if the Admin State is up and the OSPF Adjacency state is
FULL
• Displays last known neighbor if the Admin State is up and the OSPF Adjacency state
is not FULL
• Displays all zeros if a neighboring Network Element has not been established
Displays dashes if the Admin State is down
OSPF[v3] Neighbor Router ID Unique identifier of the OSPF[v3] neighbor router. Router ID is a four-byte parameter
expressed using the same dotted decimal format as an IPv4 address.
Router ID is usually the IPv4 loopback address of the neighbor.
Dependency on link conditions:
• Displays current neighbor if the Admin State is up and the OSPF Adjacency state is
FULL
• Displays last known neighbor if the Admin State is up and the OSPF Adjacency state
is not FULL
• Displays all zeros if a neighbor router has not been established
Displays dashes if the Admin State is down
OSPF[v3] Adj State OSPF Adjacency State: FULL or Down.
Display depends on <ipversion> input parameter:
• If ipv4 or omitted, displays the OSPFv2 Adjacency State
• If ipv6, displays the OSPFv3 Adjacency State
In rare instances an intermediate state may be observed, e.g., 2Way, Exchange,
ExchangeStart, or Init. Consistent display of an intermediate state may indicate
problems with OSPF convergence.
When the option selections call for displaying one interface, the command displays the same
information as: "show interface <card> <osc-port-aid> detail"

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
3.171 show cn routes redistribute
3.171.1 Purpose
This command displays the route redistribution setting of various routes into OSPF and BGP.
Specifically, three types of routes can be displayed:
• Default routes: display the state and metrics of user-defined, BGP and DHCP default routes for
redistribution into OSPF. Also display setting for redistribution of default route from OSPF to
BGP.
• Non Default routes: display settings for redistribution of specific routes from BGP to OSPF with
tagging, and for redistribution of tagged OSPF routes into BGP.
• Static routes: display metrics for user-defined static routes redistributed into BGP and OSPF.
Note that the same redistribute metric will apply to both OSPFv2 and OSPFv3.
This command applies to all 1830 shelf types.
3.171.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
3.171.3 Input Format
show cn routes redistribute
default
non_default bgp_to_ospf
non_default ospf_to_bgp
static
3.171.4 Input Parameters
Sub-command: default
Display the state and metrics of user-defined, BGP, and DHCP default routes for redistribution
into OSPF. Also display setting for redistribution of default route from OSPF to BGP.
Sub-command: non_default bgp_to_ospf
Display settings for redistribution of specific routes from BGP to OSPF, including applied tag
and metrics.
Sub-command: non_default ospf_to_bgp
Display redistribution rules of specific tagged OSPF routes into BGP, with the BGP community
setting for the route.
Sub-command: static
Display the metrics for redistribution of static routes into OSPF and BGP.
System administration commands
Data communication network commands
show cn routes redistribute

3.171.5 Examples
Display all rules and parameters for redistribution of the default route. In this example, the default
route will be coming from BGP (best network practice is to only have one source of the default

default ospf_to_bgp route metric : 10
default ospf_to_bgp route mode : disabled

# show cn routes redistribute static
static user_defined_to_ospf route redistribute metric_type : 2
static user_defined_to_ospf route redistribute metric : 20
static user_defined_to_bgp route redistribute metric : 20

3.173.1 Purpose
This command displays the configuration of the Customer LAN Port including description, port

rate limit, and OSC driven link integrity.

primary or secondary loopback of the network element. The primary loopback is also known as the
IP address, or system address, of the network element. It will also display the OPSF and OSPFv3
area index for the loopbacks.
Note: the secondary loopback cannot have an IPv6 address.
This command applies to all 1830 shelf types.
Note: IPv6 is not available on PSS-4 shelf.
IPv6 is not available on the PSS-16 and PSS-32 shelf with equipment controller type "EC", i.e.,
classic EC.

Table 3-31 IP Parameters:
Parameters Description
IP Address The IPv4 address and subnet mask of the port
IPv6 Address The IPv6 address(es) with prefix length on the port.
There can be up to 17 IPv6 addresses: 0 to 16 Global and one Local. First in the list will be the
primary Global address, which is set based on the following rules:
• If ipv6_autoconfig is disabled, then
The configured IPv6 is the primary address
• If ipv6_autoconfig is enabled, then
The first DHCPv6 assigned address (/128 prefix) is the primary address; otherwise
The first SLAAC assigned address (/64 prefix) is the primary address.
Scope Specifies if IPv6 address is Global or Link Local address.
MAC Address Media Access Control Address.
Table 3-32 Layer-2 Parameters:
Parameters Description
Config. Speed The Configured Speed of LAN ports.
Config. Duplex Mode The Configure Duplex Mode Setting: Auto, Half or Full
Actual Speed The Actual Speed of LAN ports.
Actual Duplex Mode The Actual Duplex setting: Half or Full Duplex
Proxy Arp Specifies if Proxy ARP is enabled or disabled. When enabled, the port shall reply to ARP
request from remote server for all NEs within the internal network, using its own MAC address
for the response.
Table 3-33 DHCP Parameters:
Parameters Description
DHCP Specifies if Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) server is enabled or disabled on this
interface, if enabled this
interface will respond to DHCP response from clients to allocate an IP address.
DHCP_range This is the range of IP pool for the DHCP server. The port can dole out from 1 to up 10 IP
addresses. This parameter is valid only when DHCP is enabled.
DHCP Def Gateway Specifies that this interface's IP address is distributed as the Default Gateway via DHCP. If not
enabled, no Default Gateway IP address is distributed through DHCP on this interface. This
parameter is valid when DHCP is enabled.
DHCPv6 Specifies id Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol Version 6 (DHCPv6) server is enabled or
disabled. If enabled, this interface will respond to DHCPv6 client request for an IPv6 address.
DHCPv6_range This is the range of IP pool for the DHCPv6 server. The port can dole up to 10 IPv6 addresses.
This parameter is valid only when DHCPv6 is enabled.

Table 3-34 Router Advertisement Parameters:
Parameters Description
Status Displays the Router Advertisement state.
Maximum Advert Interval Displays the maximum time allowed between sending unsolicited multicast Router
Advertisements.
Preferred Lifetime Displays the length of time in seconds (relative to the time the packet is sent) that addresses
generated from the prefix via stateless address auto configuration remain preferred.
Managed Config (M-Flag) Specifies the value to be placed in the "Managed address configuration" M-flag field in the
Router Advertisement. When enabled, hosts use the administered (stateful) protocol for
address auto configuration in addition to any addresses autoconfigured using stateless
address autoconfiguration
Autonomous Flag Specifies the value to be placed in the "Address Configuration" A-flag field in the Router
Advertisement. When enabled, indicates that the interface prefix can be used for autonomous
stateless address configuration.
Default Preference Displays the preference associated with the default router, as either "low", "medium", or
"high".
Default Lifetime Displays the lifetime associated with the default router. A value of 0 indicates that the router is
not a default router and should not appear on the default router list. The router lifetime applies
only to the router's usefulness as a default router.
Valid Lifetime Displays the length of time in seconds (relative to the time the packet is sent) that the
interface prefix is valid for the purpose of on-link determination.
Other Config(O-Flag) Specifies the value to be placed in the "Other configuration" O-flag field in the Router
Advertisement. When enabled, hosts use the administered (stateful) protocol for auto
configuration of other (non-address) information.
Table 3-35 Auto State Parameters:
Parameters Description
Auto State This parameter controls the CIT port's admin state (up/down) autonomously.
Auto State Init by NE - The Auto State function uses ICMP ping initiated from the NE to determine if the NE is in
contact with the NMS.
NMS - The Auto State function watches for SNMP GET sysUpTime messages from the NMS
to determine if the NE is in contact with the NMS.
Auto State Count If Auto State Init by is NE, the Auto State Count displays the number of consecutive instances
that the Auto State Interval expires with the Auto State IP not being reachable. When Auto
State Count is reached, the CIT port is enabled autonomously if Auto State is enabled.
If Auto State Init by is NMS, the Auto State Count is not used.
Auto State Interval If Auto State Init by is NE, this timer value displays the interval between consecutive checks
for reachability of the Auto State IP address (Source IP) when Auto State is enabled.
If Auto State Init by is NMS, this timer value displays the interval the NE allows between
consecutive SNMP GET sysUpTime messages. If the timer expires, the CIT port is enabled
autonomously if Auto State is enabled.
Auto State IP If Auto State Init by is NE, this is the Source IP address the NE uses to monitor if there is any
loss communication with the NMS.
If Auto State Init by is NMS, the Auto State IP is not used.

Parameters Description
DHCPv6 Specifies id Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol Version 6 (DHCPv6) server is enabled or

IPv6 AutoConfig Specifies if IPv6 AutoConfig is enabled. If enabled, the port will be assigned an address via

Advertisement received from the attached router. For SLAAC, the port will receive an
advertised network of 64 bits (i.e., /64 prefix length); the port will then dynamically form a 64-bit
host identifier using modified EUI-64 rules, thus creating a full IPv6 address. For DHCPv6 a full
IPv6 address, with /128 prefix length, will be assigned.

Parameters Description
Status Displays the Router Advertisement state.

interface prefix is valid for the purpose of on-link determination.
Other Config(O-Flag) Specifies the value to be placed in the "Other configuration" O-flag field in the Router
Advertisement. When enabled, hosts use the administered (stateful) protocol for auto
configuration of other (non-address) information.

Table 3-42 OSPF Parameters:
Parameters Description
OSPF Adj State OSPF Adjacency state: FULL or Down
In rare instances, an intermediate state may be observed, e.g., 2Way, Exchange,
ExchangeStart, or Init. Consistent display of an intermediate state may indicate problems with
OSPF convergence.
OSPF Area Index OSPF Area Index (0..3)
OSPF Area Id OSPF Area ID associated with the OSPF Area Index
OSPF Routing The state of OSPF routing: enabled, disabled, or redistribute
OSPF Hello Interval OSPF Hello Interval specifies how often (in seconds) a Hello packet is sent out on the
interface. Hello packets are used to establish and maintain relationships with the neighboring
networking elements.
OSPF Router Priority The OSPF Router Priority, which is used to determine which network elements on a broadcast
interface will the designated router (DR) and backup designated router (BDR). The network
element with the higher priority value is the DR. If set to zero, this network element cannot be
the DR/BDR on this interface.
OSPF Router Dead Int OSPF Router Dead Interval Router Interface. This is the time elapsed between not hearing a
router's Hello PDU before the interface OSPF state is declared down. The dead interval is a
timer used to timeout inactive adjacencies.
OSPF Metric OSPF Metric or Cost of the interface. The lower the cost, the more preferred the interface is for
the routing of packets.
OSPF Retransmit Int OSPF Retransmit Interval. The length of time, in seconds, that OSPF will wait before
retransmitting an unacknowledged link state advertisement (LSA) to an OSPF neighbor.
OSPF MD5 Status Specifies if OSPF MD5 authentication is enabled or disabled on the interface.
OSPF MD5 Key MD5 Key used for OSPF MD5 128-bit hash value key calculation on the interface.
OSPF MD5 KeyId MD5 Key ID used for OSPF MD5 128-bit hash value key calculation on the interface.

3.183 show snmpserver
3.183.1 Purpose
This command displays the current configuration for the SNMP server.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.183.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner (except for "show snmpserver community": it is for
Administrator only)
3.183.3 Input Format
show snmpserver
authfailure
trapdest
community
3.183.4 Input Parameters
authfailure
Displays the current state of authentication failure traps on network element.
trapdest
Displays the SNMP trap destinations for the network element. This command can also be
performed by a Provisioner user.
community
Displays the SNMP community strings for the network element.
The output includes communities for external access as well as communities for pure internal
use.

3.184 tools ping
3.184.1 Purpose
The ping command sends a packet to the specified destination address and waits for a reply. If a
reply is received the network element is operational. If no reply is received either the network
element is not operational, or it cannot be reached.
This command applies to 1830 PSS.
3.184.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.184.3 Input Format
tools ping <destination> [source] [broadcast] [<number_of_pings>
[<packet_size> [<time_to_live>]]]
3.184.4 Input Parameters
<destination>
Values
<ipv4-address> - IPv4 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”
<ipv6-address> - IPv6 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”
Default
Entry required
The IPv4 or IPv6 address of the network element that you are attempting to ping:
• For IPv4 unicast pings use a standard IPv4 address.
• For IPv4 multicast pings (requires the broadcast option) use the broadcast IP address
of the subnet (e.g., 192.168.10.255) or the IP broadcast (255.255.255.255).
• For IPv6 use a unicast address; multicast and anycast are not accepted.
• For IPv6 use the address ff02::1 for a link-local multicast ping (see 'broadcast' option
below).
Restrictions
The broadcast parameter is required to ping a broadcast or network address.
source
Syntax
source {<ip-address> | <interface>}
System administration commands
Data communication network commands
tools ping
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
956 Issue 1
Values
For <ip-address>:
<ipv4-address> - IPv4 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”
<ipv6-address> - IPv6 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”
For <interface>:
NETIF-{1..512} - identifies an outgoing NETIF
ETHIF-{1..64} - identifies an outgoing ETHIF
<shelf>/<slot>/{OSC, OSCSFP} - identifies an outgoing OSC or OSCSFP port.
<shelf>/<slot>/<lan-port-aid> - one of the standard LAN ports on a card, e.g., 1/1/AUX.
Default
Entry required
Set the source address to specified interface or address. Argument may be an IPv4 or IPv6
address (depending on <destination> address type) or an interface. When pinging the IPv6 link-
local address this option is required.
For OSC port names, see Appendix A, “Reference tables”, "Port name to port number
mappings".
For the different LAN interfaces on a shelf, see Appendix A, “Reference tables”, "User service
interfaces".
broadcast
Allow pinging a broadcast address. For IPv4, this parameter is required if <destination> is the
IP broadcast address (255.255.255.255) or the subnet's broadcast address (e.g.,
192.168.10.255 is the subnet broadcast for network 192.168.10.0/24).
Note: Pinging the broadcast address will solicit a response from every node on the network.
Note: Set the <number_of_pings> to at least 2 when performing a broadcast ping.
Note: This option can also be used to ping the network address (e.g., 192.168.10.0) which is
the same as pinging the broadcast address.
Note: There is no check to assure that <destination> is actually a broadcast address. Pinging a
non-broadcast address with the broadcast option is the same as pinging without the option.
Note: The 'broadcast' option is ignored if <destination> is an IPv6 address.

3.185 tools tracert
3.185.1 Purpose
This command is used to determine the route that an IP packet takes to reach the specified
destination network element within the 1830 network. The tracert command displays the IP address
of each of the network elements through which the packet passes.
Note that tracert is UDP-based, sending a sequence of UDP packets with destination port numbers
ranging from 33434 to 33534 with increasing TTL on the packets. The responses are ICMP Time
Exceeded messages used to build a list of nodes that packets traverse, until the destination is
reached or an ICMP Destination Unreachable message is received.
This command applies to 1830 PSS.
3.185.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.185.3 Input Format
tools tracert <destination> [source] [<max-hops> [<udp-packet-size>
[<probes-per-hop> [<timeout>]]]]
3.185.4 Input Parameters
<destination>
Values
<ipv4-address> - IPv4 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”
<ipv6-address> - IPv6 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”
The IPv4 or IPv6 address of the network element to which you want a trace route. Only IPv4
and IPv6 unicast addresses are accepted.
Note: The destination is the only required parameter. The others will be set to default value if
not entered. If entered destination IP, then 2nd is max hops, 3rd is UDP_packet_size, 4th is
probes per hop, and 5th is timeout. The source address/interface can optionally be entered at
any point.
source
Syntax
source {<ip-address> | <interface>}

3.187 config database
3.187.1 Purpose
This command configures the database backup and restore options.
Use this command to:
• Display the current database backup and restore configuration
• Set full path-name to file or directory for backup or restore
• Back up the database
• Restore the database
• Clear the database
• Delete the local database backup
• Sync system information on a SEEP housing unit replacement in 1830 main shelf
For more information, refer to the "Maintenance and Trouble-Clearing Guide".
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.

966 Issue 1
Values
fallback - used to retain a local backup copy when backing up the active NE database to
the remote file server.
Creates a backup of the database at the IP address and path specified by the server and the
path parameters. Before the database backup is created, you are prompted to confirm the
request:
• Enter yes to create a database backup.
• If you specified the path ending with a directory, the backup will be created with a
filename in the form of: NEname_SWgeneric_yyyy-mm-dd_hh-mm-ss.bak else if the
path was setup including a file name, the specified file name will be applied, overwriting
an eventually existing file.
Note: If the NE name is too long, it is truncated to 31 characters. When the NE name (TID)
contains a forward slash (""/"), the path must include the file name.
After "yes" entered, there will be "database backup in progress...", then there is "database
backup complete", and the CLI prompt.
• Enter no to cancel the command without backing up the database.
With equipment protected ECs in main shelf, the standby EC is utilized for backup operation
too.
The optional keyword fallback:
Backup fallback is used to create a backup of the active database on NE, put it to the server
specified with "config database server" and retain a copy called FBDB of the database backup
on the NEs NVM.
As long as the FBDB backup remains on the NE, subsequent "config database backup"
commands will implicitly update it in addition to transfer to RFS.
The presence of a FBDB backup on NE will enable the auto-restore feature of the NE.
A FBDB backup is in particular useful for remote NEs as contingency to maintain access over
DCN after the active database became unexpectedly corrupted, which causes DBINVALID
condition be active.
After such an auto restore completed successfully, DBINBVALID is cleared and DBAR condition
is raised. DBAR condition indicates the is NE running with a database auto restored locally from
FBDB.
Restrictions
The fallback option is denied with an error message if config admin storage auto-
recovery-enabled is true. A fallback database cannot be created if the auto-recovery
feature is being used. For details about the auto-recovery feature, see config admin
storage and show admin storage.

restore
Syntax
restore [force]
Values
force - used to force the restore to the node.
Restore a previously backed up database. Before the database is restored, you are prompted
to confirm the request:
• Enter yes to restore the database from the backup.
After "yes" had been entered, a "database restore in progress..." comes out, after a
while, "database restore complete" and the CLI prompt come out. Then the CLI is logged
out and the system reboots.
• Enter no to cancel the command without restoring the database.
The optional keyword force:
Restore force is used to force a database to be accepted on an NE even if it is not for this NE
(does not hold the SEEP housing unit serial number - nativity check failed, i.e. user panel serial
number for this NE does not match). This can be used for example, if a User Panel was
replaced on an NE, but before the user had a chance to successfully complete the "config
database usrpnlrepl" command, the NE restarted.
Note: A set of IP values (Loopback IP, OAMP IP, Default Route) are stored in the SEEP (Serial
EEPROM) and not restored from the backup file. This is to assure that the system will remain
reachable in case of database corruption. The 'clear ipclear' option above will clear the contents
of the SEEP.
Note: Because the OAMP IP is never overwritten on database restore, if the OAMP address is
dynamic (dhcp_client='enabled') then in the backup dhcp_client should also be enabled.
Otherwise there is a risk of the OAMP disconnect. Specifically, if dhcp_client='enabled', yet
dhcp_client='disabled' in the backup, then upon restore the OAMP will be set to 0.0.0.0 (no
address) with dhcp_client='disabled', thus disconnecting the NE. This applies similarly to IPv6
and IPv6_autoconfig.
Command Validation
The parameters of this subcommand are validated for consistency among the parameters and
for consistency with pre-existing configurations. These validations apply to all shelves if not
explicitly stated otherwise.
The database restore requires the path set up prior to end in an existing file, i.e. such as
"/backups/backupfile.bak".
Sub-command: server
Specifies the attributes for the remote backup server (remote file server). See "config database
server".

System administration commands

Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
972 Issue 1
Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 characters containing the SSH key string in OpenSSH format.
"" - to clear the string.
Default
Entry required
The hostkey parameter provisions the host public keys used for host authentication. The
number of keys configurable per host is defined by the available key indices.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings or spaces only for all key entries - no host key
authentication will be applied.
If at least one key is provisioned, all provisioned keys can be used for user authentication.
Provisioning a second key allows key rotation without service interruption. After a new key is
deployed on server side the old one should be removed. A normal secure configuration applies
one key only.
The format of the string of the ssh key supported is the OpenSSH key format which can be
generated by the ssh-keygen command - "<type name> <base64 coded key string>
[<comment>]" (Ref RFC 4253). The content of the ".pub" file can be directly copied.
The host name, ip address and port, will be taken from the provisioned ip address and port
number.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring>) deletes the provisioned key and removes it
from the system.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin
security ssh" command.
Note: The hostkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.
ip
Syntax

Values
<ipv4-address> - IPv4 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”
<ipv6-address> - IPv6 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”

phrase contains spaces, it must be surrounded by quotation marks.

Issue 1 983

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 characters containing the SSH key string in OpenSSH format.
"" - to clear the string.
Default
Entry required
The hostkey parameter provisions the host public keys used for host authentication. The
number of keys configurable per host is defined by the available key indices.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings or spaces only for all key entries - no host key
authentication will be applied.
If at least one key is provisioned, all provisioned keys can be used for user authentication.
Provisioning a second key allows key rotation without service interruption. After a new key is
deployed on server side the old one should be removed. A normal secure configuration applies
one key only.
The format of the string of the ssh key supported is the OpenSSH key format which can be
generated by the ssh-keygen command - "<type name> <base64 coded key string>
[<comment>]" (Ref RFC 4253). The content of the ".pub" file can be directly copied.
The host name, ip address and port, will be taken from the provisioned ip address and port
number.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring>) deletes the provisioned key and removes it
from the system.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin
security ssh" command.
Note: The hostkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.

3.191 config dumpdata
3.191.1 Purpose
This command performs a data dump for the specified category and creates a particular log file for
that category on active main EC.
Data dumps are created as snapshot out of NE data for their particular data category.
The main purpose of creating data dumps is their subsequent transfer out of the NE for field
maintenance.
For each data category at maximum one data snapshot in form of a log file may exist.
A dump is either cleaned up thru housekeeping, e.g.
• a EC restart or
• successful terminated file transfer to a RFS or
• overwritten by a subsequent "config dumpdata <data-category>".
Per data category, one file can be dumped.
Existing dumps (for one or multiple categories) can be transferred by means of "config debugdump
transfer" CLI command.
Per category at maximum a single dump can exist, a subsequent "config dumpdata" for the same
category will replace the category's former dumps, when still existing.
"config dumpdata" is intended for maintenance and diagnostic purposes by experienced Nokia
service personnel only. Use with caution.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.191.2 Command Access Level
Impact: gathers a data dump file for the category as specified
Access Levels: Service, Administrator
3.191.3 Input Format

all

992 Issue 1
3.193 config firmware ne
3.193.1 Purpose
This command configures the NE level firmware update behavior.
Use this command to:
• Provision firmware update behavior for particular module types across the NE.
deferred: will activate module firmware on module insertion, cold reboot, or reload or hitless
firmware activation.
hitless-auto: will activate module firmware whenever a new firmware profile supporting hitless
device firmware activation for this module type is available, e.g. after profile provisioning change or
after SW upgrade with new default profile for this port type.
auto: will activate module type firmware whenever a new firmware profile supporting device
firmware activation for this module type is available. I.e., after profile provisioning change or after
SW upgrade with new default profile for this module type. This will be service affecting.
• Display the provisioned firmware upgrade setting for a module type.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.193.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.193.3 Input Format
config firmware ne port <moduletype> [deferred | hitless-auto | auto]
3.193.4 Input Parameters
auto
"auto" provisions the NE behavior for activation of module firmware to the following module type
firmware upgrade behavior:
autonomously activate the firmware on the affected module type with a different than running
profile becoming available, e.g., after SW upgrade, or card or port level warm restart after

depending on the newly available firmware profile.
A confirmation dialog with a warning to confirm this behavior for firmware upgrade for the
affected module type is supported.
Note, autonomously activate the firmware on module insertion, module-, card- (or NE) power
cycle from the deferred mode will remain too.

3.194 config firmware card
3.194.1 Purpose
This command configures the firmware on a card.
Use this command to:
• Provision specific firmware for a card in a specific shelf and slot.
• Display the current installed firmware for a field replaceable unit.
• Perform the firmware upgrade for a card in a specific shelf and slot over a firmware reload.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.194.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.194.3 Input Format
config firmware card <slot-aid> [ [Maj.Min.Rev | default] [reload] |
hitless]
3.194.4 Input Parameters
card
Provisions the firmware package of the specified card to be loaded at the next cold start of the
card.
When conditions are acceptable for the card to be reloaded a separate
config firmware card <slot-aid> <Maj.Min.Rev> reload
or
config firmware card <slot-aid> <Maj.Min.Rev> hitless
command must be issued.
The reload argument causes an immediate reload of the provisioned firmware for the specified
card.
Warning! -- Reloading can be a service effecting event.
The hitless argument causes an immediate reload of the provisioned firmware, if it can be
achieved hitless. Otherwise, the command will be rejected.
<slot-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>
Specifies the shelf and slot of the addressed card. Enter the shelf number followed by a slash,
and the slot number.

996 Issue 1
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each

Maj.Min.Rev
Defines the intended firmware profile for the card.
"Maj.Min.Rev" defines the specific firmware version of the profile (Profile_Maj.Min.Rev). To
provision a specific set of firmware to be loaded to the card on cold restart indicate the version
using the three fields separated by periods "." This version will be loaded even after a software
upgrade, provided it has not been retired in the new version of the software.
Restrictions
"Maj.Min.Rev" configuration is not supported for the below packet cards:
<ot-packet-card>
<csw-packetswitch-card>
<dsw-packetswitch-card>
These packet cards always require the default firmware profile from the active software
release for a particular packet card type.
default
"default" defines the preferred (default) firmware package for the addressed card. To provision
the card to always use the preferred (default) firmware package, even across software
upgrades where the default might change, use keyword "default": config firmware card 1/9
default. If not specifically provisioned to a firmware package, the default version (preferred for
the current software release) will be loaded upon cold restart of the card.
When displaying the version provisioned for the card, if the card is provisioned to take the
default firmware the version number of the default version is displayed followed by a space and
an asterisk "*".
If the default firmware is explicitly provisioned the asterisk does not appear.
reload
Specifies that the provisioned firmware package will be activated immediately, if the conditions
are acceptable. The card performs a cold reboot. If traffic is affected, a warning dialog to
confirm or abort is raised!
hitless
Syntax
hitless [force]
Previously selected and provisioned firmware package will be loaded on the card by performing
a firmware hitless reload over a warm restart. It is only accepted, if it can be achieved without
traffic affect (hitless).
The force directive at the end of the line makes the hitless option re-issue safe in that attempt
to execute a hitless upgrade when no hitless upgrade is pending will not be flagged as an error.
Examples of scenarios that will not be flagged as an error are:
• The firmware is already up-to-date.

• The only firmware upgrade available cannot be applied hitlessly.
In scenarios like this, the NE will not return "Unable to complete request. Error: Request Invalid

No other error messages are affected by the force directive. For example, when you attempt to
execute a hitless upgrade on a card that does not support hitless upgrade, the NE returns

directive is included or not included.
This command with the hitless option requests a yes/no confirmation after pressing the Enter
key. The confirmation prompt can be bypassed by giving the yes directive at the end of the
command line (see Chapter 1, “Introduction to 1830 CLI”, "CLI Navigation"). The force directive
also bypasses the confirmation prompt as though the operator had included the yes directive at
the end of the command line. That is, when the force directive is used, there is no need to say
force yes at the end of the command.
If you are using scripting to execute a hitless firmware upgrade, and if you want to suppress the
error message when no hitless upgrade is pending and to bypass the confirmation prompt,
include force at the end of the command line.

3.198 config software dynamic
3.198.1 Purpose
Set the attributes for dynamically loading software.
Use this command to configure or display attributes of the software dynamic upgrade, including:
• re-synchronize the software load from external RFS
• add loadable SW entities to additional software demand list. By default, SW is loaded for present
or pre-provisioned cards

By default, dynamic loading will load all of the software that is currently needed on the NE based on
provisioning and equipage. The "config software dynamic featurelist add" command can be used to
add additional software to the NE so that it is preloaded and available for future use. Software
features added to this list will be distributed to all ECs in the NE.

Position Description
<AID> address identifier for related pack. Last row will relate data to complete NE as "node".
<Pack> by pack type.
<Bank> affected bank on pack: current or standby. standby is in use during SW upgrade only.

Syntax

Values
external - triggers a refresh and load from external RFS for dynamic loading
force - disables command validations
Default
external
Starts to re-check the requested and the needed software or firmware and load it from:
• using the refeshserver settings
and distribute inside the NE.
During a dynamic update operation, the NE software makes sure that:
All the software necessary for the packs that are present, provisioned or in the dynamic feature
list are available on the NE.
Software that is not needed by the packs present or not provisioned or not in the dynamic
feature list is removed from the NE.

3.199 config software dynamic refreshserver
3.199.1 Purpose
Set the attributes for the dynamic software refresh server, dedicated for use during committed
phase of a software release.
This server attributes are initialized autonomously to the match the regular software server when
the load is committed by the operator. After commit, the dynamic software refresh server can
provide still software for the committed load dynamically even when the next software upgrade is
initiated, e.g. before the activate for the successor load. Usually these software refresh server
settings do not need to be changed. Exceptions would be, i.e. when the software refresh server's IP
address or user credentials or the root-directory changed over time in environment.
Use this command to display or set attributes of the dynamic software server (remote file Server,
SWNE FTP/SFTP server), including:
• IP address of the server
• Software root directory on the server
• Type of protocol used to access the software download
• TCP port used to access the software download
• User identifier and password used to log in to the server
• ssh private and host keys
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types, except PSS-4.
Dynamic refresh software server configured using a local USB key does not apply and is denied. An
external software server is mandatory for this function.
3.199.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Specifies the location for dynamic software loading.
Access Levels: Administrator

3.199.4 Input Parameters
detail
Displays the dynamic software server configuration.
hostkey
Syntax
hostkey <keyindex> <keystring>
Values
For <keyindex>:
{1,2} - index of the public host key
Default
Entry required
Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 characters containing the SSH key string in OpenSSH format.
"" - for empty SSH key string.
Default
Entry required
The hostkey parameter provisions the host public keys used for host authentication. The
number of keys configurable per host is defined by the available key indices.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings or spaces only for all key entries - no host key
authentication will be applied.
If at least one key is provisioned, all provisioned keys can be used for user authentication.
Provisioning a second key allows key rotation without service interruption. After a new key is
deployed on server side the old one should be removed. A normal secure configuration applies
one key only.
The format of the string of the ssh key supported is the OpenSSH key format which can be
generated by the ssh-keygen command - "<type name> <base64 coded key string>
[<comment>]" (Ref RFC 4253). The content of the ".pub" file can be directly copied.
The host name, ip address and port, will be taken from the provisioned ip address and port
number.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring>) deletes the provisioned key and removes it
from the system.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin
security ssh" command.

Syntax

Values
For <keystring>:

Default
Entry required
Values
For <password>:
<string> - UTF-8 string, 1..64 characters in double quotes.

Default
""
The sshprivkey parameter provisions the user private keys used for user authentication on
server side.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings - no public user key authentication will be applied.
The format of the string of the SSH key supported is the OpenSSH private key PEM file format
which can be generated by the ssh-keygen command.
The format looks like:
"-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----b3BlbnNzaC1rZXktdjEAAA ...
RAQ0VDMi04MS0yAQIDBA==-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----"
The key must be surrounded by quotation marks.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring> = "") deletes the provisioned key and
removes it from the system.
The private key can be protected by a password, which is needed by the system for decryption.

Following behavior of this parameter applies:
• If a password is provided, the key is password or pass phrase protected. If a pass
phrase contains spaces, it must be surrounded by quotation marks.
• If an empty string is provided, the key is not password protected. Empty string means: ""
is provided.
• If no password string is provided, the system asks for a password. If in this case ENTER
is typed without typing a password or pass phrase the key is not password protected.
If the sshprivkey parameter will be typed in without a value, then the fingerprint of the currently
provisioned key will be shown.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin
security ssh" command.

3.201 config software server transfer
3.201.1 Purpose
This command is used for the upload of the X.509 certificate signing request (CSR) and download
of the certificate to be installed on the NE. This certificate will be presented to the WEBUI or
openAgent client, when setting up the SSL/TLS connection. Prerequisite of the CSR upload would
be the key (see 'crypto sslkey') and CSR generation (see 'config sslcsr'). After uploading the CSR
and downloading the signed certificate, the new certificate must be installed (see 'config sslcert').
The up- and download will be done to / from the NMS or certificate server.
Use this command to:
• Set / Show the attributes for the upload and download file transfers.
• Show the status of the file transfer.
• Activate the file transfer or upload the CSR / download the X.509 certificate.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.201.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Specifies the file transfer attributes for SSL/TLS certificate signing request / certificate files.
Access Levels: Administrator

hostkey
Syntax

Values
For <keyindex>:
{1,2} - index of the public host key
Default

Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 characters containing the SSH key string in OpenSSH format.

Default
Entry required
The hostkey parameter provisions the host public keys used for host authentication. The
number of keys configurable per host is defined by the available key indices.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings or spaces only for all key entries - no host key
authentication will be applied.
If at least one key is provisioned, all provisioned keys can be used for user authentication.
Provisioning a second key allows key rotation without service interruption. After a new key is
deployed on server side the old one should be removed. A normal secure configuration applies
one key only.
The format of the string of the ssh key supported is the OpenSSH key format which can be
generated by the ssh-keygen command - "<type name> <base64 coded key string>
[<comment>]" (Ref RFC 4253). The content of the ".pub" file can be directly copied.
The host name, ip address and port, will be taken from the provisioned ip address and port
number.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring>) deletes the provisioned key and removes it
from the system.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin
security ssh" command.
Note: The hostkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.

Syntax

Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 character SSH key string.

Default
Entry required
Values
For <password>:
<string> - UTF-8 string, 1..64 characters in double quotes.

Default

The sshprivkey parameter provisions the user private keys used for user authentication on
server side.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings - no public user key authentication will be applied.
The format of the string of the SSH key supported is the OpenSSH private key PEM file format
which can be generated by the ssh-keygen command
The format looks like:
"-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----b3BlbnNzaC1rZXktdjEAAA ...
RAQ0VDMi04MS0yAQIDBA==-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----"
The key must be surrounded by quotation marks.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring> = "") deletes the provisioned key and
removes it from the system.
The private key can be protected by a password, which is needed by the system for decryption.
Following behavior of this parameter applies:
• If a password is provided, the key is password or pass phrase protected. If a pass
phrase contains spaces, it must be surrounded by quotation marks.
• If an empty string is provided, the key is not password protected. Empty string means: ""
is provided.
• If no password string is provided, the system asks for a password. If in this case ENTER
is typed without typing a password or pass phrase the key is not password protected.

1042 Issue 1
3.203 config software upgrade auto
3.203.1 Purpose
This command automatically upgrades the network element software in a single step or a set of
combinations, which all include audit and at least one (or more) additional steps.
Use this command to execute any of the following combinations of activities in a single step:
• Load: Perform a software audit and also load the new software, including optionally to backup
the database. The software audit compares the software on the network element with the
software on the remote file server and also performs other checks. If all the checks in the audit
pass successfully, then the software is loaded onto the network element.
• Activate: Execute items from the previous option plus activate the new software load.
• Commit: Execute items from the previous option plus commit the new software load.
The NE performs the chosen sequence of activities automatically.
Steps not performed can be configured afterward to complete the upgrade. Use the config
software upgrade and the config software upgrade manual commands to perform these steps.
Reasons steps would not be performed include:
• The config software upgrade auto command was entered for one of the first two combinations
listed above; that is not all the steps were included
• One of the steps failed
To configure the various scenarios, see the Input Parameters for the following commands:
• This command (config software upgrade auto) - load, activate, commit
• config software upgrade manual - audit, load, activate
• config software upgrade - commit
The automatic audit, load, activate, and commit sequence will not succeed if the NE contains at
least one packet card in a PSS-8, PSS-16II, PSS-8x, PSS-12x, or PSS-24x shelf. This type of card
supports manual deferred software upgrade per card restart, once the system software is activated.
Procedures for completing an upgrade for these shelves are given in one of the following
documents:
• 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS-8/PSS-16II/PSS-16/PSS-32/PSI-4L/PSI-8L) Customer
Release Notes
• 1830 Photonic Service Switch (PSS-8x/PSS-12x/PSS-24x) Customer Release Notes
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.203.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Upgrades the software on the network element
Access Levels: Administrator

url config software server
parameter
description
port port TCP port used to access the software server
root-directory root-directory Software server root directory; see additional explanation below

software upgrade auto
Directory that contains the software release; see additional explanation below

Note: If the port is not specified in the url, then the NE uses the default value that corresponds
to the protocol specified in the url regardless of any prior protocol settings. Therefore, if you
are using a url and if you want to use a port other than the default, then always specify the
port in the url.
Warning: Choosing a non-default port may block the service in case the port is not open by
the ACL settings.
The combination of root-directory/release-dir points to the location of the software release on
the Remote File Server (RFS). Choose the location of the software release on the RFS and
choose root-directory/release-dir in the URL such that the protocol server running on the RFS
can resolve root-dir/release-dir to the complete path to the software release. Here are more
details about root-directory and release-dir:
• The root-directory must start with a "/" (slash) character. Note that when using config
software server to configure the root-directory, the slash character is optional. However,
the slash character is mandatory when configuring root-directory within a url.
• The last directory in the root-directory path must be "ARMADA".
• The release-dir is expected to be a single directory (for example, <product>-<release-
info>, See Appendix A, “Reference tables” : "Common Value Definitions" for valid
software version formats) and not a multi-level directory. Therefore, slashes to specify a
directory path are not allowed in release-dir.
• The release-dir is used only during the upgrade; it is not a persistent parameter.
See examples below of urls being mapped to software server parameters.
The activity to write the parameters from the url into the software server parameters occurs
regardless of whether the software server parameters were ever configured (the software
server parameters do not need to be configured ahead of time) or regardless of whether any
specific software server parameter already provisioned is the same as specified in the url. This
activity also occurs regardless of whether any software server parameters were entered
previously using config software server or entered previously using a url specified when
upgrading the software.
Restrictions
The url option is not available when the controller in a PSS-32, PSS-16, or PSS-4 main
shelf is an EC card.

[nobackup | force | nobackupforce]
Values

force - parameter to turn off the upgrade path check, whether the actual upgrade from start
to target release is supported.

turn off the upgrade path check. If used, for SW downgrade from committed state.
Include one of these optional directives after the url or release-dir to set the desired behavior.
If none of these parameters is included, then a database backup will be done during the "load"
operation.
3.203.5 Examples
Note: For <product>-<release-info>, see Appendix A, “Reference tables” : "Common Value
Definitions" for valid software version formats.
Perform a software audit, load, activate and commit. In this example, the database is not backed up
before the load operation downloads the software, which is activated and committed.
The second version of the example includes the yes directive to bypass the confirmation prompt.

3.204 config software upgrade manual
3.204.1 Purpose
This command manually upgrades the network element software in a series of steps.
Use this command to:
• Perform a software audit
• Load the new software and optionally back up the database
• Activate the new software load
This command does not commit the software as the primary release. See the commit parameter of
the command "config software upgrade".
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.204.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Upgrades the software on the network element
Access Levels: Administrator
3.204.3 Input Format
config software upgrade manual
activate
audit {<release-dir> | { <url> [loadtype]}} [nobackup | force |
nobackupforce]
load
3.204.4 Input Parameters
activate
Activates the software on all of the cards on the network element using the information
generated during the software audit.
audit
Performs a software audit. A software audit compares the software on the network element with
the software on the software file server and also performs other checks.
load
Load the software onto the network element using the information generated during the
software audit. If a database backup was specified it is performed during this stage.
<release-dir>
Values
<string> - A single directory name
System administration commands
Database and software commands

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Default
Entry required
See command "config software upgrade auto" for a description of the release-dir parameter.
<url>
See command "config software upgrade auto" for a description of the url parameter.
loadtype
Syntax
loadtype {full | partial}
Values
full - full SW generic load
partial - SW generic load subset tailored to actual present or provisioned hardware or
demanded software entities for line cards
Default
is the loadtype that is currently loaded
Specifies if the In-Service-Upgrade shall download and distribute the full SW generic or be
tailored to load a subset of the SW available on the RFS, to meet actual present or provisioned
hardware or demanded software entities e.g. for line cards.
[nobackup | force | nobackupforce]
Values
nobackup - parameter to turn off database backup that is otherwise done during the "load"
operation, following the "audit".
force - parameter to turn off the upgrade path check, whether the actual upgrade from start
to target release is supported.
nobackupforce - parameter to restore an existing backup from previously configured
database path (see "config database path"), to turn off database backup creation and to
turn off the upgrade path check. If used, for SW downgrade from committed state.
Include one of these optional directives after the url or release-dir to set the desired behavior.
If none of these parameters is included, then a database backup will be done during the "load"
operation.
3.204.5 Examples

Definitions" for valid software version formats.
Perform a software audit.
In the first example, the database is backed up and the upgrade path and activation script are
generated. In the other two examples, the database is not backed up before the upgrade path and
activation script are generated.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Provides information about system check server provisioning, the last check and transfer
operation details.
The operation status is always reset to "none" after a start of the active EC and not maintained
in the database.
Sub-command: server
Specifies the attributes for the remote file server (RFS) to host system check test report files.
See "config systemcheck server".
setcheckcriteria
Syntax
setcheckcriteria <test-case-id> <criteria-string>
Values
<test-case-id> - "test case id" referring to an existing test case id string as reported from
"config systemcheck criteria"
<criteria-string> - "criteria string" in JSPONL line format without CR/LF/NL or space or
question mark
Sets for one test case of system health check the configurable criteria.
With this interface, per invocation one test case criterion can be pre-set to alter its system
default provided criteria.
One or several interface invocations can be used to aggregate for a set of test cases the
related criteria before these are activated with a "config systemcheck applycheckcriteria"
command.
A "setcheckcriteria" will need to be accompanied by an "applycheckcriteria" before the criteria
configuration is stored non-volatile, if a EC restart or side-switch occurs in-between, the criteria
not yet applied will vanish and remain at the last provisioned or default value.
In a simplex EC configuration, the configurable criteria will fall back to default on EC HW
replacement.
The format of the criteria string supported is a proprietary criteria definition in JSONL format.
One string defines the configurable criteria values for a single test case id - covered in system
check function.
The generalized format looks like:
{"<test case id>":<value>,"<criteria-1":"<value>,"criteria-2":["value-2","value-3"],..}
The criteria string must have no space, no question mark no CR/LF/NL special characters.
The criteria string must be surrounded by opening { and closing } brackets.
To see the current activated values, use "config systemcheck criteria".
To apply the current default values use "config systemcheck applycheckcriteria reset-to-default"
status
Displays the status of ongoing check and transfer operation

3.206 config systemcheck server
3.206.1 Purpose
This command sets the attributes for the systemcheck report server.
Use this command to set up:
• IP address of the server
• Type of protocol
• TCP port
• User credentials
• ssh key for host and user authentication
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.206.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Specifies the remote location for system check test reports
Access Levels: Administrator
3.206.3 Input Format
config systemcheck server
hostkey
ip
port
protocol

3.206.4 Input Parameters
hostkey
Syntax
hostkey <keyindex> <keystring>
Values
For <keyindex>:
{1,2} - index of the public host key
Default

System administration commands
Database and software commands
config systemcheck server
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 1063
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 characters containing the SSH key string in OpenSSH format.
"" - to clear the string.
Default
Entry required
The hostkey parameter provisions the host public keys used for host authentication. The
number of keys configurable per host is defined by the available key indices.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings or spaces only for all key entries - no host key
authentication will be applied.
If at least one key is provisioned, all provisioned keys can be used for user authentication.
Provisioning a second key allows key rotation without service interruption. After a new key is
deployed on server side the old one should be removed. A normal secure configuration applies
one key only.
The format of the string of the ssh key supported is the OpenSSH key format which can be
generated by the ssh-keygen command - "<type name> <base64 coded key string>
[<comment>]" (Ref RFC 4253). The content of the ".pub" file can be directly copied.
The host name, ip address and port, will be taken from the provisioned ip address and port
number.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters. Please note: The cli console would
allow typing in longer strings, but the system cuts it. This will lead to invalid keys.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring>) deletes the provisioned key and removes it
from the system.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin
security ssh" command.
Note: The hostkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.
ip
Syntax
ip [<ip-address>]
Values
<ipv4-address> - IPv4 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”
<ipv6-address> - IPv6 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”
Default
0.0.0.0

Values
For <password>:
<string> - UTF-8 string, 1..64 characters in double quotes.
"" - empty string for no password.
Default
""
The sshprivkey parameter provisions the user private keys used for user authentication on
server side.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings - no public user key authentication will be applied.
The format of the string of the ssh key supported is the OpenSSH private key PEM file format
which can be generated by the ssh-keygen command
The format looks like:
"-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----b3BlbnNzaC1rZXktdjEAAA ...
RAQ0VDMi04MS0yAQIDBA==-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----"
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters. Please note: The cli console would
allow typing in longer strings, but the system cuts it. This will lead to invalid keys.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring>) deletes the provisioned key and removes it
from the system.
The private key can be protected by a password, which is needed by the system for decryption.

Database and software commands

Following behavior of this parameter applies:
If a password is provided, it applies.
If an empty string is applied, the key is not password protected.
If no password string is provided, the system asks for a password.
If the sshprivkey parameter will be typed in without a value, then the fingerprint of the currently
provisioned key will be shown.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin
security ssh" command.
Note: The sshprivkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.
userid
Syntax
userid [<string>]
Values
<string> - 1..32 characters for existing userid on the remote server
"" - to clear the userid
Default
""
Specifies the user identification for accessing the remote server. After the userid is entered, you
will be prompted to enter a password value. Enter <cr> for no password value.
The maximum supported username length is 32 characters. The maximum password length
supported is 256 characters.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
Note: The userid and password parameters can be set regardless of which protocol is set.
However, the userid and password parameters are not used if protocol is set to http or https.

3.207 config turnup
3.207.1 Purpose
Set the attributes for the turnup of the NE from file data.
Use this command to:
• Set turnup file path local to the USB drive.
• See the status from load operation.
• Trigger the load from USB key.
Turnup from file via an USB key is only applicable to the following main shelf ECs:
• 32EC2
• 32EC3
• 8EC2
• 8EC3
• 8XCEC2
• 8XCEC2II
• 12XCEC2
• CEC2
• CEC2II
• MEC2L (via MFC)
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types, except 1830 PSS-4.

3.207.3 Input Format

status

Loads the turnup file from specified path on USB key and triggers the execution of the
contained CLI commands for turnup.
The load operation requires the NE TID be set as a precondition before. If the TID is not yet set,
the load will be denied.

3.209 show firmware
3.209.1 Purpose
This command displays the installed firmware for a field replaceable unit. During a firmware
upgrade progress can be displayed.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.209.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
3.209.3 Input Format
show firmware
available
card
ne
port
upgrade
3.209.4 Input Parameters
available
Syntax
available [<card-name> | port <module-type>]
Values
<card-name> - the name of the cards with firmware programmable devices. See section
"General slot-card commands" at "config card [<card-name>] <slot-aid>" command for a list
of differentiated values.
<module-type> - the name of the module type with firmware programmable devices.
Default
""
With no argument, this option displays the card related contents of the firmware subdirectory.
With a <card-name> argument, it displays the firmware configurations that are available for
provisioning each mode of that <card-name>. <card-name> is the identifier for the cards with
firmware programmable devices, for card name values see section "General slot-card
commands" at "config card [<card-name>] <slot-aid>" command.
When configuring the card, its mode is provisioned in the "config <card-name> <slot-aid>
cardmode", and the version of the firmware for the selected mode is set in "config firmware
<card-name> <slot-aid> <maj.min.rev>".

Database and software commands

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Most cards will display profile_maj.min.rev. Here "profile_" is a key word that indicates that
there is exactly one mode for the card.
Cards supporting "cardmode" will display version of the firmware as: " <cardmode>_
<maj.min.rev>".
With a "port" parameter, it displays the module related contents of the firmware subdirectory.
With both a "port" parameter and a "<module-type>" argument, it displays the firmware profiles
available for this module type.
card
Syntax
card <slot-aid> [detail]
Values
<slot-aid> - identifies the <shelf> and <slot> of the addressed card
detail - optional parameter to display more details
Displays the firmware status of the card specified by <slot-aid>. With the argument detail,
additional information is displayed like the current firmware status (hitless, supported, pending,
active, activeDGP) for the selected (default or provisioned) profile.
<Name> <hw-variant> <type> <version> <status> information is displayed (see Output
Parameters).
ne
Syntax
ne
ne detail [port]
ne port
ne profile [port]
Without further parameters, displays the firmware installed in each card for the whole NE in
ascending order by <slot-aid>.
Cards with "profile_DGP" for listing the profile under "Loaded" indicate that although a particular
profile version is applied, at least for one of the devices on the card a different firmware version
than mentioned in the particular profile is loaded. To see which firmware is running by device,
see command "show firmware card <slot-aid> detail".
With "detail" parameter, displays in detail the firmware installed in each card for the whole NE in
ascending order by <slot-aid>.
With "port" parameter, displays the firmware installed for modules in support of firmware
upgrade for the whole NE in ascending order by <slot-aid>.
Ports with "profile_DGP" for listing the profile under "Loaded" indicate that although a particular
profile version is applied, at least for one of the devices on the optical module a different
firmware version than mentioned in the particular profile is loaded. To see which firmware is
running by optical module, see command "show firmware port <port-aid> detail".

upgrade
Syntax
upgrade [ <slot-aid> | port [<port-aid>] ]
With no parameter, displays the progress of firmware update (both for normal and hitless) for
cards.
For cards, progress is displayed by raised (and cleared when done) conditions indicating a
pack specific device number:
• FPGAINIT[1-10] (for traffic affecting upgrade) or
• FPGAINITNSA[1-10] (for hitless upgrade)
In addition, the elapsed time since the card entered that state is displayed.
With <slot-aid> argument, only progress of the selected card is displayed.
With "port" parameter, displays the progress of firmware update (both for normal and hitless) for
pluggable optical modules.
For optical modules supporting firmware upgrade, progress is displayed by raised (and cleared
when done) conditions indicating a module specific device number:
• PORTFPGAINIT[1-10] (for traffic affecting upgrade) or
• PORTFPGAINITNSA[1-10] (for hitless upgrade)

3.210.1 Purpose
This command displays the Manager Access Domain Identifier for the requested facility.
The following facility types are supporting Manager ACD setting:
• OCH facility: see CLI command "config interface <csw-card> <port-aid> <otun>".
• GBEn Facility: see CLI command "config interface <csw-card> <port-aid> <ngige>".
• OCn/STMn facility: see CLI command "config interface <csw-card> <port-aid> <ocn-stmn>".
• OTU facility: see CLI command "config otu".
• ODUNIM facility: see CLI command "config odunim".
• ODUPTF facility: see CLI command "config oduptf".
• OTSIG facility: see CLI command "config otsig".
• TCM facility: see CLI command "config tcm".
• cards with oduchannelpool support, see CLI command "show oduchannelpool <pool-aid>"
3.210.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
3.210.3 Input Format
show mgracd <entity> <facility-aid>
show mgracd <slot-aid>
3.210.4 Input Parameters
<entity>
Values
interface - specifies the type for OCH, GBEn or OCN/STM facility
otu - specifies the type for an OTU facility
otsig - specifies the type for an OTSiG facility
odunim - specifies the type for an odunim facility
oduptf - specifies the type for an oduptf facility
tcm - specifies the type for an tcm facility
Default
Entry required
Specifies the particular entity type for the facility-aid.

3.211 show software
3.211.1 Purpose
This command displays the current configuration and status of the system software.
Use this command to:
• Show the progress of the software release upgrade
• Show the current software file transfer server configuration
• Show the current software download status as a brief summary
• Show the licenses applicable to the product
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.

Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

Values

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
server - Display software download server
transfer - Display file transfer server for NMS / certificate server
Displays the current configuration for the software download server or FTP for NMS / certificate

Additionally, it displays the SSH host public keys and private key fingerprint for Equipment

shelf
Syntax
shelf <shelfnum> [brief]
Values
<shelfnum> - Specifies the shelf number.
brief - Display software loads for all cards in shelf.

followed by shelfnum (the shelf number) and brief.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelfnum> ranges for each supported
shelf type.
upgrade
Syntax
upgrade status
Values
status - Display detailed status.
Displays system software upgrade information. Enter this keyword followed by status.
The information provided includes indication about the Active software release, that is currently
running on the NE and the Working Release, which is the software release that the NE is in
process of upgrading or downgrading to.
When the protocol for the software server is set to http or https, the display includes a URL
that the NE would use for the location of the software load. The NE constructs the URL from the
configured software server parameters. See "config software upgrade auto" for the mapping
of software server parameters into a URL.
The URL is displayed only if the protocol is http or https and if all the parameters are available
to construct the URL. Otherwise, the URL is left blank.
A port number is displayed in the URL only if it is different from the default (that is, if the default
port is specified, then the port is not displayed in the URL).

Cluster commands
3.213 config admin clusterip
3.213.1 Purpose
This command configures the (TIDs) NE Names and its associated IP address for the remote
cluster NEs.
• Specify the add/drop (TIDs) NE Names with its associated IP address on optical line nodes to
connect the cluster oconns with add/drop node and communicate its IP address with add/drop
node.
• Specify the optical line (TIDs) NE Names with its associated IP address on add/drop nodes to
connect the rmconport parameters with optical line node and send SNMP traps back to the
managing optical line node.
Use this command to:
• Access subcommands for configuring the add parameter.
• Access subcommands for configuring the modify parameter.
• Access subcommands for configuring the delete parameter.
Restrictions: Note that all the clusterip values in a cluster must be IPv4 addresses exclusively or
IPv6 addresses exclusively. The cluster cannot use a mixture of both for clusterip.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.213.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Add, delete and edit an NE Name and IP address for remote cluster NE.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.213.3 Input Format
config admin clusterip
add
modify
delete
3.213.4 Input Parameters
Sub-command: add
Configure new NE Name and associates an IP address to this name for the remote cluster NE.
See "config admin clusterip add".
Sub-command: modify
Modifies the IP address associated to a defined NE Name for the remote cluster NE. See
"config admin clusterip modify".
System administration commands
Cluster commands
config admin clusterip

Sub-command: delete
Delete the NE Name definition and its associated IP address for the remote cluster NE. See
"config admin clusterip delete".
3.213.5 Examples
# config admin clusterip
add Add/Create a clusterip
modify Modify the clusterip
delete Delete the clusterip

1106 Issue 1
3.214 config admin clusterip add
3.214.1 Purpose
This command is used to add the NE Name and its associated IP address for remote cluster NE.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.214.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Adding an NE Name and its associated IP address for remote cluster NE.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.214.3 Input Format
config admin clusterip add
<ne-name> <ip-address>
3.214.4 Input Parameters
<ne-name>
Values
<ne-name> - 1 to 20 TID character ASCII string
Default
Entry required
Specifies a name for the network element, which is also used as the system TL1 Target
Identifier (TID). Enter "add" keyword to get the new entry for TID (<ne-name>) and verifying the
current IP address is not already available in the database.
Note: If the new TID (<ne-name>) is already assigned, then the command is denied.
<ip-address>
Values
<ip-address> - valid IPv4 or IPv6 address for the TID (<ne-name>).
Default
Entry required
Specifies the IPv4 or IPv6 address. In optical line nodes, it is used to communicate with the
add/drop node. In the add/drop nodes, it is used to send SNMP traps back to the managing
optical line node. If the IP address ever needs to change, it can be changed centrally in one
place (here). There is no need to change the indirect references to IP address via NE Name in
every rmconport parameter on an add/drop node, or in every cluster oconn identifier parameter
on an optical line node.
System administration commands
Cluster commands
config admin clusterip add
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 1107
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Restrictions
The command will fail for any of the following reasons:
The IP address is already assigned to another NE name
The IP address is currently provisioned non-zero address of a local interface:
• LAN interface (OAMP, E1, E2, VoIP, AUX, or CIT),
• Loopback interface (loopback, loopback1, node, notify), or
• Any UCM-managed OCS system (OCS1, OCS2, OCS3).
It is a reserved IPv4 address that cannot be used for interface (See Appendix A,
“Reference tables”).
It a not an allowed IPv6 address (See Appendix A, “Reference tables”)
3.214.5 Examples
# config admin clusterip add B10U 1.2.32.2
# config admin clusterip add B11U 2001:db8:0:23::3fe:5

show admin clusterip

3.216 config admin clusterip delete
3.216.1 Purpose
This command is used to delete a NE Name and its associated IP address for the remote cluster
NE.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.216.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Deleting an NE Name and its associated IP address for remote cluster NE.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.216.3 Input Format
config admin clusterip delete <ne-name>
3.216.4 Input Parameters
<ne-name>
Values
<ne-name> - 1 to 20 TID character ASCII string
Default
Entry required
Delete a name for the network element, which is also used as the system TL1 Target Identifier
(TID) and its associated IP address. Enter "delete" keyword to delete the TID (<ne-name>) and
its associated IP address from the database.
Note:
• If the TID (<ne-name>) is newly entry, then the command is denied.
• If the TID (<ne-name>) is already in use by topology, then the command is denied.
3.216.5 Examples
# config admin clusterip delete B10U
# config admin clusterip delete B09U
Unable to complete request.
Error: IP Address still in use by topology
3.216.6 Related Commands
show admin clusterip
System administration commands
Cluster commands

3.217 show admin clusterip
3.217.1 Purpose
This command displays the TIDs (NE names), link status and its associated IP addresses for all
remote cluster NEs.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.217.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.217.3 Input Format
show admin clusterip
3.217.4 Output Parameters
Table 3-49 show admin clusterip
Label Description
NE Name (TID) Displays the network element name
IP Address Displays the IP address associated with the NE Name (TID). The IP addresses in this table
can be all IPv4 address, or all IPv6 addresses.
Link Status Displays the status of the communication link associated to a defined NE Name/IP address.
If no response is received after an implementation, then the link status is down.
Value is {up, down, -}
3.217.5 Examples
# show admin clusterip
NE Name (TID) IP Address Link Status
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
HO5L 10.20.218.38 up
H05U 10.20.218.46 up
SH11L 10.20.218.122 up
# show admin clusterip
NE Name (TID) IP Address Link Status
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
G02L 2001:DB8:0:23::3FE:1 up
