Flexgrid enable commands
3.219 config admin flexgrid
3.219.1 Purpose
This command configures aspects of the flexible WDM grid operation on the network element.
• Specify whether optical channel add/drop to OCS or cluster associated network elements is
allowed using off-grid and extended grid (below 191.7 THz) channel center frequencies.
Use this command to:
• Enable optical channel cross-connect command to configure off-grid and extended grid channels
for OCS and cluster associated uplink or optical transponder ports.
• Show the current value for whether off-grid and extended grid channels are allowed for OCS and
cluster associated uplink or optical transponder ports.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
3.219.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Enable or disable use of off-grid and extended grid channel frequencies for optical cross-
connects involving OCS or cluster associated ports.
Access Levels: Administrator
3.219.3 Input Format
config admin flexgrid
clusterenabled
3.219.4 Input Parameters
clusterenabled
Syntax
clusterenabled [<value>]
Values
{yes, no} - enable or disable
Default
yes
Configures if cluster and OCS associated NEs can be used to add/drop off-grid and extended
grid (below 191.7 THz) channel frequencies.
This value allows for phased software upgrading of the cluster and OCS associated network
elements. When ALL OCS and cluster associated network elements have been upgraded to a
software release supporting flexible grid application, this attribute must be set to value 'yes' to
enable use of the flexible grid capability.
System administration commands
Flexgrid enable commands
config admin flexgrid
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12

1116 Issue 1
Enter parameter without value to show the current value.
Restrictions
The value cannot be set to 'no' if any cross-connects using off-grid or extended grid (below
191.7 THz) center frequencies exist on the NE and are terminated on an OCS or cluster
associated port. Such connections must first be deleted before the value can be set to 'no'.
3.219.5 Examples
# config admin flexgrid clusterenabled
Cluster and OCS flexgrid enabled: No
# config admin flexgrid clusterenabled yes

3.221 config interface <fcru-card>
3.221.1 Purpose
This command configures the dedicated Ethernet timing ports, BITS port and TOD port. Use this
command to access subcommands that allow you to configure the ports on the below cards:
• 8DC30T - F-CRU card on PSS-8 shelf
• 8DC30T2 - F-CRU card on PSS-8 shelf
• 16DC65T - F-CRU card on PSS-16II shelf
• SHFPNL - Shelf Panel on PSS-8 shelf
• USRPNL - User Panel on PSS-16II shelf
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
3.221.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
3.221.3 Input Format
config interface <fcru-card> <port-aid>
3.221.4 Input Parameters
<fcru-card>
Values
8dc30t - 8DC30T or 8DC30T2 F-CRU card on PSS-8 shelf
16dc65t - 16DC65T F-CRU card on PSS-16II shelf
shfpnl - SHFPNL Shelf Panel card on PSS-8 shelf
usrpnl - USRPNL User Panel card on PSS-16II shelf
Default
Entry required
Specifies the FCRU (Full-Function Clock Recovery Unit) card type.

Synchronization interface commands

Sub-command: 1gbe
Enters the context to set the 1Gb Ethernet port attributes. See "config interface <fcru-card>
<port-aid> 1gbe".
Sub-command: fe
Enters the context to set the FE port attributes. See "config interface <fcru-card> <port-aid> fe".
Sub-command: state
Enters the context to enable or disable the port. See "config interface <fcru-card> <port-aid>
state".
Sub-command: pm
Enters the context to set the Performance Monitoring attributes. See "config interface <fcru-
card> <port-aid> pm" to configure pm attributes.
type
Syntax
type [1gbe | fe | unassigned]
Values
1gbe - 1 Gb Ethernet client
fe - Fast Ethernet client
unassigned - set the port as unassigned
Default
unassigned
Specifies the port type.
connport
Syntax
connPort [delete | <slot-aid>] [<port>]

3.227 config interface <fcru-card> <bits-port-aid>
3.227.1 Purpose
This command configures the BITS interface attributes for the following cards.
• 16DC65T - F-CRU card on PSS-16II shelf
• SHFPNL - Shelf Panel on PSS-8 shelf
• USRPNL - User Panel on PSS-16II shelf
Use this command to:
• Specify a description for the port
• Set the admin state of the BITS port
• Set the signal type of the BITS port
• Set the SA bit for SSM transport of the BITS port
• Select the means to generate SSM information for the BITS output port
• Set the inserted signal for the BITS output port when it is squelched
• Set the impedance for the BITS port
• Set the line code for the BITS port
• Set the line build-out for the BITS output port
Note:
16DC65T card:
• This command is only applicable for the PSS-16II shelf types with 16DC65T power filter, and the
panelTimingPort is configured as "No". See "config shelf <shelf-aid>".
• For the PSS-16II shelf with two 16DC65T cards, this command is only valid on the working
F-CRU. See "config redundancy workingcru".
• For the PSS-16II shelf equipped with one 16DC65T card and one 16DC65 card, this command
is only valid on the 16DC65T card.
SHFPNL card:
• This command is applicable for the PSS-8 shelf types with one 8DC30T only or two 8DC30T
power filters.
• This command is applicable for the PSS-8 shelf types with one 8DC30T and one 8DC30 power
filter.
• This command is not applicable for the PSS-8 shelf types with one 8DC30T2 only or two
8DC30T2 power filters.
• This command is not applicable for the PSS-8 shelf types with one 8DC30T2 and one 8DC30T
power filter.
• This command is not applicable for the PSS-8 shelf types with one 8DC30T2 and one 8DC30
power filter.
USRPNL card:
• This command is only applicable for the PSS-16II shelf types with 16DC65T power filter, and
only when panelTimingPort is configured as "Yes". See "config shelf <shelf-aid>".

Synchronization interface commands

3.228 config interface <fcru-card> <tod-port-aid>
3.228.1 Purpose
This command configures the 1PPS & ToD (Time of Day) interface attributes for the following cards.
• 16DC65T - F-CRU card on PSS-16II shelf
• SHFPNL - Shelf Panel on PSS-8 shelf
• USRPNL - User Panel on PSS-16II shelf
Use this command to:
• Specify a description for the port
• Set the direction attribute for the specified ToD interface
• Set the cable correction value for the specified ToD interface
• Set the manual compensation value for the specified 1PPS interface
• Set the admin state for the specified ToD interface
• Set the degradation threshold for the specified ToD interface
Note:
This command is only valid when the clockMode of shelf PTP clock is ocMaster | ocSlave | bc | tGM
| tTsc | tBc. See "config sync <shelf-aid> ptp".
16DC65T card:
• This command is only applicable for the PSS-16II shelf types with 16DC65T power filter, and the
panelTimingPort is configured as "No". See "config shelf <shelf-aid>".
• For the PSS-16II shelf with two 16DC65T cards, this command is only valid on the working
F-CRU. See "config redundancy workingcru".
• For the PSS-16II shelf equipped with one 16DC65T card and one 16DC65 card, this command
is only valid on the 16DC65T card.
SHFPNL card:
• This command is only applicable for the PSS-8 shelf types with 8DC30T or 8DC30T2 power
filter.
USRPNL card:
• This command is only applicable for the PSS-16II shelf types with 16DC65T power filter, and
only when panelTimingPort is configured as "Yes". See "config shelf <shelf-aid>".
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
3.228.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

Syntax
toddegthd [<value>]
Values
{0x00, 0x01, 0x05, 0x03, 0x04, 0x02} - if tod message format type is "ccsa"
{6, 7, 140, 150, 160, 248} - if tod message format type is "itu"
Default
0x00 - if tod message format type is "ccsa"
6 - if tod message format type is "itu"
Sets the degradation threshold value for the 1pps&ToD interface.
Note:
• For CCSA ToD message format type, 0x00 is the highest value, and 0x02 is the lowest
value.
• For ITU-T ToD message format type, 6 is the highest value, and 248 is the lowest value.

3.234 show interface <fcru-card> <bits-port-aid>
3.234.1 Purpose
This command displays the BITS interface attributes for the following cards.
• 16DC65T - F-CRU card on PSS-16II shelf
• SHFPNL - Shelf Panel on PSS-8 shelf
• USRPNL - User Panel on PSS-16II shelf
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
Note:
16DC65T card:
• This command is only applicable for the PSS-16II shelf types with 16DC65T power filter, and the
panelTimingPort is configured as "No". See "config shelf <shelf-aid>".
• For the PSS-16II shelf with two 16DC65T cards, this command is only valid on the working
F-CRU. See "config redundancy workingcru".
• For the PSS-16II shelf equipped with one 16DC65T card and one 16DC65 card, this command
is only valid on the 16DC65T card.
SHFPNL card:
• This command is applicable for the PSS-8 shelf types with one 8DC30T only or two 8DC30T
power filters.
• This command is applicable for the PSS-8 shelf types with one 8DC30T and one 8DC30 power
filter.
• This command is not applicable for the PSS-8 shelf types with one 8DC30T2 only or two
8DC30T2 power filters.
• This command is not applicable for the PSS-8 shelf types with one 8DC30T2 and one 8DC30T
power filter.
• This command is not applicable for the PSS-8 shelf types with one 8DC30T2 and one 8DC30
power filter.
USRPNL card:
• This command is only applicable for the PSS-16II shelf types with 16DC65T power filter, and
only when panelTimingPort is configured as "Yes". See "config shelf <shelf-aid>".

Release 24.12
December 2024
1192 Issue 1
Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 characters containing the SSH key string in OpenSSH format.
"" - to clear the string.
Default
Entry required
The hostkey parameter provisions the host public keys used for host authentication. The
number of keys configurable per host is defined by the available key indices.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings or spaces only for all key entries - no host key
authentication will be applied.
If at least one key is provisioned, all provisioned keys can be used for user authentication.
Provisioning a second key allows key rotation without service interruption. After a new key is
deployed on server side the old one should be removed. A normal secure configuration applies
one key only.
The format of the string of the ssh key supported is the OpenSSH key format which can be
generated by the ssh-keygen command - "<type name> <base64 coded key string>
[<comment>]" (Ref RFC 4253). The content of the ".pub" file can be directly copied.
The host name, ip address and port, will be taken from the provisioned ip address and port
number.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring>) deletes the provisioned key and removes it
from the system.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin
security ssh" command.
Note: The hostkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.

<ipv6-address> - IPv6 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”

sshprivkey
Syntax
sshprivkey <keystring> [<password>]
Values
For <keystring>:

Default

Values
For <password>:
<string> - UTF-8 string, 1..64 characters in double quotes.

Default

The sshprivkey parameter provisions the user private keys used for user authentication on
server side.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings - no public user key authentication will be applied.
The format of the string of the SSH key supported is the OpenSSH private key PEM file format
which can be generated by the ssh-keygen command
The format looks like:
"-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----b3BlbnNzaC1rZXktdjEAAA ...
RAQ0VDMi04MS0yAQIDBA==-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----"
The key must be surrounded by quotation marks.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring> = "") deletes the provisioned key and
removes it from the system.
The private key can be protected by a password, which is needed by the system for decryption.
Following behavior of this parameter applies:
• If a password is provided, the key is password or pass phrase protected. If a pass
phrase contains spaces, it must be surrounded by quotation marks.
System administration commands
ASON management commands

© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
• If an empty string is provided, the key is not password protected. Empty string means: ""
is provided.
• If no password string is provided, the system asks for a password. If in this case ENTER
is typed without typing a password or pass phrase the key is not password protected.
If the sshprivkey parameter will be typed in without a value, then the fingerprint of the currently
provisioned key will be shown.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).

For an protected Uplink protection group, enter this keyword followed by

Values
<shelf>/<slot>/L1
Modifies the Uplink Protection Group.
The add allows the addition of a second Uplink port to create a protected Uplink configuration.
The delete allows the deletion of the protected Uplink port to modify the Uplink group from
protected to unprotected configuration.
delete

Shelf commands
4.2 config shelf
4.2.1 Purpose
This command configures a shelf on the network element.
Use this command to:
• Create and delete shelves.
• Configure the shelf operation mode (shelfmode) for specific shelf types.
• Configure the coupled shelf number of the partner shelf.
• Performs the capacity upgrade for PSS-24x shelf from 24T to 48T capacity.
• Specify a name and description for the shelf.
• Configure power branch associated parameters like expected Amperes (DC or AC), expected
Voltage (DC or AC), shelf Voltage High and Low Threshold (DC or AC), Shelf Voltage Floor, etc.
• Configure air filter maintenance parameters.
• Set the WaveTracker mode for the shelf.
• Set individual alarm severity profile for the shelf.
• Set the expected CRU type for the shelf
• Set the switch of the timing port between F-CRU and user panel.
Note: The shelf type must be specified before other parameters can be specified.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
4.2.2 Command Access Level
Impact: The settings may affect shelf behavior
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
4.2.3 Input Format
config shelf <shelf-aid>
almprof
connectivity
customerlifecyclestate
description
duedate
expectedamps
expectedcru
expectedpf

4.2.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
1 - Configure the main shelf.
{2..64} - Configure one of the non-main shelves.
Default
Entry required
Enter 1 to Configure the main shelf. Configure a non-main shelf with 2-64.
For universal PSS shelves, <shelf-aid> must match with the rotary dial setting on the
backplane.
For universal PSI-4L, PSI-8L and PSS-4II shelf types, <shelf-aid> must match with the
configured Shelf ID settings (see command "config multishelf").
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf-aid> ranges for each supported
shelf type.
Note: For PSS-4, the universal extension shelf number is 2-8.
Note: For PSI-4L and PSI-8L, the universal extension shelf number is 2-31
Note: For PSS-4II, the universal extension shelf number is 2-8.
almprof
Syntax
almprof [<string>]
Values
<string> - 1..40 character string consisting of alphanumeric characters and dashes ("-").
The first character must be alphanumeric.
Default
configured default profile of the corresponding ASAP type
The Alarm Severity Assignment profile (ASAP) name used by the equipment entity for alarm
reporting. Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting. To change the setting,
enter this keyword followed by ASAP name.
Restrictions
The specified ASAP name needs to identify an alarm profile of the type "eqpt".
This parameter is only applicable for the following shelves:
• PSS-12x
• PSS-24x
• PSS-8x

Sub-command: inventory
Syntax
inventory {todb | tohw}
Values
todb - the inventory information is copied from the shelf inventory HW to the database
tohw - the inventory information is copied from the database to the shelf inventory HW.
Default
Entry required
Copies the shelf Remote Inventory information from the shelf inventory HW into the database or
from database to the shelf inventory HW. Each of the copy directions shall provide:
• a WARNING "Use this command only in case of a shelf inventory HW replacement, if a
failure occurred and the NE cannot update shelf Inventory data from its redundant
storage autonomously after HW replacement with a spare."
and
• a (yes/no) user interaction.

shelfloadwarningthreshold
Syntax
shelfloadwarningthreshold [<value>]
Values
{50..100} - percentage range of shelf load warning threshold setting with step of 1.
Default
100%
Sets the shelf load warning threshold.
A shelf load warning alarm will be generated if the total shelf power load (the shelf worst case
power consumption, not the shelf measured power consumption) exceed the threshold. The
hysteresis for the threshold is set as 3% by default. The total shelf power load threshold=
min{provisioning value or smaller of two power entry modules or shelfExtAcPower} *
shelfloadwarningthreshold.
Restrictions
This parameter applies to PSS-8 and PSS-16II shelves.

© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
1278 Issue 1
Restrictions
This parameter can only be modified for PSS-8x, PSS-12x and PSS-24x shelf types. It can
be displayed for all shelf types (see "show shelf" parameter shelfmode).
For PSS-8x shelf type the following shelfmode changes are allowed:
• 'unknown' to 'otn1T6'
• 'unknown' to 'otn4T'
For PSS-8x additional shelfmode changes are allowed, if the following preconditions are
met:
• 'otn1T6' to 'otn4T': central switch cards must be either unequipped or still equipped with
sc16 card types.
• 'otn4T' to 'otn1T6': central switch cards shall be of type sc16 (independent whether still
plugged or re-plugged) or the switch card slots must be empty.
• Other changes are not supported.
Notes for capacity upgrade to 'otn4T':
• Get familiar with the shelf capacity upgrade procedure in the User Provisioning Guide,
before performing this step.
• It is recommended to create a database backup before performing this step.
• The shelf is reprovisioned in this step and all present IO cards and switch fabric cards
perform a cold reboot (power cycle) to load firmware required and to reconfigure the
transmission paths for the new XST4T switch fabric cards.
• Before this shelfmode change is accepted, the user has to confirm a WARNING
message accepting a traffic hit.
For PSS-12x shelf type the following shelfmode changes are allowed:
• 'unknown' to 'otn4T8'
• 'unknown' to 'otn12T'
For PSS-12x additional shelfmode changes are allowed, if the following preconditions are
met:
• 'otn4T8' to 'otn12T': central switch cards must be either unequipped or still equipped with
XST4T8 card types.
• 'otn12T' to 'otn4T8': central switch cards must be either unequipped or still equipped with
XST4T8 card types.
Other changes are not supported.
Notes for capacity upgrade to 'otn12T':
• Get familiar with the shelf capacity upgrade procedure in the User Provisioning Guide,
before performing this step.
• It is recommended to create a database backup before performing this step.
• The shelf is reprovisioned in this step and all present IO cards perform a warm reboot to
load firmware required for the new XST12T switch fabric cards.
• Before this shelfmode change is accepted, the user has to confirm a WARNING
message asking if the tsifeeze action was performed.

© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
For PSS-24x shelf type the following shelfmode changes are allowed:
• 'unknown' to 'otn24Tc'
• 'unknown' to 'otn9T6'
• 'unknown' to 'otn48Tprim': coupled-shelf-number parameter must be entered when
changing the shelfmode from unknown to otn48Tprim.
For PSS-24x additional shelfmode changes are allowed if the following preconditions are
met:
• 'otn4T8' to 'otn9T6': central switch cards must be either unequipped or already equipped
with sc96 card types.
• 'otn4T8' to 'otn24T': central switch cards must be either unequipped or still equipped with
sc48 card types.
• 'otn9T6' to 'otn24T': central switch cards must be either unequipped or still equipped with
sc96 card types.
• 'otn24T' to 'otn9T6': central switch cards must be either unequipped or still equipped with
sc96 card types and the remaining matrix capacity (rmnmtxcap) must indicate 14400 or
more free bandwidths.
• 'otn24T' to 'otn24Tc': switch capacity will not change, but shelf internal transmission
devices will be re-initialized to be prepared for PSS-24x shelf coupling.
• 'otn24Tc' to 'otn24T': switch capacity will not change; shelf internal transmission devices
will be re-initialized to legacy 24T and the shelf will be not prepared for shelf coupling.
Other changes are not supported. For details of capacity upgrade to otn48Tprim, see
"config shelf <shelf-aid> upgrade-to-48T" command.
Notes for capacity upgrade to 'otn24T':
• Get familiar with the shelf capacity upgrade procedure in the User Provisioning Guide,
before performing this step.
• It is recommended to create a database backup before performing this step.
• The shelf is reprovisioned in this step and all present IO cards perform a warm reboot to
load firmware required for the new SC24T switch fabric cards.
• Before this shelfmode change is accepted, the user has to confirm a WARNING
message asking if the tsifeeze action was performed.
Notes for shelfmode change to 'otn24Tc':
• Get familiar with the procedure in the User Provisioning Guide, before performing this
step.
• Only from otn24Tc shelfmode a further capacity upgrade to 48T can be performed in a
later release.
• Before this shelfmode change is accepted, the user must confirm a WARNING message
accepting a traffic hit.

To enable AINS for extension shelves, follow the shelf type value the optional AINS qualifier. If
set, alarms will be suppressed until the shelf is first detected.
To de-provision (delete) a shelf, enter the keyword followed by "empty". The following deny
rules apply:
• The main shelf (<shelf-aid> = 1) cannot be deleted.
• An extension shelf cannot be deleted until all non-mandatory cards have been deleted.
• An extension shelf cannot be deleted until all ODUPTFs on virtual plane of the shelf in
state NOIMP have been deleted.
Examples:
A DCM, ITLB, ITLU, MLFSB, MSH8A, MSH8-FSM, MSH4-FSB, PSC1-6, SFD40, SFD40B,
SFD44, SFD44B, SFD48 and SFD64 shelf cannot be deleted until the contained "card" has
been set to administrative state down.
A VWM-CW, VWM-DW cannot be deleted until all cards including SFD/SFC/EC have been
deleted.
Restrictions
For extension shelf types PSS-8x, PSS-12x and PSS-24x the optional parameter
shelfmode applies and must be entered, if one of these shelf-types is pre-provisioned.
For shelf type PSS-24x the optional parameter coupled-shelf-number applies and must be
entered for shelfmode otn48Tprim.
Sub-command: upgrade-to-48T
Performs the capacity upgrade from one PSS-24x shelf with 24T to a coupled, two shelf system
with 48T capacity. See command "config shelf <shelf-aid> upgrade-to-48T" for details.
Restrictions
This parameter is applicable only on PSS-24x shelves to start the upgrade from otn24Tc, to
retrieve the upgrade status, to finish the upgrade or to cancel the upgrade (setting the
shelfmode back to otn24Tc).

4.3 config shelf <shelf-aid> filter-check
4.3.1 Purpose
This command performs an air filter supervision for a shelf on the network element.
Use this command to:
• Display the status of the last run
• Initial calibration of an clean air filter
• Perform a new measurement run
This command applies to PSS-24x shelf types.
4.3.2 Command Access Level
Impact: execute a new air filter check, which impacts the FAN speed.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
4.3.3 Input Format
config shelf <shelf-aid> filter-check
detail
calibrate
runnow
4.3.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
{1..24} - allowed universal shelf number range
Specifies the shelf number of an universal shelf for which the air filter supervision shall be
performed. The shelf must be provisioned and be physically available to perform this action.
Otherwise the command execution will be rejected.
detail
Displays the result of the last air filter supervision cycle.
calibrate
Performs an initial air filter supervision calibration run for a new clean air filter. After the run
succeeded the results can be viewed by "detail" parameter. The start must be confirmed by the
user.
runnow
Performs an air filter supervision run. After the run succeeded the results can be viewed by
"detail" parameter. The start must be confirmed by the user.
Equipment management commands
Shelf commands
config shelf <shelf-aid> filter-check

4.4 config shelf <shelf-aid> filter-maintenance-timer
4.4.1 Purpose
This command configures air filter inspection interval for a shelf on the network element.
Use this command to:
• enables/disables the air filter inspection time based monitoring
• configure the air filter inspection maintenance interval
• mark the time the air filter was inspected or cleaned or replaced
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
4.4.2 Command Access Level
Impact: enables the alarm to alert the user to inspect/replace the air filter.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
4.4.3 Input Format
config shelf <shelf-aid> filter-maintenance-timer
monitor
interval
startdate
4.4.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
{1..24} - allowed universal shelf number range
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf number of an universal shelf for which the air filter options shall be
configured. The shelf must be provisioned to successfully change these options.
monitor
Syntax
monitor [on | off]
Values
on - enables the air filter time based monitoring
off - disables the air filter time based monitoring
Default
off
Equipment management commands
Shelf commands
config shelf <shelf-aid> filter-maintenance-timer
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
1294 Issue 1
Enables or disables the time based air filter monitoring in this shelf. Enter this keyword without
options to display the current value.
interval
Syntax
interval [<value>]
Values
{1..104} - inspection interval time in weeks. Range is between 1 week and 2 years.
Default
26
Sets the air filter maintenance interval. If monitoring is enabled then an alarm is raised if this
interval is exceeded. Enter this keyword without options to display the current value.
startdate
Syntax
startdate [now | <yyyy-mm-dd>]
Values
now - sets the current day
yyyy-mm-dd - sets it to a specific day, which is not in the future; yyyy=year mm=month
dd=day
Default
1970-01-01
Sets the day, when the air filter was inspected in the shelf. If the date is in the future the new
value is rejected. Enter this keyword without options to display the current value.
4.4.5 Examples
# config shelf 1 filter-maintenance-timer startdate now
# config shelf 1 filter-maintenance-timer interval 8
# config shelf 1 filter-maintenance-timer monitor
monitor : on
# config shelf 1 filter-maintenance-timer startdate 2030-01-19
ERROR: startdate is not allowed to be set to a date in the future

4.5 config shelf <shelf-aid> power-branch
4.5.1 Purpose
This command configures the power branch settings within a shelf.
Use this command to:
• Display the configuration of the power branch.
• Set the expected amps of a power branch.
This command applies to the following shelf types:
• PSS-12x, which support 3 power branches.
• PSS-24x, which support 6 power branches.
• PSS-8x, which support 1 power branch.
4.5.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Setting the expected amps influence the power calculation and alarming.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
4.5.3 Input Format
config shelf <shelf-aid> power-branch <branch-number>
detail
expectedamps
4.5.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
{1..24} - allowed universal shelf number range
Default
Entry required

configured. The shelf must be provisioned to successfully change these options.
<branch-number>
Values
{1..3} - allowed power branch number range in PSS-12x shelf
{1..6} - allowed power branch number range in PSS-24x shelf
1 - allowed power branch number in PSS-8x shelf
Default
Entry required

4.6 config shelf <shelf-aid> upgrade-to-48T
4.6.1 Purpose
This command performs the capacity upgrade from one PSS-24x shelf with 24T to a coupled, two
shelf system with 48T capacity. Enter this command without any parameter to view the upgrade
status.
Use this command to:
• Display the status of the capacity upgrade.
• Start the capacity upgrade.
• Finalize the capacity upgrade.
• Cancel the upgrade when not yet finalized.
Notes for capacity upgrade from 'otn24Tc' to 'otn48Tprim':
• Get familiar with the procedure in the User Provisioning Guide, before performing this step.
• It is recommended to create a database backup before performing this step.
• Only from otn24Tc shelfmode a further capacity upgrade to 48T can be performed.
• The new second PSS-24x shelf shall be physically connected and shall be up and running with
shelfmode "unknown".
• Other needed HW (TIC48T, SCI48T) shall be present to guarantee a hitless upgrade.
• Before this shelfmode change is accepted, the user must confirm a WARNING message
accepting a traffic hit.
This command applies to PSS-24x shelf type with otn24Tc shelfmode only.
4.6.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
4.6.3 Input Format
config shelf <shelf-aid> upgrade-to-48T
cancel
finalize
start
4.6.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
{1..24} - allowed universal shelf number range
Equipment management commands
Shelf commands
config shelf <shelf-aid> upgrade-to-48T
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 1301
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf number of the primary shelf in a dual shelf (48T) configuration (in case of
"start" this is the shelf that shall become the primary shelf). The addressed shelf must be a
provisioned PSS-24x with the following conditions:
• cancel, finalize: the shelfmode must be otn48Tprim, the upgrade status must be in-
progress
• start: the shelfmode must be otn24Tc, the coupled-shelf-number must refer to a non-
existing PSS-24x shelf (implicit shelf creation) or an existing PSS-24x shelf having the
shelfmode "unknown"
Commands that do not fit to the conditions above will be rejected.
cancel
Cancel the capacity upgrade procedure, when not yet finalized.
Note: The user needs to confirm a WARNING message before this action is performed.
finalize
Finalize the capacity upgrade procedure.
start
Syntax
start coupled-shelf-number <shelf-aid>
Values
2..24 - allowed shelf ID for the PSS-24x partner shelf
Default
Entry required
Starts the capacity upgrade from one PSS-24x shelf with 24T to a coupled, two shelf system
with 48T capacity. The second partner shelf needs to be identified by the coupled-shelf-number.
Note: The user needs to confirm a WARNING message before this action is performed.
Restrictions
This parameter is only accepted when shelf mode of the addressed shelf is otn24Tc.
4.6.5 Output Parameters

Status Description
upgrade allowed The upgrade is allowed when shelfmode is otn24Tc
in-progress The upgrade is in-progress for shelfmodes otn48Tprim, otn48Tsec

1324 Issue 1
4.8 show shelf <shelf-aid> filter-check
4.8.1 Purpose
This command shows information about the air filter supervision cycle for shelves in the network
element.
This command applies to PSS-24x shelf types.
4.8.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
4.8.3 Input Format
show shelf <shelf-aid> filter-check
4.8.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
{1..24} - allowed universal shelf number range
* - for a list of all shelves in the network element
Specifies the shelf number of an universal shelf for which the air filter options shall be retrieved.
If a "*" is entered parameters of all shelves in the network element is returned as a list.
4.8.5 Output Parameters
Table 4-2 show shelf
Label Parameter Name Description
Shelf <shelf-aid> Shelf number for which the data are displayed.
Programmed Type type
(see "config shelf" command)
Provisioned Shelf Type
Present Type - Currently Present Shelf Type
Scheduled Time filter-check-time
(see "config general" command)
Time, when the air filter supervision is scheduled.
4.8.6 Examples
# show shelf 5 filter-check
Shelf 5 Information
--------------------------------------------
Programmed Type : PSS-24x Shelf
Equipment management commands
Shelf commands

4.9 show shelf <shelf-aid> filter-maintenance-timer
4.9.1 Purpose
This command shows information about the air filter inspection maintenance for shelves in the
network element.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
4.9.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
4.9.3 Input Format
show shelf <shelf-aid> filter-maintenance-timer
4.9.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
{1..24} - allowed universal shelf number range
* - for a list of all shelves in the network element
Specifics the shelf number of an universal shelf for which the air filter options shall be retrieved.
If a "*" is entered parameters of all shelves in the network element is returned as a list.
4.9.5 Output Parameters
Table 4-3 show shelf
Label Parameter Name Description
Shelf <shelf-aid> Shelf number for which the data are displayed.
Monitor monitor
(see "config" command)
Displays the monitoring state of this shelf.
Start-Date start-date
(see "config" command)
Displays the entered start date of the maintenance interval.
Interval interval
(see "config" command)
Displays the interval of the maintenance interval in weeks.
Maintenance-Date maintenance-date The calculated inspection interval. Start-date plus interval in weeks.
Is only displayed, if monitoring is enabled.
4.9.6 Examples
# show shelf 1 filter-maintenance-timer

4.10 show shelf <shelf-aid> power-branch
4.10.1 Purpose
This command displays the power branch settings within a shelf. Is also displays the related slots to
a power-branch.
This command applies to the following shelf types:
• PSS-12x, which supports 3 power branches.
• PSS-24x, which supports 6 power branches.
• PSS-8x, which supports 1 power branch.
• PSS-4II, which supports 1 power branch.
• PSI-4L, which supports 1 power branch.
• PSI-8L, which supports 1 power branch.
4.10.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
4.10.3 Input Format
show shelf <shelf-aid> power-branch <branch-number>
analysis
slots
4.10.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
{all, 1..24} - allowed universal shelf number range for PSS-24x, PSS-12x and PSS-8x
shelves
{all, 1..8} - allowed universal shelf number range for PSS-4II shelves
{all, 1..31} - allowed universal shelf number range for PSI-4L and PSI-8L shelves.
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf number of a universal shelf for which the power branch info is displayed.
Use the keyword "all" to display all shelves
Equipment management commands
Shelf commands
show shelf <shelf-aid> power-branch
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 1329
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
<branch-number>
Values
{all, 1..3} - allowed power branch number range in PSS-12x shelf
{all, 1..6} - allowed power branch number range in PSS-24x shelf
{all, 1} - allowed power branch number range in PSS-8x shelf
{all, 1} - allowed power branch number range in PSS-4II shelf.
{all, 1} - allowed power branch number range in PSI-4L shelf.
{all, 1} - allowed power branch number range in PSI-8L shelf.
Default
Entry required
Specifies the power branch number of a universal shelf for which the options shall be
configured.
analysis
Displays, for the selected power branch, a table of power estimates and measurements for
each field replace-able unit. The table is separated into sections (see the PSI-4L and PSI-8L
example below):
• Power-branch Input - shows the measured power, voltage and current at the input side
of the power module.
• Back-plane power delivered by each power module and a total which considers the
protection scheme.
PSILPFACs are protected with 1+1 redundancy for PSI-4L. "Active Load Sharing" shall be
displayed
PSILPFACs are protected with 2+2 redundancy for PSI-8L. "Active Load Sharing" shall be
displayed
PSILPFDCs are protected with 1+1 redundancy for PSI-4L and PSI-8L. "Diode-Or Load
Sharing" shall be displayed
All passive PFs are protected with 1+1 redundancy "Diode-Or Load Sharing" shall be displayed
The summary line for redundancy considers the effects of active power sharing and a 1+1 or
2+2 power supply protection scheme.
The power delivered to the back-plane is measured directly by the PSILPFAC and so the power
consumed by the power modules is accounted for between the "Power-branch Input" section
and this section
• Back-plane power consumed by each line card and shelf infrastructure device and a
total of all such devices.
Restrictions
This parameter only applies to PSI-4L and PSI-8L shelves.

Shelf synchronization commands
4.11 config sync <shelf-aid>
4.11.1 Purpose
This command configures the shelf synchronizations options.
Use this command to:
• Set the synchronous Ethernet function status of the shelf
• Set the synchronous Ethernet line reference of the shelf
• Set the synchronous Ethernet system clock of the shelf
• Set the synchronous Ethernet output clock of the shelf
• Set the PTP clock of the shelf
This command applies to
• 1830 PSS-8 shelf types with 8DC30T or 8DC30T2 power filter.
• 1830 PSS-16II shelf types with 16DC65T power filter.
4.11.2 Command Access Level
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
4.11.3 Input Format
config sync <shelf-aid>
lineref{0..4}
ptp
sync0
syncout
syncesupp
4.11.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
{1..24} - allowed universal shelf number range
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf number of an universal shelf for which the synchronization options shall be
configured.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf-aid> ranges for each supported
shelf type.
Equipment management commands
Shelf synchronization commands
config sync <shelf-aid>

© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
1342 Issue 1
Sub-command: lineref{0..4}
Enters the context to configure the synchronous Ethernet line reference attributes of the shelf.
See "config sync <shelf-aid> lineref{0..4}".
Restrictions
This cannot be provisioned when "syncesupp" is disabled.
Sub-command: ptp
Enters the context to configure the PTP clock attributes of the shelf. See "config sync <shelf-
aid> ptp".
Sub-command: sync0
Enters the context to configure the synchronization Ethernet system clock attributes of the
shelf. See "config sync <shelf-aid> sync0".
Restrictions
This cannot be provisioned when "syncesupp" is disabled.
Sub-command: syncout
Enters the context to configure the synchronization Ethernet output clock attributes of the shelf.
See "config sync <shelf-aid> syncout".
Restrictions
This cannot be provisioned when "syncesupp" is disabled.
This parameter is not applicable to 1830 PSS-8 shelf types with 8DC30T2 power filter.
syncesupp
Syntax
syncesupp [enable | disable]
Values
enable - Synchronous Ethernet is supported for the shelf and the synchronization attributes
can be configured.
disable - Synchronous Ethernet is not supported for the shelf and the synchronization
attributes cannot be configured.
Default
disable
Configure the Synchronous Ethernet function status, the value can be enable or disable.
If it is configured as enable, the following commands are supported, and the port level
parameter 'ssmtrans' will take affect. If it is configured as disable, the following commands are
not supported, also the port level parameter 'synceoppmode' and port level parameter
'ssmtrans' will not take affect.
For PSS-8 and PSS-16II:
• config sync <shelf-aid> sync0

4.12 config sync <shelf-aid> <lineref-aid>
4.12.1 Purpose
This command configures the line timing reference attributes of the shelf synchronization clock.
Use this command to:
• Set the line timing reference priority for the system timing entity
• Set the port for the association line timing reference
• Set the admin state of the line timing reference
• Set the line reference incoming QL Enable/disable
• Manually configure the line reference incoming QL value
• Configure the performance monitoring
This command applies to
• 1830 PSS-8 shelf types with 8DC30T or 8DC30T2 power filter.
• 1830 PSS-16II shelf types with 16DC65T power filter.

Restrictions
For the following cards on PSS-8 shelf, only one or two ports on each card can be
associated with line timing reference on the same shelf as below.
• One BITS input port on PSS-8 ShelfPanel card
• One of the two Ethernet timing ports on the active 8DC30T or 8DC30T2 card
• One of the two Ethernet timing ports on the standby 8DC30T or 8DC30T2 card
• Two SyncE-enabled Ethernet ports or WANIF entities on 12CE120 packet switch card
and its paired 20P200 or 1UD200 uplink cards
• Two SyncE-enabled Ethernet ports or WANIF entities on 12CE121 packet switch card
and its paired 20P200 or 1UD200 uplink cards
• Two SyncE-enabled Ethernet ports or WANIF entities on 1CE100 packet switch card
and its paired 20P200 or 1UD200 uplink cards
• Three SyncE-enabled Ethernet ports or WANIF entities on 12CE120, 12CE121 or
1CE100 cards and its paired S13X100 subtype card or S13X100E uplink card. Two
SyncE-enable Ethernet ports or WANIF entities can be on 12CE120, 12CE121 or
1CE100 cards. And another SyncE-enabled WANIF entity can be on S13X100 subtype
card or S13X100E uplink card, and this WANIF entity is manually created ODUPTF
associated with backplane port at ODU2e or ODU4 rate.
• Two SyncE-enabled Ethernet ports on 12CE120, 12CE121 or 1CE100 cards and its
paired 1ETY100 packet uplink card
• One SyncE-enabled Ethernet port on S13X100R or S13X100E card
• One SyncE-enabled Ethernet port on 16P200 card
• Two OTC Line or Signal timing ports on PTPIOC card
• Two SyncE-enabled Ethernet ports or WANIF entities on 18CE300 packet switch card
• Three SyncE-enabled Ethernet ports or WANIF entities on 18CE300 packet switch card
and its paired S13X100 subtype card or S13X100E uplink card. Two SyncE-enable
Ethernet ports or WANIF entities can be on 18CE300 cards. And another SyncE-enabled
WANIF entity can be on S13X100 subtype card or S13X100E uplink card, and this
WANIF entity is manually created ODUPTF associated with backplane port at ODU2e or
ODU4 rate.
Note: the BITS input port on PSS-8 ShelfPanel card is not allowed to be assigned as line
timing reference if the PSS-8 shelf is equipped with 8DC30T2 card.
For the following cards on PSS-16II shelf, only one or two ports on each card can be
associated with line timing reference on the same shelf as below.
• One BITS input port on the working 16DC65T card or on UserPanel of PSS-16II shelf.
These two options are exclusive. The working 16DC65T card can be displayed with
"show redundancy workingcru" command.
• One of the three Ethernet timing ports on the active 16DC65T card
• One of the three Ethernet timing ports on the standby 16DC65T card
• Two SyncE-enabled Ethernet ports or WANIF entities on 12CE120 packet switch card
and its paired 20P200 or 1UD200 uplink cards
• Two SyncE-enabled Ethernet ports or WANIF entities on 12CE121 packet switch card

priority
Syntax
priority [<value>]
Values
0 - disabled the timing reference from the system timing selection process
{1..5} - enabled the timing reference for the system timing selection process
Default
0
Sets the priority of a line timing reference for the system timing selection process.
Note:
1. The priority "0" means that the timing reference is disabled from the selection process.
2. A greater parameter value means a lower the priority for the selection except the value
"0".
priorityForOutputTiming
Syntax
priorityForOutputTiming [<value>]
Values
0 - disabled the timing reference from the output timing selection process
{1..5} - enabled the timing reference for the output timing selection process
Default
0
Sets the priority of a line timing reference for the output timing selection process.
Note:
1. The priority "0" means that the timing reference is disabled from the selection process.
2. A greater parameter value means a lower the priority for the selection except the value
"0".
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable for PSS-8 shelf types with 8DC30T2 card.
incssmsupp
Syntax
incssmsupp [<value>]
Values
{enabled, disabled}

4.13 config sync <shelf-aid> sync0
4.13.1 Purpose
This command configures the synchronous Ethernet system clock attributes of the shelf
synchronization clock.
Use this command to:
• Perform synchronization switch command for system timing entity
• Configure the synchronization status message for system timing entity
• Set the wait-to-restore time for the system timing reference
• Set the SSM quality level degradation threshold for the system timing reference
• Configure the performance monitoring
This command applies to
• 1830 PSS-8 shelf types with 8DC30T or 8DC30T2 power filter.
• 1830 PSS-16II shelf types with 16DC65T power filter.
4.13.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
4.13.3 Input Format
config sync <shelf-aid> SYNC0
pm
qldegthd
switchcmd
syncmsg
wtr
4.13.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
{1..24} - allowed universal shelf number range
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf number of an universal shelf for which the synchronization options shall be
configured.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf-aid> ranges for each supported
shelf type.

switchcmd
Syntax
switchCmd <cmd-value> [switchto <target-value>]
Values
For <cmd-value> allowed values are:
force
lockout
man
clear
clearlockout
Default
Entry required
Values
For <target-value> allowed values are:
int - Switch to Internal
lineref0 - Switch to lineRef0
lineref1 - Switch to lineRef1
lineref2 - Switch to lineRef2
lineref3 - Switch to lineRef3
lineref4 - Switch to lineRef4
Default
int
Performs switch commands for a line timing reference entity or internal clock involved in the
system timing reference selection process.
The following is the list of the switch commands.
Force:
Forced selection of the indicated line timing reference or internal clock for system timing entity if
the reference is enabled (that is, provisioned priority is not "0") and not locked-out.
Lockout:
Lockout of a line timing reference for system timing. (Note: This command is only applicable to
lineRef{0..4})
Man:
Amanual switch command selects the timing reference, assuming it is enabled, not locked out,
not in "failed" signal status ((SYNCREFFAIL and/or SLTMSIG) or unassigned

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
(SYNCREFUNEQ) or WTR), and has a QL better than DNU in QL-enabled mode. Furthermore,
in QL-enabled mode, a manual switch can be performed only to a source which has the highest
available QL. As such, these conditions have the effect that manual switching can only be used
to override the assigned timing reference priorities. A manual switch request overrides a
previous manual switch request. (Note: This command is only applicable to lineRef{0..4})
Clear:
Clear an active manual or force switch for a line timing reference or internal clock.
Clearlockout:
Cancel the lockout of one specified line timing reference. (Note: This command is only
applicable to lineRef{0..4})
Note:
1. Lockout is the highest request and always accepted.
2. Force is accepted if no lockout request is present for the timing reference.
3. Man is accepted if no lockout or force request is present and current reference status
is Normal.
4. For switch command of "clear", it is not necessary to follow "switchto" to specify the
AID of timing reference.
5. The int in "switchto" is the internal clock identifier, it is the default value for allowable
switchto
syncmsg
Syntax
syncMsg [enabled | enabledeql | disabled]
Values
disabled - Sync status Messaging is disabled.
enabled - Sync status Messaging is enabled without enhanced QLs and extended QL-TLV
support.
enabledeql - Sync status Messaging is enabled with enhanced QLs and extended QL-TLV
support.
Default
disabled
Default
enabled
Determines if the timing reference selection for system timing is using sync status messaging
(SSM Qualities) or not, and if the enhanced quality levels and extended QL-TV are supported
for system timing or not.
The following is the detailed description of each values.
• disabled - Sync status Messaging is disabled. System timing reference selection is done
only by priorities.

Release 24.12

1358 Issue 1
• enabled - Sync status Messaging is enabled without enhanced QLs and extended QL-
TLV support. System timing reference selection is done by SSM using quality levels as
the first criteria and by priorities as the second criteria.
• enabledeql - Sync status Messaging is enabled with enhanced QLs and extended QL-
TLV support. System timing reference selection is done by SSM using enhanced quality
levels as the first criteria and by priorities as the second criteria.
Note:
1. The enhanced quality levels and extended QL-TLV for system timing are supported
only when the syncmsg of sync0 is set to "enabledeql".
2. When the syncmsg of sync0 is changed from "enabledeql" to "enabled", the request
will be rejected if enhanced QL value is provisioned for the following parameter. The
user should change the QL value to the default setting or other legacy QL value.
When the syncmsg of sync0 is changed from "enabledeql" or "enabled" to "disabled",
the value of the following parameters will be reset to the default value.
• provql: provisioned QL of line timing reference for system timing
• qldegthd: QL degradation threshold on system timing
• ssmtrans: transmitted SSM on SyncE enabled Ethernet ports or WANIFs

{ePRTC, PRTC, ePRC, PRS, STU, ST2, ST3E, ST3} - SONET mode
Default
SEC - for node working in SDH mode
Default
ST3 - for node working in SONET mode
Configures the SSM quality level degradation threshold value for system timing reference
Restrictions
The parameter can be provisioned only when syncMsg of sync0 is set to "enabled" or
"enabledeql".
the following enhanced QLs are valid only when syncMsg of sync0 is set to "enabledeql".
• ePRTC
• PRTC
• ePRC
• eSEC

wtr
Syntax
wtr [<value>]
Values
{0..12} - gain in minutes
Default
5 minutes
Specifies the value of wait to restore time for all line references.
Note: This value is only for ETSI mode.
Sub-command: pm
Sets the Performance Monitoring attributes. See "config sync <shelf-aid> <syncentity-aid> pm"
to configure pm attributes.
4.13.5 Examples
# config sync 1 SYNC0 switchcmd force switchto lineRef1
# config sync 1 SYNC0 syncmsg disable
# config sync 1 SYNC0 wtr 5
# config sync 1 SYNC0 switchcmd clear
# config sync 1 SYNC0 switchcmd clearlockout switchto lineref1
# config sync 1 SYNC0 SwitchCmd man switchto int
Error: Request Failed - the man switch command is only applicable to
lineref{0-4}
# config sync 1 SYNC0 SwitchCmd lockout switchto int
Error: Request Failed - the lockout switch command is only applicable to

switchcmd
Syntax
switchCmd <cmd-value> [switchto <target-value>]
Values
For <cmd-value> allowed values are:
force
lockout
man
clear
clearlockout
For <target-value> allowed values are:
lineref0 - Switch to lineRef0
lineref1 - Switch to lineRef1
lineref2 - Switch to lineRef2
lineref3 - Switch to lineRef3
lineref4 - Switch to lineRef4
Default
lineref0
Performs switch commands for a line timing reference entity or internal clock involved in the
system timing reference selection process. This command is only applicable to lineRef{0..4}.
The following is the list of the switch commands.
Force:
Forced selection of the indicated line timing reference or internal clock for system timing entity if
the reference is enabled (that is, provisioned priority is not "0") and not lock-out. Note: This
command is only applicable to lineRef{0..4}.
Lockout:
Lockout of a line timing reference for system timing. Note: This command is only applicable to
lineRef{0..4}.
Man:
Manual selection of the indicated line timing reference for the system timing entity if the
reference is enabled (that is, provisioned priority is not "0") and not lock-out and the priority of
the indicated line time reference is higher than the one of the current reference. Note: This
command is only applicable to lineRef{0..4}.
Clear:
Clear an active manual or force switch for a line timing reference.

syncmsg
Syntax
syncMsg [enabled | enabledeql | disabled]
Values
disabled - Sync status Messaging is disabled.
enabled - Sync status Messaging is enabled without enhanced QLs and extended QL-TLV
support.
enabledeql - Sync status Messaging is enabled with enhanced QLs and extended QL-TLV
support.
Default
disabled
Default
enabled
Determines if the timing reference selection for output timing is using sync status messaging
(SSM Qualities) or not, and if the enhanced quality levels and extended QL-TV are supported
for output timing or not.
The following is the detailed description of each value.
• disabled - Sync status Messaging is disabled. Output timing reference selection is done
only by priorities.
• enabled - Sync status Messaging is enabled without enhanced QLs and extended QL-
TLV support. Output timing reference selection is done by SSM using quality levels as
the first criteria and by priorities as the second criteria.
• enabledeql - Sync status Messaging is enabled with enhanced QLs and extended QL-
TLV support. Output timing reference selection is done by SSM using quality levels as
the first criteria and by priorities as the second criteria.
Note:
1. The enhanced quality levels and extended QL-TLV for output timing are supported
only when the syncmsg of syncout is set to "enabledeql".

Values
{0..1000}
Default
0
Sets the duration in minutes of the holdover-in-specification mode as per ITU-T G.8275
Appendix VIII
The hldovrinspecdu attribute is applicable only when PTP profile mode is "itug8275dot1".
Setting the hldovrinspecdu attribute when PTP profile mode is "ieee1588" shall be rejected.
Note : hldovrinspecdu is the short name for holdoverinspecificationduration
Restrictions
- This parameter shall always be 0 when clockMode = tGm or tTsc
- Configuring none-0 value when clockMode is tGm or tTsc shall be rejected.

physical port is already associated to another PTP port, the command will be denied.

1384 Issue 1
Virtual PTP ports.
A virtual PTP port is a logic port which is created over a physical ToD port. The virtual PTP ports
will be created automatically in the deactivated status by default and will be associated with the
ToD input ports for the following cases if the ToD port is an input port or the direction is input.
The port number range for virtual PTP port is {1021, 1022}:
• When the TimeReference is changed from "extPPS" or "PTP" to "extToD" or "extToD_
PTP", and the admin state of ToD port is "Up".
• When the TimeReference is "extToD" or "extToD_PTP" and the admin state of the ToD
port is changed from "Down" to "Up".
Restrictions
Ports that are equipped with the following modules are not supported, since these modules
do not support PTP. If the "moduletype" of the physical port is the one of the follow
modules, it is not allowed to crate PTP port with this physical port and the command will be
denied. When one physical port has been associated with PTP port, the provisioning
command will be denied if the "moduletype" of this physical port is the one of the following
modules.
• SG-S-1.1
• SG-L-1.1
• SG-S-4.1
• SG-L-4.1
• SG-E1
• SG-T1
• SG-S1.1C
delete
Syntax
delete <value>
Values
{1..128} - Specifies the index of an existing ptp port on PSS-8 or PSS-16II shelf
Deletes a specified PTP port.
All virtual PTP ports will be deleted automatically for the following cases:
• When the current TimeReference is "extToD" or "extToD_PTP" and TimeReference is
changed to "extPPS" or "PTP".
• When the TimeReference is "extToD" or "extToD_PTP" and the admin state of ToD input
port is changed from "Up" to "Down".

4.19 config sync <shelf-aid> ptp clock1 <port-aid>
4.19.1 Purpose
This command configures the attributes of a specific PTP port or virtual PTP port of the shelf PTP
clock.
Use this command to:
• Set the transmitting interval for the Announce message
• Set the transmitting interval for the Sync message
• Set the transmitting interval for the Delay_Req message
• Set the receipt timeout value for the Announce message
• Set the receipt timeout value for the Sync message
• Set the receipt timeout value for the Delay_Resp message
• Set the ptp port role for the PTP port
• Set the localPriority attribute for the PTP port or virtual PTP port
• Set the gmPriority1 attribute for the virtual PTP port
• Set the gmPriority2 attribute for the virtual PTP port
• Set the gmClockAccuracy attribute for the virtual PTP port
• Set the masterOnly attribute for the PTP port
• Set the asymmetry correction value for the PTP port
• Set the addressing mode for the PTP port
• Set the VLAN-ID for the PTP port
• Set the destination MAC address for the PTP port
• Set the admin state attribute for the PTP port or virtual PTP port
• Clear the PTP messages counter for the PTP port
• Set the notMaster attribute for the PTP port
• Set the monitorReceiver attribute for the PTP port
• Set the monitorSender attribute for the PTP port
This command applies only when the clockMode of the shelf ptp clock is not ptpDisabled.
The provisioning for the virtual PTP port is not applicable when the clockMode of the shelf ptp clock
is ocSlave or T-TSC.
This command applies to
• 1830 PSS-8 shelf types with 8DC30T or 8DC30T2 power filter.
• 1830 PSS-16II shelf types with 16DC65T power filter.
4.19.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

synctimeout
Syntax
synctimeout [<value>]
Values
{2..255}
Default
3
Sets detection time for the detection of the SYNC message loss alarm. The value of the
detection time specifies the number of syncInterval that has to pass without receipt of an SYNC
message before the occurrence of the SYNC message loss alarm.
Note: the syncInterval is specified in the message interval field of received SYNC message on
the current slave port, i.e. the base of 2 of the message interval, the unit is second.

4.20 config sync <shelf-aid> ptp clock1 pm
4.20.1 Purpose
This command configures the performance monitoring (PM) attributes of the shelf PTP clock.
Use this command to:
• Clear current 15-minute and 1-day bins in all groups on this interface
• Configure the PTP time offset PM options
• Configure the PTP t-ms delay PM options
• Configure the PTP t-sm delay PM options
• Configure the PTP mean-path delay PM options
• Configure the PTP time offset accumulation PM options
• Configure the PTP time error by reference comparison PM options
This command applies only when the clockMode of the shelf ptp clock is not ptpDisabled.
This command applies to
• 1830 PSS-8 shelf types with 8DC30T or 8DC30T2 power filter.

refstat
Displays the signal status for the line timing reference as forwarded to the system timing.
The following values are reported for this parameter:
• Not-assigned - Synchronization line timing reference is unassigned.
• Normal - Line timing reference is assigned and operating normally without faults.
• Signal-failure - Synchronization line timing reference failure.

4.25 show sync <shelf-aid> sync0
4.25.1 Purpose
This command displays the system timing attributes the shelf synchronization clock.
Use this command to:
• Display the timing reference source for the system timing entity
• Display the synchronization status message for system timing entity
• Display the synchronization clock mode state
• Display the synchronization switch state
• Display the wait-to-restore timer for system timing entity
• Display the details information of the system timing entity
• Display the system quality level
• Display the SSM quality level degradation threshold for system timing reference
• Display the performance monitoring
• Display the current frequency offset of the active timing reference
This command applies to
• 1830 PSS-8 shelf types with 8DC30T or 8DC30T2 power filter.
• 1830 PSS-16II shelf types with 16DC65T power filter.
4.25.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
4.25.3 Input Format
show sync <shelf-aid> SYNC0
activeref
clkmodstat
detail
pm
qldegthd
refswstate
syncMsg
sysql
treffoff
wtr

4.25.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
{1..24} - allowed universal shelf number range
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf number of an universal shelf for which the synchronization options shall be
configured.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf-aid> ranges for each supported
shelf type.
activeref
Displays information about the current selected (active) line timing reference for system timing
entity.
The following values are reported for this parameter:
• none
• lineRef{0..4}
clkmodstat
Shows the clock mode status for the system timing entity.
The following values are reported for this parameter:
• locked - the system timing is locked to a line timing reference signal
• autohldovr - Auto hold-over mode for system timing entity. This value indicates that all
timing references available for the system timing selection have failed and the clock is
using history data previously acquired (when it was operating in the normal mode) to
control its output signal.
• autofrng - Auto free-running mode for system timing entity. This value indicates that all
timing references available for the system timing selection have failed and that no
history data previously acquired (when it was operating in the normal mode) is available.
• forcefrng - Forced free-running mode for system timing entity.
detail
Displays the current settings for the system timing entity.
syncMsg
Shows information about sync messaging (SSM Qualities) for system timing.
The following values are reported for this parameter:
• disabled
• enabled
• enabledeql

1436 Issue 1
defaultds
Displays the default attributes of the ptp clock.
The following attributes are reported for defaultds:
• clockIndex - the ptp clock index in the system
• clockID - the ptp clock identifier
• domain - the domain that the ptp clock belongs to
• priority1 - the priority1 attribute
• priority2 - the priority2 attribute
• localPriority - the localPriority attribute. It is valid only when PTP profile mode is
"itug8275dot1".
• clock-class - the clock class attribute.
• clock-accuracy - the clock accuracy attribute
• offsetScaledLogVariance - the offsetScaledLogVariance attribute
• two-step-flag - indicate if the ptp clock uses two-step mode or not
• number-of-ports - the number of ptp ports
• ePRTC-support - indicate if the T-GM is timed by ePRTC (enabled) or PRTC (disabled).
It is applicable only when PTP profile mode is "itug8275dot1".
• synchronizationUncertain-indication-monitoring - indicate if the synchronization uncertain
indication monitoring is enabled or not. It is applicable only when PTP profile mode is
"itug8275dot1".
• maxStepsRemoved - the maxStepsRemoved attribute. It is applicable only when PTP
profile mode is "itug8275dot1".
• adminState - the administrative status of the ptp clock
• deviceType - the deviceType attribute, computed from clockMode. It is valid only when
PTP profile mode is "itug8275dot1".
• profileVersion - the profile Version attribute. It is valid only when PTP profile mode is
"itug8275dot1".
• profileIdentifier - the profile Identifier, computed from profile version. It is valid only when
PTP profile mode is "itug8275dot1".
• holdoverInSpecificationDuration - the duration in minutes during which the T-BC clock is
configured to stay in holdover-in-specification as per ITU-T G.8275 Appendix VIII (if
favorable conditions are met) when PTP profile mode is "itug8275dot1".

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
currentds
Displays the current status of the ptp clock.
The following attributes are reported for currentds:
• offSetFromMaster - the time difference between the master clock and the local clock.
The unit is ns.
• meanPathDelay - the mean propagation time between the master clock and the local
clock. The unit is ns.
• currentTime - the current ptp time of the local clock. The format is as below: "S.N",
where "S" stands for the second part of time (48 octets) and "N" stands for the nano-
second part of time (32 octets).
• currentUTCTime - the current UTC time of the local clock. The format is as below:
'YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss', where "YYYY-MM-DD" stands for the year, month and day
part of time and "hh:mm:ss" stands for the hour, minute and second part of time.
• clockState - the status of the local clock. It shows one of the following values:
• Unknown: the local clock is in an unknown state.
• FreeRun: the local clock does not synchronize its time to the network, instead, it
generates the time locally.
• Acquiring: the local clock is just starting to lock to the selected reference.
• Phasetracking: the local clock is aligning its time to the reference before going to the
locked state.
• Holdover: the local clock is in the holdover status in ieee1588 profile. This value
indicates that all time references have failed, and the clock is using history data
previously acquired (when it was operating in the locked state) to control its time.
• Holdover-in-spec: the local clock is in the holdover-in-specification status in
itug8275dot1 profile. This value indicates that all time references have failed, and the
clock is using history data previously acquired (when it was operating in the locked
state) to control its time, and the holdoverInSpecificationRemainingDuration value is
positive.
• Holdover-out-of-spec: the local clock is in the holdover-out-of-specification status in
itug8275dot1 profile. This value indicates that all time references have failed, and the
clock is using history data previously acquired (when it was operating in the locked
state) to control its time, and the holdoverInSpecificationRemainingDuration value is null.
• Locked: the local clock is stablely locked to a ptp port or external 1pps&ToD interface.
• lockedPtpPort - the ptp port or ToD port which the d clockStatue = locked. The value of
1021 refers to the ToD1 port while the value of 1022 refers to the ToD2 port.
• stepsRemoved - the number of communication path traversed between the grandmaster
clock and the local clock.
• holdoverInSpecificationRemainingDuration - the remaining duration in minutes for the
"Holdover-in-spec" clockstate, before evolving to the "Holdover-out-of-spec' clockstate,
in itug8275dot1 profile.

parentds
Displays the attributes of the parent clock and grandmaster clock (which the local clock is
synchronizing to).
The following attributes are reported for parentds:
• clockID - clock identifier of the parent clock
• ptp-port-number - the ptp port's number of the parent clock which the local clock is
synchronizing to
• statisticCollected - indicate if the parent clock statistics are collected or not
• offsetScaledLogVariance - the offset scaled log variance of the current master, observed
by the local clock. It is applicable only statisticCollected is true
• phaseChangeRate - the phase change rate of the current master, observed by the local
clock. It is applicable only statisticCollected is true
• grandmasterClockId - the clock identifier of the grandmaster
• grandmasterClass - the clock class of the grandmaster. Refer to Section 7.6.2.4 of
IEEE1588-2008
• grandmasterAccuracy - the clock accuracy of the grandmaster. Refer to Section 7.6.2.5
of IEEE1588-2008
• grandmasterOffsetScaledLogVariance - the offset scaled log variance of the
grandmaster
• grandmasterPriority1 - priority1 value of the grandmaster
• grandmasterPriority2 - priority2 value of the grandmaster
timepropertiesds
Displays the time properties of the ptp clock.
The following attributes are reported for timepropertiesds:
• currentUtcOffset - the current offset between TAI and UTC. Unit is second
• currentUtcOffsetValid - indicate if the value of the currentUtcOffset is valid or not
• leap59 - indicate if the last minute of the current UTC day contains 59 seconds or not
• leap61 - indicate if the last minute of the current UTC day contains 61 seconds or not
• timeTraceable - indicate if the timescale and value of current UTC offset are traceable to
a primary reference or not
• frequencyTraceable - indicate if the frequency determining the timescale is traceable to
a primary reference or not
• ptpTimescale - indicate if the clock timescale of the grandmaster clock is ptp or not-
TRUE = PTP timescale- FALSE= ARB timescale
• ptpTimeSource - the source of time used by the grandmaster clock.
• synchronizationUncertain - indicate if the SynchronizationUncertain flag of incoming
Announce message from the parent clock is TRUE or FALSE. It is applicable only when
PTP profile mode is "itug8275dot1" and the syncuncertainmon is "enable".

4.36 config slot
4.36.1 Purpose
This command configures a slot in a shelf.
Use this command to:
• Pre-provision the network element database to expect a specific card type in the slot.
• Specify the administrative state of the card in the slot.
• Specify the power administrative state of the card in the slot.
• Set individual alarm severity profile for the slot.
Note: The slot type must be specified before the state can be provisioned.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
4.36.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Setting the admin state to down may impact traffic.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
4.36.3 Input Format
config slot <slot-aid>
almprof
customerlifecyclestate
duedate
lifecyclestate
power-admin-state
productcode
productcodesup
state
type
4.36.4 Input Parameters
<slot-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot> - to address a specific slot
* - display a list of all slots in the network element
Default
Entry required

productcodesup
Syntax
productcodesup [<value>]
Values
disabled - product code is not used for card supervision
enabled - product code is used for card supervision
Default
disabled
The parameter productcodesup controls whether card product code is used for card
supervision.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting. To change the setting, enter this keyword
followed by an allowed value.
Notes:
• If the value disabled is provisioned, then productcode is not used as a contributor to
raise a card mismatch alarm.
• If the value enabled is provisioned and the provisioned productcode value is not a prefix
of the unit part number value as read from the card inventory, then a card mismatch
alarm is raised.
• If the value enabled is provisioned and the provisioned productcode value is an empty
string (i.e. no card is provisioned) and a card is plugged in, then a card mismatch alarm
is raised.
Restrictions
This parameter applies only when customer-appl-mode indicates an "openROADM".
state
Syntax
state [<value>]
Values
up - set the admin state to in-service.
down - set the admin state to out-of-service.
mt - set the admin state to maintenance.
Default
down
Sets the administrative state of the card in the slot.
Enter this keyword followed by one of the defined values or enter this keyword alone to display
the current administrative state of the card.

4.37 config slot <slot-aid> type
4.37.1 Purpose
This command configures a slot for a specific card type.
Use this command to:
• Pre-provision the network element database to expect a specific card type in the slot.
• Change the setting for a pre-provisioned card type to the card type that is currently inserted into
the slot.
AINS (automatic in-service): When pre-provisioning a slot for a specific card type, you can set the
ains qualifier to specify that no alarms are generated for the card until it is first inserted in the slot.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
4.37.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Configures the card type for the specified slot
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
4.37.3 Input Format
config slot <slot-aid> type {empty | <card-name>} [subtype] [ains]
4.37.4 Input Parameters
<slot-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot> - to address a specific slot
* - display a list of all slots in the network element
Default
Entry required
Specifies the <shelf> and <slot> that is reserved for, or contains, the card. Enter the shelf
number followed by a slash and the slot number.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
empty
Configure the addressed slot as empty. This deprovisions (deletes) the card.
If you insert a card into a slot configured as empty, the slot is automatically configured for the
inserted card type using its default values.

Restrictions
This parameter applies to all 1CE100, 1UX500, 2UC400, 2UC1T, 8P20, ASC2, ASC4, ASG,
D6AD2T4, IR9, IR20, IRDM32, MVAC, MXN824, S13X100, S13X400, S2AD200, S4X400,
S5AD400 and S6AD600 subtype cards.
Subtype modification is only allowed for 8P20 subtype cards.
The operation shall only be allowed, if the slot is empty or if the new card sub-type is
already plugged-in.
And the operation to change the 8P20 subtype shall be rejected in below cases:
- pluggable modules are not compatible between 8P20 and 8P20B
- Y-cable protection is provisioned on 8P20

1494 Issue 1
4.38 config slot migration
4.38.1 Purpose
This command migrates a slot from one card type to another card type of the same family with a
superset of the functionality of the former card.
Use this command to:
• configure slots to be migrated to new card types.
• activate slot migration.
• display a list of slots set to be migrated.
• clear the list of slots to be migrated.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
4.38.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Migrates one or more slots to a new type. Activate initiates a warm reset of the network
element.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
4.38.3 Input Format
config slot migration
<slot-aid> [migrateto]
activate
clear
4.38.4 Input Parameters
<slot-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot> - to address a specific slot
* - display a list of all slots in the network element with migration target <card-name>
assigned to a value other than none.
Specifies the <shelf> and <slot> that is reserved for, or contains, the card. Enter the shelf
number followed by a slash and the slot number.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
Sub-command: migrateto
Syntax
migrateto [<card-name>]
Equipment management commands
General slot-card commands

wtocm-f - Provision the target slot type migration to a wtocm-f card.
none - Clear the slot type migration for the slot.
Default
none
Sets the migration target <card-name> for the slot. Enter parameter without value to display the
current value. Value none indicates no migration target is set for the slot. Note that any set
migration targets will be retained if the equipment controller or network element undergo a reset
or the equipment controller undergoes a side switch prior to activating the migration using the
activate command.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Sub-command: activate
Activates migration of ALL slot migrations defined on the network element. A prompt gives the
user an opportunity to confirm and proceed with yes or not proceed with no. After the command
is entered the network element will undergo a warm reset, and as the NE goes through the
warm reset the card type of the slots with migration targets will be migrated to the target type. If
any of the slots with migration targets assigned are not either present type empty or present
type equal to the migration target type, the command is denied. Note there is no way to back-
out after this command. To go back to the old configuration a database back-up must be
restored.
Restrictions
Command is rejected if the slot present type is not empty or equal to the target <card-
name>.
Command is rejected if none of the slots have been set to a migration target.
clear
Clears ALL the slot migration targets defined on the network element.
4.38.5 Examples
# config slot migration 1/5 migrateto wtocm-f
# config slot migration 1/5 migrateto
Target Type: WTOCM-F
# config slot migration 1/9 migrateto
Target Type: None
# config slot migration activate
WARNING: You are about to perform a migration of slot type(s).
This will cause a network element warm reset.
Enter 'yes' to confirm, 'no' to cancel: no
Command aborted
# config slot migration activate
WARNING: You are about to perform a migration of slot type(s).
This will cause a network element warm reset.

reset
Syntax
reset <value> [force]
Values
cold - A cold restart reinitializes the card software and hardware, and is service affecting.
warm - A warm restart re-initializes the card application software only, and is not service
affecting.
force - optional parameter together with cold.
Performs a restart of the card.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the ports and the card to admin down or admin mt.
tolerance
Syntax
tolerance [<degrees>]
Values
{0..10} - temperature tolerance range for °C
{0..18} - temperature tolerance range for °F
Default
3 - for °C
5 - for °F
The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword to display the current tolerance. To
change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify the card
temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature that must
occur before the alarm is cleared. For example, if the high temperature alarm is triggered at
55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C, the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to below 52°C.
Similarly, where lowtemp is at 5°C, the alarm is cleared when the card warms to above 8°C.
Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE
(see "config admin").
Restrictions
This parameter does not apply to MEC2L card.

tolerance
Syntax
tolerance [<degrees>]
Values
{0..10} - temperature tolerance range for °C
{0..18} - temperature tolerance range for °F
Default
3 - for °C
5 - for °F
The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword without options to display the current
tolerance. To change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify
the card temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature
that must occur before the alarm is cleared. For example, if the high temperature alarm is
triggered at 55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C, the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to
below 52°C. Similarly, where lowtemp is at 5°C, the alarm is cleared when the card warms to
above 8°C. Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on
the NE (see "config admin").
