Default
""
Specifies the card description. Enter this keyword without option to display the current
description. To change the description, enter this keyword followed by a character string that

text.
hightemp
Syntax
hightemp [<degrees>]
Values
-5..90 - temperature range for °C
23..194 - temperature range for °F
Default
90 - for °C
194 - for °F
The high temperature threshold for the card. Enter this keyword without option to display the
current temperature threshold. To change the threshold, enter this keyword followed by an
integer value to specify the temperature above which the high temperature alarm is triggered.
Specify the threshold in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE
(see "config admin").
Note: The high temperature threshold (hightemp) minus the temperature tolerance (tolerance)
must be greater than the low temperature threshold (lowtemp) plus the temperature tolerance
(tolerance).

"Card-<shelf>-<slot>"

reset
Syntax
reset {cold | warm} [force]
Values
cold - A cold restart reinitializes the card software and hardware, and is service affecting.
warm - A warm restart re-initializes the card software only, and is not service affecting.
force - optional parameter together with cold.
Performs a restart of the card.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the ports and the card to admin down or admin mt.

100G OT card commands

Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 1955
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
0..10 - temperature tolerance range for °C
0..18 - temperature tolerance range for °F
Default
3 - for °C
5 - for °F
The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword without options to display the current
tolerance. To change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify
the card temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature
that must occur before the alarm is cleared. For example, if the high temperature alarm is
triggered at 55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C, the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to
below 52°C. Similarly, where lowtemp is at 5°C, the alarm is cleared when the card warms to
above 8°C. Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on
the NE (see "config admin").

# config card 130sca1 1/12 reset cold force

reset
Syntax
reset {cold | warm} [force]
Values
cold - A cold restart reinitializes the card software and hardware and is service affecting.
warm - A warm restart re-initializes the card software only and is not service affecting.
force - optional parameter together with cold.
Performs a restart of the card.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the ports and the card to admin down or admin mt.
tolerance
Syntax
tolerance [<degrees>]
Values
{0..10} - temperature tolerance range for °C.
{0..18} - temperature tolerance range for °F.
Default
3 - for °C
5 - for °F
The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword to display the current tolerance. To
change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify the card
temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature that must
occur before the alarm is cleared. For example, if the high temperature alarm is triggered at
55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C, the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to below 52°C.
Similarly, where lowtemp is at 5°C, the alarm is cleared when the card warms to above 8°C.
Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE
(see "config admin").

Main - 1DPP24M with main mode provides 21 E1 access, one line port (STM-1/OC-3) as
the uplink, clock recovery/distribution and grooms total 42 E1 into one STM-1/OC-3.
Extension - 1DPP24M with extension mode provides 21 E1 access, connects with main
mode 1DPP24M in ESSI serial bus through backplane.
Default
main
The Card Mode parameter determines the operational mode of the 1DPP24M. Two card mode
values are supported.

Values

The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword to display the current tolerance. To
change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify the card
temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature that must
occur before the alarm is cleared. For example, if the high temperature alarm is triggered at
55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C, the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to below 52°C.
Similarly, where lowtemp = 5°C, the alarm is cleared when the card warms to above 8°C.
Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE
(see "config admin").
Sub-command: sync0
Configure the timing synchronization attributes. See "config card 1dpp24m <slot-aid> SYNC0".
Note: This cannot be provisioned when syncesupp is disabled.

4.148 config card 1dpp24m <slot-aid> <lineref-aid>
4.148.1 Purpose
This command configures the line timing reference synchronization attributes for 1dpp24m OT.
Use this command to:
• Set the line timing reference priority
• Set the port for the association line timing reference
• Set the admin state of the line timing reference
• Manually configure the line reference incoming QL value
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
4.148.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
4.148.3 Input Format
config card 1dpp24m <slot-aid> <lineref-aid>
admStat
assPort
priority
provql
4.148.4 Input Parameters
<slot-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot> - specific slot in one shelf.
* - reports a list of all controllers in the system.
Specifies the shelf and slot that is reserved for, or contains, the card. Enter the shelf number
followed by a slash and the slot number, or enter a * to display a list of 1dpp24m cards on the
network element by location.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
<lineref-aid>
Values
lineref{0..2} - line timing reference synchronization
Display the line timing reference synchronization type.

admStat
Syntax
admStat [up | down]
Values
{up, down}

up

options below:
assPort
Syntax
assPort [<value>]
Values
C{1..21} - for lineRef0
C{1..21} - for lineRef1
L1 - for lineRef2
Null - no port is associated to the line timing reference
Default
Null
Each line timing reference can be associated to a port. Specifices which port can be assigned
as line timing reference for the system timing entity.
priority
Syntax
priority [<value>]
Values
{0..8} - Range of Priority
0 - disabled the timing reference from the system timing selection process
{1..8} - enabled the timing reference for the system timing selection process
Default
0
Set the priority of a line timing reference for the system timing selection process.
Note:
The priority "0" means that the timing reference is disabled from the selection process.

are unassigned.
Changing the card mode to a different value automatically clears any non-default provisioning
of firmware release (package identifier) and automatically triggers a cold restart of the card to
download the default version of the firmware line corresponding to the new card mode.

lowtemp
Syntax
lowtemp [<degrees>]
Values
-45..90 - temperature range for °C.
-49..194 - temperature range for °F.
Default
-40 - for °C.
-40 - for °F.
The low temperature threshold for the card. Enter this keyword to display the current threshold.
To change the threshold, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify the
temperature below which the low temperature alarm is triggered. Specify the threshold in °C or
°F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE (see "config admin").
Note: The low temperature threshold plus the temperature tolerance must be lower than the
high temperature threshold minus the temperature tolerance.
tolerance
Syntax
tolerance [<degrees>]
Values
0..10 - temperature tolerance range for °C
0..18 - temperature tolerance range for °F
Default
3 - for °C
5 - for °F
The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword without options to display the current
tolerance. To change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify
the card temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature
that must occur before the alarm is cleared. For example, if the high temperature alarm is
triggered at 55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C, the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to
below 52°C. Similarly, where lowtemp is at 5°C, the alarm is cleared when the card warms to
above 8°C. Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on
the NE (see "config admin").

reset
Syntax

Values

force - optional parameter together with cold.

4.160 config card <dsw-card>
4.160.1 Purpose
This command configures card options for distributed switching cards (dsw-card):
• 11QPA4B
• 16P200
• 1UD200
• 1ETY100
• 20P200
• 8P20 as card identifier for the subtypes: 8P20, 8P20B
• D5X500
• D5X500L
• D5X500Q
• S4X400 as card identifier for the subtypes: S4X400H, S4X400L
• S13X100E
• S13X100 as card identifier for the subtypes: S13X100R, S13X100L
• S13X400 as card identifier for the subtypes: S13X400H
Use this command to:
• Specify a name and description for the card
• Set the card mode
• Set the interworking mode (D5X500Q card only)
• Set the linemode (D5X500Q, D5X500, D5X500 cards only)
• Set the card temperature thresholds and tolerance
• Select the backplane clock reference for the card
• Reset the card
• Specify an initial configuration profile ID for a typical service auto setup on card level
Note: If you are preconfiguring the network element, you must configure a slot to accept the <dsw-
card> card before you can configure the card options. See command "config slot <slot-aid> type".
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
4.160.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Temperature threshold values, if set incorrectly, can lead to card overheating and possible
failure. A cold reset is service affecting.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

denied

• If the User attempts to provision a 100GbE client, then this provisioning will be denied

• If the User attempts to provision an OTU4 client, then this provisioning will be denied

be denied.

• If the User attempts to provision an OTU4 client, then this provisioning will be denied
• If the User attempts to provision the backplane ports, then this provisioning will be

provisioning shall be denied.

provisioning shall be denied.

Syntax

Values

tolerance
Syntax
tolerance [<degrees>]
Values
{0..10} - temperature tolerance range for °C.
{0..18} - temperature tolerance range for °F.
Default
3 - for °C
5 - for °F
The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword to display the current tolerance. To
change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify the card
temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature that must
occur before the alarm is cleared. For example, if the high temperature alarm is triggered at
55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C, the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to below 52°C.
Similarly, where lowtemp is at 5°C, the alarm is cleared when the card warms to above 8°C.
Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE
(see "config admin").

4.163 config card <ld-card>
4.163.1 Purpose
This command configures card options for an amplifier or OSCT/OSCTAPR card.
Note on subtype cards:
ASG is used as card identifier for the subtypes: ASG, ASGLP
Use this command to:
• Specify a name and description for the card
• Set the card temperature thresholds and tolerance
• Reset the card
Note: If you are preconfiguring the network element, you must configure a slot to accept a card
before you can configure the card options. See "config slot <slot-aid> type".
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
4.163.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Temperature threshold values, if set incorrectly, can lead to card overheating and possible
failure. A cold reset is service affecting.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

reset
Syntax
reset {cold | warm} [force]
Values
cold - A cold restart reinitializes the card software and hardware, and is service affecting.
warm - A warm restart re-initializes the card software only, and is not service affecting.
force - optional parameter together with cold.
Performs a restart of the card.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the ports and the card to admin down or admin mt.
Restrictions
warm reset is not applicable to OSCTAPR card.

Syntax

Values

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
2062 Issue 1
Default
3 - for °C
5 - for °F
The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword to display the current tolerance. To
change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify the card
temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature that must
occur before the alarm is cleared. For example, if the high temperature alarm is triggered at
55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C, the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to below 52°C.
Similarly, where lowtemp is at 5°C, the alarm is cleared when the card warms to above 8°C.
Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE
(see "config admin").

4.165 config card <ra-card>
4.165.1 Purpose
This command configures card options on:
• RA2P, two-pumps Raman Amplifier
• RA2P-96, two-pumps Raman Amplifier with 96-channel support
• RA4P, four-pumps Raman Amplifier
• RA5P, five-pumps Raman Amplifier
• RA5PB, five-pumps Raman Amplifier with Back-reflection
Use this command to:
• Specify a name and description for the card
• Set the card temperature thresholds and tolerance
• Reset the card
Note: If you are preconfiguring the network element, you must configure a slot to accept a card
before you can configure the card options. See "config slot <slot-aid> type".
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
4.165.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Temperature threshold values, if set incorrectly, can lead to card overheating and possible
failure. A cold reset is service affecting.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
4.165.3 Input Format
config card <ra-card> <slot-aid>

lowtemp
name
reset
tolerance

Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
2074 Issue 1
Values
cold - A cold restart reinitializes the card software and hardware, and is service affecting.
warm - A warm restart re-initializes the card software only, and is not service affecting.
force - optional parameter together with cold.
Performs a restart of the card.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the ports and the card to admin down or admin mt.
tolerance
Syntax
tolerance [<degrees>]
Values
{0..10} - temperature tolerance range for °C
{0..18} - temperature tolerance range for °F
Default
3 - for °C
5 - for °F
The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword to display the current tolerance. To
change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify the card
temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature that must
occur before the alarm is cleared. For example, if the high temperature alarm is triggered at
55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C, the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to below 52°C.
Similarly, where lowtemp is at 5°C, the alarm is cleared when the card warms to above 8°C.
Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE
(see "config admin").

reset
Syntax
reset {cold | warm} [force]
Values
cold - A cold restart reinitializes the card software and hardware and is service affecting.
warm - A warm restart re-initializes the card software only and is not service affecting.
force - optional parameter together with cold.
Performs a restart of the card.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the ports and the card to admin down or admin mt.

Syntax

Values

{0..18} - temperature tolerance range for °F
Default
3 - for °C
5 - for °F
The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword without option to display the current
tolerance. To change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify
the card temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature

2106 Issue 1
The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword without option to display the current
tolerance. To change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify
the card temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature
that must occur before the alarm is cleared. For example, if the high temperature alarm is
triggered at 55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C, the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to
below 52°C. Similarly, where lowtemp is at 5°C, the alarm is cleared when the card warms to
above 8°C. Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on
the NE (see "config admin").

2128 Issue 1
Values
cold - A cold restart reinitializes the card software and hardware and is service affecting.
warm - A warm restart re-initializes the card software only and is not service affecting.
force - optional parameter together with cold.
Performs a restart of the card.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the ports and the card to admin down or admin mt.
tolerance
Syntax
tolerance [<degrees>]
Values
{0..10} - temperature tolerance range for °C
{0..18} - temperature tolerance range for °F
Default
3 - for °C
5 - for °F
The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword to display the current tolerance. To
change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify the card
temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature that must
occur before the alarm is cleared. For example, if the high temperature alarm is triggered at
55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C, the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to below 52°C.
Similarly, where lowtemp is at 5°C, the alarm is cleared when the card warms to above 8°C.
Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE
(see "config admin").

4.179 config card <vac-card>
4.179.1 Purpose
This command configures the card options on:
• MVAC as card identifier for MVAC, MVACF - Multiple Variable Attenuator card, Multiple Variable
Attenuator card Flex
• MVAC8B - Multiple Variable Attenuator card 8-Port Bidirectional
• SVAC - Single Variable Attenuator card
Use this command to:
• Specify a name and description for the card
• Set the card temperature thresholds and tolerance
• Reset the card
Note: If you are preconfiguring the network element, you must configure a slot to accept a card
before you can configure the card options. See "config slot <slot-aid> type".
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

failure. A cold reset is service affecting.

4.183 config card <sfd-sfc-card>
4.183.1 Purpose
This command configures card options for SFDs and SFCs.
Use this command to:
• Specify a name and description for the card
• Configure one fiber mux or two fiber mode for SFC cards
SFC2 includes SFC2A - SFC2D
SFC4 includes SFC4A, SFC4B
SFC8 includes SFC8 only
SFD5 includes SFD5A - SFD5H
SFD8 includes SFD8A - SFD8D
SFD2 includes SFD2A - SFD2R
SFD4 includes SFD4A - SFD4H

Syntax
reset {cold | warm} [force]
Values

warm - A warm restart re-initializes the card software only, and is not service affecting.
force - optional parameter together with cold.
Performs a restart of the card.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the ports and the card to admin down or admin mt.

The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword to display the current tolerance. To
change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify the card
temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature that must
occur before the alarm is cleared. For example, if the high temperature alarm is triggered at
55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C, the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to below 52°C.
Similarly, where lowtemp is at 5°C, the alarm is cleared when the card warms to above 8°C.
Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE
(see "config admin").

4.189.1 Purpose
This command configures card options for a WR20-TF, WR20-TFM or WR20TFML wavelength
router card.
Use this command to:
• Specify a name and description for the card

<slot-aid> type").

4.194 config card <ops-card>
4.194.1 Purpose
This command configures card options for OPS protection switch card types:
• OPSA
• OPSFLEX
• OPSB
• OPSB5
• OPSUM
• OPSUML
Use this command to:
• Specify a name and description for the card.
• Set the card temperature thresholds and tolerance
• Reset the card
• Set the protection mode (OPSA only)
Note: If you are preconfiguring the network element, you must configure a slot to accept an OPS
card before you can configure the card options (See "config slot <slot-aid> type").
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
4.194.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Temperature threshold values, if set incorrectly, can lead to card overheating and possible
failure. A cold reset is service affecting.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

2188 Issue 1
hightemp
Syntax
hightemp [<degrees>]
Values
-5..90 - temperature range for °C
23..194 - temperature range for °F
Default
90 - for °C
194 - for °F
The high temperature threshold for the card. Enter this keyword to display the current threshold.
To change the threshold, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify the
temperature above which the high temperature alarm is triggered. Specify the threshold in °C or
°F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE (see "config admin").
Note: The high temperature threshold minus the temperature tolerance must be greater than
the low temperature threshold plus the temperature tolerance.
lowtemp
Syntax
lowtemp [<degrees>]
Values
-5..90 - temperature range for °C.
23..194 - temperature range for °F.
Default
-5 - for °C.
23 - for °F.
The low temperature threshold for the card. Enter this keyword to display the current threshold.
To change the threshold, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify the
temperature below which the low temperature alarm is triggered. Specify the threshold in °C or
°F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE (see "config admin").
Note: The low temperature threshold plus the temperature tolerance must be lower than the
high temperature threshold minus the temperature tolerance.

Syntax
name [<string>]

Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 2189
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
<string> - ASCII string {1..31} characters
"" - to clear the name
Default
"Card-<shelf>-<slot>"
Specifies a name for the card. Enter this keyword without options to display the current name.
To change the name, enter this keyword followed by a character string that provides the name
of the card. If the name contains spaces, use quotes around the text.
reset
Syntax
reset {cold | warm} [force]
Values
cold - A cold restart reinitializes the card software and hardware and is service affecting.
warm - A warm restart re-initializes the card software only and is not service affecting.
force - optional parameter together with cold.
Performs a restart of the card.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the ports and the card to admin down or admin mt.
tolerance
Syntax
tolerance [<degrees>]
Values
0..10 - temperature tolerance range for °C
0..18 - temperature tolerance range for °F
Default
3 - for °C
5 - for °F
The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword to display the current tolerance. To
change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify the card
temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature that must
occur before the alarm is cleared.
For example, if the high temperature alarm is triggered at 55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C,
the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to below 52°C. Similarly, where lowtemp = 5°C, the
alarm is cleared when the card warms to above 8°C.
Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE
(see "config admin").

4.199 config card <mcs-card>
4.199.1 Purpose
This command configures card options for MCS card types:
• Multi-cast Switch 8x16 (MCS8-16)
• Multi-cast Switch 8x16 L - Band (MCS8-16L)
• Multi-cast Switch 16x15 (MCS1615)
• Multi-cast Switch 16x15 L - Band (MCS1615L)
Use this command to:
• Specify a name and description for the card
• Set the channel count limit
• Set the card temperature thresholds and tolerance
• Reset the card
Note: If you are preconfiguring the network element, you must configure a slot to accept an MCS
type card before you can configure the card options. See "config slot <slot-aid> type".
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
4.199.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Temperature threshold values, if set incorrectly, can lead to card overheating and possible
failure. A cold reset is service affecting.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

Syntax
gain [<value>]
Values

Default
18.00 dB
Specifies the amplifier gain. Enter this keyword without arguments to display the current gain
setting, or with a valid value to change the gain setting for the amplifier.
The provisioned gain value is only used on optical lines using manual power management.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingain <= gain <= maxgain + deltamaxgain.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingain, maxgain, or deltamaxgain, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
2228 Issue 1
Values
0..10 - temperature tolerance range for °C
0..18 - temperature tolerance range for °F
Default
3 - for °C
5 - for °F
The temperature tolerance for card. Enter this keyword to display the current tolerance. To
change the tolerance, enter this keyword followed by an integer value to specify the card
temperature tolerance. The temperature tolerance defines the change in temperature that must
occur before the alarm is cleared.
For example, if the high temperature alarm is triggered at 55°C and the tolerance is set to 3°C,
the alarm is not cleared until the card cools to below 52°C. Similarly, where lowtemp = 5°C, the
alarm is cleared when the card warms to above 8°C.
Specify the tolerance in °C or °F, depending on the temperature units configured on the NE
(see "config admin").

Redundancy commands
4.218 config redundancy
4.218.1 Purpose
This command configures the redundant equipment and functions.
Use this command to:
• Display the current NE database synchronization status and redundant equipment and functions
activity states.
• Switch between the active and inactive cards of a particular type.
• Switches the WT clock reference for all the cards in the shelf.
• Switches between the active and inactive redundant CRU in the specified shelf.
• Set the working and protection of the redundant F-CRU in the shelf.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
The term "CSW shelf" (centrally switched shelf) has been defined to reference a set of shelf types
comprising of:
• PSS-8x
• PSS-12x
• PSS-24x
Note: This command is not applicable to PSS-4II shelf.
4.218.2 Command Access Level
Impact: An activity switch may result in unsynchronized databases.

4.219 config redundancy fabric
4.219.1 Purpose
This command configures the redundancy of fabric cards in centrally switched (CSW) shelves.
Use this command to:
• Display the current status of the fabric cards within a central switching shelf (e.g. PSS-8x, -12x,
-24x)
• Lockout one fabric card from the related equipment protection group (if supported)
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
Restriction:
The lockout mechanism (i.e. this command) is only supported by established equipment protection
groups. OTN switch fabrics are only provisioned if the corresponding shelfmode parameter value is
set accordingly; the switch fabric type is determined by that value. The command will be rejected for
non-existing switch fabric groups. Use the config shelf command to set the shelfmode parameter
appropriately.
Extended restriction for 48T switching fabrics (coupled PSS-24x shelf pair):
The lockout command can only be successfully applied to the primary shelf and configures the
switch fabrics in the primary and secondary shelf at the same time. For a secondary shelf, this
command gets rejected. In this case, use the command "show shelf" with the current shelf number
to obtain the shelf number from the related primary shelf.
The term "CSW shelf" (centrally switched shelf) refers to a set of shelf types with central switch
fabric cards. Following shelves are concerned:
• PSS-8x
• PSS-12x
• PSS-24x
4.219.2 Command Access Level
Impact: A lockout of a switch fabric enforces the use of the remaining cards. If those are partially
failed (fabric time slot or fabric backplane link damaged) then this will impair the associated
transmission signal (probably in both the payload and the overhead transportation). If one of the
remaining cards becomes unavailable (removed or powered-off or card type mismatch) then the
equipment protection group will temporarily ignore the lockout command in order restore the
complete traffic outage (best effort).
In case of a coupled PSS-24x shelf pair (48T switching capacity), the statements above apply for
both involved shelves. Note that mentioned failures could only be present in the secondary shelf
while the parameter use of "detail" will only show the failure states from one (e.g. the primary) shelf.
Therefore it is recommended to use the "show redundancy fabric" command before applying a
lockout to not run into the described scenario with partially failed fabrics (that may cause some
traffic outage). Also in respect of the aspect that lockout gets ignored upon a complete card failure,
this applies to any remaining switching fabric in both involved shelves (e.g. if one remaining fabric
in the secondary shelf fails then the lockout is ignored in both shelves).
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

Redundancy commands

4.219.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
<shelf-aid> - target shelf
Enter the shelf number of a switching shelf with fabric cards to configure the fabric protection
group.
lockout
Syntax
lockout [<value>]
Values
{SWC1, SWC2, SWC3} - specified switch card to be locked out (all CSW shelves)
clear - removes the lockout for the fabric protection group (all CSW shelves)
Default
clear
Performs a lockout of the specified OTN fabric from the equipment protection. In case of a
coupled PSS-24x shelf pair (48T switching capacity), the lockout command will be executed in
both, the primary and the secondary shelf.
Enter the keyword without a fabric value to display the current parameter setting.
Enter the keyword with a specific fabric value to exclude the related card from transmission and
overhead transportation. The EPS LED will go off once succeeded. In case of coupled PSS-24x
shelf pair, the EPS LED of the referring SWC in both shelves will go off.
Enter the keyword with the value clear to re-enable all fabrics for transmission and overhead
transportation. It depends whether there is a need to restore transmission/overhead
immediately after the clear, whether the fabric (that was formerly locked out) will be used
immediately or not. If so the EPS LED will indicate green (InUse), if not the EPS LED will
indicate amber (NotInUse). In case of coupled PSS-24x shelf pair, the EPS LED status will be
re-evaluated in each of the involved shelves individually.
Note that before a different fabric can be locked out, a present lockout must be cleared.
Restrictions
In case of a 48T configuration (two coupled PSS-24x shelves), the command will be
rejected if addressed against the secondary shelf with the following error message:
"This command can only be executed for the primary shelf if used in a 48T configurations"

4.220 show redundancy
4.220.1 Purpose
The command displays the status of redundant equipment and functions. It indicates whether
standby equipment/function is ready to take over the active role.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
The term "CSW shelf" (centrally switched shelf) refers to a set of shelf types with central switch
fabric cards. Following shelves are concerned:
• PSS-8x
• PSS-12x
• PSS-24x
Displayed card types relate to programmed card types. For switch fabric cards in CSW shelves will
display the present card type in addition.
In case of a coupled PSS-24x shelf pair (48T switching capacity), the command displays only the
status of the addressed shelf (primary or secondary). Use the command "show shelf" with the
current shelf number to obtain the other shelf number being involved in the paired setup.
Note: This command is not applicable to PSS-4II shelf.
4.220.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer.

show redundancy [<shelf-aid>]
clkswitch
cruswitch
detail
fabric
workingcru
4.220.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
<shelf-aid> - target shelf.
It specifies a specific shelf or if omitted it displays a list of all redundant equipment and
functions in the system.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.

Inventory commands
4.221 config shelf inventory
4.221.1 Purpose
This command allows to configure inventory data for universal shelves, which do not support an
electronic shelf inventory label.
Use this command to:
• set the CLEI code of the shelf
• set the part number of the shelf
• set the serial number of the shelf
This command applies to the following 1830 PSS shelf types:
• PSS-32
• PSS-16
• PSS-16II
• PSS-8
4.221.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
4.221.3 Input Format
config shelf inventory <shelf-aid>
cleicode
detail
partnumber
serialnumber
4.221.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
1..24 - Specifies the shelf
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf address identifier.

4.222 show card inventory
4.222.1 Purpose
This command displays remote inventory information for a specific card, or for all cards in a shelf,
or for all cards on the network element.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf type applicability of the card.
4.222.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
4.222.3 Input Format
show card inventory <slot-aid>
4.222.4 Input Parameters
<slot-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot> - address a single card.
<shelf>/* - address all cards in one shelf.
* - address all cards in the node.
Default
Entry required
Specifies the location of the card you want to query. Enter the shelf number followed by a slash
and the slot number. Or enter the shelf number followed by a slash and a * to display a list of all
cards in one shelf. Or enter a * to display a list of all cards on the network element. See
Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric values of <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type. When a specific <shelf>/<slot> is entered, a full detail, multi-line report will
be displayed. If a wildcard retrieve is requested, then a single-line per card report will be
displayed.
4.222.5 Output Parameters

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
4.223 show interface inventory
4.223.1 Purpose
This command displays the remote inventory information for a SFP/XFP/CFP/.. pluggable module
in a port on a card, or for all ports on a card, or for all ports on a shelf, or for all ports on the network
element.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf type applicability of the card.
4.223.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
4.223.3 Input Format
show interface inventory <port-aid>
4.223.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/<port> - address a single port.
<shelf>/<slot>/* - address all port of a single card.
<shelf>/* - address all port of one shelf.
* - address all ports in the node.
Default
Entry required
Specifies the location of the port you want to query.
Enter the shelf number followed by a slash and the slot number followed by a slash and the port
number to display the details of the addressed pluggable port.
Or enter the shelf number followed by a slash and the slot number followed by a slash and a *
to display a list of all pluggable ports in one shelf.
Or enter the shelf number followed by a slash and a * to display a list of all pluggable ports in
one shelf.
Or enter a * to display a list of all pluggable ports on the network element.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric values of <shelf>, <slot> and <port>
ranges for each supported shelf type and card.
When a specific <shelf>/<slot>/<port> is entered, a full detail, multi-line report will be displayed.
If a wildcard retrieve is requested then a single-line per port report will be displayed.
Equipment management commands
Inventory commands
show interface inventory
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
2314 Issue 1
Restrictions
Single sub-ports do not report inventory data (for example C2_3). When a single sub-port is
addressed the command is denied.
4.223.5 Output Parameters
Table 4-29 Pluggable Module Inventory Output Parameters
Label Description
Module Vendor Company Vendor: NOK or COTS
Module Type Nokia module name of the present module.
CLEI Code CLEI code from present module inventory.
Unit Part Number Part number from present module inventory.
Software Part Number Software part number from present module inventory.
Factory Identifier Factory manufacture identifier from present module inventory.
Module Vendor Serial Num Serial number from present module inventory.
Date Date of manufacture from present module inventory.
Maximum Case Temperature Max Case Temp from present module inventory.
Frequency Optical Frequency / wavelength from present module inventory
IM/ICS Interchange Marking or Item Change Status from the present module inventory.
Acronym Code Nokia Acronym Code from the present module inventory.
Extra Data Additional collected data from present module. In the current release all "-".
Firmware Revision Firmware Revision from the present module inventory.
Power Class Power Class from the present module inventory.
Power Class Information
On pluggable modules supporting power class reporting from the inventory, the stored power class
of the present module will be reported. The power class can have values from 1 to 8 and the values
correspond to defined power consumption values. In case of power class 8 the stored maximum
power consumption value will be added: 8/12.5.

2318 Issue 1
4.224 show shelf inventory
4.224.1 Purpose
This command displays the remote inventory information for a specific shelf or for all shelves on the
network element.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
The following shelf types support an electronic inventory label and can report it for any present
shelf: PSS-4, PSS-4II, PSS-12x, PSS-24x, PSS-8x, PSI-4L and PSI-8L
For the following shelf types an electronic inventory label is not available, and the information can
be reported only, after it was manually entered via command "config shelf inventory": PSS-32, PSS-
16, PSS-16II, PSS-8.
4.224.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
4.224.3 Input Format
show shelf inventory <shelf-aid>
4.224.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
{1..8} - Specifies the PSS-4 or PSS-4II shelf
{1..24} - Specifies the shelf
{1..31} - Specifies the PSI-4L, PSI-8L shelves
* - displays a list of all shelves
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf. Enter the shelf address identifier or enter a * to display a list of all shelves
on the network element.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf-aid> ranges for each supported
shelf type.
4.224.5 Output Parameters
Shelf External Inventory Data Output Parameters
Label Description
Vendor Company long name for the present shelf
Equipment management commands
Inventory commands

Amplifier common commands
5.2 config interface <card> <oscsfp-port-aid>
5.2.1 Purpose
This command configures the optical supervisory channel (OSC) small form factor pluggable (SFP)
interface port.
Use this command to:
• Display the current settings for the port
• Configure the description
• Configure the LCP parameters
• Configure the port mode
• Configure the OSC functionality
• Configure the state of PPP on the port
• Configure the state of the port
• Configure PM for the port
• Configure OSPF and OSPFv3 parameters
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.2.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
5.2.3 Input Format
config interface <card> <oscsfp-port-aid>
description
detail
lcp-echo-failure
lcp-echo-interval
mode
ospf
ospf3
ots [moduletype | oscmtu]
pm
ppp-state
routestate

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
1..600
Default
3
Specifies the number of times an NE repeats an LCP echo request to its peer on the PPP link.
The definition below for "lcp-echo-interval" describes how an NE uses these two "lcp-echo"
parameters to determine that the PPP link on the OSC has failed.
lcp-echo-interval
Syntax
lcp-echo-interval [<value>]
Values
1..600 - time in seconds
Default
3 seconds
Specifies the number of seconds a Network Element (NE) waits to receive an echo response.
The NE sends an LCP echo request to its peer on the PPP link every "lcp-echo-interval"
seconds. Whenever the NE does not receive a response within this time, the NE increments a
counter. If the counter reaches the value specified by "lcp-echo-failure" (see format of this
parameter above), then the PPP protocol terminates the connection and attempts to establish a
new connection.
Note that the counter is reset to zero whenever a response is received.
mode
Syntax

Values
100BASEFX - set the port to carry a 100BaseFX signal
OC3 - set the port to carry an OC-3 signal
STM1 - set the port to carry an STM-1 signal
Default
OC3 if ANSI
STM1 if ETSI
Specifies the port mode.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
• Set to enabled to enable PPP on the OSCSFP interface, in which case the interface will
carry IP traffic.
• Set to disabled to disable PPP on the OSCSFP interface, in which case the interface
will not carry IP traffic. The OSC, however, will still carry CUSTLAN traffic.
Note that an OSC has both DCN traffic through the OSCSFP, and CUSTLAN traffic (if there is a
CUSTLAN port). This parameter has no effect on CUSTLAN traffic. Use the command 'config
interface <card> <custlan-port>' to enable/disable the CUSTLAN port only. The 'state'
parameter (below) controls whether the OSC is up or down, and when down, no traffic (IP or
CUSTLAN) is carried on the OSC.
Enter this parameter without a value to display the current setting.
routestate
Syntax
routestate [<value>]
Values
disabled - disable OSPF on the interface
enabled - enable OSPF on the interface
redistribute - distribute the neighbor address into OSPF, but do not enable OSPF
Default
enabled
Set the OSPF routing state of the OSCSFP interface. Enter this keyword without a parameter to
display the current OSPF routing state.
• Set to enabled to enable OSPF routing on the OSCSFP interface. OSPF attempts to
form adjacencies with other devices and distributes the neighbor IP address and mask
into OSPF.
• Set to disabled to disable OSPF routing on the OSCSFP interface. The neighbor IP
address and mask are not distributed into OSPF.
• Set to redistribute to distribute the neighbor IP address and mask into OSPF, but do not
form an adjacency. Also called Passive mode, the NE treats the interface as a network
outside its autonomous system. Since the OSCSFP is a PPP connection utilizing
loopbacks, the neighbor's loopback address will distributed into OSPF.
route6state
Syntax
route6state [<value>]
Values
disabled - disable OSPFv3 on the interface
enabled - enable OSPFv3 on the interface
redistribute - distribute the neighbor address into OSPFv3, but do not enable OSPFv3

Release 24.12
December 2024
2360 Issue 1
Default
enabled if the IPv6 address of the primary loopback is non-zero (i.e., is not ::/0)
disabled if the IPv6 address of the primary loopback is zero (i.e., is ::/0)
Set the OSPFv3 routing state of the interface. Enter this keyword without any parameters to
display the current OSPFv3 routing state.
• Set to enabled to enable OSPFv3 routing on the OSCSFP interface. OSPFv3 attempts
to form adjacencies with the neighbor NE on the OSCSFP, and the OSCSFP interface is
distributed to other network elements via OSPFv3.
• Set to disabled to disable OSPFv3 routing OSCSFP interface. The interface is not
distributed to other network elements via OSPFv3.
• Set to redistribute to redistribute this interface into OSPFv3, but do not form
adjacencies with the neighbor NE. Also called Passive mode, the NE treats the port as a
network outside its autonomous system. Since the OSCSFP is a PPP connection
utilizing loopbacks, the neighbor's loopback address will distributed into OSPF.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See "config interface <card> <port-aid> state"
with the specific <card> type for additional details on the state parameter.
Note that when administrative state is set to down, no traffic is carried on the OSC or the
CUSTLAN (if it exists).

Specifies the port type.

5.3 show interface <card> <osc-port-aid> detail
5.3.1 Purpose
This command displays summary of all service activity on the interface port.
Use this command to:
• Display the current settings for OSC/OSCSFP port.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
Note: IPv6 and OSPFv3 are not available on PSS-4 shelf.
IPv6 and OSPFv3 are not available on the PSS-16 and PSS-32 shelf with equipment controller type
"EC", i.e., classic EC.
5.3.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.3.3 Input Format
show interface <card> <osc-port-aid> detail

5.3.5 Output Parameters
Table 5-1 Generic, Status and other Parameters:
Output Parameter Description
Admin State Administrative state of the interface: Up, Down or MT
Oper State Operational state of the interface: Up or Down
Note that if the Admin State and/or Oper State is Down, the interface will not carry IP
traffic nor will there be CUSTLAN traffic on this OSC/OSCSFP (if the card has a
CUSTLAN interface).
State Qualifier The State Qualifier for the card with this interface
Oper Capability Operational capability of the card
Values: Enabled, Disabled, Partially Enabled
Module Type The pluggable module type used for the interface
OSC Mode Indicates whether the OSC is operating in OC3, STM1, or 100BASEFX mode. May not
be present, in which case it is OC3.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Table 5-1 Generic, Status and other Parameters: (continued)
Output Parameter Description
Extended Temperature Range This parameter specifies the extended temperature range settings for the port.
Applicable to EILA, EILAL, IRDM32, IRDM32L, OMDCL.
OSC SFP Module Temperature Temperature reported by the SFP module.
Not available for all cards.
Supvy Received power Optical power received by the OSCSFP receiver. Applicable for ASG subtypes, ASWG,
ASWG-L, AWBILA, AWBING, EILA, EILAL, IPREAMP, IR9 subtypes, IR20 subtypes,
IRDM20, IRDM32 subtypes, IRDM32L, IROADM9R and OMDCL.
Supvy Transmitted power Optical power transmitted by the OSCSFP transmitter. Applicable for ASG subtypes,
ASWG, ASWG-L, AWBILA, AWBING, EILA, EILAL, IPREAMP, IR9 subtypes, IR20
subtypes, IRDM20, IRDM32 subtypes, IRDM32L, IROADM9R and OMDCL.
Description A description for the interface
PPP State This parameter is the state of the PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol) on the interface. Either
enabled or disabled. If disabled the interface will not carry IP traffic. Note that the
CUSTLAN will still carry traffic if PPP is disabled.
LCP echo failure This parameter specifies the number of times an NE repeats an LCP echo request to
its peer on the PPP link. The definition below for "LCP echo interval" describes how an
NE uses these two "LCP echo" parameters to determine that the PPP link on the ECC
has failed.
LCP echo interval This parameter specifies the number of seconds a Network Element (NE) waits to
receive an echo response. The NE sends an LCP echo request to its peer on the PPP
link every "LCP echo interval" seconds. Whenever the NE does not receive a response
within this time, the NE increments a counter. If the counter reaches the value specified
by "LCP echo failure", then the PPP protocol terminates the connection and attempts to
establish a new connection.
Note that the counter is reset to zero whenever a response is received.
OSC Config MTU Size Configured Maximum Transmission Unit size, in units of bytes
OSC Actual MTU Size Actual (negotiated) Maximum Transmission Unit size, in units of bytes. "-" will be
displayed if the MTU size has not yet been negotiated.
IPv6 Link Local Address IPV6 link local address of this Network Element
Table 5-2 OSPF Parameters:
Output Parameter Description
OSPF Routing Administrative state of OSPF Routing;
Enabled, Disabled, or Redistribute.
Redistribute (or passive) means that the IP address is redistributed into OSPF, but the
interface does not participate in OSPF.
OSPF Adj State OSPF Adjacency state: FULL or Down
In rare instances, an intermediate state may be observed, e.g., 2Way, Exchange,
ExchangeStart, or Init. Consistent display of an intermediate state may indicate
problems with OSPF convergence.

2366 Issue 1
Table 5-2 OSPF Parameters: (continued)
Output Parameter Description
OSPF Neighbor IP Address IPv4 loopback address of the neighboring Network Element.
Dependency on link conditions:
• Displays dashes if the Admin State is down
• Displays last known neighbor if the OSPF Adjacency state is not FULL
OSPF Neighbor Router ID Unique identifier of the OSPFv2 neighbor router. Router ID is a four-byte parameter
expressed using the same dotted decimal format as an IPv4 address.
OSPFv2 Router ID is usually the IPv4 loopback address of the neighbor.
Dependency on link conditions:
• Displays dashes if the Admin State is down
• Displays last known neighbor if the OSPF Adjacency state is not FULL
OSPF Area Index OSPF Area Index
OSPF Area ID OSPF Area ID associated with the OSPF Area Index
OSPF Hello Interval OSPF Hello interval specifies how often (in seconds) a Hello packet is sent out on the
interface. Hello packets are used to establish and maintain relationships with
neighboring network elements.
OSPF RtrDeadInterval OSPF Router Dead Interval Router Interface. This is the time elapsed between not
hearing a router's Hello PDU before the interface OSPF state is declared down. The
dead interval is a timer used to timeout inactive adjacencies.
OSPF Metric OSPF Metric or Cost of the interface. The lower the cost, the more preferred the
interface is for the routing of packets.
OSPF Retransmit Interval OSPF Retransmit Interval, which is the length of time, in seconds, that OSPF will wait
before retransmitting an unacknowledged link state advertisement (LSA) to an OSPF
neighbor.
OSPF MD5 Status Specifies if OSPF MD5 authentication is enabled or disabled on the interface.
OSPF MD5 Key MD5 Key used for OSPF MD5 128 bit hash value key calculation on the interface.
OSPF MD5 KeyId MD5 Key ID used for OSPF MD5 128 bit hash value key calculation on the interface.
Table 5-3 OSPFv3 Parameters:
Output Parameter Description
OSFPFv3 Routing Administrative state of OSPFv3 Routing;
Enabled, Disabled, or Redistribute.
Redistribute (or passive) means that the IP address is redistributed into OSPF, but the
interface does not participate in OSPF.
OSPFv3 Adj State OSPF Adjacency state: FULL or Down
In rare instances, an intermediate state may be observed, e.g., 2Way, Exchange,
ExchangeStart, or Init. Consistent display of an intermediate state may indicate
problems with OSPF convergence.

This command displays summary information about the flexible grid capabilities of the degree,
viewed at the outside fiber plant facing amplifier card(s).
Use this command to:
• Display a table of list of the flexible grid capabilities of the optical degree.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

2384 Issue 1
5.5 show interface <card-type> <port-aid> controlpwr
5.5.1 Purpose
Displays the target power and measured power for controlled channels, including user defined XCs
and internal line loading ASE channels if exist.
Note:
It is possible to see MC with width 0 GHz in controlpwr command if the MC is a thru/mesh XC or a
drop XC with auto keyed or auto unkeyed type. Width 0 GHz can happen for them if they have not
received the Link State Advertisement from head end node yet. Once the information has been
received, user can run controlpwr command again and see the updated width and PSD data.
Use this command to:
• Display the table of channelized power levels at a port.
• Display a single provisioned channel's channelized power level at a port.
• Display only rows of the table of channels power levels at a port corresponding to provisioned
channels.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.5.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.5.3 Input Format
show interface <card-type> <port-aid> controlpwr
<frequency>
channels

Default

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
lcp-echo-failure
Syntax
lcp-echo-failure [<value>]
Values
1..600
Default
3
Specifies the number of times an NE repeats an LCP echo request to its peer on the PPP link.
The definition below for "lcp-echo-interval" describes how an NE uses these two "lcp-echo"
parameters to determine that the PPP link on the OSC has failed.
lcp-echo-interval
Syntax
lcp-echo-interval [<value>]
Values
1..600 - time in seconds
Default
3 seconds
Specifies the number of seconds a Network Element (NE) waits to receive an echo response.
The NE sends an LCP echo request to its peer on the PPP link every "lcp-echo-interval"
seconds. Whenever the NE does not receive a response within this time, the NE increments a
counter. If the counter reaches the value specified by "lcp-echo-failure" (see format of this
parameter above), then the PPP protocol terminates the connection and attempts to establish a
new connection.
Note that the counter is reset to zero whenever a response is received.
mode
Syntax
mode [<value>]
Values
100BASEFX - set the port to carry a 100baseFX signal
OC3 - set the port to carry an OC-3 signal
STM1 - set the port to carry an STM-1 signal
Default
OC3 if ANSI
STM1 if ETSI
Specifies the port mode for the OSC interface port.

Sub-command: pm
Display or clear performance monitoring information for a specific interface. See "config

routestate
Syntax
routestate [<value>]
Values
disabled
enabled
redistribute
Default
enabled
Set the OSPF routing state of the OSC interface. Enter this keyword without a parameter to
display the current OSPF routing state.
• Set to enabled to enable OSPF routing on the OSC interface. OSPF attempts to form
adjacencies with other devices and distributes the neighbor IP address and mask into
OSPF.
• Set to disabled to disable OSPF routing on the OSC interface. The neighbor IP address
and mask are not distributed into OSPF.
• Set to redistribute to distribute the neighbor IP address and mask into OSPF, but do not
form an adjacency. Also called Passive mode, the NE treats the interface as a network
outside its autonomous system.
route6state
Syntax
route6state [<value>]
Values
enabled
disabled
redistribute

2410 Issue 1
Default
enabled if the IPv6 address of the primary loopback is non-zero (i.e., is not ::/0)
disabled if the IPv6 address of the primary loopback is zero (i.e., is ::/0)
Set the OSPFv3 routing state of the interfae. Enter this keyword without any parameters to
display the current OSPFv3 routing state.
• Set to enabled to enable OSPFv3 routing on the OSC interface. OSPFv3 attempts to
form adjacencies with the neighbor NE on the OSC, and the OSC interface is distributed
to other network elements via OSPFv3.
• Set to disabled to disable OSPFv3 routing OSC interface. The interface is not
distributed to other network elements via OSPFv3.
• Set to redistribute to redistribute this interface into OSPFv3, but do not form
adjacencies with the neighbor NE. Also called Passive mode, the NE treats the port as a
network outside its autonomous system, and distributes this network to other network
elements via OSPFv3.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Default
enabled
Configures pulsing of the EDFA amplifier, while "APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is enabled, the EDFA will pulse between its on and off states, while
"APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is disabled, the EDFA will shutdown, when "APR Active - Line" is
reported.
An attempt to enable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Enabling EDFA pulsing will allow for APR auto recovery in spans with Raman
amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shutdown the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is reported
for this port. This might not allow automatic APR recovery for spans with Raman amplifiers. Do
you want to proceed?
Restrictions
This parameter applies to LD cards at ILAs and to egress LD cards at DGEs and add/drop
nodes. Attempts to enable or disable EDFA pulsing at an LD that is not at an ILA or is not
an egress LD will be denied.
This parameter is not applicable if APR is disabled.
aprenabled
Syntax

Values
enabled - The optical amplifier will shut down if the fiber span has been cut, and cannot
restart until the span has been repaired.
disabled - If the LD is used in an ILA or as an egress LD in an add/drop node, the amplifier
can start up and remain on even if the fiber span has been cut.
Default
enabled
Specifies whether APR is enabled or disabled for an egress LD in an add/drop node, or for an
LD in an ILA. Set APR to disabled, if the span is operated without an optical supervisory
channel.

aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [<value>]
Values
auto
force
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before this command can be carried out.
auto - automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier, and will have an
impact on service. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the optical amplifier to restart
automatically. Do you want to proceed?
This parameter only applies to ALPHG, AHPHG, AHPLG and A2325A packs.

Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 2495
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Default
off
Specifies the per channel target input power, used by auto power management. Note that if
MVAC8B/MVACF services are added to the degree the add amplifier connects to (where no
such services existed previously), the targetpower will be set to minimum (targetpower, -22)
dBm to provide a good initial value. If the value is "off" when the first MVAC8B/MVACF service
is added to the degree the add amplifier connects to, the targetpower will be set to -22 dBm.
When the value is "off" it is not used by auto power management in calculating the add
amplifier target input power.
See "show interface <aar-card> <ampin-port-aid>" for related parameter targetpoweractive,
which displays the target presently in use.
Restrictions
This parameter only applies to ports AMPIN{5..8}.
If the user sets the value from a numerical value to "off", the user must confirm the change
before it is implemented. The value is not reset to "off" automatically when the last OCh
using the amplifier is deleted.
5.45.5 Examples
For the output example of the "detail" parameter, refer to the "show interface <aar-card> <ampin-
port-aid>" command.

Sub-command: asemode
Syntax
asemode [cancel | power [<value>]]
Values
-5..10 - power in dBm
Default

Accesses testing functionality on the port.

on the port.
• Enter asemode to turn the amplifier on in ASE output power mode.
• Enter asemode cancel to cancel ASE output power mode and return to normal mode.
• Enter asemode power followed by a value to set the output power level that will be
used in ASE output power mode.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
targetpower
Syntax
targetpower [<value>]
Values
-24.5..-16.0 - power in dBm
off
Default
off
Specifies the per channel target input power, used by auto power management. Note that if
MVAC8B/MVACF services are added to the degree the add amplifier connects to (where no
such services existed previously), the targetpower will be set to minimum (targetpower, -22)
dBm to provide a good initial value. If the value is "off" when the first MVAC8B/MVACF service
is added to the degree the add amplifier connects to, the targetpower will be set to -22 dBm.
When the value is "off" it is not used by auto power management in calculating the add
amplifier target input power. See "show interface <aar2x-card> <ampin-port-aid>" for related
parameter targetpoweractive, which displays the target presently in use.
Restrictions
This parameter only applies to ports AMPIN{5A..8A}, and AMPIN{5B..8B}.
Setting the parameter on the A port also sets the same value on the corresponding B port,
and vice versa.
If the user sets the value from a numerical value to "off", the user must confirm the change
before it is implemented. The value is not reset to "off" automatically when the last OCh
using the amplifier is deleted.
5.56.5 Examples
For the output example for the "detail" parameter, refer to the "show interface <aar2x-card>
<ampin-port-aid>" command.
# config interface aar2x8a 1/5/ampin2 description
Interface Description: input port
# config interface aar2x8a 1/3/ampin8a targetpower -20.0

asemode

Values

apredfapulse
Syntax
apredfapulse [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - enables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
disabled - disables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
Default
enabled
Configures pulsing of the EDFA amplifier, while "APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is enabled, the EDFA will pulse between its on and off states, while
"APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is disabled, the EDFA will shutdown, when "APR Active - Line" is
reported.
An attempt to enable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Enabling EDFA pulsing will allow for APR auto recovery in spans with Raman
amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shutdown the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is reported

for this port. This might not allow automatic APR recovery for spans with Raman amplifiers. Do

Restrictions
This parameter applies to LD cards at ILAs and to egress LD cards at DGEs and add/drop

aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [<value>]
Values
auto
force
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before this command can be carried out.
auto - automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier, and will have an
impact on service. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the optical amplifier to restart
automatically. Do you want to proceed?
deltamaxgain
Syntax
deltamaxgain [<value>]
Values
0..5 - gain in dB
Specifies the maximum allowed difference between the provisioned gain and the measured
gain before an alarm is raised.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingain <= gain <= maxgain + deltamaxgain.

losmode
Syntax
losmode [<value>]
Values
{auto,losn}
Default
auto
Sets the behavior of the amplifier when the input optical signal to the amplifier is in Loss of
Signal state.
If used in an Add/Drop configuration, the default will be set to LOSN and APRholdoff timer will
be set to 250ms default.
When configured to value auto the LD will take on the normal shutdown behavior for the LD.
When configured to value losn the LD will not shut off when the input optical signal is in LOS.
maxgain
Syntax
maxgain [<value>]
Values
26..40 - gain in dB
Default
26.00 dB
Specifies the maximum amplifier gain. Enter this keyword without arguments to display the
current gain setting, or with a valid value to change the gain setting for the amplifier.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingain <= gain <= maxgain + deltamaxgain.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingain, maxgain, or deltamaxgain, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.

- Enter asemode to turn the amplifier on in ASE output power mode. - Enter asemode cancel

5.74.5 Examples
The following example shows how the testing status can be checked:
# config interface am2032a 1/14/lineout testing
Testing in progress: false
The following example shows how the asemode can be enabled (error if there are cross-
connections):
# config interface am2032a 1/14/lineout testing asemode
# config interface am2032a 1/14/lineout testing asemode
Unable to complete request.
Error: Request failed - Port has cross-connect
The following example shows how asemode testing is stopped:
# config interface am2032a 1/14/lineout testing asemode cancel
The following example shows how asemode output power can be modified:
# config interface am2032a 1/14/lineout testing asemode power 3.0
# config interface am2032a 1/14/lineout testing asemode power
ASE Mode Power Value : 3.00 dBm

5.93.4 Input Parameters
<lineout-port-aid>

<shelf>/<slot>/LINEOUT
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot

See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
apredfapulse
Syntax
apredfapulse [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - enables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
disabled - disables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
Default
enabled
Configures pulsing of the EDFA amplifier, while "APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is enabled, the EDFA will pulse between its on and off states, while
"APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is disabled, the EDFA will shutdown, when "APR Active - Line" is
reported.
An attempt to enable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Enabling EDFA pulsing will allow for APR auto recovery in spans with Raman
amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shutdown the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is reported

aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [<value>]
Values
auto
force
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before this command can be carried out.
auto - automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier, and will have an
impact on service. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the optical amplifier to restart
automatically. Do you want to proceed?
deltamaxgain
Syntax

Values
0..5 - gain in dB
Specifies the maximum allowed difference between the provisioned gain and the measured
gain before an alarm is raised.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingain <= gain <= maxgain + deltamaxgain.

apredfapulse
Syntax
apredfapulse [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - enables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
disabled - disables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
Default
enabled
Configures pulsing of the EDFA amplifier, while "APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is enabled, the EDFA will pulse between its on and off states, while
"APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is disabled, the EDFA will shutdown, when "APR Active - Line" is
reported.
An attempt to enable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Enabling EDFA pulsing will allow for APR auto recovery in spans with Raman
amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shutdown the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is reported

for this port. This might not allow automatic APR recovery for spans with Raman amplifiers. Do

Restrictions
This parameter applies to LD cards at ILAs and to egress LD cards at DGEs and add/drop
nodes. Attempts to enable or disable EDFA pulsing at an LD that is not at an ILA or is not
an egress LD will be denied.
aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [<value>]
Values
auto
force
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before this command can be carried out.
auto - automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier, and will have an
impact on service. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the optical amplifier to restart
automatically. Do you want to proceed?
deltamaxgain
Syntax
deltamaxgain [<value>]
Values
0..5 - gain in dB
Specifies the maximum allowed difference between the provisioned gain and the measured
gain before an alarm is raised.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingain <= gain <= maxgain + deltamaxgain.

apredfapulse
Syntax
apredfapulse [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - enables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
disabled - disables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
Default
enabled
Configures pulsing of the EDFA amplifier, while "APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is enabled, the EDFA will pulse between its on and off states, while
"APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is disabled, the EDFA will shutdown, when "APR Active - Line" is
reported.
An attempt to enable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Enabling EDFA pulsing will allow for APR auto recovery in spans with Raman
amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shutdown the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is reported
for this port. This might not allow automatic APR recovery for spans with Raman amplifiers. Do
you want to proceed?

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Restrictions
This parameter applies to LD cards at ILAs and to egress LD cards at DGEs and add/drop
nodes. Attempts to enable or disable EDFA pulsing at an LD that is not at an ILA or is not
an egress LD will be denied.
aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [<value>]
Values
auto
force
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before this command can be carried out.
auto - automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier, and will have an
impact on service. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the optical amplifier to restart
automatically. Do you want to proceed?
deltamaxgain
Values
0..5 - gain in dB
Specifies the maximum allowed difference between the provisioned gain and the measured
gain before an alarm is raised.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingain <= gain <= maxgain + deltamaxgain.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingain, maxgain, or deltamaxgain, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.

aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [<value>]
Values
auto
force
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before this command can be carried out.
auto - automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier, and will have an
impact on service. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the optical amplifier to restart
automatically. Do you want to proceed?
For the configuration with IPREAMP:
An attempt to configure the aprmode from "force" to "auto" will be denied if the aprmode is
"force" at the LineOut port of the IPREAMP.

oppdirection

of connected to linein port for OLP topology).
totalpower
Displays the total optical power for the port.
userdcmin
Displays whether an external DCM is connected at the line ingress.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable when the port is external (or pseudo external in the case
of connected to OPS Sig port for OLP topology).
Sub-command: wavekey
Displays wavekey information on this interface. See "show interface <card-type> <port-aid>
wavekey".
