amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shutdown the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is reported
for this port. This might not allow automatic APR recovery for spans with Raman amplifiers. Do
you want to proceed?
Restrictions
This parameter applies to LD cards at ILAs and to egress LD cards at DGEs and add/drop
nodes. Attempts to enable or disable EDFA pulsing at an LD that is not at an ILA or is not
an egress LD will be denied.
aprenabled
Syntax
aprenabled [<value>]
Values
enabled - The optical amplifier will shut down if the fiber span has been cut, and cannot
restart until the span has been repaired.
disabled - If the LD is used in an ILA or as an egress LD in an add/drop node, the amplifier
can start up and remain on even if the fiber span has been cut.
Default
enabled
Specifies whether APR is enabled or disabled for an egress LD in an add/drop node, or for an
LD in an ILA. Set APR to disabled, if the span is operated without an optical supervisory
channel.
Restrictions
The option to disable APR is accepted only when
• The slot present type is not empty
• Power-limited version of ASWG card is present.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before this command can be carried out.
auto - automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier, and will have an
impact on service. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the optical amplifier to restart
automatically. Do you want to proceed?
For the configuration with IPREAMP:
An attempt to configure the aprmode from "force" to "auto" will be denied if the aprmode is
"force" at the LineOut port of the IPREAMP.
deltamaxgain
Syntax
deltamaxgain [<value>]
Values
0..5 - gain in dB
Default
0 dB
Specifies the maximum allowed difference between the provisioned gain and the measured
gain before an alarm is raised.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingain <= gain <= maxgain + deltamaxgain.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingain, maxgain, or deltamaxgain, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.

Values
7..22 - gain in dB, when gainrange is low
13..29 - gain in dB, when gainrange is high
Default
7.00 dB (aswg)
Specifies the amplifier gain. Enter this keyword without arguments to display the current gain
setting, or with a valid value to change the gain setting for the amplifier.
The provisioned gain value is only used on optical lines using manual power management.
If gainrange is changed, and the current value of gain is outside of the allowed range for the
new value of gainrange, then gain is moved to the nearest allowed range.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingain <= gain <= maxgain + deltamaxgain.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingain, maxgain, or deltamaxgain, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.
gainpowermode
Syntax
gainpowermode [gain | power]
gainpowermode power outputpower [<value>]
Values
gain - constant gain mode
power - constant output power mode
<value> - target output power value. Range is -4 dBm to 10 dBm.
Default
gain for gain or power mode
5 dBm for target output power
Sets the amplifier to constant gain mode or constant output power mode
If "power" is specified without given an output power value, the amplifier will work in constant
output power mode at the default target output power value. If an target output power value is
specified following "outputpower", the amplifier will work in constant output power mode at the
specified power value. Also, LOS mode will be set to LOS N when the amplifier is set to power
mode.
If "gain" is specified, the amplifier will work in constant gain mode with LOS mode set to auto.
Use the gain command to specify the amplifier gain.

5.197.4 Input Parameters
<lineout-port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/LINEOUT
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each

aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [<value>]
Values
auto
force
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before this command can be carried out.
auto - automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier, and will have an
impact on service. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the optical amplifier to restart
automatically. Do you want to proceed?

apredfapulse
Syntax
apredfapulse [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - enables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
disabled - disables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
Default
enabled
Configures pulsing of the EDFA amplifier, while "APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is enabled, the EDFA will pulse between its on and off states, while
"APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is disabled, the EDFA will shutdown, when "APR Active - Line" is
reported.
An attempt to enable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Enabling EDFA pulsing will allow for APR auto recovery in spans with Raman
amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shutdown the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is reported
for this port. This might not allow automatic APR recovery for spans with Raman amplifiers. Do
you want to proceed?
Restrictions
This parameter applies to LD cards at ILAs and to egress LD cards at DGEs and add/drop
nodes. Attempts to enable or disable EDFA pulsing at an LD that is not at an ILA or is not
an egress LD will be denied.
deltamaxgainl

Specifies the maximum allowed difference between the provisioned gain and the measured
gain before an alarm is raised.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingainl <= gainl <= maxgainl + deltamaxgainl.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingainl, maxgainl, or deltamaxgainl, the above condition may not hold until a

gainl
Syntax
gainl [<value>]
Values

Default
7.00 dB
Restrictions
Range for gainrangel = low is 7..22 dB
Range for gainrangel = high is 13..29 dB
Specifies the amplifier gain. Enter this keyword without arguments to display the current gain
setting, or with a valid value to change the gain setting for the amplifier.
The provisioned gain value is only used on optical lines using manual power management.
If gainrangel is changed, and the current value of gain is outside of the allowed range for the
new value of gainrangel, then gainl is moved to the nearest allowed range.

set such that mingainl<= gainl <= maxgainl + deltamaxgainl.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingainl, maxgainl, or deltamaxgainl, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.

means the high span alarm feature is disabled.

of connected to linein port for OLP topology).
userdcmin
Displays whether an external DCM is connected at the line ingress.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable when the port is external (or pseudo external in the case
of connected to OPS Sig port for OLP topology).

aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [<value>]
Values
auto
force
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before this command can be carried out.
auto - automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
2914 Issue 1
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier, and will have an
impact on service. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the optical amplifier to restart
automatically. Do you want to proceed?
apredfapulse
Syntax
apredfapulse [{enabled [pulse] | disabled}]
Values
enabled - enables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
pulse - Optional value for user to turn the EDFA amplifier on (and then off) once
disabled - disables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
Default
enabled
Configures pulsing of the EDFA amplifier, while "APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is enabled, the EDFA will pulse between its on and off states, while
"APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is disabled, the EDFA will shut down, when "APR Active - Line" is
reported.
An attempt to enable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Enabling EDFA pulsing will allow for APR auto recovery in spans with Raman
amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
Follow enabled with pulse to trigger pulsing of the EDFA amplifier between its on and off states
immediately. This command can only be carried out when apredfapulse is enabled and APR-
Line is active on this port.
An attempt to trigger an immediate pulse will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Pulsing will immediately turn the EDFA amplifier on (and then off) at a power level not
exceeding +12 dBm. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shutdown the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is reported
for this port. This might not allow automatic APR recovery for spans with Raman amplifiers. Do
you want to proceed?

aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [<value>]
Values
auto
force
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port.The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before this command can be carried out.
auto - automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.

AWBILA
config interface awbila <lineout-port-aid>
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
2954 Issue 1
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier, and will have an
impact on service. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the optical amplifier to restart
automatically. Do you want to proceed?
apredfapulse
Syntax
apredfapulse [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - enables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
disabled - disables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
Default
enabled
Configures pulsing of the EDFA amplifier, while "APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is enabled, the EDFA will pulse between its on and off states, while
"APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is disabled, the EDFA will shutdown, when "APR Active - Line" is
reported.
An attempt to enable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Enabling EDFA pulsing will allow for APR auto recovery in spans with Raman
amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shutdown the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is reported
for this port. This might not allow automatic APR recovery for spans with Raman amplifiers. Do
you want to proceed?
Restrictions
This parameter applies to LD cards at ILAs and to egress LD cards at DGEs and add/drop
nodes. Attempts to enable or disable EDFA pulsing at an LD that is not at an ILA or is not
an egress LD will be denied.

deltamaxgainc
Values

Specifies the maximum allowed difference between the provisioned gain and the measured
gain before an alarm is raised.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingainc <= gainc <= maxgainc + deltamaxgainc.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingainc, maxgainc, or deltamaxgainc, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.

pm".
spanlossthreshold
Displays the OTS fiber span loss threshold used in "HISPANLOSS" alarm. A value of -99
means the high span alarm feature is disabled.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable when the port is external (or pseudo external in the case
of connected to linein port for OLP topology).
userdcmin
Displays whether an external DCM is connected at the line ingress.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable when the port is external (or pseudo external in the case
of connected to OPS Sig port for OLP topology).

bandmode
Syntax
bandmode [<value>]
Values
C - for C band only operation. In this mode only C band parameters are available to
provision and display. L band parameters are not available.

deltamaxgainc
Values
0..5 - gain in dB
Specifies the maximum allowed difference between the provisioned gain and the measured
gain before an alarm is raised.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingainc <= gainc <= maxgainc + deltamaxgainc.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingainc, maxgainc, or deltamaxgainc, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.

Restrictions
Range for gainrange = low is 8..23 dB
Range for gainrange = high is 14..30 dB
Specifies the amplifier gain. Enter this keyword without arguments to display the current gain
setting, or with a valid value to change the gain setting for the amplifier.
The provisioned gain value is only used on optical lines using manual power management.
If gainrange is changed, and the current value of gain is outside of the allowed range for the
new value of gainrange, then gain is moved to the nearest allowed range.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingainc <= gainc <= maxgainc + deltamaxgainc.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingainc, maxgainc, or deltamaxgainc, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.

Values

low - low gain range, covering gains of 8..23 dB.

actually taken.
deltamaxgainl
Values
0..5 - gain in dB
Specifies the maximum allowed difference between the provisioned gain and the measured
gain before an alarm is raised.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingainl <= gainl <= maxgainl + deltamaxgainl.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingain, maxgain, or deltamaxgain, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.

Specifies the amplifier gain. Enter this keyword without arguments to display the current gain
setting, or with a valid value to change the gain setting for the amplifier.
The provisioned gain value is only used on optical lines using manual power management.
If gainrangel is changed, and the current value of gain is outside of the allowed range for the
new value of gainrange, then gain is moved to the nearest allowed range.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingainl <= gainl <= maxgainl + deltamaxgainl.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingainl, maxgainl, or deltamaxgainl, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.

Release 24.12
December 2024
3058 Issue 1
Values
enabled - enables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier.
pulse - Optional value for user to turn the EDFA amplifier on (and then off) once.
disabled - disables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier.
Default
enabled
Configures pulsing of the EDFA amplifier, while "APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is enabled, the EDFA will pulse between its on and off states, while
"APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is disabled, the EDFA will shut down, when "APR Active - Line" is
reported.
An attempt to enable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Enabling EDFA pulsing will allow for APR auto recovery in spans with Raman
amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
Follow enabled with pulse to trigger pulsing of the EDFA amplifier between its on and off states
immediately. This command can only be carried out when apredfapulse is enabled and APR-
Line is active on this port.
An attempt to trigger an immediate pulse will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Enabling EDFA pulsing will allow for APR auto recovery in spans with Raman
amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message.
Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shut down the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is
reported for this port. This might not allow automatic APR recovery for spans with Raman
amplifiers. Do you want to proceed?
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable if APR is disabled.

auto
force
Core optics management commands

Release 24.12

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before this command can be carried out.
auto - automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier and will have an
impact on service. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the optical amplifier to restart
automatically. Do you want to proceed?

16.00 dB
Specifies the amplifier gain. Enter this keyword without arguments to display the current gain
setting, or with a valid value to change the gain setting for the amplifier.
The provisioned gain value is only used on optical lines using manual power management.
If gainrange is changed, and the current value of gain is outside of the allowed range for the
new value of gainrange, then gain is moved to the nearest allowed range.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingain <= gain <= maxgain + deltamaxgain.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable to EILA card.

5.321.4 Input Parameters
<linein-port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/LINEIN
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each

aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [<value>]
Values
auto
force
pulse
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before setting aprmode to force or back to auto.
auto - Automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - Force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.
pulse - Optional value to turn the EDFA on (and then off) to allow detecting the optical
supervisory channel and recover from APR.
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier. It will have an
impact on service and might cut optical supervisory communication on this line. Do you want to
proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the EDFA to restart automatically. Do you
want to proceed?
Follow auto with pulse to enable pulsing of the EDFA between its on and off states to detect the
optical supervisory channel and recover from APR. This command can only be carried out
when aprmode is in auto and APR-Line is active for the LINEIN port.
An attempt to enable pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be

apredfapulse
Syntax
apredfapulse [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - enables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
disabled - disables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
Default
enabled
Configures pulsing of the EDFA amplifier, while "APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is enabled, the EDFA will pulse between its on and off states, while
"APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is disabled, the EDFA will shutdown, when "APR Active - Line" is
reported.
An attempt to enable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Enabling EDFA pulsing will allow for APR auto recovery in spans with Raman
amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shutdown the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is reported
for this port. This might not allow automatic APR recovery for spans with Raman amplifiers. Do
you want to proceed?

subsequent power adjustment is run.

cancel

power

power [<value>]

5.325.5 Examples
The following example shows how the testing status can be checked:
# config interface a2p2125 1/14/lineout testing
Testing in progress: false
The following example shows how the asemode can be enabled (error if there are cross-
connections):
# config interface a2p2125 1/14/lineout testing asemode
# config interface a2p2125 1/14/lineout testing asemode
Unable to complete request.
Error: Request failed - Port has cross-connect
The following example shows how asemode testing is stopped:
# config interface a2p2125 1/14/lineout testing asemode cancel
The following example shows how asemode output power can be modified:
# config interface a2p2125 1/14/lineout testing asemode power 3.0
# config interface a2p2125 1/14/lineout testing asemode power
ASE Mode Power Value : 3.00 dBm

aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [<value>]
Values
auto
force
pulse
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before setting aprmode to force or back to auto.
auto - Automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - Force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.
pulse - Optional value to turn the EDFA on (and then off) to allow detecting the optical
supervisory channel and recover from APR.
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier. It will have an
impact on service and might cut optical supervisory communication on this line. Do you want to
proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the EDFA to restart automatically. Do you
want to proceed?
Follow auto with pulse to enable pulsing of the EDFA between its on and off states to detect the
optical supervisory channel and recover from APR. This command can only be carried out
when aprmode is in auto and APR-Line is active for the LINEIN port.
An attempt to enable pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be

Configures pulsing of the EDFA amplifier, while "APR Active - Line" is reported.

amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shutdown the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is reported

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Sets the Raman AGC target gain. In both auto and manual power management mode, this
target value is applied immediately.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable to RA2P only.
aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [{auto [pulse] | force}]
Values
auto
force
pulse
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before setting aprmode to force or back to auto.
auto - Automatic shutdown of the Raman amplifier pumps in response to a fiber cut, and
automatic restart of the pumps after the fiber has been repaired.
force - Force a shutdown of the Raman pumps, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.
pulse - Optional value to turn the Raman amplifier on (and then off) to allow detecting the
optical supervisory channel and recover from APR.
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the Raman amplifier. It will have an
impact on service and might cut optical supervisory communication on this line. Do you want to
proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the Raman amplifier to restart
automatically. Do you want to proceed?
Follow auto with pulse to enable pulsing of the Raman amplifier between its on and off states to
detect the optical supervisory channel and recover from APR. This command can only be
carried out when aprmode is in auto and APR-Line is active for the LINEIN port.
An attempt to enable pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be
accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Pulsing will turn the Raman amplifier on (and then off) to detect the optical
supervisory channel and recover from APR. Please verify that any open fibers or connectors
have been repaired. Do you want to proceed?

Values

5.370 config interface <asc-card>
5.370.1 Purpose
This command configures the interface ports on the (<asc-card>) Amplified splitter/combiner
subtype cards:
• ASC2 as card identifier for the subtypes: ASC2.
• ASC4 as card identifier for the subtypes: ASC4, ASC4L.
Use this command to access subcommands that allow you to:
• Configure SIGIN ports.
• Configure SIGOUT ports.
• Configure {A..F}IN ports.
• Configure {A..F}OUT ports.
• Configure {A..D}IN ports.
• Configure {A..D}OUT ports.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.370.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None

asc4

5.378 show interface <asc-card> <sigin-port-aid>
5.378.1 Purpose
This command displays the SIGIN ports on the (<asc-card>) Amplified splitter/combiner subtype
cards:
• ASC2 as card identifier for the subtypes: ASC2.
• ASC4 as card identifier for the subtypes: ASC4, ASC4L.
Use this command to:
• Display the current settings for the port.
• Display drop gain for the port.
• Display the extra input loss for the port
• Display total input power.
• Display LOS mode for the port.
• Display the PM.
• Display the VOA setting for the port.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables”, "Reference tables" for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

alienwavebank
Syntax
alienwavebank [no | yes]
Values
no - single alien unkeyed optical cross-connection allowed at an LC port.
yes - multiple alien unkeyed optical cross-connections allowed at an LC port
Default
no
Specifies if an MLFSB LC port set to topology external supports multiple alien optical cross-
connects. For value 'no' the cross-connect characteristics are advertised to the network if OSPF
is enabled. For value 'yes' no advertisements to the network are supported; therefore, the user
or network management system must take care to set the optical cross-connect user
technology type attributes at all optical cross-connects along each lightpath.
Restrictions
Value can only be changed for a topology external port if there are no optical cross-
connections using the port.
clearasontopo
Clears the ASONTOPO alarm set against the port. If the ASONTOPO alarm is not currently
raised against the port AID and the clearasontopo command is executed to clear the alarm, the
command will be accepted but no action is actually taken.

5.422 show interface mxn824 <sig-port-aid>
5.422.1 Purpose
This command displays the SIG ports on the following MXN824 WSS subtype cards:
• MXN824 as card identifier for the subtypes: MXN824, MXN824L
Use this command to:
• Display channel power information.
• Display the current settings for the port.
• Display total input and output power.
• Display the PM.
• Display the WSS relative attenuation.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables”, "Reference tables" for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.422.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.422.3 Input Format
show interface mxn824 <sig-port-aid>
channel
detail
inpower
outpower
pm
wssrelativeatten
5.422.4 Input Parameters
<sig-port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/SIG{1..8}
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number.

Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 3441
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
channel
Syntax
channel [summary | <frequency>]
Values
summary - to display a summary of channel utilization on this port and which AD ports add/
drop the channels.
<frequency> - <flexgridchannel> - selection of the channel.
Displays the channel power information. Optionally follow with an integer value for a channel to
display only that channel or summary for a summary of all channels.
detail
Displays the current settings for the port.
inpower
Displays the total input power in dBm.
outpower
Displays the total output power in dBm.
Sub-command: pm
Displays the performance monitoring attributes. See "show interface mxn824 <port-aid> pm"
command for details.
wssrelativeatten
Syntax
wssrelativeatten [<frequency>]
Values
<flexgridchannel> - selection of the channel.
Displays a table of the WSS relative attenuation in dB for the channels provisioned. Applies to
the SIG port for the add direction. Specifying a channel by <frequency> displays just the
channel of interest.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables”, "Reference tables" for valid numeric <flexgridchannel>
range. Only provisioned channels can be displayed.

5.425 config interface {wr8-88a | wr8-88af | wr2-88}
5.425.1 Purpose
This command configures the interface ports on an 8 degree (WR8-88A or WR8-88AF) or a 2
degree (WR2-88) wavelength router card.
Use this command to:
• Access subcommands that allow you to configure the ADDIN[1-8], DROPOUT, MESHOUT[1-3],
SIG, or THRU port on WR8-88A or WR8-88AF
• Access subcommands that allow you to configure the ADDIN, DROPOUT, SIG, or THRU port on
WR2-88
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.425.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
5.425.3 Input Format
config interface {wr8-88a | wr8-88af | wr2-88} <port-aid>
5.425.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/THRU - WR8-88A, WR8-88AF, WR2-88
<shelf>/<slot>/SIG - WR8-88A, WR8-88AF, WR2-88
<shelf>/<slot>/DROPOUT - WR8-88A, WR8-88AF, WR2-88
<shelf>/<slot>/MESHOUT{1..3} - WR8-88A, WR8-88AF
<shelf>/<slot>/ADDIN{1..8} - WR8-88A, WR8-88AF
<shelf>/<slot>/ADDIN - WR2-88
* - display list of ports
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number, or * to list all of the {wr8-88a | wr8-88af | wr2-88} cards
on the network element.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.

5.434 show interface {wr8-88a | wr8-88af | wr2-88}
5.434.1 Purpose
This command displays the configuration of the interfaces on a 8 degree wavelength router (WR8-
88A or WR8-88AF) card or 2 degree (WR2-88) wavelength router card.
Use this command to:
• Display the configuration for a specific interface port
• Display WaveKey and power information for a specific interface port. You can optionally filter the
results for the port to show information for the in or out direction only, or for a channel in the in or
out direction.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.434.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.434.3 Input Format
show interface {wr8-88a | wr8-88af | wr2-88} <port-aid>
detail
wavekey
wssatten <frequency>
wssrelativeatten <frequency>
wssreference <frequency>
5.434.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/THRU - WR8-88A, WR8-88AF, WR2-88
<shelf>/<slot>/SIG - WR8-88A, WR8-88AF, WR2-88
<shelf>/<slot>/DROPOUT - WR8-88A, WR8-88AF, WR2-88
<shelf>/<slot>/MESHOUT{1..3} - WR8-88A, WR8-88AF
<shelf>/<slot>/ADDIN{1..8} - WR8-88A, WR8-88AF
<shelf>/<slot>/ADDIN - WR2-88
* - display list of ports
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number, or * to list all of the WR8-88A or WR8-88AF or WR2-88
cards on the network element.
Core optics management commands
WR2-88 and WR8-88A and WR8-88AF
show interface {wr8-88a | wr8-88af | wr2-88}
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 3467
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
detail
Displays a detailed summary of all service activity on this interface
Sub-command: wavekey
Displays wavekey information on this interface. See "show interface <card-type> <port-aid>
wavekey".
wssatten <frequency>
Displays the last configured user set attenuation value for channel freq.
Note: Applies to the SIG port only.
wssrelativeatten <frequency>
Display a listing showing the current relative attenuation applied by the Wavelength Selective
Switch for each channel transmitted from the port. Only applicable channels cross connected
through the port are shown with a value. If freq is given, displays the value for the specified
channel.
Note: Applies to the SIG port only.
wssreference <frequency>
Display the shelf, slot, and port of the LD card that is providing the reference point for WSS
adjustments for each channel transmitted from the port.
Note: Applies only to WR cards at level 0 in the configuration.

3478 Issue 1
aprholdoff
Syntax
aprholdoff [<value>]
Values
{yes, no}
Default
no
Sets the hold-off time for Automatic Power Reduction. This setting only needs to be changed
when the WR is deployed in a network using Optical Line Protection.When configured to value
yes the hold-off time prior to APR will be applied. When configured to value no the hold-off time
will not be applied prior to APR.
clearasontopo
Clears the ASONTOPO alarm set against the SIG port.
If the ASONTOPO alarm is not currently raised against the port AID and the clearasontopo
command is executed to clear the alarm, the command will be accepted but no action is
actually taken.
description

Values
<string> - ASCII string, 1..255 characters
"" - to clear the description
Default
""

describes the interface, or enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current
description for the interface.

addpowermin
Syntax
addpowermin [<value>]
Values
-20.00..-5.00 - per channel optical power in dBm.
Default
-13.00 dBm
Specifies minimum input power to the ADT port from the add path. Enter this keyword without
arguments to display the current value. Enter this keyword followed by a valid value to change
the setting. If the optical line is auto power managed the change must be applied by running an
egress adjustment.
Restrictions
Access Levels: Administrator only

alienwavebank
Syntax
alienwavebank [<value>]
Values
no - single alien unkeyed optical cross-connection allowed at ADT port
yes - multiple alien unkeyed optical cross-connections allowed at ADT port
Default
no
Specifies if the ADT port set to topology external supports multiple alien optical cross-connects.
For value 'no' the cross-connect characteristics are advertised to the network if OSPF is
enabled. For value 'yes' no advertisements to the network are supported; therefore, the user or
network management system must take care to set the optical cross-connect user technology
type attributes at all optical cross-connects along each lightpath.
Restrictions
Value can only be changed for a topology external ADT port if there are no optical cross-
connections using the port.
This parameter applies to IR4, IR9 subtypes and IROADM9R cards.

apredfapulse
Syntax
apredfapulse [{enabled [pulse] | disabled}]
Values
enabled - enables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
pulse - Optional value for user to turn the EDFA amplifier on (and then off) once
disabled - disables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
Default
enabled
Configures pulsing of the EDFA amplifier, while "APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is enabled, the EDFA will pulse between its on and off states, while
"APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is disabled, the EDFA will shut down, when "APR Active - Line" is
reported.
An attempt to enable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Enabling EDFA pulsing will allow for APR auto recovery in spans with Raman
amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed X dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
Follow enabled with pulse to trigger pulsing of the EDFA amplifier between its on and off states
immediately. This command can only be carried out when apredfapulse is enabled and APR-
Line is active on this port.
An attempt to trigger an immediate pulse will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Pulsing will immediately turn the EDFA amplifier on (and then off) at a power level not
exceeding X dBm. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:

Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shut down the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is

This parameter is not applicable if APR is disabled.
The option value (pulse) in this parameter is applicable for two possible cases:

2. For IRDM32 card where "APR Active - Line" is reported, no active "APR Forced" or "APR
Active - Port Switch" conditions, and its lineout port is connected with the SigCx port of
OMDCL and the LinexIn port of the same OMDCL card is configured with the external OSC
(OSCInExternal=true).
In a C+L configuration with OMDCL, if both C and L bands are provisioned, and if this
parameter is configured on one band, the same parameter on the other band is
synchronized. This restriction is only applicable to IRDM32 subtype cards and IRDM32L.

Syntax

Values

aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [<value>]
Values
auto
force
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before this command can be carried out.
auto - automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the
EDFA after the fiber has been repaired.
force - force a shutdown the EDFA, even if the fiber is currently carrying traffic.
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from auto to force will require a confirmation
from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to force will shut down the optical amplifier and will have an
impact on service. Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to change the value of this parameter from force to auto will also require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Changing the APR mode to auto will allow the optical amplifier to restart
automatically. Do you want to proceed?
For the configuration with IPREAMP:
An attempt to configure the aprmode from "force" to "auto" will be denied if the aprmode is
"force" at the LineOut port of the IPREAMP.

Values

"" - to clear the description
Default
""
Specifies a description for the interface port. Enter this keyword followed by string that
describes the interface or enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current
description for the interface.

Specifies the egress amplifier gain. Enter this keyword without arguments to display the current
gain setting, or with a valid value to change the gain setting for the amplifier.
For IROADMF, IROADMV, and IROADM9M, the gain value can be changed in manual power
management mode by advanced users, for niche applications. In auto power management
mode, the gain value is fixed at the default value.
For other IROADM types, the gain value can be changed in auto or manual power management
modes. The specified value will be used.
For IR4 card:
An attempt to change the value of this parameter to a value other than 20 dB will require a
confirmation from the user. The confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: The egress OA is designed to work in fixed gain at 20 dB. Changing the gain to a
different value may affect the OA performance. Do you want to proceed (yes/no)?
Restrictions
The value can only be set if the port is manually power managed for IROADMF, IROADMV,
and IROADM9M cards.
This parameter is not applicable to IRDM32L.

Syntax

{auto,losn}

Sets the behavior of the amplifier when the input optical signal to the amplifier is in Loss of
Signal state.

be set to 250ms default.
When configured to value auto the LD will take on the normal shutdown behavior for the LD.
When configured to value losn the LD will not shut off when the input optical signal is in LOS.

5.451 config interface <iroadm-card> <lineout-port-aid> pm
5.451.1 Purpose
Configure the performance management parameters on a card (<iroadm-card>):
• ir4 - 4 ADT ports IROADM
• ir9 as card identifier for ir9 subtypes: ir9, ir9lp - 9 ADT ports IROADM
• ir20 as card identifier for ir20 subtypes: ir20, ir20lp - 20 ADT ports IROADM
• iroadmf - Fixed gain IROADM
• iroadmv - Variable gain IROADM
• iroadm9m - 9 ADT ports Metro IROADM
• iroadm9r - 9 ADT ports Regional / Long Haul IROADM
• irdm20 - 20 ADT ports IROADM
• irdm32 as card identifier for irdm32 subtypes: irdm32, irdm32lp - 32 ADT ports IROADM
• irdm32l - 32 ADT ports L band IROADM
Use this command to:
• Clear all bins in all groups on this line interface.
• Configure the transmitted optical power group pm options.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

Specifies the card description. Enter this keyword without option to display the current

Values

15.0 dB

for the optical supervisory channel. Enter this keyword without arguments to display the current
setting.

5.454 config interface <iroadm-card> <oscsfp-port-aid>

Configure the optical supervisory channel (OSC) small form factor pluggable (SFP) interface port
on a card:
• ir4 - 4 ADT ports IROADM
• ir9 as card identifier for ir9 subtypes: ir9, ir9lp - 9 ADT ports IROADM
• ir20 as card identifier for ir20 subtypes: ir20, ir20lp - 20 ADT ports IROADM
• iroadmf - Fixed gain IROADM
• iroadmv - Variable gain IROADM
• iroadm9m - 9 ADT ports Metro IROADM
• iroadm9r - 9 ADT ports Regional / Long Haul IROADM
• irdm20 - 20 ADT ports IROADM
• irdm32 as card identifier for irdm32 subtypes: irdm32, irdm32lp - 32 ADT ports IROADM
• irdm32l - 32 ADT ports L band IROADM

commands".

5.455 config interface <iroadm-card> <oscsfp-port-aid> pm
5.455.1 Purpose
Configure the OSCSFP performance monitoring parameters on a card (<iroadm-card>):
• ir4 - 4 ADT ports IROADM
• ir9 as card identifier for ir9 subtypes: ir9, ir9lp - 9 ADT ports IROADM
• r20 as card identifier for ir20 subtypes: ir20, ir20lp - 20 ADT ports IROADM
• iroadmf - Fixed gain IROADM
• iroadmv - Variable gain IROADM
• iroadm9m - 9 ADT ports Metro IROADM
• iroadm9r - 9 ADT ports Regional / Long Haul IROADM
• irdm20 - 20 ADT ports IROADM
• irdm32 as card identifier for irdm32 subtypes: irdm32, irdm32lp - 32 ADT ports IROADM
• irdm32l - 32 ADT ports L band IROADM
Use this command to:
• Clear all bins in all groups on this line interface.
• Configure the received optical power group pm options.
• Configure the transmitted optical power group pm options.
• Configure the interface group pm options.
• Configure the sonet/sdh group pm options.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

5.456 show interface <iroadm-card>
5.456.1 Purpose
This command displays the interface port on a card (<iroadm-card>):
• ir4 - 4 ADT ports IROADM
• ir9 as card identifier for ir9 subtypes: ir9, ir9lp - 9 ADT ports IROADM
• ir20 as card identifier for ir20 subtypes: ir20, ir20lp - 20 ADT ports IROADM
• iroadmf - Fixed gain IROADM
• iroadmv - Variable gain IROADM
• iroadm9m - 9 ADT ports Metro IROADM
• iroadm9r - 9 ADT ports Regional / Long Haul IROADM
• irdm20 - 20 ADT ports IROADM
• irdm32 as card identifier for irdm32 subtypes: irdm32, irdm32lp - 32 ADT ports IROADM
• irdm32l - 32 ADT ports L band IROADM
Use this command to access subcommands that allow you to :
• Display LINEIN port
• Display LINEOUT port
• Display OSCSFP port
• Display OSC port
• Display DCM port
• Display ADT port
• Display OTDRRX port
• Display OTDRTX port
• Display CUSTLAN port.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.456.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer

controlpwr
Displays the target power and measured power for controlled channels, including user defined
XCs and internal line loading ASE channels if exist. See "show interface <card-type> <port-aid>
controlpwr".
detail
Displays the current detailed information for the port.
dropdisposition
Display the drop disposition for a specific channel or a drop disposition list for all channels of
the IROADM LINEIN port. Please refer to Values of this parameter for detailed information.
Syntax
dropdisposition [<frequency> | all]
Values
<frequency> - Display the drop disposition for a specific channel of the IROADM LINEIN
port.
all - Display a drop disposition list for all the channels of the IROADM LINEIN port.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable to the IRDM20, IRDM32 subtype, IRDM32L and IR20
subtype cards.
extamp
Displays if external amplification is used.
Restrictions
This parameter is applicable for IR9 subtypes, IR20 subtypes, IROADM9R, IRDM20 and
IRDM32 subtype packs.
This parameter is only applicable to a port with topology connected to external.
flexgrid
Displays a detailed summary of flexible grid characteristics of the degree in the ingress
direction. See "show interface <card-type> <port-aid> flexgrid".

Restrictions
The parameter is only applicable to a port with topology connected to external (or

Sub-command: iwtocm
Displays the integrated Wavelength Tracker optical channel monitor attributes corresponding to
the LINEIN (ingress direction). See "show interface <card-type> <port-aid> iwtocm".
oscopr
Displays the current approximate optical power of the optical supervisory channel received at
the LINEIN port, calculated from the OSCSFP received power, OSC drop VOA and OSC drop
insertion loss. Note that in the configuration where a RA2P-96 precedes the IROADM LINEIN
port, the power value will be shown as "U/A" for unavailable because the OSC signal is not
dropped at the IROADM LINEIN in this configuration.
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable to IROADMF, IROADMV and IROADM9M cards.
otsspanloss
Displays the calculated fiber span loss for the OTS segment.
Sub-command: pm
Display the performance monitoring (pm) attributes for the LINEIN port. See "show interface
<iroadm-card> <linein-port-aid> pm".
spanlossthreshold
Displays the OTS fiber span loss threshold used in "HISPANLOSS" alarm. A value of -99
means the high span alarm feature is disabled.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable when the port is external (or pseudo external in the case
of connected to linein port for OLP topology).
Sub-command: spantype
Displays whether the port is supporting single-fiber bidirectional transmission or two-fiber
transmission. If single-fiber transmission is supported, also displays the channel plan, and
channel plan flex receive
Restrictions
This parameter applies to IROADM9R-LP, IR9LP and IR4 cards only
userdcmin
Displays whether an external DCM is connected at the line ingress (not associated using the
linedcm parameter).
Sub-command: wavekey
Displays the Wavelength Tracker attributes for the LINEIN port. See "show interface <card-
type> <port-aid> wavekey".

5.463 show interface <iroadm-card> <lineout-port-aid> pm
5.463.1 Purpose
This command displays the performance monitoring parameters of the LINEOUT port on a card
(<iroadm-card>):
• ir4 - 4 ADT Ports IROADM
• ir9 as card identifier for ir9 subtypes: ir9, ir9lp - 9 ADT ports IROADM
• ir20 as card identifier for ir20 subtypes: ir20, ir20lp - 20 ADT ports IROADM
• iroadmf - Fixed gain IROADM
• iroadmv - Variable gain IROADM
• iroadm9m - 9 ADT ports Metro IROADM
• iroadm9r - 9 ADT ports Regional / Long Haul IROADM
• irdm20 - 20 ADT ports IROADM
• irdm32 as card identifier for irdm32 subtypes: irdm32, irdm32lp - 32 ADT ports IROADM
• irdm32l - 32 ADT ports L band IROADM
Use this command to:
• Display the opout group PM
• Display the opochout group PM
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.463.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.463.3 Input Format
show interface <iroadm-card> <lineout-port-aid> pm
opout
opochout

apredfapulse
Syntax
apredfapulse [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - enables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
disabled - disables pulsing of the EDFA amplifier
Default
enabled
Configures pulsing of the EDFA amplifier, while "APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is enabled, the EDFA will pulse between its on and off states, while
"APR Active - Line" is reported.
If pulsing of EDFA amplifier is disabled, the EDFA will shutdown, when "APR Active - Line" is
reported.
An attempt to enable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Enabling EDFA pulsing will allow for APR auto recovery in spans with Raman
amplifier. (EDFA pulses will not exceed +12dBm total power). Do you want to proceed?
An attempt to disable APR EDFA pulsing will require a confirmation from the user. The
confirmation will be accompanied by the following message:
Warning: Disabling EDFA pulsing will shutdown the EDFA when "APR Active - Line" is reported
for this port. This might not allow automatic APR recovery for spans with Raman amplifiers. Do
you want to proceed?
aprmode
Syntax
aprmode [<value>]
Values
auto
force
Default
auto
Configures the mode for Automatic Power Reduction (APR) at the port. The port state must be
set to maintenance or down before this command can be carried out.
auto - automatic shutdown of the EDFA in response to a fiber cut, and automatic restart of the

Sub-command: ason
This sub-command with its parameter is for internal use only. For more details see Chapter 3,
“System administration commands”, "ASON management commands".
detail
Displays a detailed summary of parameters on this interface.
flexgrid
Displays a detailed summary of flexible grid characteristics of the degree in the ingress
direction. See "show interface <card-type> <port-aid> flexgrid".
Restrictions
The parameter is only applicable to a port with topology connected to external (or
connected to OLP mode OPS SIG port).
inpower
Displays the ingress power.
oscopr
Displays the current approximate optical power of the optical supervisory channel received at
the LINEIN port, calculated from the OSCSFP received power and OSC drop insertion loss.
otsspanloss
Displays the calculated fiber span loss for the OTS segment.
Sub-command: pm
Display the performance monitoring (pm) attributes for the LINEIN port. See "show interface
ipreamp <linein-port-aid> pm".
spanlossthreshold
Displays the OTS fiber span loss threshold used in "HISPANLOSS" alarm. A value of -99
means the high span alarm feature is disabled.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable when the port is external (or pseudo external in the case
of connected to linein port for OLP topology).
Sub-command: wavekey
Displays the Wavelength Tracker attributes for the LINEIN port. See "show interface <card-
type> <port-aid> wavekey".

3756 Issue 1
etr
Displays the extended temperature range (ETR) setting for the port with values:
• True: the port can only support modules which are ETR rated.
• False: the port can support modules with or without ETR
Pluggable modules with extended temperature range (ETR) are required if etr is True. A
pluggable module mismatch alarm will be raised if the provisioned module does not support
ETR.

Sub-command: ason

This sub-command with its parameter is for L-band nternal use only. For more details see

detail
Display the current settings for the port.
flexgrid
Displays a detailed summary of flexible grid characteristics of the degree in the ingress
direction. See "show interface <card-type> <port-aid> flexgrid".
Restrictions
The parameter is only applicable to a port with topology connected to external (or
connected to OLP mode OPS SIG port).
oscopr
Displays the current approximate optical power of the optical supervisory channel received at
the LINEIN port, calculated from the OSCSFP received power, OSC drop VOA and OSC drop
insertion loss.
otsspanloss
Displays the calculated fiber span loss for the OTS segment.
oscinexternal
Displays if the OSC is external that the OSC signal transmitted over cascaded OTs, or the OSC
is not external that the OSC signal is transmitted over the OSC wavelength.
pm
Displays the performance monitoring (PM) attributes for the LINEIN port. See "show interface
omdcl <linein-port-aid> pm".
spanlossthreshold
Displays the OTS fiber span loss threshold used in "HISPANLOSS" alarm. A value of -99
means the high span alarm feature is disabled.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable when the port is external (or pseudo external in the case
of connected to linein port for OLP topology).

3784 Issue 1
osnrmeasure
Syntax
osnrmeasure [<value>]
Values
enabled - activate the OSNR measurement function for this specified WTOCMA IN port.
disabled - stop the OSNR measurement function for this specified WTOCMA IN port.
Default
disabled
Turn on/off the OSNR measurement on specified WTOCMA IN port.
Once enabled, the WTOCMA will scan channels in this port for OSNR measurement in normal
mode and allow the user to select channels in this port for on demand OSNR scan (See "config
card wtocma <slot-aid> ondemandOSNR [start | abort | status]").
Once disabled, the WTOCMA will not proceed OSNR measurement for any channel in this
port.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable for WTOCMA card.

Note:
If a port on an LD, RA2P-96, or MON-OTDR is connected to the otdr port, the associated port
of the LD or RA2P-96 must be linked to an external fiber span.
If an OTDR port has a connection to an LD or RA2P-96 port, and the link to the external fiber
span is deleted at the LD or RA2P-96 port, then the connection from the OTDR port to the LD
or RA2P-96 port is automatically deleted.
External connection is used for applications not covered by a port association, such as a dark
fiber case, where the connection is set to external and the scan is triggered from the OTDR
port.
For connections to the OTDRTX or OTDRRX ports of C band cards, use the OTDR, OTDRWB,
and OTDRM card.
For connections to the OTDRTX or OTDRRX ports of L band cards use the OTDRWB card.
For external connections and connections to MON-OTDR ports, use either the OTDR or
OTDRWB or OTDRM card.

Sub-command: profile
Use this command to modify one of the custom scan profiles in the node. See "config otdrscan
profile".
Profile updates will not take effect until the profile is applied. When the scan is launched,
validation against allowed parameters or any profile changes is performed. Note that the
attributes validation is done with following sequence: pulselength, range, and resolution.
If the attributes are not allowed, the scan will be denied, with an appropriate error message. If
the profile has been updated since the last scan, a message notifying the user that the profile
needs to be applied for changes to take effect.
Sub-command: profilem
Use this command to modify one of the custom scan profiles in the node. See "config otdrscan
profilem".
Profile updates will not take effect until the profile is applied. When the scan is launched,
validation against allowed parameters or any profile changes is performed. Note that the
attributes validation is done with following sequence: pulselength, range, and resolution.
If the attributes are not allowed, the scan will be denied, with an appropriate error message. If
the profile has been updated since the last scan, a message notifying the user that the profile
needs to be applied for changes to take effect.

Values
<filename> - selected sor file to be deleted.

Release 24.12

3804 Issue 1
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for full list of otdr supported cards and applicable ports.
detail
Displays the detailed description of the scan settings.
description
Syntax
description [<string>]
Values
<string> - 1..30 character ASCII string
"" - to clear the description
Default
""
An optional string of up to 30 characters to describe the tested fiber span. Enter this keyword
without any parameters to display the current description.
filename
Syntax
filename [<string>]
Values
<string> - up to 25 characters consisting of alphabetical and numeric characters and
dashes (hyphens). No other special characters or symbols can be used, and there can be
no spaces in the filename.
Default
""
The filename represents where the scan results are stored and is required to be provisioned
prior to launching the scan. If no filename is specified and there is already a provisioned
filename, the current filename will be used for the next scan, and will be appended with time
stamp. If there is no filename provisioned against the port the otdrscan is denied.
Follow this with a string of up to 25 characters to set the file name for a scan. At the end of the
scan, the filename is appended with port aid and time stamp and is saved in ".sor" format i.e:
filename_sh_sl_pt_yyyymmdd_hh-mm-ss.sor
The filename can include alphabetical and numeric characters and dashes (hyphens). No other
special characters or symbols can be used, and there can be no spaces in the filename.
If the parameter filename is entered without a string, then the current filename will be displayed.
profile
Syntax
profile [<id>]

scan
Syntax
scan [abort]
Runs the OTDR scan settings on the port. A filename is required to store the scan results,
before running the scan command. Optionally follow this keyword with abort, to abort the OTDR
scan.
If the OTDR is in use, and cannot run the requested scan, the request will be put in a
queue.The scan will run when the OTDR becomes available.
If the OTDR port is not associated with an LD port, the scan is rejected.
Core optics management commands
OTDR Scan
config otdrscan <port-aid>
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
3806 Issue 1
If a scan is aborted, the otdrscan result file associated with the port is not stored on the NE.
The abort function is applicable to an OTDRscan in running state only. An attempt to abort a
scan in pending state will return an error.
status
Displays the status of the OTDR to which this port is connected.
If the status is busy, the command will also display the scanning time remaining on the current
OTDR scan. The display is in min:ss. There can be additional processing time after the
scanning has completed before the OTDR is ready for the next scan.
Returned values for Scans initiated on the OTDR card or cards with embedded OTDR ports
are:
Running - The OTDR is currently performing an OTDR trace on the selected port.
Pending - The OTDR is pending underlying resources being available.
Complete - The OTDR trace was completed. Time Stamp is added to indicate the last
completed scan.
Aborted - The OTDR scan is aborted on the selected port.

5.552 config otdrscan resultstransfer server
5.552.1 Purpose

hostkey
Syntax
hostkey <keyindex> <keystring>
Core optics management commands
OTDR Scan
config otdrscan resultstransfer server
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 3817
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
For <keyindex>:
{1,2} - index of the public host key
Default
Entry required
Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 characters containing the SSH key string in OpenSSH format.
"" - to clear the string.
Default
Entry required
The hostkey parameter provisions the host public keys used for host authentication. The
number of keys configurable per host is defined by the available key indices.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings or spaces only for all key entries - no host key
authentication will be applied.
If at least one key is provisioned, all provisioned keys can be used for user authentication.
Provisioning a second key allows key rotation without service interruption. After a new key is
deployed on server side the old one should be removed. A normal secure configuration applies
one key only.
The format of the string of the ssh key supported is the OpenSSH key format which can be
generated by the ssh-keygen command - "<type name> <base64 coded key string>
[<comment>]" (Ref RFC 4253). The content of the ".pub" file can be directly copied.
The host name, ip address and port, will be taken from the provisioned ip address and port
number.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring>) deletes the provisioned key and removes it
from the system.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin
security ssh" command.
Note: The hostkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.

command displays the current protocol.
Note: ftp or http can only be provisioned if admin ui mode is normal.
Warning: If the ui mode is changed, the protocol and port settings remain the same, even if
the protocol is not allowed with the new ui mode (for example, change from normal to
encrypted with protocol ftp). Furthermore, as stated in the description of the config ui mode
command, changing the ui mode will also reset the Access Control List to the system default
settings. Therefore, if you change the ui mode, ensure after changing the ui mode that the
combination of protocol, port, and ACL settings allow traffic for the service.
Restrictions
The protocols http and https are not available when the controller in a PSS-32, PSS-16, or
PSS-4 main shelf is an EC card.
sshprivkey
Syntax
sshprivkey <keystring> [<password>]
Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 character SSH key string.
"" - to clear the string.
Default
Entry required
Core optics management commands
OTDR Scan
config otdrscan resultstransfer server
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
3820 Issue 1
Values
For <password>:
<string> - UTF-8 string, 1..64 characters in double quotes.
"" - empty string for no password.
Default
""
The sshprivkey parameter provisions the user private keys used for user authentication on
server side.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings - no public user key authentication will be applied.
The format of the string of the SSH key supported is the OpenSSH private key PEM file format
which can be generated by the ssh-keygen command
The format looks like:
"-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----b3BlbnNzaC1rZXktdjEAAA ...
RAQ0VDMi04MS0yAQIDBA==-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----"
The key must be surrounded by quotation marks.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring> = "") deletes the provisioned key and
removes it from the system.
The private key can be protected by a password, which is needed by the system for decryption.
Following behavior of this parameter applies:
• If a password is provided, the key is password or pass phrase protected. If a pass
phrase contains spaces, it must be surrounded by quotation marks.
• If an empty string is provided, the key is not password protected. Empty string means: ""
is provided.
• If no password string is provided, the system asks for a password. If in this case ENTER
is typed without typing a password or pass phrase the key is not password protected.
If the sshprivkey parameter will be typed in without a value, then the fingerprint of the currently
provisioned key will be shown.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin
security ssh" command.
Note: The sshprivkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
result
Returns the file path to the local directory of the last completed scan on the port.
scanresult
Displays the result of the most recent OTDR scan at that port.
Returned values are:
Not scanning
In progress
Canceled
Failed
status
Displays the status of the OTDR to which this port is connected.
If the status is busy, the command will also display the scanning time remaining on the current
OTDR scan. The display is in min:ss. There can be additional processing time after the
scanning has completed before the OTDR is ready for the next scan.
Returned values for Scans initiated on the OTDR card or cards with embedded OTDR ports
are:
Running - The OTDR is currently performing an OTDR trace on the selected port.
Pending - The OTDR is pending underlying resources being available.
Complete - The OTDR trace was completed. Time Stamp is added to indicate the last
completed scan.
Aborted - The OTDR scan is aborted on the selected port.
fileNameList
Lists the OTDR scan files that are currently stored on the network element. Only the files that
are associated with this port are displayed.
File names and the date and time that the file was stored are shown. If file names are reused,
then the different scans can be distinguished by their dates and times.
wavelength
The wavelength used for the OTDR scan. The wavelength is 1610 nm for the OTDR and
OTDRM and 1625 nm for the OTDRWB and the OMDCL cards.

5.563 config interface opsa <a-port-aid> switch
5.563.1 Purpose
This command configures the switch threshold and tolerance on the A and B ports of an optical
protection switch (OPSA) card.
Use this command to:
• Set the threshold calculation mode to auto or manual
• Set the switching threshold and tolerance for manual configured ports
• Set the transmit eVOA attenuation for manual power managed lines
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.563.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Threshold values specify when the OPSA card performs a protection switch. eVOA
attenuation values affect the transmission power levels.
Access Levels: Service, Administrator: switchthresh, switchtol, voaattenuation
Service: calculationmode
5.563.3 Input Format

calculationmode
mininputpower
switchthresh
switchtol
voaattenuation

number, a slash, and the port number.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
calculationmode
Syntax
calculationmode [auto | manual]

Release 24.12

3848 Issue 1
Values
{auto, manual}
Specifies the operating mode for the OPSA switch threshold calculations.
When the OPSA card is in OMSP mode,calculationmode will always be set to manual. An
attempt to change the value to auto will be denied.
When the OPSA card is in OLP mode, calculationmode will always be set to manual. An
attempt to change the value to auto will be denied.
Note: One must be logged in as a service user in order to have access to the OPSA
calculationmode.
switchthresh
Syntax
switchthresh [<value>]
Values
-30..5 - threshold value in dBm, for OCHP
-30..17 - threshold value in dBm, for OMSP
-31.5..5 - threshold value in dBm, for OLP
Default
-30.00 for OCH protection
-4.00 for OMS protection
-28.00 for OLP protection
Specifies the switching threshold to be used when calculationmode is set to manual. The
switching threshold defines the power level below which a protection switch is triggered. Enter
this keyword followed by a value for the switching threshold, in dBm. In static networks you
need to calculate this value based on the planned OPSA received power.
Note: This command applies to ports A and B only
Note: Entering a switchthresh value is denied if the calculationmode is set to auto.
switchtol
Syntax
switchtol [<value>]
Values
0.00..5.00 - value in dB
Default
2.00
Specifies the switching threshold tolerance to be used when calculationmode is set to manual.
Enter this keyword followed by a value for the switching threshold tolerance, in dB. Enter this
Core optics management commands
OPSA
config interface opsa <a-port-aid> switch

Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 3849
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
keyword alone to display the current value.
The switching threshold tolerance defines the level by which the signal must improve above the
switching threshold before the switch is allowed to revert to its original configuration. For
example, if port A is the active port and has a switchthresh of -18.00 dBm, and the input to port
A goes below -18.00 dBm, a switch will be made to port B. If the switchtol is 1.00 dB, then the
switch will be allowed to revert to port A only if the input power at A is -17.00 dBm or higher.
Switching is not revertive. The switch back to A is made manually or in response to the signal
power at B going below its switchthresh value.
Note: This command applies to ports A and B only.
Note: Entering a switchtol value is denied if the calculationmode is set to auto.
voaattenuation

0..20 - attenuation in dB
-1 - maximum attenuation
Default
-1.00 - OCHP
0 - OLP, OMSP
Specifies the attenuation value for the VOA in the egress direction for manually power managed
lines. Attempts to enter a voaattenuation value when the line is in auto power managed mode
will be denied.
Enter this keyword followed by a value for the VOA attenuation, in dB.
Enter this keyword alone to display the current value.

"False"

The minimum input power value is provided by WS-P. This target power is used by the Span

Core optics management commands
OPS card
config interface <ops-card> <ab-port-aid> switch
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
3888 Issue 1
Default
2.00 - Value for OPSB
Default
1.00 - Value for OPSB5.
Specifies the switching threshold tolerance to be used when calculationmode is set to manual.
Enter this keyword followed by a value for the switching threshold tolerance, in dB. Enter this
keyword alone to display the current value.
The switching threshold tolerance defines the level by which the signal must improve above the
switching threshold before the switch is allowed to revert to its original configuration. For
example, if port A is the active port and has a switchthresh of -18.00 dBm, and the input to port
A goes below -18.00 dBm, a switch will be made to port B. If the switchtol is 1.00 dB, then the
switch will be allowed to revert to port A only if the input power at A is -17.00 dBm or higher.
Switching is not revertive. The switch back to A is made manually or in response to the signal
power at B going below its switchthresh value.
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable to OPSB5. An attempt to change this value will be denied.
5.579.5 Examples
(config-interface-opsb)# 1/4/a
(config-interface-opsb-1/4/a)# switch switchthresh -20

3924 Issue 1
Values
auto - sets the power management of the port to automatic
manual - sets the power management of the port to manual
Set the type of power management for the port. Enter this keyword without any parameters to
display the current type.
Restrictions
The AA2DONW and AA2DONWB card only support manual power management mode.
Sub-command: wavekey
Configures the wavekey settings on the interface. See "config interface powermgmt <line-port-
aid> wavekey" command.
wtdusage
Syntax
wtdusage [<value>]
Values
maint - Suspends channel monitoring and channel power control to allow maintenance
operations involving the WTOCM-type card monitoring the degree. Transition to this value
only permitted from wtocm. Transition from this value only permitted to wtocm. Prompt
requires to confirm with yes or deny with no after entering this value. If no, value is not
changed.
wtdonon - All power per channel measurements and channel alarms are detected using the
WaveTracker Decoder (WTD) equipped on the cards. This setting is used for embedded
WT decoding.
wtdoffoff - All WTD in the line will NOT report power per channel or channel alarms. This is
the default value, and this parameter must be set to an appropriate value as part of turning
up the system.
wtdonoff - All WTD in the line will report power per channel measurements and will NOT
report channel alarms.
wtocm - All power per channel measurements and channel alarms are detected on the
WTOCM card and reported at the assigned LD Card port.
Wtdinferred - Reserved for use in ILA nodes. PPC measurements at certain points are
calculated and reported at LD card output port in the amplified direction (Sig Out or Line
Out depending on LD type).
Default
wtdoffoff
Set the type of channel power monitoring for the port. Enter this keyword without any
parameters to display the current type.

5.595 config interface powermgmt <line-port-aid> wavekey decode
5.595.1 Purpose
This command configures the expected loss parameters for the wavekey decoder port.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.595.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Setting the power management options may impact services.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

number, a slash, and the port number. * will also display any Anydirection

autoegressadjustenabled
Syntax
autoegressadjustenabled [<value>]
Values
{Yes, No}
Default
Yes - Valid for IROADMF, IROADMV and IROADM9M
No - Valid for all other LDs, EILA, EILAL, IPREAMP, IROADM and OMDCL cards.
When set to true by giving keyword yes, sets SCOT to automatically run a limited egress
adjustment in response to triggers from the downstream degree. When set to false by giving
keyword no, this functionality is disabled. Enter the parameter without following keyword yes or
no to show the current value.
Restrictions
