Value "yes" is denied if smoothing is "yes". Refer to config powermgmt egress for
parameter smoothing.
Value "yes" is not applicable in an IROADM OMSP configuration.
Value "yes" is denied if parameter psdmodeenabled is value "yes".

type
Syntax
type [<value>]
Values
auto - sets the power management of the port to automatic
manual - sets the power management of the port to manual
Set the type of power management for the port. Enter this keyword without any parameters to

Restrictions
If the ASWG amplifier is in power mode and power management type is to be changed to
auto, a warning message appears to confirm the change.
In an IROADM OMSP configuration, if this parameter is configured on one path, the same
parameter on the other path is synchronized.
wtdusage
Syntax
wtdusage [<value>]
Values
maint - Suspends channel monitoring and channel power control to allow maintenance
operations involving the WTOCM-type card monitoring the degree. Transition to this value
only permitted from wtocm. Transition from this value only permitted to wtocm. Prompt
requires to confirm with yes or deny with no after entering this value. If no, value is not
changed.
wtdonon - All power per channel (PPC) measurements and channel alarms are detected
using the WaveTracker Decoder (WTD) equipped cards.
wtdoffoff - All WTD in the line will NOT report power per channel or channel alarms. This is
the default for Greenfield networks until provisioned to another value, except if an IROADM
degree.
wtdonoff - All WTD in the line will report power per channel measurements and will NOT
report channel alarms.
wtocm - All PPC measurements and channel alarms are detected on the WTOCM card and
reported at the assigned LD Card port, or at the corresponding IROADM ports, or are
detected by the IROADM card integrated WTOCM.
wtdinferred - Reserved for use in ILA nodes. PPC measurements at certain points are
calculated and reported at LD card output port in the amplified direction (Sig Out or Line
Out depending on LD type).

• If policy is set to unassigned, the power offset is set with respect to 50 GHz reference

• If policy is set to powerdensity, the power offset is set with respect to the value of

parameter value to unassigned.

consistent values.

Values

setfrompolicy
Syntax
setfrompolicy {<OTUBitRate> <Encoding>, all} [<direction>]
Values
all - specifies all system technology types shall be updated by the command.
Configure one or all the system technology type target power offsets on this interface based on
policy parameter. System technology types are in the 1-1000 range for OTUBitRate and
Encoding enumerations.
• If policy is set to powerperchannel, the power offset is set to 0 dB for the specified
technology types.
• If policy is set to powerdensity, the power offset is set with respect to the value of
referencewidth for the specified technology types. In this case the offsets are scaled
based on the usual width given the technology type.
Note that updating the target power offsets in this way will update the power targets for any
channels that use the affected technology types on the interface and direction. Omitting
direction on a bi-directional LD interface will cause both directions to be updated.
Restrictions
This command is denied if parameter policy is set to unassigned.
In an IROADM OMSP configuration, if this parameter is configured on one path, the same
parameter on the other path is synchronized.

This is an access command that is used to perform an automated power adjustment and configure
the options used when performing an automated power adjustment.
Use this command to:
• Access a subcommand that allows you to configure general data used by power management
• Access a subcommand that allows you to adjust the ingress power
• Access a subcommand that allows you to adjust the egress power
• Access a subcommand that allows you to adjust the add direction power in an anydirection add/
drop block.
• Access a subcommand that allows you to adjust the drop direction power in an anydirection add/
drop block.
• Access a subcommand that allows you to display the settings used when adjusting the powers

3964 Issue 1
adjust
Syntax
adjust [<value>]
Values
abort - abort the power adjustment and return the power levels to their original values.
result - display the result of the power adjustment.
status - display the completion status of the power adjustment.
Adjust the add direction power and amplifier gain to reach the target power specified for the
selected add/drop block.
detail
Display details of the add direction of the add/drop block.
gain
Will display the current gain.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingain <= gain <= maxgain + deltamaxgain.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingain, maxgain, or deltamaxgain, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.
maxgain
Syntax
maxgain [<value>]

the values of mingain, maxgain, or deltamaxgain, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.
Restrictions
This parameter does not apply to IROADMF, IROADMV, and IROADM9M egress cards. Its
value is shown as the same as the egress OA gain value in the 'detail' command output.
This parameter does not apply to the C+L packs: AWBEGR, AWBING, AWBILA, OMDCL.
This parameter does not apply to the ASG subtypes in ILA configuration, EILA, EILAL, IR4,
IR9 subtypes, IR20 subtypes, IROADM9R, IRDM20, IRDM32 subtypes and IRDM32L.
mingainc
Syntax
mingainc [<value>]
Displays the minimum allowed gain or that can be set by value. The minimum gain is
determined by the WaveSuite Planner.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingainc <= gainc <= maxgainc + deltamaxgainc.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingainc, maxgainc, or deltamaxgainc, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.
Restrictions
This parameter applies to the C band gain on the following LDs only: AWBEGR.
mingainl
Syntax
mingainl [<value>]
Displays the minimum allowed gain or that can be set by value. The minimum gain is
determined by the WaveSuite Planner.
In auto power management mode, when a power adjustment is run, the amplifier gain will be
set such that mingainl <= gainl <= maxgainl + deltamaxgainl.
Note that this condition is only guaranteed after a power adjustment is run. If the user changes
the values of mingainl, maxgainl, or deltamaxgainl, the above condition may not hold until a
subsequent power adjustment is run.
Restrictions
This parameter applies to the L band gain on the following LDs only: AWBEGR, ASWG-L.

5.605 config powermgmt general
5.605.1 Purpose
Use this command to:
• Access subcommands to provision channel technology types for the node.
• Access subcommands to provision wtocm channel power measurement correction by
technology type.
• Configure network element options for Raman amplifiers.
• Configure network element options for CARDDGR alarm clearing.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.605.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Changing the power management settings may impact services.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
5.605.3 Input Format
config powermgmt general
carddgrclearing
ramanlowgainalgo
techtypes [create | delete | brief | modify]
5.605.4 Input Parameters
Sub-command: carddgrclearing
Syntax
carddgrclearing [<value>]
Values
enabled - Configure automatic clearing of CARDDGR alarm to enabled.
disabled - Configure automatic clearing of CARDDGR alarm to disabled.
Default
enabled
Enables or disables automatic clearing of the CARDDGR alarm. If disabled, the CARDDGR
alarm can only be cleared by resetting the alarmed card. If enabled, when the periodic test of
the criteria for CARDDGR is performed the system clears a raised CARDDGR alarm if the
defects are not present. Enabling or disabling is node scope for the card types applicable for
the CARDDGR alarm.

Syntax

Allows user to define new channel optical technology types for the node. These types must be
defined to support features using the technology types. The information about which technology
types need to be defined for the node will normally come from the WaveSuite Planner (WS-P).

technology. <OTUBitRate> and <Encoding> are enumerated values, therefore integers are
expected.
brief

This command automatically adjusts the NE ingress power in one direction and configures

ingress LD when applicable.

the adjustment.

subsequent power adjustment is run.

5.607 show interface powermgmt
5.607.1 Purpose
This command displays the power management options for the specified ingress or egress port, or
anydirection node Add/Drop port.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.607.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.607.3 Input Format
show interface powermgmt <port-aid>
5.607.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/LINE - Bi-directional LD cards
<shelf>/<slot>/LINEOUT - Uni-directional LD cards
<shelf>/<slot>/LINEIN - Uni-directional LD cards, RA2P, or RA2P-96
<shelf>/<slot>/SIG - WR8-88A cards
<shelf>/<slot>/LINEOUT - IROADM cards
<shelf>/<slot>/LINEIN - IROADM cards or RA2P
<shelf>/<slot>/LINEIN - AWBING, AWBILA, RA4P, RA5P or RA5PB
<shelf>/<slot>/LINEOUT - AWBILA, AWBEGR
<shelf>/<slot>/LINEOUT - IPREAMP
<shelf>/<slot>/LINEIN - IPREAMP
<shelf>/<slot>/LINE{1,2}IN - EILA, EILAL
<shelf>/<slot>/LINE{1,2}OUT - EILA, EILAL, OMDCL
* - display list of ports
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number, or enter * to display a brief summary for all of the ingress
and egress ports on the network element. * will also display any Anydirection Add/Drop blocks
by <sig-port-aid>. <linein-port-aid> (uni-directional LD cards, IROADM cards or RA cards)
supports a limited set of commands.
Core optics management commands
Optical power management commands

4052 Issue 1
policy
Displays the policy for handling technology type dependent target power offsets on this
interface.
For software upgrades, if a system defined technology type is new in the release:
• If policy is set to unassigned, the power offset is set with respect to 50 GHz reference
width.
• If policy is set to powerperchannel, the power offset is set to 0 dB.
• If policy is set to powerdensity, the power offset is set with respect to the value of
referencewidth.
Note that for technology types existing in the release being upgraded from, the target power
offsets are not changed by the software upgrade. System defined technology types are in the
1-1000 range for OTUBitRate and Encoding.
referencewidth
Displays the reference width. Used in combination with the policy value to determine the effect
of setfrompolicy sub-command and defaults for future system determined technology types
which become available after software upgrade to a new release. When policy is powerdensity,
target power offset will be calculated as 10*log10( Width for technology type / reference width).
5.613.5 Examples
#show interface powermgmt 1/2/lineout poweroffsetdata out

Power
(enum) (enum) Description Description
Offset(dB)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1 1 otm10G709 nrz 0.00
1 7 otm10G709 nrzCFP1 0.00
2 1 otm11G049 nrz 0.00
...
#show interface powermgmt 1/2/lineout poweroffsetdata referencewidth
Tech Type Target Power Offset Reference Width: 75.0 GHz
#show interface powermgmt 1/2/lineout poweroffsetdata policy
Tech Type Target Power Offset Policy: powerdensity

5.615 show powermgmt
5.615.1 Purpose
This command displays the network element power management status or configuration.
Use this command to:
• Display the current power management configuration on the network element.
• Display the status of a power balancing operation on the network element.
• Display the sum of channel power on the network element.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.615.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.615.3 Input Format

5.616 show powermgmt sumochpowers
5.616.1 Purpose
This command displays the sum of the channel powers on the network element.
Use this command to:
• Display the sum of measured channel powers on the network element.
• Display the sum of expected channel powers on the network element.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.616.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.616.3 Input Format
show powermgmt sumochpowers <list-of-xc-ids> <list-of-port-aids>
5.616.4 Input Parameters
<list-of-xc-ids>
Syntax
<xc-id> [<xc-id>]*
all
Values
<xc-id> - Integer value
all - skip the filter on specific parameter, if "all" is entered.
Default
Entry required
Specifies one or list of xc-ids for adding the channel powers on specified ports. Up to 140 xc-ids
can be entered.
Enter the list of xc-ids with a space in between each <xc-id>.
<list-of-port-aids>
Syntax
<port-aid> [<port-aid>]
Values
<port-aid>:
<shelf>/<slot>/<port>

4096 Issue 1
Wavekey general commands
5.617 show wavekey
5.617.1 Purpose
This command displays Wavelength Tracker information.
Use this command to:
• Display the WaveKey properties on an interface port that has Wavelength Tracker monitoring
capabilities.
• Display the power and programmed WaveKeys on the interface ports that generate the
Wavelength Tracker WaveKeys (OT, SVAC, and MVAC cards).
• Display the unexpected WaveKeys detected on a port.
• Display the WaveKey usage per allocation domain.
Note: If an optical line has been provisioned to use the WTOCM then wavekey reports will display -
for ports other than LD card LineOut and SigOut.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.617.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.617.3 Input Format
show wavekey
unexpected
wtdomain
wtmonitor
wtsource
5.617.4 Input Parameters
Sub-command: unexpected
Display the unexpected WaveKeys detected on a port. See "show wavekey unexpected".
Sub-command: wtdomain
Display the Wave Key usage and which channels are unlocked for Wave Key re-use, per
domain. See "show wavekey wtdomain".
Sub-command: wtmonitor
Displays the WaveKey properties on an interface port that has Wavelength Tracker monitoring
capabilities. See "show wavekey wtmonitor".
Core optics management commands
Wavekey general commands

5.618 show wavekey unexpected
5.618.1 Purpose
This command displays the unexpected WaveKeys detected on a port.
Use this command without any parameters to show the unexpected WaveKeys detected on all ports
on the network element or use the command line parameters as filters to display the current
WaveKey settings for:
• A specific port.
• The in or out direction on the port.
• A specific channel carried over the port.
Note this command does not display unexpected keys for a WTOCM-type port interface directly.
(Unexpected keys detected by a WTOCM-type card port for provisioned channels will be reported
to the monitored port, e.g. LD LINEOUT, and displayed by this command.) See related commands
for WTOCM-type port interface command to display unexpected key information directly at a
WTOCM-type card port interface.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.618.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.618.3 Input Format
show wavekey unexpected
<port-aid> [in | out]
5.618.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/<port> - Valid Wavelength Tracker decoder port.
Displays only the unexpected WaveKeys detected on the decoder for the given port for all
applicable directions for the port. Omit this keyword to display all unexpected WaveKeys
detected on the node.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
in
Syntax
in [<frequency>]
Core optics management commands
Wavekey general commands

© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
For <frequency>:
<flexgridchannel> - selection of the channel.
Displays only the unexpected WaveKeys detected on the decoder for the given direction. Enter
this keyword followed by a channel number to display the unexpected WaveKeys for that
channel only.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <flexgridchannel> range. Only
provisioned channels can be retrieved.
out
Syntax
out [<frequency>]
Values
For <frequency>:
<flexgridchannel> - selection of the channel.

channel only.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <flexgridchannel> range. Only
provisioned channels can be retrieved.

<flexgridchannel> - selection of the channel.
Shows the programmed and received WaveKeys and channel power inforrmation for the out
direction on the selected port. Enter this keyword followed by a channel frequency to display
WaveKey information for that channel only, or enter this keyword without any parameters to
display WaveKey information for all channels on the port.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <flexgridchannel> range. Only
provisioned channels can be retrieved.
Restrictions
This parameter is not available if the Wavelength Tracker decoder for the given <port-aid>
does not support the "out" direction.
summary
Displays the expected channels and summary of expected keys configured, if channel is
received, and if unexpected channel is received. Only provisioned channels are displayed.

4108 Issue 1
5.620 show wavekey wtsource
5.620.1 Purpose
This command displays the power and programmed WaveKeys on the interface ports that generate
the Wavelength Tracker WaveKeys. These ports reside on SVAC, MVAC and OT cards.
Use this command to:
• Display a summary of the expected and measured output power on all channels with an admin
state of up
• Display all of the programmed WaveKeys on every OT, SVAC, and MVAC port on the network
element.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.620.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.620.3 Input Format
show wavekey wtsource
power
keys
5.620.4 Input Parameters
power
Displays a summary of the expected and measured output power on all channels which are in
admin state of up.
keys
Displays all of the programmed WaveKeys on every OT and SVAC port on the network
element.
The list includes for each port the:
• WaveKey transmitter state
• administrative state
• operational state
5.620.5 Examples
# show wavekey wtsource
# show wavekey wtsource power
Admin Oper

4110 Issue 1
5.621 show wavekey wtdomain
5.621.1 Purpose
This command displays the usage of Wavelength Tracker key signatures in the network.
Wavelength Tracker key signatures are allocated to WDM channels based on assignment bins for
ranges of optical channel frequencies. This command's output table shows the start frequency of
each bin. The frequency displayed for each bin is included in the allocation bin. The highest
frequency bin for a transmission band ends 25 GHz above the displayed frequency.
Use this command to:
• Display a summary of Wavelength Tracker signature usage per allocation bin per domain and
transmission band.
• Display a summary of Wavelength Tracker duplicate locked/un-locked state per allocation bin per
domain and transmission band.
• Display the WT signature usage and duplicate locked/un-locked state for the allocation bin
corresponding to a given optical channel frequency.
5.621.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.621.3 Input Format
show wavekey wtdomain <domain>
trxband
channel
5.621.4 Input Parameters
<domain>
Values
0 - WT domain number.
The Wavelength Tracker key assignment domain number. Presently the value is restricted to 0.
When entered with no following key words, displays the full summary table of WT key usage for
the domain number and transmission bands supported by the node.
trxband
Syntax
trxband <band>
Values
{c, l} - the WDM transmission band
Core optics management commands
Wavekey general commands

5.622 config interface <card-name> <port-aid> wavekey
5.622.1 Purpose
This command configures the Wavelength Tracker properties on an optics card interface with
Wavelength Tracker decoder function.
Use this command to:
• Access commands to configure the Wavelength Tracker properties of a channel.
• Display a table of expected channels with indication if the channels are missing or not missing.
• Display a table summary for the expected channels indicated their configuration of keys,
received status and unexpected channel status.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.622.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Wavelength Tracker WaveKeys must be consistent across the network. Expected power
and power deviations must conform to the link budget.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
5.622.3 Input Format
config interface <card-name> <port-aid> wavekey

5.623 config interface <card-name> <port-aid> wavekey in <frequency>
5.623.1 Purpose
This command configures the Wavelength Tracker properties of receive ports with the Wavelength
Tracker functionality on optics cards.
Use this command to:
• Display current Wavelength Tracker settings for a channel.
• Configure expected power for a channel.
• Configure power deviation threshold for a channel.
• Configure power tolerance for a channel.
• Show a list of unexpected Wave Keys received on a channel.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.623.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Wavelength Tracker WaveKeys must be consistent across the network. Expected power
and power deviations must conform to the link budget.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

4132 Issue 1
Values
help - display the valid and default values.
-99..21.00 - specify the expected input power in dBm.
off - disable wavekey monitoring.
Default
-99 dBm.
Configures the expected power for the channel (dBm).
Restrictions
If the port is auto power managed, the expected power cannot be set, except for the
following ports when the involved connection is a dangling add or add/drop connection:
WR20-TF ADT or AD ports, WR20-TFM ADT or AD ports, IROADM9R ADT ports, IRDM20
ADT ports, WR8-88A(F) Addin ports.
devpower
Syntax
devpower [help | <value>]
Values
help - Display the valid and default values.
0.00..10.00 - Specify the power deviation threshold in dB.
Default
2.5 dB
Configures the expected power deviation (dB). The deviation is the amount the channel power
can deviate from the expected value before being considered out of range.
tolpower
Syntax
tolpower [help | <value>]
Values
help - display the valid and default values.
0.00..5.00 - specify the tolerance value in dB.
Default
0 dB
Configures the expected power tolerence (dB). The expected power +/- the deviation -/+ the
tolerance defines the threshold for considering a channel in range.
unexpected
Displays a list of unexpected WaveKeys received on the port.

detail
Displays the current Wavelength Tracker configuration for the specified channel and measured
channel power.
power
Syntax
power [help | <value> | off]
Values
help - display the valid and default values.
-99..21.00 - specify the expected output power in dBm.
off - disable wavekey monitoring.
Default
-99 dBm.
Configures the expected power for the channel (dBm).
devpower
Syntax
devpower [help | <value>]
Values
help - Display the valid and default values.
0.0..10.00 - Specify the power deviation threshold in dB.
Default
2.5 dB
Configures the expected power deviation (dB). The deviation is the amount the channel power
can deviate from the expected value before being considered out of range.
tolpower
Syntax
tolpower [help | <value>]
Values
help - display the valid and default values.
0.00..5.00 - specify the tolerance value in dB.

5.625 show interface <card-name> <port-aid> wavekey
5.625.1 Purpose
This command displays channel information as detected by the Wavelength Tracker decoder.
Use this command to:
• Display a table of expected channels, their configuration for Wavelength Tracker and current
measured values.
• Display a table of expected channels with indication if the channels are missing or not missing.
• Display a table summary for the expected channels indicated their configuration of keys,
received status and unexpected channel status.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.625.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.625.3 Input Format

Values
For <frequency>:
<flexgridchannel> - selection of the channel.
Displays the Wavelength Tracker properties for specific wavelengths passing through the port in
the receive direction. If optional value <frequency> is given, only the row for the corresponding
channel is shown.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <flexgridchannel> range. Only
provisioned channels can be retrieved.
Restrictions
This parameter is not available if the Wavelength Tracker decoder for the given <port-aid>
does not support the "in" direction.
missing
Displays the expected channels and whether they are missing or not missing. Only provisioned
channels will be retrieved.
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable to EILA, EILAL, IPREAMP, IRDM32 subtypes, IRDM32L or
cards without Wavelength tracker decoder capabilities.
Sub-command: out
Syntax
out [<frequency>]
Values
For <frequency>:
<flexgridchannel> - selection of the channel.
Displays the Wavelength Tracker properties for specific wavelengths passing through the port in
the transmit direction. If optional value <frequency> is given, only the row for the corresponding
channel is shown.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <flexgridchannel> range. Only
provisioned channels can be retrieved.
Restrictions
This parameter is not available if the Wavelength Tracker decoder for the given <port-aid>
does not support the "out" direction.
summary
Displays the expected channels and summary of expected keys configured, if channel is
received, and if unexpected channel is received. Only provisioned channels are displayed.
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable to ipreamp card.

4164 Issue 1
Show channel power and WaveKey information where applicable from the optical channel
monitor with respect to the given <port-aid>. Optionally follow with a channel frequency to
display only that channel or summary for a summary of all channels. For channel, detected
power is reported with respect to the integrated OCM input itself, and reported with respect to
the related tap point from the optical amplifier module corresponding to the given <port-aid>.
For the LINEOUT, the tap point is before the output VOA after the gain block. For the LINEIN,
the tap point is after the gain block.
Note: for IRDM32 subtypes and IRDM32L waveKey information is not applicable.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <flexgridchannel> range. Only
provisioned channels can be configured.
unexpected
Show a summary of channels being detected that are reporting unexpected channels with
respect to the given <port-aid>. This command shows detail for both provisioned channel slots
and unprovisioned channel slots. The reported channel frequencies are approximate for
unprovisioned channels. Power values are reported with respect to the integrated OCM itself.
Restrictions
For IROADM with ASE line loading enabled, this command returns no output as spectrum
is filled with traffic carrying channels or ASE channels.

For MXN based add/drop block it specifies the shelf/slot of the MXN connected to an IRDM20
degree.
Restrictions
For DegreeXPTest, the applicable cards are IRDM20, IRDM32 and IR20. Path restricted to
between IRDM20 end points or between an IRDM20 end point and an IRDM32 or IR20 end
point.
detail
Displays the detailed settings for the test function. The output includes the
• source,
• destination,
• transmit and receive power of the test channel,
• test result, and
• date of the test.
Note: The test result column in the display of this command should be kept aligned with the
result command.
record
Syntax

Values
1..3

width
Syntax
width [<value>]
Values
{37.5..125.0} - GHz, in steps of 12.5 GHz.
Default
50 GHz
Specifies the spectral slot width of the alien OT channel on the port.
Restrictions
The allowed values are card depending.
CWR8-88 ports:
• 50 GHz
ASC2 subtypes, ASC4 subtypes, MCS8-16, MCS8-16L, MCS1615, MCS1615L, MLFSB,
MXN824, PSC1-6 ports:
• 37.5, 50, 62.5, 75, 87.5, 100, 125 GHz
SFD44 and SFD44B ports:
• 37.5, 50,
• 62.5, 75, 87.5 (only when ITLB or ITLU is used)
SFD48 ports:
• 37.5, 50, 62.5, 75, 87.5, 100 GHz
SFD64 ports:
• 37.5, 50, 62.5, 75 GHz
The parameter cannot be changed, when a PCONN XC is in place.
5.634.5 Examples
# config alienOT mcs1615 1/24/AD1 1 modify frequency 9601.875
# config alienOT mcs1615 1/24/AD1 1 modify width 50
# config alienOT mcs1615 1/24/AD1 1 modify compensationmodule C2ACO
# config alienOT mcs1615 1/24/AD1 1 modify profileid 20
# config alienOT mcs1615 1/24/AD1 1 modify description "known profile and known comp
module"
# config alienOT mcs1615 1/24/AD1 1 modify description "real alien configuration"
# config alienOT mcs1615 1/24/AD1 1 modify frequency 9601.875
# config alienOT mcs1615 1/24/AD1 1 modify width 50
# config alienOT mcs1615 1/24/AD1 1 modify compensationmodule ALIEN
# config alienOT mcs1615 1/24/AD1 1 modify profileid 99999

5.635 show alienOT
5.635.1 Purpose
This command displays the parameter for alien OT channels on the access port on the following
cards:
• asc2 subtypes ({A..F}{1..2}IN ports)
• asc4 subtypes ({A..D}{1..4}IN ports)
• cwr8-88 (CLS port)
• mcs1615 (AD ports)
• mcs1615l (AD ports)
• mcs8-16 (AD ports)
• mcs8-16l (AD ports)
• mlfsb (M{1..6}{A..F}{1,2} ports)
• mxn824 (AD ports)
• psc1-6 ({A..E}{1..6} ports)
• sfd44
• sfd44b
• sfd48
• sdd64
Use this command to:
• List configured alien OT channels on the network element, a card type or an individual port
• Display individual parameters for a selected alien OT channel
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
5.635.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
5.635.3 Input Format

has-add-xc
Displays the unidirectional Add PCONN XC id of the alien OT channel.
Return Values:
• 0: no PCONN XC present
• >0: Identification number of the PCONN XC
has-drop-xc
Displays the unidirectional Drop PCONN XC id of the alien OT channel.
Return Values:
• 0: no PCONN XC present
• >0: Identification number of the PCONN XC
profileid
Displays the OTSiG profile identifier of the alien OT channel.
Return values:
• >0: assigned OTSiG profile with the corresponding profileid number.
width
Displays the spectral slot width of the alien OT channel.

4246 Issue 1
11DPE12 interface commands
6.2 config interface 11dpe12
6.2.1 Purpose
This command configures the interface ports on the 11DPE12 card. Use this command to access
subcommands that allow you to configure the client C{1-12} ports, the line ports L{1-2} or eVOA
ports VA{1..2}.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.2.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
6.2.3 Input Format
config interface 11dpe12 <port-aid>
6.2.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..12} - Specifies client port 1 ~ port 12
<shelf>/<slot>/L{1..2} - Specifies line port 1 ~ port 2
<shelf>/<slot>/VA{1..2} - Specifies eVOA port 1 ~ port 2
* - display list of ports
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number, or * to list all of the 11DPE12 cards on the network
element.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
6.2.5 Examples
#config interface 11dpe12 *
Port Admin Oper State
Location Function Description Dir State State Qualifier
---------------------------------------------------------
3/2/L1 Network Bi Up Down SGEO
3/2/L2 Network Bi Up Down SGEO
3/2/C1 Client Bi Up Down SGEO
3/2/C2 Client Bi Up Down SGEO
3/2/C3 Client Bi Up Down SGEO

6.3 config interface 11dpe12 <client-port-aid>
6.3.1 Purpose
This command configures the C{1-12} client ports on the 11DPE12 card.
Use this command to:
• Specify a description for the port
• Display the current settings for the port
• Set the 1 Gb Ethernet attributes
• Set the FE attributes
• Set the loopback mode
• Set the performance monitoring
• Set the administrative state
• Set the client port type
• Set the virtual time slot attributes
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.3.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
6.3.3 Input Format

pm
state

<vtsn>

6.7 config interface 11dpe12 <client-port-aid> <vtsn>
6.7.1 Purpose
This command configures the C{1-12} client ports with the CE-VLAN ID map attributes on the
11DPE12 card. This command is only applicable when the card mode is set to Subrate or QinQ
mode (See "config card 11dpe12 <slot-aid>"). Use this command to set the CE-VLAN ID map for
each VTS within the port.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.7.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
6.7.3 Input Format
config interface 11dpe12 <client-port-aid> <vtsn>
cevlanid
6.7.4 Input Parameters
<client-port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..12} - Specifies client port 1 ~ 12
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
<vtsn>
Values
{vts1, vts2, vts3, vts4, vts5, vts6, vts7, vts8, vts9, vts10}
Specifies the virtual time slot within the port.
cevlanid
Syntax
cevlanid [<value>] [direction]
Values
Egress - The mapping direction is out from the port
Ingress - The mapping direction is into the port
IngressAndEgress - Ingress and Egress
Configures the CE-VLAN ID map for the specified VTS within the port.

Enter the keyword followed by the ID number or ID ranges separated by comma.
In Subrate mode, the client VTS/CE-VLAN ID mapping is bidirectional. Users do not need to

In QinQ mode, the client VTS/CE-VLAN ID mapping is unidirectional. Users must specify the
CE-VLAN ID map direction.
6.7.5 Examples
# config interface 11dpe12 1/7/C1 vts2 cevlanid 1-200,300
# config interface 11dpe12 1/7/c1 vts1 cevlanid none

# config interface 11dpe12 1/7/C1 vts2 cevlanid none egress
# config interface 11dpe12 1/7/C1 vts2 cevlanid 1-200 ingressAndEgress
# config interface 11dpe12 1/7/C1 vts2 cevlanid none ingressAndEgress
# config interface 11dpe12 1/3/C1 vts1 cevlanid 1-200
Error: Request Failed - invalid card rate mode.
# config interface 11dpe12 1/3/C1 vts1 cevlanid 1,2,4,1-200 egress
Error: Request Failed - invalid card rate mode. Only QinQ mode needdirection.
# config interface 11dpe12 1/3/C1 vts1 cevlanid 1,2,4,1-200

# config interface 11dpe12 1/3/C1 vts1 cevlanid none
Error: Request Failed - invalid card rate mode. QinQ mode must provide direction.

Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual

Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

aid> state" for details.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual

bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

aid> state" for details.

och - to assign the port.
unassigned - to set the port as unassigned.
Specifies the port type.

command is denied.

6.19.1 Purpose
This command displays the interface ports on the 11DPE12 card. Use this command to access
subcommands that allow you to configure the client ports C{1-12}, the line ports L{1-2}, or eVOA
ports VA{1..2}.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.19.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
6.19.3 Input Format
show interface 11dpe12 <port-aid>
6.19.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..12} - Specifies client port 1 ~ 12
<shelf>/<slot>/L{1..2} - Specifies line port 1 ~ 2
<shelf>/<slot>/VA{1..2} - Specifies eVOA port 1 ~ port 2
* - display list of ports
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number, or * to list all of the 11DPE12 interfaces on the network
element.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
6.19.5 Examples
# show interface 11dpe12 *

3/2/C3 Client Bi Up Down SGEO
3/2/C4 Client Bi Down Down UAS
3/2/C5 Client Bi Down Down UAS

4362 Issue 1
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

<port-aid> state" for details.

laserOn - transmitter stays on
laserOff - turn off the transmitter
Default
laserOn
Specifies how the near end client facing transmitter port reacts to a Loss of Signal (LOS), Loss
of Frame (LOF) or other defects from the far-end client-facing receiver.
Restrictions
This attribute can be provisioned only when the portRole is UNI and FlowCM is APS/PCC
or CCM.
lptca
Syntax
lptca[disable | shutdownany | shutdownall]
Values
disable - disable the LPT consequent action
shutdownany - turn off the transmitter when the client port any flow has failure
shutdownall - turn off the transmitter when the client port all flows have failure
Default
disable
Specifies how the near end client facing transmitter port reacts to Link pass through function
(pass the Loss of Signal (LOS), Loss of SYNC (LSS) or other defects from the far-end client-
facing receiver).

4390 Issue 1
Values

For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote

NE.

rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

Default
5 seconds
Specify the SLR timeout timer, in seconds, expressed as a decimal integer, applied for all MEPs
on this card. This value is used to override the default timeout value and is the amount of time
that the MEP waits for a reply message after sending the message request. Upon the expiration
of message timeout, the requesting card assumes that the message response is not received.
Any response received after the request times out is silently discarded.

pmon".

create
Syntax
create [manet [ [maname <value>] [format <value>] [ccminterval <value>] ] | macomp [vid
<integer>] ]
Creates an MA within a MD on the pack. An MA includes a manet and a macomp.
Parameter definition for maname:
Values
<string>
Set the name of the maintenance name. It is unique within the specified maintenance domain.
If MD name format is 'character string', then the Maname is {1..(44-X)} characters, X is the
length of MD name. If MD name format is 'none', then the Maname is {1..45} characters.
If MD name format is 'none' and the MA name format is ITU ICC format, then the Maname is 13
ASCII chars string. (Note: The ITU ICC consists of two subfields: the ITU carrier code (ICC)
followed by a unique MEG ID code (UMC).
The ITU Carrier Code consists of 1 6 left-justified characters, alphabetic (that is, {A..Z}) and or
numeric (that is, {0..9}). The UMC code immediately follows the ICC and shall consist of {7..12}
characters, with trailing NULLs, completing the 13-character MEG ID Value. UMC character can
be any character defined in ITU-T T.50, excluding " and space. The UMC shall be a matter for
the organization to which the ICC has been assigned, provided that uniqueness within a
country is guaranteed.)
Parameter definition for format:
Values
string
ITUICC
Default
string

decimal places. {0..100.0000000}. '0' means TCA is disabled.

0

detail
Display specific MEP on demand single end loss measurement information.
6.108.5 Output Parameters
MEP on-demand Synthetic loss measurement
The following information is displayed for specific MEP on-demand Synthetic loss measurement:
Label Description
MAC-address specify the Unicast MAC address for the destination. 48 - gain in bytes.
Note: as this attribute is not stored in DB, so the value retrieved may be 00:00:00:00:00:00
Priority specify the priority of LMM packet will be sent to the destination. {0..7}.
7
Send-count The number of messages to send, expressed as a decimal integer. The count parameter is used to override the
default number of message requests sent. Each message request must either timeout or receive a reply before
the next message request is sent. The message interval value must be expired before the next message request
is sent. {2..101}.
2
interval The interval parameter in 0.1 seconds, expressed as a decimal integer. This parameter is used to override the
default request message send interval and defines the minimum amount of time that must expire before the next
message request is sent. {100ms, 1s, 10s, 1m, 10m}.
10
TF_TF The total number of service packets received during the execution of the test. {1..100}
TF_LF The total number of service packets transmitted from the local node but not received on the remote node during
the execution of the test. {1..100}10
TN_TF The total number of service packets transmitted from the remote node. {1..100}
TN_LF The total number of service packets transmitted from the remote node but not received on the local node during
the execution of the test the number of packets received during the execution of the test. {1..100}
Unack The number of unacknowledged lost LM packets during the execution of the test, that is the number of LMM
packets transmitted from the local node but LMR not received on the remote node during the execution of the
test. {1..100}

# config card 11DPE12A 1/7 ethoam md1 ma10 mep1 two-way-lm-test detail

6.109.5 Output Parameters
MEP on-demand Synthetic loss measurement
The following information is displayed for specific MEP on-demand Synthetic loss measurement:
Label Description
Test-ID a value to identify a unique test flow, automatically assigned by NE. 48 - gain in bytes MAC
Dest-MAC-
address
specify the Unicast MAC address for destination. NOTE - As this attribute is not stored in DB, so the value
retrieved may be 00:00:00:00:00:00.
Priority specify the priority of SLM packet will be sent to the destination. {0..7}.Default: 7
Remote-MEPID MEP ID of the peer MEP.
Send-count The number of messages to send, expressed as a decimal integer. The count parameter is used to override the
default number of message requests sent. Each message request must either timeout or receive a reply before the
next message request is sent. The message interval value must be expired before the next message request is
sent. {1..100}.Default: 1
Size This is the size of the data portion of the data TLV, in bytes. If 0 is specified no data TLV is added to the packet.
{0..1500} - gain in bytes.Default: 0
Interval The interval parameter in 0.1 seconds, expressed as a decimal integer. This parameter is used to override the
default request message send interval and defines the minimum amount of time that must expire before the next
message request is sent. {100ms, 1s, 10s, 1m, 10m}.Default: 10
Received-count the number of SLR packets received during the execution of the test. {1..100}.
In-loss the number of SLR packets transmitted from the remote node but not received on the local node during the
execution of the test the number of packets received during the execution of the test. {1..100}
Unack the number of unacknowledged lost packets during the execution of the test, that is the number of SLM packets
transmitted from the local node but the corresponding SLR not received on the remote node during the execution
of the test. {1..100}
Out-loss the number of SLM packets transmitted from the local node but not received on the remote node during the
execution of the test. {1..100}

slash.

supported shelf type.

ethoam pmon-lm-policy".

Sub-command: pmon-dm-policy

11DPE12e interface commands
6.119 config interface 11dpe12e
6.119.1 Purpose
This command displays the interface ports on the 11dpe12e card. Use this command to access
subcommands that allow you to configure the client C{1-12} ports, the line ports L{1-2} or eVOA
ports VA{1..2}.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.119.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
6.119.3 Input Format
config interface 11dpe12e <port-aid>
6.119.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..12} - Specifies client port 1 ~ port 12
<shelf>/<slot>/L{1..2} - Specifies line port 1 ~ port 2
<shelf>/<slot>/VA{1..2} - Specifies eVOA port 1 ~ port 2
* - display list of ports
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number, or * to list all of the 11dpe12e cards on the network
element.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
6.119.5 Examples
#config interface 11dpe12e *
Port Admin Oper State
Location Function Description Dir State State Qualifier
--------------------------------------------------------------
3/2/L1 Network Bi Up Down SGEO
3/2/L2 Network Bi Up Down SGEO
3/2/C1 Client Bi Up Down SGEO
3/2/C2 Client Bi Up Down SGEO
3/2/C3 Client Bi Up Down SGEO

stpid
Syntax
stpid [stpid1 | stpid2 | stpid3 | stpid4]
Values
stpid1 - The client stpid is provisioned with global stpid1.
stpid2 - The client stpid is provisioned with global stpid2.
stpid3 - The client stpid is provisioned with global stpid3.
stpid4 - The client stpid is provisioned with global stpid4.
Default
stpid1
SVLAN Tag Protocol Identifier (STPID) - it is used for CE-VLAN tagged packets in QinQ mode.
synceoppmode
Syntax
synceoprmode [sync | non-sync]
Values
sync - Configure SyncE Operation Mode to sync
non-sync - Configure SyncE Operation Mode to non-sync
Default
sync
Configure port Synchronous Ethernet Operation Mode. When the port is in SYNC mode,
recovered clock of its input signal can be selected as a reference clock to the system clock.
When the port is in NON-SYNC mode, the recovered clock of its input signal shall not be a
candidate to system timing references.
6.121.5 Examples
# config interface 11dpe12e 1/7/c1 1gbe stpid stpid2
# config interface 11dpe12e 1/7/c1 1gbe ssmtrans NONE
# config interface 11dpe12e 1/7/c1 1gbe SYNCEOPRMODE NON-SYNC
# config interface 11dpe12e 1/7/c1 1gbe autoneg disable
Error: Request Failed - invalid port state
# config interface 11dpe12e 1/7/c1 1gbe stpid stpid2
Error: Request Failed - invalid card rate mode

Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

<port-aid> state" for details.

This command configures the ODU2 attributes for the LINE L{1-2} ports on the 11dpe12e card.

6.129 config interface 11dpe12e <line-port-aid> pm
6.129.1 Purpose
This command configures the LINE ports L{1-2} with Performance Monitoring attributes on the
11dpe12e card.
Use this command to:
• Clear current 15-minute and 1-day bins in all groups on this line interface
• Configure the digital wrapper group options
• Configure the Ethernet group options
• Configure the received optical power group PM options
• Configure the transmitted optical power group PM options
• Configure the PCS layer monitor group PM options
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.129.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
6.129.3 Input Format
config interface 11dpe12e <line-port-aid> pm
clearall
dw
ethernet
opr
opt
pcs
6.129.4 Input Parameters
<line-port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/L{1..2} - Specifies the line port 1 ~ port 2
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
clearall
Clears current 15-minute and 1-day bins in all groups on this interface.

• Set the port type

Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information

December 2024
4638 Issue 1
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 11dpe12e
<port-aid> state" for details.
type
Syntax
type [och | unassigned]
Values
och - to assign the port.
unassigned - to set the port as unassigned.
Specifies the port type.
If a new value is requested to be set for this parameter and rmconport !="" is present, then the
command is denied.

ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]

rejected.

up

Default

Specifies the mapping mode for constant bit rate client signals OC48 and STM16 into OPUk.
Restrictions
This parameter applies only for OC48 and STM16.
If LO ODUK XC exists on the port or the container is not null, the operation to modify
mappingmode shall be rejected.
Mixing async-mappingmode OC48/STM16 clients with other GMP-mapping clients (e.g.
GbE, FE, OC3/STM1, OC12/STM4) within the same port group is rejected. 11DPM4M has
two port groups, i.e group C{1..4} and group C{5..8}.
• if there is already an existing port provisioned with the GMP mapping clients, then
provisioning with OC48/STM16 with asynch mappingmode within the same port group is
rejected
• if there is an OC48/STM16 client port provisioned with asynch mappingmode, then
provisioning with other client signal type within the same port group is rejected

4734 Issue 1
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual

bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 11DPM4M
<port-aid> state" for details.
type
Syntax

Values
otu2 - to assign the port.
unassigned - to set the port as unassigned.
Specifies the port type.
Note: If Line port is associated with any LO-ODUk cross-connection, setting the port to
unassigned is denied.
If a new value is requested to be set for this parameter and rmconport !="" is present, then the
command is denied.

Values

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
1gbe - for 1 Gbps Ethernet client
fc100 - for FC100 Fibre Channel client
fc200 - for FC200 Fibre Channel client
fc400 - for FC400 Fibre Channel client
fe - for 100Mbps Fast Ethernet client
oc3 - for SONET OC-3 client
oc12 - for SONET OC-12 client
oc48 - for SONET OC-48 client
stm1 - for SDH STM-1 client
stm4 - for SDH STM-4 client
stm16 - for SDH STM-16 client
otu1 - for OTU1 client
unassigned - to set the port as unassigned
Configures the port type.
The 8 client ports of 11DPM8 are split into two groups, C1,C2,C3,C4 are in one group,
C5,C6,C7,C8 are in another group.
Each group supports up to 8 timeslot of OPU2 (i.e. 1xODU2), the mapping of client type and
number of TS are as the following table.
For example, in case C1 and C2 are assigned as FC400 and each of them will occupy 4 TS of
OPU2, the total 8 TS are all in use. Since no TS is left for the other two ports in the same group,
C3 and C4 cannot be assigned anymore.
Table 6-11 Timeslots (TS) per Client Type
Client Type Number of TS
FE 1
GbE 1
OTU1 2
OC3/STM1 1
OC12/STM4 1
OC48.STM16 2
FC100 1
FC200 2
FC400 4

mappingmode
Syntax
mappingmode [ async | bitsync ]
Values
async - asynchronous mapping CBR into ODUk information structure by the ODUkP/CBRx
adaptation function.
bitsync - synchronous mapping CBR into ODUk information structure by the ODUkP
adaptation function.
Default
bitsync
Specifies the mapping mode for constant bit rate client signals OC48 and STM16 into OPUk.
Restrictions
This parameter applies only for OC48 and STM16.
Mixing async-mappingmode OC48/STM16 clients with other GMP-mapping clients (e.g.
GbE, FE, OC3/STM1, OC12/STM4) within the same port group is rejected. 11DPM8 has
two port groups, i.e group C{1..4} and group C{5..8}
• if there is already an existing port provisioned with the GMP mapping clients, then
provisioning with OC48/STM16 with asynch mappingmode within the same port group is
rejected
• if there is an OC48/STM16 client port provisioned with asynch mappingmode, then
provisioning with other client signal type within the same port group is rejected
If LO ODUK XC exists on the port or the container is not null, the operation to modify
mappingmode is rejected.

Values

"" for <identifier>

For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

aid> state" for details.

unassigned - to set the port as unassigned.
Specifies the port type.

unassigned is denied.
If a new value is requested to be set for this parameter and rmconport !="" is present, then the
command is denied.

Restrictions
The range upper limit is limited depending on the pluggable modules inserted in the line

WDM node a cluster O-CONN is provisioned to the line port).

Set to ains to configure Automatic In-Service.
ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value

Set the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port.
Enter number of hours and minutes
For system default value see "config general ainstimer"
enabled

disabled

down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This may
affect service.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
If a GCC channel associated with the port is enabled then setting the port to down shall be
rejected.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Set to up to enable the port.

Values
For type 3gsdi and hdsdi:
nominal - nominal bitrate for 3gsdi (2.97Gbps) or hdsdi (1.485Gbps)

nominal

signals.
Restrictions
For hdsdi and 3gsdi signal type provision, the sdirate is optional. It is allowed to enter hdsdi/
3gsdi type either with or without specifying sdirate value. if sdirate is not specified, the
default sdirate (nominal) is kept.

Values
1..1250000
Default
1250
Degrade threshold (degthr) specifies a number of errored blocks as used for dDEG detection
for the ODUPTF facility.
A second is declared as good if the number of detected errored blocks within one second is
less than degthr; otherwise the second is declared as bad second.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.

laserOn

of Frame (LOF) or other defects from the far-end client-facing receiver.

for the SDH signal, or the errored B1 errors for dDEG degration for the Sonet Signal.
A second is declared as good if the number of detected errors within one second is less than
degthr; otherwise the second is declared as bad second.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 11dpm12 <port-
aid> state" for details.
type
Syntax
type [otu2 | unassigned]
Values
otu2 - to assign the port.
unassigned - to set the port as unassigned.
Specifies the port type.
Note: If Line port is associated with any LO-ODUk cross-connection, setting the port to
unassigned is denied.
If a new value is requested to be set for this parameter and rmconport !="" is present, then the
command is denied.

4916 Issue 1
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 11dpm12 <port-
aid> state" for details.
type
Syntax
type [och | unassigned]
Values
och - to assign the port.
unassigned - to set the port as unassigned.
Specifies the port type.
If a new value is requested to be set for this parameter and rmconport !="" is present, then the
command is denied.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Set to ains to configure Automatic In-Service.
ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Set the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port.
Enter number of hours and minutes
For system default value see "config general ainstimer"
enabled
Set ains for the port to on.
disabled
Set ains for the port to off. The default value for ains is disabled.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This can
affect service.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
If a GCC channel associated with the port is enabled then setting the port to down shall be
rejected.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Set to up to enable the port.

This command displays the interface ports on the 11dpm12 card.
Use this command to:
• Access subcommands that allow you to display details for the client ports (C{1-12}), or the line
ports (L{1-2}), or the eVOA ports (VA{1-2})
• Display all the 11dpm12 ports on the NE
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.226.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
6.226.3 Input Format
show interface 11dpm12 <port-aid>
6.226.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values

<shelf>/<slot>/L{1..2} - Specifies line port 1 ~ 2
<shelf>/<slot>/VA{1..2} - Specifies eVOA port 1 ~ port 2
* - display list of ports
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number, or * to list all of the 11dpm12 ports on the network
element.

supported shelf type.

Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 4939
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
channel
Display the expected wavelength of the pluggable module.
container
Display the container used by client for ODU2 multiplexing.
losprop
Display the loss propagation behavior setting.
moduletype
Display the pluggable module type used on the specified interface port.
degintvl
Degrade interval (degintvl) specifies the number of consecutive bad seconds (see parameter
"degthr") to be detected before declaring a dDEG (signal degrade) defect for the HDSDI signal
in both ingress and egress direction. The defect is cleared if degintvl consecutive good seconds
(see parameter "degthr") are detected.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.
degthr
Degrade threshold (degthr) specifies a number of errored blocks as used for dDEG detection
for the FE.
A second is declared as good if the number of detected errored blocks within one second is
less than degthr; otherwise the second is declared as bad second.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.

Channel : 1551

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
4970 Issue 1
Default
no default
Restrictions
This command is available for testing Epipe and VPLS services.
• When enabled, the command affects all services provisioned on the port.
• Before enabling this command, turn off all layer 2 control protocol (such as LACP, EFM,
802.1x and so on) on the device and its peer to prevent errors such as protocol flaps
due to timeout and so on.
• When port loopback with mac-swap enabled, for unicast and unknown-unicast packets,
if the packet matches the configured source and destination MAC address it is swapped
and looped back in the service. For broadcast and multicast packets, if the packet
matches the configured source MAC address, its source MAC address is used as the
destination MAC address and the system MAC address is used as the source MAC
address. The packet is looped back in the service as a unicast packet. All other packets
sent to the loopback port are dropped, because forwarding of these packets after
loopback can potentially cause network wide problems.
• When the loop back is enabled, ensure that Ethernet parameters such as, speed,
duplex, auto-negotiation and so on are not modified
• When the loopback is enabled, ensure that service parameter and attributes such as
ingress qos policy, ingress ACLs, and so on are not modified.
This command allows for configuration of port loopback with MAC swap. It enables a physical
layer loopback, so that packets which egress on the SAPs created on an ethernet port are
looped back into the system. After loopback, on ingress to the system, the MAC addresses in
the Ethernet header are swapped (that is, the source MAC address and destination MAC
address is exchanged with each other) by the system before being processed as per the
service configuration of the SAP.
Use of port loopback with mac-swap requires that another port is assigned for system use (no
service). The system uses the resources of the assigned port for providing this feature.
The system needs one unused port to be configured to be used as a loopback-no-svc-port. On
some packs an internal unused port is available for loopback. Some internal port are only 1G
rate, if the loopback needs a 10G rate port, a user face plate or mate port needs to be used.
• On the 11QPE24 port C24 is not used and is available to be used for loopback-no-svc-
port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11QCE12X port C23 and C24 an unused internal port and is available to be used
for loopback-no-svc-port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11OPE8 a virtual unused internal port is available for loopback-no-svc-port. A
physical face plate port can also be used.
Refer to "config card <card-name> <slot-aid> system loopback-no-svc-port mac-swap <port>"
for more info on loopback-no-svc-port.
The recommended procedure for using port loopback with mac-swap is:
• Configure the service and SAP on which loopback is to be enabled.
• Configure the assigned loopback port to be used.

11OPE8 interface commands

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
• Send bi-directional learning frames on the SAP under test and spoke or uplink from a
traffic tester or one can install static MAC for this purpose. Installing a static MAC is
highly recommended, since the recommended procedure for enabling port loopback is to
shutdown the port, enable loopback and then execute no shutdown the port.
• Enable port loopback and specify the service, SAP, and the source MAC address (SA)
and the destination MAC address (DA). All packets with source Mac matching SA are
the only ones processed in the context of the SAP on ingress after the loopback. Any
other traffic, is dropped on ingress, to avoid issues due to mac movement and flooding
issues in other services/SAPs, since the whole port is in loopback.
• When the port is in loopback, software disable learning and aging on the specified SAP.
Once the loopback configuration is removed for the port, then the software enables
learning and aging for specified SAP. Hence, port loopback with mac-swap cannot be
used for learning or aging.
• It is not recommend to change the service parameters for the SAP and the service when
loopback is active. Additionally use of commands which clears the FDB, and so on is
highly discouraged.
• Remove the loopback on the sap port to bring the sap out of MAC swap with loopback
mode.

term-mac-swap

term-mac-swap [service <svc-id> sap <sap-id> src-mac <SA> dst-mac <DA> | disabled]
OT management commands
11OPE8 interface commands
config interface 11ope8 <x-port-aid>
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
4982 Issue 1
Values
<svc-id> - The unique service identification number or string identifying the service in the
service domain. This ID must be unique to this service and may not be used for any other
service of any type.
<sap-id> - Specifies the SAP Id.
<SA> - Specifies the source MAC address. SA is a 6-byte unicast mac-address
(xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx or xx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx).
<DA> - Specifies the destination MAC address. DA is a 6-byte unicast mac-address
(xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx or xx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx).
disabled - removes the MAC swap loopback
Default
no default
Restrictions
This command is available for testing Epipe and VPLS services.
• When enabled, the command affects all services provisioned on the port.
• Before enabling this command, turn off all layer 2 control protocol (such as LACP, EFM,
802.1x and so on) on the device and its peer to prevent errors such as protocol flaps
due to timeout and so on.
• When port loopback with mac-swap enabled, for unicast and unknown-unicast packets,
if the packet matches the configured source and destination MAC address it will be
swapped and looped back in the service. For broadcast and multicast packets, if the
packet matches the configured source MAC address, its source MAC address will be
used as the destination MAC address and the system MAC address will be the source
MAC address. The packet is looped back in the service as a unicast packet. All other
packets sent to the loopback port will be dropped. Since forwarding of these packets
after loopback can potentially cause network wide problems.
• When the loop back is enabled, ensure that Ethernet parameters such as, speed,
duplex, auto-negotiation and so on are not modified
• When the loopback is enabled, ensure that service parameter and attributes such as
ingress qos policy, ingress ACLs, and so on are not modified.
This command allows for configuration of port loopback with MAC swap. It enables a physical
layer loopback, so that packets which egress on the SAPs created on an ethernet port are
looped back into the system. After loopback, on ingress to the system, the MAC addresses in
the Ethernet header are swapped (that is,the source MAC address and destination MAC
address is exchanged with each other) by the system before being processed as per the
service configuration of the SAP.
Use of port loopback with mac-swap requires that another port is assigned for system use. The
system uses the resources of the assigned port for providing this feature.
The system needs one unused port to be configured to be used as a loopback-no-svc-port. On
some pack an internal unused port is available for loopback. Some internal port are only 1G
rate, if the loopback needs a 10G rate port, a user face plate needs to be used.
OT management commands
11OPE8 interface commands
config interface 11ope8 <x-port-aid>
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 4983
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
• On the 11QPE24 port C24 is not used and is available to be used for loopback-no-svc-
port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11QCE12X port C23 and C24 an unused internal port and is available to be used
for loopback-no-svc-port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11OPE8 a virtual unused internal port is available for loopback-no-svc-port. A
physical face plate port can also be used.
Refer to "config card <card-name> <slot-aid> system loopback-no-svc-port mac-swap <port>"
for more info on loopback-no-svc-port.
The recommended procedure for using port loopback with mac-swap is:
• Configure the service and SAP on which loopback is to be enabled.
• Configure the assigned loopback port to be used.
• Send bi-directional learning frames on the SAP under test and spoke or uplink from a
traffic tester or one can install static MAC for this purpose. Installing a static MAC is
highly recommended, since the recommended procedure for enabling port loopback is to
shutdown the port, enable loopback and then execute no shutdown the port.
• Enable port loopback and specify the service, SAP, and the source MAC address (SA)
and the destination MAC address (DA). All packets with source Mac matching SA are
the only ones processed in the context of the SAP on ingress after the loopback. Any
other traffic, is dropped on ingress, to avoid issues due to mac movement and flooding
issues in other services/SAPs, since the whole port is in loopback.
• When the port is in loopback, software disable learning and aging on the specified SAP.
Once the loopback configuration is removed for the port, then the software enables
learning and aging for specified SAP. Hence, port loopback with mac-swap cannot be
used for learning or aging.
• It is not recommend to change the service parameters for the SAP and the service when
loopback is active. Additionally use of commands which clears the FDB, and so on is
highly discouraged.
• Remove the loopback on the sap port to bring the sap out of MAC swap with loopback
mode.
