Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 5007
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Default
no default
Restrictions
This command is available for testing Epipe and VPLS services.
• When enabled, the command affects all services provisioned on the port.
• Before enabling this command, turn off all layer 2 control protocol (such as LACP, EFM,
802.1x and so on) on the device and its peer to prevent errors such as protocol flaps
due to timeout and so on.
• When port loopback with mac-swap enabled, for unicast and unknown-unicast packets,
if the packet matches the configured source and destination MAC address it will be
swapped and looped back in the service. For broadcast and multicast packets, if the
packet matches the configured source MAC address, its source MAC address will be
used as the destination MAC address and the system MAC address will be the source
MAC address. The packet is looped back in the service as a unicast packet. All other
packets sent to the loopback port will be dropped. Since forwarding of these packets
after loopback can potentially cause network wide problems.
• When the loop back is enabled, ensure that Ethernet parameters such as, speed,
duplex, auto-negotiation and so on are not modified
• When the loopback is enabled, ensure that service parameter and attributes such as
ingress qos policy, ingress ACLs, and so on are not modified.
This command allows for configuration of port loopback with MAC swap. It enables a physical
layer loopback, so that packets which egress on the SAPs created on an ethernet port are
looped back into the system. After loopback, on ingress to the system, the MAC addresses in
the Ethernet header are swapped (that is,the source MAC address and destination MAC
address is exchanged with each other) by the system before being processed as per the
service configuration of the SAP.
Use of port loopback with mac-swap requires that another port is assigned for system use. The
system uses the resources of the assigned port for providing this feature.
The system needs one unused port to be configured to be used as a loopback-no-svc-port. On
some pack an internal unused port is available for loopback. Some internal port are only 1G
rate, if the loopback needs a 10G rate port, a user face plate needs to be used.
• On the 11QPE24 port C24 is not used and is available to be used for loopback-no-svc-
port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11QCE12X port C23 and C24 an unused internal port and is available to be used
for loopback-no-svc-port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11OPE8 a virtual unused internal port is available for loopback-no-svc-port. A
physical face plate port can also be used.
Refer to "config card <card-name> <slot-aid> system loopback-no-svc-port mac-swap <port>"
for more info on loopback-no-svc-port.
The recommended procedure for using port loopback with mac-swap is:
• Configure the service and SAP on which loopback is to be enabled.
• Configure the assigned loopback port to be used.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
5008 Issue 1
• Send bi-directional learning frames on the SAP under test and spoke or uplink from a
traffic tester or one can install static MAC for this purpose. Installing a static MAC is
highly recommended, since the recommended procedure for enabling port loopback is to
shutdown the port, enable loopback and then execute no shutdown the port.
• Enable port loopback and specify the service, SAP, and the source MAC address (SA)
and the destination MAC address (DA). All packets with source Mac matching SA are
the only ones processed in the context of the SAP on ingress after the loopback. Any
other traffic, is dropped on ingress, to avoid issues due to mac movement and flooding
issues in other services/SAPs, since the whole port is in loopback.
• When the port is in loopback, software disable learning and aging on the specified SAP.
Once the loopback configuration is removed for the port, then the software enables
learning and aging for specified SAP. Hence, port loopback with mac-swap cannot be
used for learning or aging.
• It is not recommend to change the service parameters for the SAP and the service when
loopback is active. Additionally use of commands which clears the FDB, and so on is
highly discouraged.
• Remove the loopback on the sap port to bring the sap out of MAC swap with loopback
mode.

ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h

down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Sets to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This can
affect service.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
mt
Sets to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Sets to up to enable the port.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to up shall be rejected.

6.265 show interface 11ope8 <x-port-aid> odu2
6.265.1 Purpose
This command displays the ODU2 attributes for the ports X{1..6} on the 11ope8 card.
Use this command to:
• Display the payload type filed of the Payload Structure Identifier in the ODUk frame
• Display the Payload Type Mismatch response
• Display the ODU2 Trail Trace Identifier attributes
• Display the ODUkp to CBRx mapping mode
• Display the ODU2 incftfl attributes
• Display the ODU2 incres attributes
• Display the ODU2 incexp attributes
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

tti

supported shelf type.

OT management commands
11QCE12X interface commands
config interface 11qce12x <client-port-aid>
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 5073
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
<svc-id> - The unique service identification number or string identifying the service in the
service domain. This ID must be unique to this service and may not be used for any other
service of any type.
<sap-id> - Specifies the SAP Id.
<SA> - Specifies the source MAC address. SA is a 6-byte unicast mac-address
(xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx or xx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx).
<DA> - Specifies the destination MAC address. DA is a 6-byte unicast mac-address
(xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx or xx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx).
disabled - removes the MAC Swap loopback
Default
no default
Restrictions
This command is available for testing Epipe and VPLS services.
• When enabled, the command affects all services provisioned on the port.
• Before enabling this command, turn off all layer 2 control protocol (such as LACP, EFM,
802.1x and so on) on the device and its peer to prevent errors such as protocol flaps
due to timeout and so on.
• When port loopback with mac-swap enabled, for unicast and unknown-unicast packets,
if the packet matches the configured source and destination MAC address it will be
swapped and looped back in the service. For broadcast and multicast packets, if the
packet matches the configured source MAC address, its source MAC address will be
used as the destination MAC address and the system MAC address will be the source
MAC address. The packet is looped back in the service as a unicast packet. All other
packets sent to the loopback port will be dropped. Since forwarding of these packets
after loopback can potentially cause network wide problems.
• When the loop back is enabled, ensure that Ethernet parameters such as, speed,
duplex, auto-negotiation and so on are not modified
• When the loopback is enabled, ensure that service parameter and attributes such as
ingress qos policy, ingress ACLs, and so on are not modified.
This command allows for configuration of port loopback with MAC swap. It enables a physical
layer loopback, so that packets which egress on the SAPs created on an ethernet port are
looped back into the system. After loopback, on ingress to the system, the MAC addresses in
the Ethernet header are swapped (that is,the source MAC address and destination MAC
address is exchanged with each other) by the system before being processed as per the
service configuration of the SAP.
Use of port loopback with mac-swap requires that another port is assigned for system use. The
system uses the resources of the assigned port for providing this feature.
The system needs one unused port to be configured to be used as a loopback-no-svc-port. On
some pack an internal unused port is available for loopback. Some internal port are only 1G
rate, if the loopback needs a 10G rate port, a user face plate needs to be used.

11QCE12X interface commands
config interface 11qce12x <client-port-aid>
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
5074 Issue 1
• On the 11QPE24 port C24 is not used and is available to be used for loopback-no-svc-
port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11QCE12X port C23 and C24 an unused internal port and is available to be used
for loopback-no-svc-port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11OPE8 a virtual unused internal port is available for loopback-no-svc-port. A
physical face plate port can also be used.
Refer to "config card <card-name> <slot-aid> system loopback-no-svc-port mac-swap <port>"
for more info on loopback-no-svc-port.
The recommended procedure for using port loopback with mac-swap is:
• Configure the service and SAP on which loopback is to be enabled.
• Configure the assigned loopback port to be used.
• Send bi-directional learning frames on the SAP under test and spoke or uplink from a
traffic tester or one can install static MAC for this purpose. Installing a static MAC is
highly recommended, since the recommended procedure for enabling port loopback is to
shutdown the port, enable loopback and then execute no shutdown the port.
• Enable port loopback and specify the service, SAP, and the source MAC address (SA)
and the destination MAC address (DA). All packets with source Mac matching SA are
the only ones processed in the context of the SAP on ingress after the loopback. Any
other traffic, is dropped on ingress, to avoid issues due to mac movement and flooding
issues in other services/SAPs, since the whole port is in loopback.
• When the port is in loopback, software disable learning and aging on the specified SAP.
Once the loopback configuration is removed for the port, then the software enables
learning and aging for specified SAP. Hence, port loopback with mac-swap cannot be
used for learning or aging.
• It is not recommend to change the service parameters for the SAP and the service when
loopback is active. Additionally use of commands which clears the FDB, and so on is
highly discouraged.
• Remove the loopback on the sap port to bring the sap out of MAC swap with loopback
mode.
Sub-command: pm
Sets the Performance Monitoring attributes. See "config interface 11qce12x <client-port-aid>
pm" to configure pm attributes.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 11qce12x
<port-aid> state" for details.

11QCE12X interface commands

Nokia 1830 PSS

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
5088 Issue 1
Values
<svc-id> - The unique service identification number or string identifying the service in the
service domain. This ID must be unique to this service and may not be used for any other
service of any type.
<sap-id> - Specifies the SAP Id.
<SA> - Specifies the source MAC address. SA is a 6-byte unicast mac-address
(xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx or xx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx).
<DA> - Specifies the destination MAC address. DA is a 6-byte unicast mac-address
(xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx or xx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx).
disabled - removes the MAC Swap loopback
Default
no default
Restrictions
This command is available for testing Epipe and VPLS services.
• When enabled, the command affects all services provisioned on the port.
• Before enabling this command, turn off all layer 2 control protocol (such as LACP, EFM,
802.1x and so on) on the device and its peer to prevent errors such as protocol flaps
due to timeout and so on.
• When port loopback with mac-swap enabled, for unicast and unknown-unicast packets,
if the packet matches the configured source and destination MAC address it will be
swapped and looped back in the service. For broadcast and multicast packets, if the
packet matches the configured source MAC address, its source MAC address will be
used as the destination MAC address and the system MAC address will be the source
MAC address. The packet is looped back in the service as a unicast packet. All other
packets sent to the loopback port will be dropped. Since forwarding of these packets
after loopback can potentially cause network wide problems.
• When the loop back is enabled, ensure that Ethernet parameters such as, speed,
duplex, auto-negotiation and so on are not modified
• When the loopback is enabled, ensure that service parameter and attributes such as
ingress qos policy, ingress ACLs, and so on are not modified.
This command allows for configuration of port loopback with MAC swap. It enables a physical
layer loopback, so that packets which egress on the SAPs created on an ethernet port are
looped back into the system. After loopback, on ingress to the system, the MAC addresses in
the Ethernet header are swapped (that is,the source MAC address and destination MAC
address is exchanged with each other) by the system before being processed as per the
service configuration of the SAP.
Use of port loopback with mac-swap requires that another port is assigned for system use. The
system uses the resources of the assigned port for providing this feature.
The system needs one unused port to be configured to be used as a loopback-no-svc-port. On
some pack an internal unused port is available for loopback. Some internal port are only 1G
rate, if the loopback needs a 10G rate port, a user face plate needs to be used.
OT management commands
11QCE12X interface commands
config interface 11qce12x <x-port-aid>
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 5089
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
• On the 11QPE24 port C24 is not used and is available to be used for loopback-no-svc-
port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11QCE12X port C23 and C24 an unused internal port and is available to be used
for loopback-no-svc-port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11OPE8 a virtual unused internal port is available for loopback-no-svc-port. A
physical face plate port can also be used.
Refer to "config card <card-name> <slot-aid> system loopback-no-svc-port mac-swap <port>"
for more info on loopback-no-svc-port.
The recommended procedure for using port loopback with mac-swap is:
• Configure the service and SAP on which loopback is to be enabled.
• Configure the assigned loopback port to be used.
• Send bi-directional learning frames on the SAP under test and spoke or uplink from a
traffic tester or one can install static MAC for this purpose. Installing a static MAC is
highly recommended, since the recommended procedure for enabling port loopback is to
shutdown the port, enable loopback and then execute no shutdown the port.
• Enable port loopback and specify the service, SAP, and the source MAC address (SA)
and the destination MAC address (DA). All packets with source Mac matching SA are
the only ones processed in the context of the SAP on ingress after the loopback. Any
other traffic, is dropped on ingress, to avoid issues due to mac movement and flooding
issues in other services/SAPs, since the whole port is in loopback.
• When the port is in loopback, software disable learning and aging on the specified SAP.
Once the loopback configuration is removed for the port, then the software enables
learning and aging for specified SAP. Hence, port loopback with mac-swap cannot be
used for learning or aging.
• It is not recommend to change the service parameters for the SAP and the service when
loopback is active. Additionally use of commands which clears the FDB, and so on is
highly discouraged.
• Remove the loopback on the sap port to bring the sap out of MAC swap with loopback
mode.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
5110 Issue 1
Default
no default
Restrictions
This command is available for testing Epipe and VPLS services.
• When enabled, the command affects all services provisioned on the port.
• Before enabling this command, turn off all layer 2 control protocol (such as LACP, EFM,
802.1x and so on) on the device and its peer to prevent errors such as protocol flaps
due to timeout and so on.
• When port loopback with mac-swap enabled, for unicast and unknown-unicast packets,
if the packet matches the configured source and destination MAC address it will be
swapped and looped back in the service. For broadcast and multicast packets, if the
packet matches the configured source MAC address, its source MAC address will be
used as the destination MAC address and the system MAC address will be the source
MAC address. The packet is looped back in the service as a unicast packet. All other
packets sent to the loopback port will be dropped. Since forwarding of these packets
after loopback can potentially cause network wide problems.
• When the loop back is enabled, ensure that Ethernet parameters such as, speed,
duplex, auto-negotiation and so on are not modified
• When the loopback is enabled, ensure that service parameter and attributes such as
ingress qos policy, ingress ACLs, and so on are not modified.
This command allows for configuration of port loopback with MAC swap. It enables a physical
layer loopback, so that packets which egress on the SAPs created on an ethernet port are
looped back into the system. After loopback, on ingress to the system, the MAC addresses in
the Ethernet header are swapped (that is,the source MAC address and destination MAC
address is exchanged with each other) by the system before being processed as per the
service configuration of the SAP.
Use of port loopback with mac-swap requires that another port is assigned for system use. The
system uses the resources of the assigned port for providing this feature.
The system needs one unused port to be configured to be used as a loopback-no-svc-port. On
some pack an internal unused port is available for loopback. Some internal port are only 1G
rate, if the loopback needs a 10G rate port, a user face plate needs to be used.
• On the 11QPE24 port C24 is not used and is available to be used for loopback-no-svc-
port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11QCE12X port C23 and C24 an unused internal port and is available to be used
for loopback-no-svc-port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11OPE8 a virtual unused internal port is available for loopback-no-svc-port. A
physical face plate port can also be used.
Refer to "config card <card-name> <slot-aid> system loopback-no-svc-port mac-swap <port>"
for more info on loopback-no-svc-port.
The recommended procedure for using port loopback with mac-swap is:
• Configure the service and SAP on which loopback is to be enabled.
• Configure the assigned loopback port to be used.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
• Send bi-directional learning frames on the SAP under test and spoke or uplink from a
traffic tester or one can install static MAC for this purpose. Installing a static MAC is
highly recommended, since the recommended procedure for enabling port loopback is to
shutdown the port, enable loopback and then execute no shutdown the port.
• Enable port loopback and specify the service, SAP, and the source MAC address (SA)
and the destination MAC address (DA). All packets with source Mac matching SA are
the only ones processed in the context of the SAP on ingress after the loopback. Any
other traffic, is dropped on ingress, to avoid issues due to mac movement and flooding
issues in other services/SAPs, since the whole port is in loopback.
• When the port is in loopback, software disable learning and aging on the specified SAP.
Once the loopback configuration is removed for the port, then the software enables
learning and aging for specified SAP. Hence, port loopback with mac-swap cannot be
used for learning or aging.
• It is not recommend to change the service parameters for the SAP and the service when
loopback is active. Additionally use of commands which clears the FDB, and so on is
highly discouraged.
• Remove the loopback on the sap port to bring the sap out of MAC swap with loopback
mode.

fe
detail
pm

number, a slash, and the port number.

supported shelf type.

6.313.1 Purpose
This command configures the interface ports on the 11QPA4 card. Use this command to access
subcommands that allow you to configure the client (C{1-4}) port, line (L{1-4} ) port or eVOA (VA{1-
4}) port.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.313.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None

6.313.3 Input Format

6.313.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..4} - Specifies client port 1 ~ port 4
<shelf>/<slot>/L{1..4} - Specifies line port 1 ~ port 4
<shelf>/<slot>/VA{1..4} - Specifies eVOA port 1 ~ port 4
* - display list of ports
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number, or * to list all of the 11QPA4 cards on the network
element.

supported shelf type.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-

"" for <identifier>

For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

aid> state" for details.

6.324 config interface 11qpa4 <line-port-aid> odu2
6.324.1 Purpose
This command configures the ODU2 attributes for the LINE (L{1-4}) port on the 11QPA4 card.
Use this command to:
• Set the ODUkp to CBRx mapping mode
• Set the payload type filed of the Payload Structure Identifier in the ODUk frame
• Set the Payload Type Mismatch response
• Set the ODU2 Trail Trace Identifier attributes
• Set the Delay Measurement parameters including dmcmepmode
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.324.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

Syntax

Values

async - asynchronous CBR mapping

bitsync
ODUkp to CBRx mapping mode. This attribute specifies the mappng mode that wil be used

Syntax
dmcmepmode [bypass | destination | source]
Values
source - Generates the DM bits, and measures the DM bit transition
destination - Loop-back the received DM bits
bypass - The DM bit is transparent transmitted
Default
bypass
Set the Connection Monitoring End Point mode of the Delay Measurement on the specified
ODUk entity. Enter this keyword to display the current setting.

5224 Issue 1
Default
2 (0x2) - for asynchronous CBR mapping for OC192/STM64 signals
3 (0x3) - for bit synchronous CBR mapping for OC192/STM64 signals
5 (0x5) - for GFP-F mapping of 10GbE signals
129 (0x81) - for bit synchronous CBR mapping of FC1200 signals
130 (0x82) - for bit synchronous CBR mapping of 10GbE signals at 11.049Gb/s

134 (0x86) - for bit synchronous CBR mapping of DDR signals.
253 (0xFD) - Client port is not assigned with a signal type.
Specifies the value of the Payload Type field of a Payload Structure Identifier in the ODUk
frame.
Note: 11QPA4 implemented bit synchronous CBR mapping of 10GbE signals at 11.096Gb/s to
ODU2 prior to ITU standards and the pldtype is set to the value to 131 (0x83). When
interworking with a G.709 standard-compliant OTs is required, the pldtype must be set to value
3 (0x3).
Restrictions
This attribute only applies when the client signal is not an OTM0.2 signal.

Values

ADDDROP
Operational mode of the 11QPA4. This parameter applies to all line ports.

5236 Issue 1
Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 11qpa4 <port-
aid> state" for details.
type
Syntax
type [och | unassigned]
Values
och - to assign the port.
unassigned - to set the port as unassigned.
Specifies the port type.

6.330 config interface 11qpa4 <port-aid> <otun-odun> tti
6.330.1 Purpose
This command configures the Trail Trace Identifier attributes for OTU2 and ODU2 of the line ports
(L{1..4}) and client ports (C{1..4}) on the 11QPA4 card.
Use this command to:
• Set the expected incoming source access point identifier.
• Set the transmitted source access point identifier.
• Configure the trace identifier compare mode.
• Configure the trace identifier mismatch response consequent action.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.330.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
6.330.3 Input Format
config interface 11qpa4 <port-aid> <otun-odun> tti
exp_sapi
timmresp
trccmp
tx_sapi
6.330.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/L{1..4} - Specifies the line port 1 ~ port 4
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..4} - Specifies the client port 1 ~ port 4
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.

exp_sapi
Syntax
exp_sapi [<value>]
Values
<value> - ASCII string 1..15 characters, enclosed in optional quotations.
Default
Null character (15 bytes each with hex value 00)
Specifies the expected incoming Source Access Point Identifier (SAPI).
timmresp
Syntax
timmresp [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - enables consequent action in case of dTIM (e.g. AIS insertion)
disabled - disables consequent action in case of dTIM (e.g. AIS insertion)
Default
disabled
Configures the consequent action for dTIM defect (Trail trace Identifier MisMatch RESPonse).
Restrictions
This parameter is applicable to line ports and client ports {otu2} only.
trccmp
Syntax
trccmp [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - comparison is activated
disabled - comparison is de-activated

affect service.
Restrictions

rejected.
mt

Restrictions
C1/VA1, C2/VA2, C3/VA3, C4/VA4 are mutually exclusive. Cn (n=1..4) port can be assigned
with a signal type only if the VAn (n=1..4) is unassigned.
To provision the client port as tengige, either the line port must be provisioned as otu2eeth
or otu2enimeth type first, or the BP port is provisioned as XFI first.
For tengige signal type provision, the odurate is optional. It is allowed to enter tengige type
with or without specifying odurate value. if odurate is not specified, the default odurate
value (null) is kept.
If mgracd == cp or mgracd == mpcp is provisioned for a port then setting the type to
unassigned shall be rejected.
Note:
• see command "config/show mgracd" w.r.t. mgracd provisioning.
odurate
Syntax
odurate <value>
Values
odu2e - 10GbE signal with CBR mapping into OPU2e/ODU2e.
Default
none
Configures to generate the terminated ODU2e entity at the client side
Restrictions
The odurate parameter is optional for tengige type provision. It is only required when the
line port is provisioned as otu2enimeth type, or the BP port is provisioned as XFI.

Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force]]
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

Sub-command: ains
Syntax
ains [ainstimer | disabled | enabled]
Default
disabled
Sets to ains to configure Automatic In-Service
ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Sets the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port.
Enter number of hours and minutes.
For system default value see "config general ainstimer".
enabled
Set ains for the port to on.
disabled
Set ains for the port to off.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This can
affect service.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
If a GCC channel associated with the port is enabled then setting the port to down shall be
rejected.

Syntax

Values
enabled - enable the terminal loopback
disabled - disable the terminal loopback
Default
disabled
Restrictions
A terminal loopback cannot be enabled on a "C" port if autonegotiation is disabled or
limited, and the port speed is 10 or 100 (see "show port"). Disable MAC learning for each
SAP on the port (see "show ... service <id> sap"). Start the test traffic after the loopback is
enabled and stop it before the loopback is disabled. Note that during a terminal loopback, C
port stats accumulate Input and Output counts from the looped traffic.
Configures the terminal loopback of the port. Enter this keyword without option to display the
current setting. To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by enabled or disabled.
term-mac-swap
Syntax
term-mac-swap [service <svc-id> sap <sap-id> src-mac <SA> dst-mac <DA> | disabled]
OT management commands
11QPE24 interface commands
config interface 11qpe24 <client-port-aid>
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 5365
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
<svc-id> - The unique service identification number or string identifying the service in the
service domain. This ID must be unique to this service and may not be used for any other
service of any type.
<sap-id> - Specifies the SAP Id.
<SA> - Specifies the source MAC address. SA is a 6-byte unicast mac-address
(xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx or xx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx).
<DA> - Specifies the destination MAC address. DA is a 6-byte unicast mac-address
(xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx or xx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx).
disabled - removes the MAC Swap loopback
Default
no default
Restrictions
This command is available for testing Epipe and VPLS services.
• When enabled, the command affects all services provisioned on the port.
• Before enabling this command, turn off all layer 2 control protocol (such as LACP, EFM,
802.1x and so on) on the device and its peer to prevent errors such as protocol flaps
due to timeout and so on.
• When port loopback with mac-swap enabled, for unicast and unknown-unicast packets,
if the packet matches the configured source and destination MAC address it will be
swapped and looped back in the service. For broadcast and multicast packets, if the
packet matches the configured source MAC address, its source MAC address will be
used as the destination MAC address and the system MAC address will be the source
MAC address. The packet is looped back in the service as a unicast packet. All other
packets sent to the loopback port will be dropped. Since forwarding of these packets
after loopback can potentially cause network wide problems.
• When the loop back is enabled, ensure that Ethernet parameters such as, speed,
duplex, auto-negotiation and so on are not modified
• When the loopback is enabled, ensure that service parameter and attributes such as
ingress qos policy, ingress ACLs, and so on are not modified.
This command allows for configuration of port loopback with MAC swap. It enables a physical
layer loopback, so that packets which egress on the SAPs created on an ethernet port are
looped back into the system. After loopback, on ingress to the system, the MAC addresses in
the Ethernet header are swapped (that is,the source MAC address and destination MAC
address is exchanged with each other) by the system before being processed as per the
service configuration of the SAP.
Use of port loopback with mac-swap requires that another port is assigned for system use. The
system uses the resources of the assigned port for providing this feature.
The system needs one unused port to be configured to be used as a loopback-no-svc-port. On
some pack an internal unused port is available for loopback. Some internal port are only 1G
rate, if the loopback needs a 10G rate port, a user face plate needs to be used.

Nokia 1830 PSS

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
5366 Issue 1
• On the 11QPE24 port C24 is not used and is available to be used for loopback-no-svc-
port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11QCE12X port C23 and C24 an unused internal port and is available to be used
for loopback-no-svc-port. A physical face plate port can also be used.
• On the 11OPE8 a virtual unused internal port is available for loopback-no-svc-port. A
physical face plate port can also be used.
Refer to "config card <card-name> <slot-aid> system loopback-no-svc-port mac-swap <port>"
for more info on loopback-no-svc-port.
The recommended procedure for using port loopback with mac-swap is:
• Configure the service and SAP on which loopback is to be enabled.
• Configure the assigned loopback port to be used.
• Send bi-directional learning frames on the SAP under test and spoke or uplink from a
traffic tester or one can install static MAC for this purpose. Installing a static MAC is
highly recommended, since the recommended procedure for enabling port loopback is to
shutdown the port, enable loopback and then execute no shutdown the port.
• Enable port loopback and specify the service, SAP, and the source MAC address (SA)
and the destination MAC address (DA). All packets with source Mac matching SA are
the only ones processed in the context of the SAP on ingress after the loopback. Any
other traffic, is dropped on ingress, to avoid issues due to mac movement and flooding
issues in other services/SAPs, since the whole port is in loopback.
• When the port is in loopback, software disable learning and aging on the specified SAP.
Once the loopback configuration is removed for the port, then the software enables
learning and aging for specified SAP. Hence, port loopback with mac-swap cannot be
used for learning or aging.
• It is not recommend to change the service parameters for the SAP and the service when
loopback is active. Additionally use of commands which clears the FDB, and so on is
highly discouraged.
• Remove the loopback on the sap port to bring the sap out of MAC swap with loopback
mode.
Sub-command: pm
Sets the Performance Monitoring attributes. See "config interface 11qpe24 <client-port-aid>
pm" to configure pm attributes.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 11qpe24 <port-
aid> state" for details.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
term-mac-swap
Syntax
term-mac-swap [service <svc-id> sap <sap-id> src-mac <SA> dst-mac <DA> | disabled]
Values
<svc-id> - The unique service identification number or string identifying the service in the
service domain. This ID must be unique to this service and may not be used for any other
service of any type.
<sap-id> - Specifies the SAP Id.
<SA> - Specifies the source MAC address. SA is a 6-byte unicast mac-address
(xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx or xx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx).
<DA> - Specifies the destination MAC address. DA is a 6-byte unicast mac-address
(xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx or xx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx).
disabled - removes the MAC Swap loopback
Default
no default
Restrictions
This command is available for testing Epipe and VPLS services.
• When enabled, the command affects all services provisioned on the port.
• Before enabling this command, turn off all layer 2 control protocol (such as LACP, EFM,
802.1x and so on) on the device and its peer to prevent errors such as protocol flaps
due to timeout and so on.
• When port loopback with mac-swap enabled, for unicast and unknown-unicast packets,
if the packet matches the configured source and destination MAC address it will be
swapped and looped back in the service. For broadcast and multicast packets, if the
packet matches the configured source MAC address, its source MAC address will be
used as the destination MAC address and the system MAC address will be the source
MAC address. The packet is looped back in the service as a unicast packet. All other
packets sent to the loopback port will be dropped. Since forwarding of these packets
after loopback can potentially cause network wide problems.
• When the loop back is enabled, ensure that Ethernet parameters such as, speed,
duplex, auto-negotiation and so on are not modified
• When the loopback is enabled, ensure that service parameter and attributes such as
ingress qos policy, ingress ACLs, and so on are not modified.
This command allows for configuration of port loopback with MAC swap. It enables a physical
layer loopback, so that packets which egress on the SAPs created on an ethernet port are
looped back into the system. After loopback, on ingress to the system, the MAC addresses in
the Ethernet header are swapped (that is,the source MAC address and destination MAC
address is exchanged with each other) by the system before being processed as per the
service configuration of the SAP.
Use of port loopback with mac-swap requires that another port is assigned for system use. The
OT management commands

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

Nokia 1830 PSS

Issue 1 5399
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual

bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

exp_sapi

timmresp
Syntax
timmresp [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - enables consequent action in case of dTIM (e.g. AIS insertion)
disabled - disables consequent action in case of dTIM (e.g. AIS insertion)
Default
disabled
Configures the consequent action for dTIM defect (Trail trace Identifier MisMatch RESPonse).
trccmp
Syntax
trccmp [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - comparison is activated
disabled - comparison is de-activated
Default
disabled
Configures the dTIM detection mode for the facility (trace compare). Turns the comparison
between the incoming sapi value and the provisioned (that is, exp_sapi) value as either on or
off.
tx_sapi

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Sets the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port. Enter number of hours and minutes. For
system default value see "config general ainstimer".
enabled
Sets ains for the port to on.
disabled
Sets ains for the port to off. The default value for ains is disabled.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Sets to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This
may affect service.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
If a GCC channel associated with the port is enabled then setting the port to down shall be
rejected.
mt
Sets to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Sets to up to enable the port.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to up shall be rejected.

6.394.1 Purpose
This command displays the ODU2 attributes for the ports X{1..4} on the 11qpe24 card.
Use this command to:
• Display the payload type filed of the Payload Structure Identifier in the ODUk frame
• Display the Payload Type Mismatch response
• Display the ODU2 Trail Trace Identifier attributes
• Display the ODUkp to CBRx mapping mode
• Display the ODU2 incftfl attributes
• Display the ODU2 incres attributes
• Display the ODU2 incexp attributes

direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.

command is executed if "yes" is entered.

wkat
Syntax
wkat [<string>]
Specifies a well-known-answer-test for the interface port.Enter this keyword followed by string
of 32 hexadecimal characters, or enter this keyword without any parameters to display the
current description for the interface. The WKAT string is used to authenticate the far end and
validate the keys are correct.
Note:WKAT content beyond the first 16 characters is ignored in comparisons. The 16
characters still provide substantial authentication of the expected likelihood of connection to
only the intended port at the far end.
nextkey
Syntax

Specifies a next encryption key for the interface port. Enter this keyword followed by string of 64
hexademical characters, or enter this keyword without any parameters to display the date/time
of when the nextkey was set.

Enable or disable encryption for the port.
switchkey
Commands the port to switch to the next key for encryption.

description for the interface.
detail
Displays the current settings for the port.
Sub-command: och
Sets the OCH interface port parameters. See "config interface 11QPEN4 <va-port-aid> och".
Sub-command: pm
Sets the Performance Monitoring attributes associated with the eVOA port. See "config
interface 11QPEN4 <va-port-aid> pm".
power
Syntax
power [<value>]
Values
-20..-4.5 - gain in dBm
Default
-20 dBm
Sets the transmitted optical output power of the port.
Power change is rejected if the line port is managed via cluster by a WDM node (i.e. in the
WDM node a cluster O-CONN is provisioned to the line port).
Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
OT management commands
11QPEN4 interface commands

Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 5491
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 11QPEN4
<port-aid> state" for details.
type
Syntax
type [och | unassigned]
Values
och - to assign the port.
unassigned - to set the port as unassigned.
Specifies the port type.
If a new value is requested to be set for this parameter and rmconport !="" is present, then the
command is denied.

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface
{11star1|11star1a} <port-aid> state" for details.

6.456.1 Purpose
This command displays the client (C1) port 10G Fibre Channel attributes on the {11star1|11star1a}
card.
Use this command to:
• Display the Automatic In-Service Debounce time
• Display the channel frequency of the pluggable module
• Display the loss propagation parameter
• Display the pluggable module type
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer

channel
losprop
moduletype

Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
ainstimer
Displays the configured Automatic In-Service Debounce time.
channel
Displays the wavelength of the pluggable module.

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

{0..4}

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

<port-aid> state" for details.

5722 Issue 1
ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Set the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port.
Enter number of hours and minutes
For system default value see "config general ainstimer"
enabled
Set ains for the port to on.
disabled
Set ains for the port to off. The default value for ains is disabled.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This may
affect service.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
If a GCC channel associated with the port is enabled then setting the port to down shall be
rejected.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Set to up to enable the port.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to up shall be rejected.

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual

<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

Values
enabled - comparison is activated
disabled - comparison is de-activated
Default
disabled
Configures the dTIM detection mode for the facility (trace compare). Turns the comparison
between the incoming sapi value and the provisioned (that is, exp_sapi) value as either on or
off.

mt

5842 Issue 1
Power change is rejected if the line port is managed via cluster by a WDM node (i.e. in the
WDM node a cluster O-CONN is provisioned to the line port).
Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 112scx10
<port-aid> state" for details.
type
Syntax
type [otu4]
Values
otu4 - set the port to OTU4
Specifies the port type.

Syntax
losprop [laserOn | laserOff]
Values

laserOn
Specifies how the near end client facing transmitter port reacts to a Loss of Signal (LOS), Loss

provisions the moduletype upon initial insertion.
user - If the user wants to use a pluggable module that is not on the qualified list of pluggable
modules, without generating an alarm.
If it is requested to change the parameter and the port AdminState is UP, then the command
shall be denied.

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force]]
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.

ainstimer
Syntax

Values

down
Syntax

Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This may
affect service.
Restrictions

If a GCC channel associated with the port is enabled then setting the port to down shall be
rejected.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Set to up to enable the port.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to up shall be rejected.

This command displays the OTU1F, OTU2 or OTU2E client port (C{1-10}) attributes on the
112sdx11 card.
Use this command to:
• Display the AINS timer value
• Display the expected channel value of the pluggable module
• Display the pluggable module type
• Display the loss propagation behavior
• Display the OTU2 rate
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.585.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
6.585.3 Input Format
show interface 112sdx11 <client-port-aid> <otu-entity>
ainstimer
channelrx
channeltx
losprop
moduletype
6.585.4 Input Parameters
<otu-entity>
Values
{otu1f, otu2, otu2e} - otu entities
This describes the possible enitities of otu for this particular card 112sdx11.
<client-port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..10} - Specifies the client port 1 ~ port 10
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number.

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string

bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

mt

up

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 112snx10
<port-aid> state" for details.
type
Syntax

Values
otu4 - assign the port to OTU4

ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Set the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port.
Enter number of hours and minutes
For system default value see "config general ainstimer"
enabled
Set ains for the port to on.
disabled
Set ains for the port to off. The default value for ains is disabled.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This
command is service affecting.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Set to up to enable the port.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to up shall be rejected.

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string

<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

6.647 config interface <12p120-card> <port-aid> <otn>
6.647.1 Purpose
This command configures the client (C{1..6}) port and line (L{1..6}) port OTU2/OTU2e attributes on
the following cards (<12p120-card>):
• 12P120
• 12P120S
Use this command to:
• Set the receive channel frequency
• Set the transmit channel frequency of the pluggable module
• Set the loss propagation behavior
• set the hold off timer attribute
• Set the pluggable module type
Note: The OTU layer is managed via non-card specific facility commands "config/show otu".

Values

Degrade interval (degintvl) specifies the number of consecutive bad seconds (see parameter

Syntax

1..856388 - for ODU4
Default
40000 - for ODU4
Degrade threshold (degthr) specifies a number of errored blocks as used for dDEG detection
for the ODU4.
A second is declared as good if the number of detected errored blocks within one second is
less than degthr; otherwise the second is declared as bad second.

degthr
Degrade threshold (degthr) specifies a number of errored blocks as used for dDEG detection
for the tengige.
A second is declared as good if the number of detected errored blocks within one second is
less than degthr; otherwise the second is declared as bad second.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.

Syntax

Degrade interval (degintvl) specifies the number of consecutive bad seconds (see parameter

Values

0 - Disabled
Default
0
Degrade threshold (degthr) specifies a number of errored blocks as used for dDEG detection
for the tengige.
A second is declared as good if the number of detected errored blocks within one second is
less than degthr; otherwise the second is declared as bad second.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state

<port-aid> state" for details.

ainstimer

Display the wavelength of the pluggable module.

Displays the encapsulation mode used to transport the 10 GbE LAN signal.
errfrmdrop
Displays whether inbound error frames are discarded or passed.
losprop

moduletype
Displays the pluggable module type used on the specified interface port.
degintvl
Degrade interval (degintvl) specifies the number of consecutive bad seconds (see parameter
"degthr") to be detected before declaring a dDEG (signal degrade) defect for the client tengige.
The defect is cleared if degintvl consecutive good seconds (see parameter "degthr") are
detected.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.
degthr
Degrade threshold (degthr) specifies a number of errored blocks as used for dDEG detection
for the tengige.
A second is declared as good if the number of detected errored blocks within one second is
less than degthr; otherwise the second is declared as bad second.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.

command is executed if "yes" is entered.

reset
Syntax
reset {cold | warm} [force]
Values
cold - A cold restart reinitializes the module firmware and hardware and is service affecting.
warm - A warm restart re-initializes the module firmware only and is not service affecting.
force - optional parameter together with cold.
Performs a restart of the port/module.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the port AdminState to DOWN or MT.
If it is requested to perform a cold reset and the force option is not specified and the port
AdminState is UP, then the command shall be denied.

Values

<shelf>/<slot>/L{1..2} - Specifies the line port 1 ~ port 2
* - display list of ports
Default
Entry required

number, a slash, and the port number, or * to list all of the 16P200 ports on the network
element.

supported shelf type.

6.747 show interface 16p200 <port-aid> <fcn>
6.747.1 Purpose
This command displays the Fibre Channel port attributes on the 16P200 card.
Use this command to:
• Display the Automatic In-Service Debounce time
• Display the channel frequency
• Display the loss propagation behavior
• Display the hold-off timer for LOSPROP action
• Display the pluggable module type
• Display the laser control behavior for server signal degrade
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.747.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
6.747.3 Input Format
show interface 16p200 <port-aid> <fcn>
ainstimer
channel
holdofftimer
losprop
moduletype
ssdca
6.747.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..12} - Specifies the client port 1 ~ port 12
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
6462 Issue 1
<fcn>
Values
fc1600
fc3200
fc800
Default
Entry required
Specify the signal type of Fibre Channel port.
ainstimer
Displays the Automatic In-Service debounce time.
channel
Displays the channel frequency.
holdofftimer
Displays the hold-off time for LOSPROP action. The values are in 10 milli seconds. Enter this
keyword without value to display the current setting of this parameter.
losprop
Displays the loss propagation setting.
moduletype
Displays the pluggable module type used on the specified interface port.
ssdca
Displays the client laser behavior for server signal degrade setting.

# show interface 16P200 1/3/C1 fc3200 ainstimer

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
OT management commands
1DPP24M interface commands
config interface 1dpp24m <line-port-aid>

Configures the loopback. For the usage of the individual values refer parameters in this

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Sets the transmitted optical output power of the port.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by one allowed value.
Power change is rejected if the line port is managed via cluster by a WDM node (i.e. in the
WDM node a cluster O-CONN is provisioned to the line port).
Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Default
up
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 1ud200 <port-
aid> state" for details.

Release 24.12

6522 Issue 1
type
Syntax
type <type-value>
Values
otu4 - set port to type otu4
otu4x2 - set port to type otu4x2
otu4waneth - set port to type otu4waneth
unassigned - set <port-aid> to unassigned
Default
unassigned
Specifies the port type. Enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current type
for the interface.
Note:When port type is set to otu4waneth, see command "config interface 1ud200 <port-aid>
otu4" for port configuration.
If a new value is requested to be set for this parameter and rmconport !="" is present, then the
command is denied.
Command Validation
The following pre-condition is needed when assigning the type parameter.
If the port is not in state down, setting the type to unassigned is denied.
If the administrative state of the card is currently down then any attempt to provision a new port
shall be rejected.
The interface type can only be assigned as "OTU4WANETH" only if the card is involved in a
packet switch group.
If the SDEE state is present on the associated ODUPTF in case of provisioned type ==
otukethwan then setting the type to unassigned shall be rejected.
If the SDEE state is present for the port then setting the type to unassigned shall be rejected.
If mgracd == cp or mgracd == mpcp is provisioned for a port then setting the type to
unassigned shall be rejected.
Note:
• see command "config/show mgracd" w.r.t. mgracd provisioning.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

Specifies the receive channel frequency. Not settable for internal topology connections.

Note :

The RX wavelength for SI64.1BD and SS64.2BD is 1270.

command is denied.
SS64CTU restriction:
The moduletype 'SS64CTU' supports only a 100Ghz grid. Therefore, the step size within the
specified value range is 10.000 instead of 5.000 and the range is 9200 to 9600 for an OTU2/
OTU2e port.
Note:
Amodule mismatch alarm will be raised if a channel value is provisioned which cannot be
supported by SS64CTU moduletype.

Backplane port 1 type can only be changed, if ports {1..10} are all unassigned.
Backplane port 2 type can only be changed, if ports {11..20} are all unassigned.

to 'XFI or 'interlaken_PIF' per packetswitch provision setting.
When the card is removed from a packet switch group, the backplane port type is automatically
set to 'unassigned'.
