6610 Issue 1
Default
7
Degrade interval (degintvl) specifies the number of consecutive bad seconds (see parameter
"degthr") to be detected before declaring a dDEG (signal degrade) defect for the client signal.
The defect is cleared if degintvl consecutive good seconds (see parameter "degthr") are
detected.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
degthr
Syntax
degthr [<value>]
Values
0..194000 - for 100GBE
Default
0 for disable
Degrade threshold (degthr) specifies a number of errored blocks as used for dDEG detection
for the client signal.
A second is declared as good if the number of detected errored blocks within one second is
less than degthr; otherwise the second is declared as bad second.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
losprop
Syntax
losprop [laseron | laseroff]
Values
laseron - transmitter stays on
laseroff - turn off the transmitter
Default
laseron
Specifies how the near end client facing transmitter port reacts to a Loss of Signal (LOS), Loss
of Frame (LOF) or other defect from the far-end client-facing receiver. Enter this keyword to
display the current setting.

power
Syntax
power [<value>]
Values
-12.00..+3.00 - gain in dBm
Sets the transmitted optical output power of the port.

WDM node a cluster O-CONN is provisioned to the line port).
Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 260scx2 <port-
aid> state" for details.

ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]

Enter number of hours and minutes

down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This
command may affect service.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Set to up to enable the port.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to up shall be rejected.

Issue 1 6637

Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
degintvl
Degrade interval (degintvl) specifies the number of consecutive bad seconds (see parameter
"degthr") to be detected before declaring a dDEG (signal degrade) defect for the client signal.
The defect is cleared if degintvl consecutive good seconds (see parameter "degthr") are
detected.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.
degthr
Degrade threshold (degthr) specifies a number of errored blocks as used for dDEG detection
for the client signal.
A second is declared as good if the number of detected errored blocks within one second is
less than degthr; otherwise the second is declared as bad second.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.
6.802.5 Examples
# show interface 260scx2 1/3/C1 hundredGige losprop
LOSPROP Action: laserOn

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 43sca1 <port-
aid> state" for details.
type
Syntax
type [otu3]
Values
otu3 - set the port to OTU3

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

exp_sapi
Syntax
exp_sapi [<value>]
Values
<value> - ASCII string 1..15 characters, enclosed in optional quotations.
Default
Null character (15 bytes each with hex value 00)
Specifies the expected incoming Source Access Point Identifier (SAPI).
timmresp
Syntax
timmresp [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - enables consequent action in case of dTIM (e.g. AIS insertion)
disabled - disables consequent action in case of dTIM (e.g. AIS insertion)
Default
disabled
Configures the consequent action for dTIM defect (Trail trace Identifier MisMatch RESPonse).
trccmp
Syntax
trccmp [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - comparison is activated
disabled - comparison is de-activated
Default
disabled
Configures the dTIM detection mode for the facility (trace compare). Turns the comparison
between the incoming sapi value and the provisioned (that is, exp_sapi) value as either on or
off.
tx_sapi
Syntax
tx_sapi [<value>]
Values
<value> - ASCII string 1..15 characters, enclosed in quotation marks.

6736 Issue 1
ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Set the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port.
Enter number of hours and minutes
For system default value see "config general ainstimer"
enabled
Set ains for the port to on.
disabled
Set ains for the port to off. The default value for ains is disabled.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This can
affect service.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance
up
Set to up to enable the port.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to up shall be rejected.

Degrade interval (degintvl) specifies the number of consecutive bad seconds (see parameter
"degthr") to be detected before declaring a dDEG (signal degrade) defect for the tengige.

degthr
Syntax

Values
1..128000 - 10GBE LAN
0 - Disabled
Default
0
Degrade threshold (degthr) specifies a number of errored blocks as used for dDEG detection
for the tengige.
A second is declared as good if the number of detected errored blocks within one second is
less than degthr; otherwise the second is declared as bad second.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.

NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.

rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

Degrade threshold (degthr) specifies a number of errored blocks as used for dDEG detection
for the ODU3e2.
A second is declared as good if the number of detected errored blocks within one second is
less than degthr; otherwise the second is declared as bad second.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.

6798 Issue 1
Set to ains to configure Automatic In-Service.
ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Set the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port.
Enter number of hours and minutes
For system default value see "config general ainstimer"
enabled
Set ains for the port to on.
disabled
Set ains for the port to off. The default value for ains is disabled.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This can
affect service.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance
up
Set to up to enable the port.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to up shall be rejected.

6812 Issue 1
ainstimer
Displays the Automatic In-Service Debounce time.
channel
Displays the wavelength of the pluggable module.
encmode
Displays the encapsulation mode used to transport the 10GbE LAN signal.
errfrmdrop
Displays whether inbound error frames are discarded or passed.
losprop
Displays the loss propagation behavior setting.
moduletype
Displays the pluggable module type to be used on the specified interface port.
degintvl
Degrade interval (degintvl) specifies the number of consecutive bad seconds (see parameter
"degthr") to be detected before declaring a dDEG (signal degrade) defect for the client tengige.
The defect is cleared if degintvl consecutive good seconds (see parameter "degthr") are
detected.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.
degthr
Degrade threshold (degthr) specifies a number of errored blocks as used for dDEG detection
for the tengige.
A second is declared as good if the number of detected errored blocks within one second is
less than degthr; otherwise the second is declared as bad second.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.

# show interface 43scx4 1/3/C1 tengige losprop
LOSPROP Action: laserOn

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 43sta1p <port-
aid> state" for details.

Sub-command: ospf
Configure OSPF parameter for a specific interface.
helloint
Syntax
helloint [<value>]
Values
1..65535 - time in seconds
Default
10 seconds
HELLO INTERVAL of the OSPF Interface. This is the time elapsed before the next HELLO PDU
is sent.
Note: Any 1830 OSC interfaces being used to connect to a 1696R must have their OSPF Hello
value configured as 1 second and their OSPF Router Dead Interval value provisioned to 5
seconds. If this is not done, there will be a Data Link Failure on the OSC and loss of
communication until it is done.
deadint
Syntax
deadint [<value>]
Values
1..65535 - time in seconds
Default
40 seconds
DEAD INTERVAL of the OSPF Interface. The dead interval is a timer used to timeout inactive
adjacencies. The dead interval value must always be greater than the hello interval value.
metric
Syntax
metric [<value>]
Values
1..65535

disabled - comparison is de-activated
Default
disabled
Configures the dTIM detection mode for the facility (trace compare). Turns the comparison

off.

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state

43stx4p} <port-aid> state" for details.

If the line port is involved in an OCH cross-connection in either direction, then the command
shall be denied.
If the line port is involved in an O-Conn/Topology of type External and the port AdminState is
not DOWN, then the command shall be denied.
Sub-command: tti
Configure OTU3 Trail Trace Identifier attributes. See "config interface {43stx4 | 43stx4p} <port-
aid> <otun-odun> tti".

# config interface 43stx4 1/3/l1 otu3 channel 9600

type
Syntax
type [1gbe | oc48 | stm16 | unassigned]
Values
1gbe - 1 Gb Ethernet client
oc48 - SONET OC-48 client
stm16 - SDH STM-16 client
unassigned - set the port as unassigned
Configures the port type.
Configuring the port type of client port C1 automatically configures the same port type on line
port L1. Likewise for client port C2 and line port L2.

rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

aid> state" for details.

6972 Issue 1
ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Set the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port.
Enter number of hours and minutes
For system default value see "config general ainstimer"
enabled
Set ains for the port to on.
disabled
Set ains for the port to off. The default value for ains is disabled.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This can
affect service.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance
up
Set to up to enable the port.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to up shall be rejected.

6.943 config interface 4dpa4
6.943.1 Purpose
This command configures the interface ports on the 4DPA4 card. Use this command to access
subcommands that allow you to configure the client ports (C{1-4}), or the line ports (L{1-2}) or the
eVOA ports (VA{1-2}).
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.943.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
6.943.3 Input Format
config interface 4dpa4 <port-aid>
6.943.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/L{1..2} - Specifies line port 1 ~ port 2
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..4} - Specifies client port 1 ~ port 4
<shelf>/<slot>/VA{1..2} - Specifies eVOA port 1 ~ port 2
* - Specifies all ports
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number, or * to list all of the 4dpa4 cards on the network element.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.

include a list of individual timeslots and/or a list of timeslot ranges. The syntax is: <x1[-
y1][,x2][-y2][,x3][-y3]..>. If only one timeslot is specified, the request is for a contiguous
range of timeslots starting at that value.

clients.)

FE - Enter 0 or single timeslot from {1..16}.
DVBASI - Enter 0, or a vtslist representing two timeslots from {1..16}. The vtslist can
include a list of individual timeslots and/or a list of timeslot ranges. The syntax is: <x1[-
y1][,x2][-y2][,x3][-y3]..>. If only one timeslot is specified, the request is for a contiguous
range of timeslots starting at that value.
SDSDI - Enter 0, or a vtslist representing two timeslots from {1..16}. The vtslist can include
a list of individual timeslots and/or a list of timeslot ranges. The syntax is: <x1[-y1][,x2][-
y2][,x3][-y3]..>. If only one timeslot is specified, the request is for a contiguous range of
timeslots starting at that value.
HDSDI - Enter 0 or a vtslist representing ten timeslots from {1..16}. The vtslist can include a
list of individual timeslots and/or a list of timeslot ranges. The syntax is: <x1[-y1][,x2][-
y2][,x3][-y3]..>. If only one timeslot is specified, the request is for a contiguous range of
timeslots starting at that value.
Specifies the line port, and the timeslot on the line port, that the client port will be mapped to.
Both line and vts parameters must be included. Both must be zero, or both must be non-zero.
Restrictions
This parameter applies only in FlexMux card mode. (It does not apply to DualTran FC400
clients.)

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 4dpa4 <port-
aid> state" for details.
type
Syntax
type [otu1 | unassigned]
Values
otu1 - assign the port.
unassigned - set the port as unassigned.
Specifies the port type. Applies only in FlexMux card mode. In DualTran card mode, the line
port is assigned/unassigned automatically when the corresponding client port is assigned/
unassigned.

If it is requested to change the parameter and the port AdminState is UP, then the command
shall be denied.
oprmode
Syntax
oprmode [<value>]
Values
ADDDrop - Add/Drop mode. Client port signals can be added and dropped to/from the line
ports. There is no regen function.
CROSSREGEN - Cross Regeneration Mode. Line-to-line regen function is activated. Client
ports cannot be used.
Default
ADDDROP
Operational mode of the 4DPA4. This parameter applies to both line ports, but it can be set only
on port L1. The L2 value is read-only, and is always equal to the L1 value. This parameter can
be set only in FlexMux card mode. The value is always ADDROP in DualTran card mode.
Sub-command: tti
Configures OTU1 Trail Trace Identifier attributes. See "config interface 4dpa4 <port-aid> <otun-
odun> tti".

option.

direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.

command is executed if "yes" is entered.

rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
7122 Issue 1
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface 4qpa8 <port-
aid> state" for details.
type
Syntax
type [och | unassigned]
Values
och - assign the port.
unassigned - set the port as unassigned.
Specifies the port type.
If a new value is requested to be set for this parameter and rmconport !="" is present, then the
command is denied.

Default
unassigned
The signal type provisioned on the ports.
Restrictions
Mixing async-mappingmode OC48/STM16 clients with other GMP-mapping clients (e.g.
GbE, FE, OC3/STM1, OC12/STM4, FCn, SDI) within the same port group is rejected. 8P20
subtype cards have two port groups, i.e group C{1..4} and group C{5..8}
• if there is already an existing port provisioned with the GMP mapping clients, then
provisioning with STM16 with asynch mappingmode within the same port group is
rejected
• if there is a STM16 client port provisioned with asynch mappingmode, then provisioning
with other client signal type within the same port group is rejected

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
The parameters of this subcommand are validated for consistency among the parameters and
for consistency with pre-existing configurations. These validations apply to all shelves if not
explicitly stated otherwise.
If the administrative state of the card is currently down then any attempt to provision a new port
shall be rejected.
If port L1 is assigned, then this command to assign port C7 is rejected.
If port L2 is assigned, then this command to assign port C8 is rejected.
If port VA1 is assigned, then this command to assign port C5 is rejected.
If port VA2 is assigned, then this command to assign port C6 is rejected.
The 8 client ports of 8P20 subtype cards are split into two groups, C1,C2,C3,C4 are in one
group, C5,C6,C7,C8 are in another group.
Each group supports up to 8 timeslot of OPU2 (i.e. 1xODU2), the mapping of client type and
number of TS are as the following table.
For example, in case C1 and C2 are assigned as FC400 and each of them will occupy 4 TS of
OPU2, the total 8 TS are all in use. Since no TS is left for the other two ports in the same group,
C3 and C4 cannot be assigned anymore.
Table 6-17 Timeslots (TS) per Client Type
Client Type Number of TS
FE 1
GbE 1
OTU1 2
OC3/STM1 1
OC12/STM4 1
OC48/STM16 2
FC100 1
FC200 2
FC400 4
SDSDI 1
HDSDI 2
3GSDI 3
If mgracd == cp or mgracd == mpcp is provisioned for a port then setting the type to
unassigned shall be rejected.
Note:
• see command "config/show mgracd" w.r.t. mgracd provisioning.

This command configures the Ethernet client port attributes on the following 8P20 subtype cards:

Use this command to:
• Set the auto negotiation status

• Set the loss propagation behavior
• Set the pluggable module type

6.1003 config interface <8p20-card> <client-port-aid> <sdi>
6.1003.1 Purpose
This command configures the Serial Digital Interface (SDI) port attributes on the following 8P20
subtype cards:
• 8P20 as card identifier for the subtypes: 8P20, 8P20B.
Use this command to:
• Set the SDI interface type
• Set the expected channel value for the pluggable module
• Set the loss propagation behavior
• Set the pluggable module type
• Select the container that will be used for client signal to ODU2 multiplexing
• Set the hold-off timer status
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

7194 Issue 1
Restrictions
This parameter applies only for OC48 and STM16.
Mixing async-mappingmode OC48/STM16 clients with other GMP-mapping clients (e.g.
GbE, FE, OC3/STM1, OC12/STM4) within the same port group is rejected. 8P20 subtypes
has two port groups, i.e group C{1..4} and group C{5..8}
• if there is already an existing port provisioned with the GMP mapping clients, then
provisioning with STM16 with asynch mappingmode within the same port group is
rejected
• if there is a STM16 client port provisioned with asynch mappingmode, then provisioning
with other client signal type within the same port group is rejected
If LO ODUK XC exists on the port, the operation to modify mappingmode shall be rejected.

Values
facility
terminal
Default
Entry required
Configures the loopback. For the usage of the individual values refer parameters in this
command.
If it is requested to enable a loopback for one type (e.g. facility) and there is already a loopback

be rejected.

disabled - disable the terminal loopback

Sub-command: pm
Sets the Performance Monitoring attributes associated with the line port. See "config interface
<8p20-card> <line-port-aid> PM"
Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface <8p20-card>
<port-aid> state" for details.

Syntax

Values

Specifies the port type.
If a new value is requested to be set for this parameter and rmconport !="" is present, then the
command is denied.
Command Validation
The parameters of this subcommand are validated for consistency among the parameters and
for consistency with pre-existing configurations. These validations apply to all shelves if not
explicitly stated otherwise.
If port BP1 or C7 is assigned, then this command to assign port L1 is rejected.
If port BP2 or C8 is assigned, then this command to assign port L2 is rejected.
If line port is associated with any LO-ODUk cross-connection, then this command to unassign
line port is rejected.
If the administrative state of the card is currently down then any attempt to provision a new port
shall be rejected.

Sets to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.

Specifies the port type for the client or line port.
Line port provisioning rules:
• Line port type values {otu4, otu4x2} can be provisioned independently on L1 and L2.
• If the first line port (L1 or L2) is set to type={otu4, otu4x2}, then any attempt to provision
the second line port to type={otu4Half, otu4Halfx5} shall be denied.
• Both L1 and L2 type values need to be set to unassigned before {otu4Half, otu4Halfx5}
can be provisioned.
• When L1 is provisioned with type=otu4Half, then L2 is automatically set to type=otu4Half
• When L1 is provisioned with type=otu4Halfx5, then L2 is automatically set to
type=otu4Halfx5
• To change the port type value for a specific line port, the port type must first be set to
unassigned

be denied.

port shall be rejected.

6.1035 config interface <d5x500-card> <port-aid> <otun>
6.1035.1 Purpose
This command allows to provision OCH related parameters of OTUk interface on the d5x500 type
cards:
• d5x500 - C-Band card with CFP4 client interfaces
• d5x500l - L-Band card with CFP4 client interfaces
• d5x500q - C-Band card with QSFP28 client interfaces
Note:
• The OTU layer is managed via non-card specific facility commands "config/show otu".
Use this command to:
• Set the grid step size which is based on the application (subsea or non-subsea)
• Set the receive channel frequency of each line port
• Set the receive channel frequency offset of each line port (subsea application)
• Set the transmit channel frequency of each line port
• Set the transmit channel frequency offset of each line port (subsea application)
• Set the management mode for line transmission configuration (D5X500Q only)
• Set the line port according to the OTSIG model (D5X500Q only)
• Set the operation mode
• Set the Regen response action
• Set the encoding
• Set the transmit optical power on each line port
• Set the alarm profile
• Set the line signal degrade attributes (D5X500 and D5X500Q only)
This command can only be applied if the line port type is configured to:
• otu4
• otu4x2
• otu4Half
• otu4Halfx5
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

degucbthr
Syntax
degucbthr [<value>]
Values
1..20000 - indicates the number of detected UCBs per 100G within the interval degucbintvl.
Default
11 - for sdfec-g2
Degrade threshold (degucbthr) specifies a number of uncorrectable errored blocks from the
FEC decoder in the interval degucbintvl as used for dDEGUCB detection for a line port.
Degrade threshold (degucbthr) is provisioned per each 100G at the line interface. The following
calculation is done internally for each line interface type:
• When the line interface is provisioned for 100G transmission (i.e. line type = otu4): the
provisioned value for degucbthr is used.
• When the line interface is provisioned for 200G transmission (i.e., line type = otu4x2):
the provisioned value for degucbthr is internally multiplied by 2. Thus, the actual degrade
threshold value is degucbthr x 2.
• When the line interface is provisioned for 50G transmission (i.e., line type = otu4Half):
the provisioned value for degucbthr is internally multiplied by 0.5. Thus, the actual
degrade threshold value is degucbthr x 0.5.
• When the line interface is provisioned for 250G transmission (i.e., line type =
otu4Halfx5): the provisioned value for degucbthr is internally multiplied by 2.5. Thus, the
actual degrade threshold value is degucbthr x 2.5.
An interval degucbintvl is declared as good if the number of detected uncorrectable errored
blocks within one degucbintvl interval is less than the actual degrade threshold value; otherwise
the interval is declared as bad.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by one allowed value.
Restrictions
This parameter applies to the D5X500 and D5X500Q cards only.

managementmode
Syntax
managementmode [<value>]
Values
otu - line transmission is configured via individual parameter settings
otsig - line transmission is configured in an OTSiG like approach
Default
otu
Specifies the mode how a user manages the line transmission configuration with values as
follows:
- otu: line transmission configuration is done via the sub-commands:
• config interface <d5x500-card> <port-aid> <otn> <encoding> or
• config interface <d5x500-card> <port-aid> <otn> encoding [txshape | phasenc] or
• config OTU <otu-aid> fectype
- otsig: line transmission configuration is done via the sub-command:
• config interface <d5x500-card> <port-aid> <otn> otsig
Restrictions
The parameter and parameter values are applicable as follows:
• value otu: This value is applicable for the following <d5x500-card>: d5x500q
• value otsig: This value is applicable for the following <d5x500-card>: d5x500q
• The parameter is not applicable for <d5x500-card> = {d5x500, d5x500l}
The value managementmode = otsig is only allowed for <otun> = OTU4x2. For all other
values of <otun>, any attempt to set managementmode = otsig is denied.
If the managementmode is changed from otu to otsig, then the NE checks whether there exists
an OTSiG profile matching the current line transmission configuration; i.e.:
• The payload rate value of the profile is equal to payload rate derived from configured
type parameter value of the interface (payload rate == 100G for type == otu4, payload
rate == 200G for type == otu4x2).
• The encoding rate value of the profile is equal to the value as configured for the
encoding parameter of the interface.
• The fectype value of the profile is equal to the value as configured for fectype parameter
of one of OTU facilities associated with the interface/port.
OT management commands
D5X500 interface commands
config interface <d5x500-card> <port-aid> <otun>
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 7317
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
• The phase encoding value of the profile is equal to the value as configured for the
encoding parameter of the interface.
• The txshape value of the profile is equal to the value as configured for the txshape
parameter of the interface.
• The clotutype value of the profile is equal to the value "OTU4"
If a matching profile exists, then the NE sets the parameter profileId to the profileid value of the
matching OTSiG profile.
If no matching profile exists, then the value 0 is used for the parameter profileId and the current
line transmission configuration is kept/frozen until a new value profileid value is provisioned by
a user.
If the managementmode is changed from otsig to otu, then the NE re-sets the value for the
parameter profileid to factory default.
It is allowed to have one line port provisioned with managementmode = otu and the other line
port provisioned with managmentmode = otsig.
If managmentmode = otsig, then no parameters in the profileID can be changed.
The parameters in the profileID include: encoding FEC type, txshape and phasenc. The
phasenc value (absolute or differential) must be the same on L1 and L2.
Example 1:
If both line ports are set to managementmode = otsig, with profileID 20, the phasenc value for
each line is phasenc = absolute. Any attempt to change the phasenc value to phasenc =
differential shall be denied. If managementmode is changed to managementmode = otu on L1,
the value phasenc = absolute is kept. If the User then changes the value to phasenc =
differential on L1, then this value will also be applied to L2. The result on L2 is that the profileID
value will go from profileID 20 to profileID 0.
Example 2:
If both line ports are set to managmentmode = otu, then the provisioned value for the phasenc
parameter will be applied to both ports. Changing the phasenc value on one line port will also
change the phasenc value on the second line port. If the User now sets managementmode =
otsig on L2 (with profileID 20), L2 will be set to phasenc = absolute, and L1 would either stay
with phasenc = absolute or change to phasenc = absolute (if it was initially set to phasenc =
differential).

7320 Issue 1
Notes:
• IO card specific requirements may specify additional restrictions.
The D5X500 cards support the following rate (T) value in otustruct values with different OTSi
members:
• 'otu4#<i>&otu4#<j>' - if OTSiG consists of 1x200G OTSi
The D5X500 cards support the following ID assignment for otustruct value for OTU4 type:
• ID=={1..5}
The assigned OTSiG Payload Rate from the profileID must match the payload rate as derived
from the otustruct value.
As the total capacity can be derived from the otustruct of each OTSIG, it shall not cross the
max capacity which the card can support.
And each OTSi payload rate can also be calculated from OTSIG capacity divided by OTSi port
numbers, each OTSi payload rate shall not cross the max rate which the OTSi port can support.
As the sequence for each OTUs specified in otustruct determines their multiplex order in
OTSIG, the same sequence number should be given on both ends for the same client service.
It must be guaranteed by user as there is no overhead on OTSIG level to transport this
information.
Note:
• The conclusion is, that the otustruct string value must be the same on both ends if ID
part within the string is not considered.
An OTUID value can only be used once within an OTUSTRUCT value. If the User attempts to
use the same OTUID value more than one time for the term 'T#ID' within an OTUSTRUCT
value, then the command will be denied.
When serverports are unassigned, and the managementmode parameter value is changed to
managementmode = otsig on a line port, the otustruct for that port is initially set to its default
value.
When managementmode = otsig, the otustruct value can be modified from the default value to
a new value:
• For the L1 port: otustruct = otu4#<i>&otu4#<j>, which translates to serverport
configuration OTUID <i> = l1_ch1 and OTUID <j> = l1_ch2
• For the L2 port: otustruct = otu4#<k>&otu4#<l>, which translates to serverport
configuration OTUID <k> = l2_ch1 and OTUID <l> = l2_ch2
Note: It is possible to modify both OTUIDs in the otustruct at the same time, using one
command execution. Alternatively, the OTUIDs can be changed one at a time. Software will
determine if the OTUIDs are available.
If serverports are provisioned initially with managmentmode = otu, and then the
managmentmode value is changed to managmentmode = otsig, then Software will
automatically set the otustruct value according to the serverport configuration.
Example:
• For line port L1: If serverport values OTUID<i> = l1_ch1 and OTUID<j> = l1_ch2, then
Software will translate this serverport configuration to otustruct = otu4#<i>&otu4#<j>
OT management commands
D5X500 interface commands
config interface <d5x500-card> <port-aid> <otun>
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 7321
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
• For line port L2: If serverport values OTUID<k> = l2_ch1 and OTUID<l> = l2_ch2, then
Software will translate this serverport configuration to otustruct = otu4#<k>&otu4#<l>
Note: Changing from managementmode = otu to managmentmode = otsig can be done without
having to delete serverports. When managmentmode = otsig and otustruct value is set, then
the "config otu" command is no longer used to provision serverport values.
If one serverport is unassigned and the other serverport is provisioned with managmentmode =
otu, and then the managmentmode value is changed to managmentmode = otsig, then
Software will:
1. check all five OTUIDs to see which OTUID values are unassigned (that is, not being
used) with respect to serverports, and then
2. choose the first (i.e., lowest OTUID number) to fill in the otustruct.
Example:
• For line port L1: If serverports are initially set to OTUID 3 = l1_ch2, and l1_ch1 is
unassigned when managmentmode = otu. Now if the managmentmode value is changed
to otsig, the otustruct is not complete because l1_ch1 is unassigned. Software will then
check all five OTUIDs to see which OTUIDs are not currently being used, and then
choose the lowest OTUID number to fill in the otustruct. Suppose in this example, that
OTUID 2 is the lowest unused OTUID. Then OTUID 2 will be assigned to serverport l1_
ch1. The result is otustruct = otu4#2&otu4#3
Note: In this scenario, Software is used to initially complete the otustruct. The User can then
modify the otustruct to use the intended OTUIDs.
If managmentmode = otsig was provisioned initially, but then is changed to managmentmode =
otu:
• Software will automatically set the serverport values based on the otustruct value
• The profileID goes back to the value 0.
Example:
For line port L1: Initially, otustruct = otu4#<i>&otu4#<j>. When the managmentmode is changed
to managementmode = otu, Software will automatically translate this into the following
serverport values:
• OTUID <i> = l1_ch1
• OTUID <j> = l1_ch2
The same process is used for line port L2.
Note: If the otustruct value is changed, then the serverport parameter of the associated OTUID
facility is changed accordingly.
When oprmode = regen and managmentmode = otu, the serverports are automatically set with
the following fixed values:
For <otun> = otu4x2:
• OTUID 1 = l1_ch1
• OTUID 2 = l1_ch2
• OTUID 3 = l2_ch1

This command allows to provision modulation format (encoding) related parameters of OTUk
interface on the d5x500 type cards:

phasenc
Syntax
phasenc [<value>]
Values
absolute - indicates high performance mode
differential - indicates compatibility mode. This value is allowed for all encoding values with
the exception of SPQPSK (that is, the combination of differential and SPQPSK is not
allowed)
Default
absolute - if the other port on the card is unassigned
provisioned value from the other port - if the other port is assigned.
Specifies the phase encoding mode applied to the optical carrier of the line port.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by one allowed value.
Specific phasenc provisioning behaviour:
• The phasenc value must be the same for L1 and L2.
• For encoding={8QAM, 16QAM (200G), QPSK}, phasenc can be set on either L1 or L2.
The phasenc value set for the first line interface will define the phasenc value on the
second line interface.
• For encoding={BPSK, 16QAM_250G}, phasenc is set on L1. Phasenc on L2 is auto-
provisioned from L1. Any attempt to provision phasenc on L2 when encoding={BPSK,
16QAM_250G} shall be denied.
• If the first line interface is provisioned with encoding={8QAM, 16QAM (200G), QPSK,
BPSK, 16QAM_250G} and phasenc=differential, then any attempt to provision the
second line interface with encoding=SPQPSK shall be denied.
• If the first line interface is provisioned with encoding=SPQPSK, then any attempt to
provision the second line interface with any encoding value and phasenc=differential
shall be denied.
When modifying the phasenc parameter value:
• In a non-dangling OT application, all OCH XC must first be deleted before the phasenc
parameter can be modified

Values
cold - A cold restart reinitializes the module firmware and hardware and is service affecting.
warm - A warm restart re-initializes the module firmware only and is not service affecting.
force - optional parameter together with cold.
Performs a restart of the port/module.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the port AdminState to DOWN or MT.
If it is requested to perform a cold reset and the force option is not specified and the port
AdminState is UP, then the command shall be denied.
The reset command is performed as best effort action; i.e. the command is accepted if no

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Restrictions
This parameter is applicable only for line port.

(for example the moduletype parameter).
2. All parameters which will become new applicable for the new type shall be set to the factory
default value as specified for this type
(for example hundredgige ssfdelayca parameter will be set to 'idle').
3. The parameter modulecapfile applicable for type otsi shall be set in order to reference the
module capability file based on the already configured moduletype value.

-- is rejected, if one of the following constraints is met:
1. The port is used for service.
2. The port is currently assigned to type otsi and is a member of an OTSiG.
3. The parameter value for rmconport is not an empty string.
Note:
A port of type otuk/otsi is considered in context of this rule as used for service, if for an
associated OTU facility the SDEE state is present.
-- the following behaviour shall be applied (besides the type parameter value change):
1. All parameters defined for type equipment shall be kept unchanged (for example the
moduletype parameter).
2. Other parameters like loopback, portrole shall be reset to the specified factory default.

6.1050 config interface d6ad2t4 <port-aid> equipment
6.1050.1 Purpose
This command configures the port/interface equipment attributes on following D6AD2T4 subtype
cards:
• D6AD2T4 as card identifier for the subtypes: D6AD2T4H, D6AD2T4L
Use this command to:
• set the pluggable module type
This command can only be applied if interface type is configured to:
• equipment - Equipment port
An equipment port models only the equipment sub-part/parameters of a port on an IO card. This
allows as user to provision the transmission port via two steps:
1. In the first step only the equipment data is provisioned (for example moduletype).
2. In the second step the transmission port including type is provisioned (for example port is
configured as hundredgige port).
Notes:
1. The user can change/convert an equipment port to a transmission port or vice versa while
keeping all equipment configuration data.
2. The user can also convert from one transmission port type (for example hundredgige) to
another transmission port type (for example OTU4) using the equipment port type as
intermediate step.
3. There are no facilities (i.e. OTU, ODUNIM, ODUPTF) associated with an equipment port. In
context of change/convert of an equipment port the associated facilities are auto-deleted or
auto-created by the NE.
4. The NE will monitor and report all equipment defects/alarms as defined by the equipment alarm
profile (parameter almprof - "config interface d6ad2t4 <port-aid>" command).
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

moduletype

7388 Issue 1
csfdelaytimer
Syntax
csfdelaytimer [<value>]
Values
{0..255} - period using 10 milli-second as base unit (value is multiple of 10 ms)
Default
0
This parameter controls the period for which a laseroff CA (via losprop), triggered by a CSF
condition, is delayed. i.e. the laser shut down is performed after CSFDELAYTIMER has
expired, as long as the CSF condition is still present. During the delay time, no replacement
signal is inserted (it is expected that the far-end has inserted LFI). The delay timer is reset if
CSF is deasserted before it has expired and is re-triggered on another occurrence of CSF. If
losprop is configured for laseron, then there is no replacement signal inserted (it is expected
that the far-end still inserts LFI).
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.

Values
8023-bj - IEEE 802.3bj FEC is configured

8023-bj

Syntax

Values
enabled - enable FEC_bypass_indication
Default
enabled
Fecbypassind (FEC Bypass Indication) determines whether the corresponding option as
defined in IEEE 802.3 is set or not. If enabled this implies:
• dHISER defect detection based on the number of RS-FEC symbol errors is enabled
• LFI is inserted as a consequent action if dHISER is present.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
This parameter controls the period for which a laseroff CA (via losprop), triggered by a CSF
condition, is delayed. i.e. the laser shut down is performed after CSFDELAYTIMER has
expired, as long as the CSF condition is still present. During the delay time, no replacement
signal is inserted (it is expected that the far-end has inserted LFI). The delay timer is reset if
CSF is deasserted before it has expired and is re-triggered on another occurrence of CSF. If
losprop is configured for laseron, then there is no replacement signal inserted (it is expected
that the far-end still inserts LFI).
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.

enabled
Fecbypassind (FEC Bypass Indication) determines whether the corresponding option as
defined in IEEE 802.3 is set or not. If enabled this implies:
• dHISER defect detection based on the number of RS-FEC symbol errors is enabled
• LFI is inserted as a consequent action if dHISER is present.

6.1053 config interface d6ad2t4 <port-aid> 800gbe
6.1053.1 Purpose
This command configures the 800gbe client port attributes on the following D6AD2T4 subtype
cards:
• D6AD2T4 as card identifier for the subtypes: D6AD2T4H, D6AD2T4L
Use this command to:
• Set the ASAP profile.
• Reset the position of analyzer.
• Set the FEC bypass indication.
• Insert a single 66B error.
• Set the loss propagation behavior.
• Set the pluggable module type.
• Set the laser behavior for server signal degrade.
• Configure the ssf delay timer for LFI holdoff, to insert IDLE in the event of SSF up to a maximum
of the delay time. After that, the consequent action is defined by losprop..
• Configure the Ethernet maintenance signal after ODU SSF detection, while SSFDELAY-TIMER
is running.
• Configure csfdelaytimer for CSF holdoff, up to a maximum of the delay timer. After that, the
consequent action is defined by losprop.
• Configure the test signal.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

Default

0p1ghz-channelrx
Syntax
0p1ghz-channelrx [<freq>]
Values
For D6AD2T4 with subtype H:
none - No channel set
{9130.000..9605.000} - DWDM center frequencies
{9605.010..9610.000} - extended DWDM center frequencies for dangling OT usage
For D6AD2T4 with subtype L:
none - No channel set
{8610.000..9085.000} - DWDM center frequencies
Default
none
Specifies the receive channel frequency using 4.3 format. Enter a value in steps of N x 0.010 to
select a channel frequency on the 0.1GHz grid, or a value in steps of N x 0.625 to select a
center frequency on the 6.25GHz grid, or any value using 4.3 format. Examples are 9130.010,
9130.625, 9130.875 or 9130.250. in GHz. Enter this keyword without option to display the
current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by one of the <freq> value.
The channelrx parameter value is calculated from the 0p1ghz-channelrx value. When photonic
cross-connect has been provisioned, and then afterwards the user selects a 0p1ghz-channelrx
value, if the calculated channelrx value does not match the <itu> value configured by the
photonic cross-connect command, then 0p1ghz-channelrx provisioning is denied.
When the 0p1ghz-channelrx is provisioned before the photonic cross-connect is configured, if
the <itu> value in the photonic cross-connect command does not match the calculated
channelrx value, then the photonic cross-connect provisioning is denied.
When the port is provisioned as otsi w/o being assigned as a member of an OTSiG (i.e. otsigid
== none), setting the 0p1ghz-channelrx parameter to a value that is not the default value is
denied.

6.1059 show interface d6ad2t4 <port-aid> equipment
6.1059.1 Purpose
This command displays the port/interface equipment attributes on following D6AD2T4 subtype
cards:
• D6AD2T4 as card identifier for the subtypes: D6AD2T4H, D6AD2T4L
Use this command to:
• Display the Automatic In-Service Debounce time
• Display the pluggable module data
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1059.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
6.1059.3 Input Format
show interface d6ad2t4 <port-aid> equipment
ainstimer
moduletype
6.1059.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..6} - Specifies client ports
<shelf>/<slot>/C1_{1..4} - Specifies client breakout ports on C1
<shelf>/<slot>/C2_{1..4} - Specifies client breakout ports on C2
<shelf>/<slot>/C3_{1..4} - Specifies client breakout ports on C3
<shelf>/<slot>/C4_{1..4} - Specifies client breakout ports on C4
<shelf>/<slot>/C5_{1..4} - Specifies client breakout ports on C5
<shelf>/<slot>/C6_{1..4} - Specifies client breakout ports on C6
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.

6.1060 show interface d6ad2t4 <port-aid> hundredGige
6.1060.1 Purpose
This command displays the client port hundredGige attributes on the following D6AD2T4 subtype
cards:
• D6AD2T4 as card identifier for the subtypes: D6AD2T4H, D6AD2T4L
Use this command to:
• Display the automatic in-service timer.
• Display the ASAP profile.
• Display the csfdelaytimer value.
• Display the Digital Diagnostics Monitoring (DDM) data.
• Display the Forward Error Correction (FEC) type.
• Display the FEC bypass indication.
• Display the loss propagation behavior.
• Display the pluggable module type.
• Display the client laser behavior for server signal degrade.
• Display the ssfdelayca value.
• Display the ssfdelaytimer value.
• Display the test signal.
• Display the test signal result.

6.1060.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/C1_{1..4} - Specifies client breakout ports on C1
<shelf>/<slot>/C2_{1..4} - Specifies client breakout ports on C2
<shelf>/<slot>/C3_{1..4} - Specifies client breakout ports on C3
<shelf>/<slot>/C4_{1..4} - Specifies client breakout ports on C4
<shelf>/<slot>/C5_{1..4} - Specifies client breakout ports on C5
<shelf>/<slot>/C6_{1..4} - Specifies client breakout ports on C6
Default
Entry required
Specifies the access identifier of the port.
Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot number, a slash, and the port label to access the port.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables”, for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
ainstimer
Displays the Automatic In-Service Debounce time.
almprof
Displays the name of the ASAP (Alarm Severity Assignment Profile) used for alarm reporting.
csfdelaytimer
Displays the period (in 10ms units) for which a laseroff CA (via losprop), triggered by a CSF
condition, is delayed. i.e. the laser shut down is performed after CSFDELAYTIMER has
expired, as long as the CSF condition is still present. During the delay time, no replacement
signal is inserted (it is expected that the far-end has inserted LFI). The delay timer is reset if
CSF is deasserted before it has expired and is re-triggered on another occurrence of CSF. If
losprop is configured for laseron, then there is no replacement signal inserted (it is expected
that the far-end still inserts LFI).
ddm
Displays on demand the digital diagnostics monitoring data of the pluggable module.
OT management commands

Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 7435
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
fectype
Displays the fectype on the port.
fecbypassind
Displays the FEC bypass indication setting for the hundredGige client port.
losprop
Displays the loss propagation setting.
moduletype
Displays the pluggable module type to be used on the specified interface port.
ssdca
Displays the laser behavior for server signal degrade setting.
ssfdelayca
Displays the Ethernet maintenance signal that is inserted after ODU SSF detection, while
SSFDELAYTIMER is running (from start of timer until the defect is cleared or the timer expires).
ssfdelaytimer
Displays the period (in 10ms units) for which a laseroff CA (via losprop), triggered by an SSF
condition, is delayed. i.e. the laser shut down is performed after SSFDELAYTIMER has expired,
as long as the SSF condition is still present. During the delay time, IDLE is inserted. The delay
timer is reset if SSF is deasserted before it has expired and is re-triggered on another
occurrence of SSF. LF is inserted after the timer expires, if losprop is configured for laseron.
testsignal
Displays the test signal setting.
testsignalresult
Displays the current measurements for an enabled ethernet idle test signal where a sync
header error has been inserted.
6.1060.5 Examples
# show interface d6ad2t4 1/3/C3_1 hundredGige losprop
LOSPROP Action: laserOn
# show interface d6ad2t4 1/3/c3_1 hundredGige ddm

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Module Type : Q56DD-400G-4xLR1-DR4++
Digital Diagnostic Monitoring (DDM) data:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Supply Voltage : 3.00 mV

6.1063 show interface d6ad2t4 <port-aid> otsi
6.1063.1 Purpose
This command displays OTSi attributes for OTSi interfaces under one OTSIG on the following
D6AD2T4 subtype cards:
• D6AD2T4 as card identifier for the subtypes: D6AD2T4H, D6AD2T4L
Use this command to:
• Display the receive channel frequency on the 0.1GHz grid
• Display the transmit channel frequency on the 0.1GHz grid
• Display the calculated receive channel frequency value
• Display the calculated transmit channel frequency value
• Display the automatic In-Service Debounce time
• Display the ASAP profile
• Display the designated port operation mode of each line port
• Display the AID of partner port if the line port has been in regen designated port mode
• Display the link span type
• Display the transmit power on each line port
• Display the 1-second pre-fec BER
• Display the OTSIGID the port belongs to
• Display the pluggable module type
• Display the name of the module capability file
This command can only be applied if the line port type is configured to:
• otsi
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1063.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer

7446 Issue 1
designatedportmode
Displays the designated port mode for OTSi port in commissioning phase before the OTSIG is
created on the port.
designatedregenpair
Displays the associated line port from a different card which has been used as a partner port for
3R.
gridstepsize
Displays the grid step size.
linkspan
Displays the DWDM link span type for this line port to be connected with which requires
different receiver sensitivity and optics control mode.
modulecapfile
Displays the name of the module capability file. The contents of the file can be displayed via the
command "show capabilityfile".
moduletype
Returned values:
BMDCO12 for D6AD2T4
BMDCO12L for D6AD2T4L
Displays the pluggable module type to be used on the specified interface port.
otsigid
Displays the OTSIGID the port belongs to. If it does not belong to any OTSIG, it shall be shown
as none.
power
Displays the transmitted optical output power of the OTSi port.
prefecber
Displays the 1-second pre-FEC BER.

ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Set the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port.
Enter number of hours and minutes
For system default value see "config general ainstimer"
enabled
Set ains for the port to on.
disabled
Set ains for the port to off. The default value for ains is disabled.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This may
affect service.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Set to up to enable the port.

6.1081.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values

<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..8} - Specifies client port 1 ~ port 8
* - display list of ports
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number, or * to list all of the mvac8b cards on the network
element.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.

Set to ains to configure Automatic In-Service.
ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Set the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port.
Enter number of hours and minutes
For system default value see "config general ainstimer"
enabled
Set ains for the port to on.
disabled
Set ains for the port to off. The default value for ains is disabled.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This may
affect service.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Set to up to enable the port.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Note: This parameter only takes effect only "when config card PTPCTL syncesupp" is set to
"enable" and the port's SYNCEOPRMODE is set to "sync".
Restrictions
the following enhanced QLs are valid only when "config sync <shelf-aid> sync0 syncmsg"
syncMsg is set to "enabledeql".
• ePRTC
• PRTC
• ePRC
• eSEC
The parameter is not applicable when the module type is 1000B-T2.
synceoprmode
Syntax
synceoprmode [sync | non-sync]
Values
{sync | non-sync}
Default
sync
Configure port Synchronous Ethernet Operation Mode. When the port is in SYNC mode,
recovered clock of its input signal can be selected as a reference clock to the system clock.
When the port is in NON-SYNC mode, the recovered clock of its input signal shall not be a
candidate to system timing references.
Restrictions
When the "moduletype" parameter of the port is "1000B-T2", the value "sync" is not
applicable and the provisioning will be denied.
6.1089.5 Examples
# config interface PTPCTL 1/7/P1 1gbe ssmtrans NONE
# config interface PTPCTL 1/7/P1 1gbe SYNCEOPRMODE NON-SYNC
# config interface PTPCTL 1/7/P1 1gbe ssmtrans ePRC
Error: Request Failed - Enhanced QLs and extended QL-TLV are not supported

Values

Configure port Synchronous Ethernet Operation Mode. When the port is in SYNC mode,

1pps&ToD interface Output
Table 6-19 Information for the specified 1pps&ToD interface
Label Description
direction Indicate the direction of the interface, either input or output.
ppsFormat Indicate the format of the 1pps signal, which is:
- 1 pulse per second
todFormat Indicate the format of the tod signal, which is:
- UBX
- ITU-T
cableCorrection Indicate the configured cable correction value. The unit is ns.
compensationIn Indicate the compensation value for 1PPS input. The unit is ns.
compensationOut Indicate the compensation value for 1PPS output. The unit is ns.

7558 Issue 1
Default
disabled
Set to ains to configure Automatic In-Service.
ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Set the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port.
Enter number of hours and minutes
For system default value see "config general ainstimer"
enabled
Set ains for the port to on.
disabled
Set ains for the port to off. The default value for ains is disabled.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This may
affect service.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Set to up to enable the port.

6.1109 show interface PTPIO
6.1109.1 Purpose
This command displays the interface ports on the PTPIO card. Use this command to show
attributes of the PTPIO ports.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1109.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
6.1109.3 Input Format
show interface PTPIO <port-aid>
6.1109.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/LINE{1..2} - Specifies line port 1 ~ port 2
<shelf>/<slot>/SIG{1..2} - Specifies sig port 1 ~ port 2
<shelf>/<slot>/ITP{1..2} - Specifies ITP timing port 1 ~ port 2
<shelf>/<slot>/TP{1..2} - Specifies TP timing port 1 ~ port 2
* - display list of ports
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number, or * to list all of the PTPIO cards on the network element.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.

6.1117 config interface PTPIOC <osc-port-aid>
6.1117.1 Purpose
This command configures the OSC Line ports and OSC Signal ports on PTPIOC cards.
Use this command to:
• Specify a description for the OSC port
• Display the current settings for the OSC port
• Configure port mode for the OSC port
• Configure module type for the OSC port
• Configure PM for the OSC port
• Configure the state of the OSC port
• Specify the fiber connectivity of the OSC port
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1117.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
6.1117.3 Input Format
config interface PTPIOC <osc-port-aid>
connport
description
detail
mode
moduletype
pm
state
6.1117.4 Input Parameters
<osc-port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/{OSC1L, OSC2L} - Specifies OSC Line port 1 ~ port 2
<shelf>/<slot>/{OSC1S, OSC2S} - Specifies OSC Signal port 1 ~ port 2
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number.

PTPIOC interface commands
config interface PTPIOC <osc-port-aid>
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 7577
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
description
Syntax
description [<string>]
Values
<string> - 255 character ASCII string
"" - to clear the description
Default
""
Specifies a description for the interface port. Enter this keyword followed by a string that
describes the interface, or enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current
description for the interface.
detail
Displays the current detailed settings for the port.
mode
Syntax
mode [<value>]
Values
100BASEFX - set the OSC port to carry a 100baseFX signal
OC3 - set the OSC port to carry an OC-3 signal
STM1 - set the OSC port to carry an STM-1 signal
Default
OC3 - if ANSI
STM1- if ETSI
Specifies the port OSC mode for OSC Line port and OSC Signal port.
Restrictions
Do not set to 100BaseFx mode if the OSC is to carry IPv6 traffic; the 100BaseFx mode
does not support IPv6. Setting 100BaseFx will be denied if there is an IPv6 loopback.
The value 100BASEFX is not applicable when the moduletype is SUL1GOU, SUL1GOD,
SS1GOU or SS1GOD.
moduletype
Syntax
moduletype [auto | <values>]

7578 Issue 1
Values
The allowed value for OSC1S and OSC2S:
SS-16.1A - short range OC-3 or FE signal.
SS-16.2O - short range OC-3 or FE signal.
auto
The allowed value for OSC1L and OSC2L:
SULS1BOU - 1506nm BIDI SFP Upstream.
SULS1BOD - 1514nm BIDI SFP Downstream.
SS1GOU - 1506nm BIDI short range 1GE SFP Upstream.
SS1GOD - 1514nm BIDI short range 1GE SFP Downstream.
SUL1GOU - 1506nm BIDI ULH 1GE SFP Upstream.
SUL1GOD - 1514nm BIDI ULH 1GE SFP Downstream.
SULS1OU - 1514nm BIDI ULH FE/STM-1 OSC SFP Upstream.
SULS1OD - 1517nm BIDI ULH FE/STM-1 OSC SFP Downstream.
auto
Default
auto
Specifies the SFP moduletype of the OSC Line port and OSC Signal port.
auto - The network element accepts any of the qualified pluggable module, and automatically
provisions the moduletype upon initial insertion.
Sub-command: pm

configure pm attributes.
Sub-command: state

connport
Syntax
connPort [delete | <slot-aid>] [<port>]

Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 7579
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
<slot-aid> - the slot-aid of the connected card in the form <shelf>/<slot>
delete - clear a previous value
<port> value:
oscin - specify the Rx of OSC port on LD, OSCT or IROADM card
oscout - specify the Tx of OSC port on LD, OSCT or IROADM card
oscsfp - specify the OSCSFP port on LD, OSCT or IROADM card
osc{1..2}in - specify the Rx of OSC{1..2} port on optical mux/demux card
osc{1..2}out - specify the Tx of OSC{1..2} port on optical mux/demux card
oscsfp{1..2}sfp - specify the OSCSFP{1..2} port on optical mux/demux card
Default
Entry required
Specify the fiber connectivity between OSC port on PTPIOC card and OSC or OSCSFP port on
LD, OSCT or IROADM card.
Note:
1. When delete the previous connectivity provisioning, the <slot-aid> and <port> values
are not required.
2. For OSC line ports (OSC1L and OSC2L), it shall be connected to the Rx or Tx of OSC
port on LD, OSCT or IROADM card, or the Rx or TX of OSC{1..2} port on optical mux/
demux card.
3. For OSC signal port (OSC2S and OSC2S), it shall be connected to the OSCSFP port
on LD, OSCT or IROADM card, or the OSCSFP{1..2} port on optical mux/demux card.
Restrictions
The <port> value "oscin", "oscout", "osc{1..2}" in and "osc{1..2}out" are applicable for OSC
line ports (OSC1L and OSC2L) only, and the <port> value "oscsfp" and "oscsfp{1..2}" are
applicable for OSC signal ports (OSC1S and OSC2S) only.
This command is valid only if the OSC line port or OSC signal port is connected to the
following LD, OSCT, IROADM or optical mux/demux cards.
• LD cards: A2325A, AHPHG, AHPLG, ALPHG, AM2125A, AM2125B, AM2318A, ASWG,
AM2032A, ASG, ASGLP, AA2DONW, AA2DONWB, AWBILA
• OSCT cards: OSCT, OSCTAPR
• IROADM cards: IROADMF, IROADMV, IROADM9M, IROADM9R, IRDM20, IRDM32,
IRDM32LP, IR9, IR9LP
• Optical mux/demux card: OMDCL

description
Syntax
description [<string>]
Values
<string> - 255 character ASCII string
"" - to clear the description
Default
""
Specifies a description for the interface port. Enter this keyword followed by a string that
describes the interface, or enter this keyword without any parameters to display the current
description for the interface.
detail
Displays the current detailed settings for the port.
type
Syntax
type [ots | unassigned]
Values
ots - OTS type port.
unassigned - set the port as unassigned
Default
unassigned
Specifies the port type for the OTC Line port.
Sub-command: pm
Sets the Performance Monitoring attributes. See "config interface PTPIOC <port-aid> pm" to
configure pm attributes.
Sub-command: state
Configures the administrative state for the port. See command "config interface PTPIOC <port-
aid> state" for details.
Sub-command: ots
Sets the OTS type attributes for OTC Line ports on the PTPIOC card. See "config interface
PTPIOC <otcline-port-aid> ots".
