Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 7583
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
connport
Syntax
connPort [delete | <slot-aid>] [<port>]
Values
<slot-aid> - the slot-aid of the connected card in the form <shelf>/<slot>
delete - clear a previous value
<port> value:
oscin - specify the Rx of OSC port on LD, OSCT or IROAMD card
oscout - specify the Tx of OSC port on LD, OSCT or IROAMD card
osc{1..2}in - specify the Rx of OSC{1..2} port on OMDCL card
osc{1..2}out - specify the Tx of OSC{1..2} port on OMDCL card
expin - specify the Rx of EXP port on SFDC8[A-E] card
expout - specify the Tx of EXP port on SFDC8[A-E] card
Default
Entry required
Specify the fiber connectivity between OTC line port on PTPIOC card and the port on LD,
OSCT, IROADM, optical mux/demux or optical filter card.
Note:
1. When delete the previous connectivity provisioning, the <slot-aid> and <port> values
are not required.
2. For OTC line ports (OTC1L and OTC2L), it shall be connected to the Rx or Tx of the
following ports
• OSC port on LD, OSCT or IROADM card
• OSC{1..2} port on OMDCL card
• EXP port on SFDC8[A-E] card
Restrictions
This command is valid only if the OTC line port is connected to the following LD, OSCT,
IROADM, optical mux/demux or optical filter cards.
• LD cards: A2325A, AHPHG, AHPLG, ALPHG, AM2125A, AM2125B, AM2318A, ASWG,
AM2032A, ASG, ASGLP, AA2DONW, AA2DONWB, AWBILA
• OSCT cards: OSCT, OSCTAPR
• IROADM cards: IROADMF, IROADMV, IROADM9M, IROADM9R, IRDM20, IRDM32,
IRDM32LP, IR9, IR9LP
• Optical mux/demux card: OMDCL
• Optical filter card: SFDC8

6.1119 config interface PTPIOC <otcline-port-aid> ots
6.1119.1 Purpose
This command configures the OTS type attributes for OTC Line ports on the PTPIOC card.
Use this command to:
• Set the port mode for OTC Line port.
• Set the transmit frequency for the pluggable module
• Set the pluggable module type
• Set SSM/Quality Level Transmission
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1119.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
6.1119.3 Input Format
config interface PTPIOC <otcline-port-aid> ots
mode
moduletype
ssmtrans
6.1119.4 Input Parameters
<otcline-port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/{OTC1L, OTC2L} - Specifies OTC Line port 1 ~ port 2
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
mode
Syntax
mode [<value>]
Values
100BASEFX - Set the port to carry a 100BaseFX signal. The valid value when the
moduletype is "SULS1BOU", "SULS1BOD", "SULS1OU" or "SULS1OD"
1GE - Set the port to carry a 1GE signal. The valid value when the moduletype is
"SS1GOU", "SS1GOD", "SUL1GOU" or "SUL1GOD"

SULS1BOD - 1514nm BIDI ultra long range FE SFP Downstream.
SS1GOU - 1506nm BIDI short range 1GE SFP Upstream.
SS1GOD - 1514nm BIDI short range 1GE SFP Downstream.
SUL1GOU - 1506nm BIDI ULH 1GE SFP Upstream.
SUL1GOD - 1514nm BIDI ULH 1GE SFP Downstream.
SULS1OU - 1514nm BIDI ULH FE/STM-1 OSC SFP Upstream.
SULS1OD - 1517nm BIDI ULH FE/STM-1 OSC SFP Downstream.
auto
Default
auto
Specifies the pluggable module type to be used on the specified interface port. Enter this
keyword to display the current setting.
auto - The network element accepts any of the qualified pluggable module, and automatically
provisions the moduletype upon initial insertion.

mode
{ACT, ePRTC, PRTC, ePRC, PRS, STU, ST2, ST3E, ST3, DUS, NONE} - SONET mode
Default
ACT
Manually configures SSM/Quality Level Transmission in each port.

6.1120 config interface PTPIOC <otcsig-port-aid>
6.1120.1 Purpose
This command configures the OTC Signal ports on the PTPIOC card.
Use this command to:
• Specify a description for the port
• Display the current settings for the port
• Configure port type for the port
• Configure PM for the port
• Configure the state of the port
• Specify the fiber connectivity of the port
Note: This command is not valid when the workMode of PTPIOC card is configured as "relay"
mode.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1120.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

1gbe

Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number.

connport
Syntax
connPort [delete | <slot-aid>] [<port>]
Values
<slot-aid> - the slot-aid of the connected card in the form <shelf>/<slot>
delete - clear a previous value
<port> value:
P{1..6} - specify the Ethernet timing ports on PTPCTL card
C{1..12} - specify the client ports on 11DPE12A card
C{1..22} - specify the client ports on 11QCE12X card
P{1..2} - specify the Ethernet timing ports on 8DC30T or 8DC30T2 card
P{1..3} - specify the Ethernet timing ports on 16DC65T card
{OTC1S, OTC2S} - Specifies OTC Signal port 1 ~ port 2 on PTPIOC card
Default
Entry required
Specify the fiber connectivity between OTC signal port on PTPIOC card and Ethernet timing
port on other SyncE/PTP enabled card, or between OTC signal port on PTPIOC card and OTC
signal port on another PTPIOC card.
Note:When delete the previous connectivity provisioning, the <slot-aid> and <port> values are
not required.
Restrictions
This command is valid only if the OTC signal port is connected to the following cards.
• PTPCTL
• 11DEP12A
• 11QCE12X
• 8DC30T
• 8DC30T2
• 16DC65T
• PTPIOC

ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Sets the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port.
Enter number of hours and minutes
For system default value see "config general ainstimer"
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable when the port type is "ots".
enabled
Sets ains for the port to on.
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable when the port type is "ots".
disabled
Sets ains for the port to off. The default value for ains is disabled.
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable when the port type is "ots".
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Sets to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This
may affect service.

7624 Issue 1
Restrictions
The backplane cannot be assigned with Interlaken or Interlaken_PIF when client port (C21
or C32) is provisioned with type={hundredgige, OTU4} or client port (C31 or C32) is
provisioned with type= {fortygige, OTU3}.
The value 'Interlaken_PIF' of the backplane port type is read-only and configured by
packetswitch command.
When the card is added into a packet switch group, the backplane port type is automatically
set to 'Interlaken_PIF'.
When the card is removed from a packet switch group, the backplane port type is
automatically set to 'unassigned'.
Backplane port type cannot be configured if cardmode = client-hairpin
If the administrative state of the card is currently down then any attempt to provision a new
port shall be rejected.

and BP ports are not allowed;

ports and BP ports are not allowed;

allowed.

• L1 port is not allowed to be assigned;
• C21 port is not allowed to be assigned;
• Backplane ports are not allowed to be provisioned;

6.1136 config interface <s13x100-card> <port-aid> <ngige>
6.1136.1 Purpose
This command configures the GbEn client ports (tenGige, fortyGige, hundredGige) on the S13X100
type/subtype cards:
• S13X100 as card identifier for the subtypes: S13X100L, S13X100R
• S13X100E
Use this command to:
• Set the channel frequency for port attribute
• Set the loss propagation behavior for port attribute
• Set the pluggable module type for port attribute
• Set the error frame drop behavior for 10GbE
• Set the odurate for 10GbE
• Set the fectype for 100GbE
• Set the laser behavior for server signal degraded
• Set the Ethernet Holdoff parameters
• Set the signal mode for 100GbE
• Set Synchronous Ethernet Operation Mode for 10GbE and 100GbE
• Set SSM/Quality Level Transmission for 10GbE and 100GbE
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

encoding parameter of the interface.
• The fectype value of the profile is equal to the value as configured for fectype parameter
of one of OTU facilities associated with the interface/port.
• The phase encoding value of the profile is equal to the value as configured for the

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
enabled
Set ains for the port to on.
disabled
Set ains for the port to off.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This
command may affect service.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
If a GCC channel associated with the port is enabled then setting the port to down shall be
rejected.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Set to up to enable the port.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to up shall be rejected.

Display the pre-fec BER averaged for the elapsed N seconds.
fecubc
Syntax
fecubc <period>
Display the FECUBC (uncorrected bits count) accumulated for the elapsed N seconds.
<period>
Values
1..60 - in seconds
Default
1
Specify the accumulation seconds for preFECBER or FECUBC. These two values (BER &
UBC) are on-demand measurement and the returned results are the values for the elapsed N
seconds.
managementmode
Displays the mode how a user manages the line transmission configuration.
otsig
Displays the current OTSiG setting for the port and covers the following parameters:
• otsigid: identifier for the OTSiG within one card (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• otustruct: OTU structure transported via the line port (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• otsilist: list of ports of the OTSiG (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• profileid: OTSiG profileid assigned for the port (value is settable by user)
• otsigcapacity: capacity of the OTSiG (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• otsipayloadrate: payload rate of the OTSi (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• mgracd: Manager Access Control Domain of the OTSiG (value is settable by user)
If profileid != 0, then also the following transmission parameters of the assigned profile are
shown:
• OTSi baudrate
• OTSi Client OTU Type (clotutype)
• OTSi Forward Error Correction (fectype)
• OTSi modulation format (encoding)
• OTSi Phase Encoding mode (phasenc)
• OTSi Trasmit Shape (txshape)
Note:
• This command displays the line transmission in a similiar way like done via command
"show otsig", but the data is shown on port entity and not on OTSiG entity. No OTSiG
entity will be exist in this case.

Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable for line ports and for OTU2, OTU2E ports provisioned
with portrole=line.

6.1156 config interface s13x400 <port-aid> <ngige>
6.1156.1 Purpose
This command configures the GbEn client ports (tenGige, hundredGige) on the following S13X400
subtype cards:
• S13X400 as card identifier for the subtypes: S13X400H
Use this command to:
• Set the ASAP profile.

of the delay time. After that, the consequent action is defined by losprop.

running.

ssfdelaytimer
Syntax
ssfdelaytimer [<value>]
Values
{0..31} - period using 100 milli-second as base unit (value is multiple of 100 ms)
Default
0
This parameter controls the period for which a laseroff CA (via losprop), triggered by an SSF
condition, is delayed. i.e. the laser shut down is performed after SSFDELAYTIMER has expired,
as long as the SSF condition is still present. During the delay time, IDLE is inserted. The delay
timer is reset if SSF is deasserted before it has expired and is re-triggered on another
occurrence of SSF. LF is inserted after the timer expires, if losprop is configured for laseron.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.

7788 Issue 1
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Restrictions

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Line port provisioning rules:
• To change the port type value for a specific line port, the port type must first be set to
unassigned
When modifying the type parameter value on the line port:
• In a non-dangling OT application, all OCH XC must first be deleted before the port type
parameter can be modified
• In a dangling OT application, the line port state must be set to down before the port type
parameter can be modified
The client ports do not need to have the same type provisioning. That is, a mix of client port
types is allowed.
If a new value is requested to be set for this parameter and rmconport !="" is present, then the
command is denied.
Restrictions
If the administrative state of the card is currently down then any attempt to provision a new
port shall be rejected.

Values

nofec - no FEC is configured
Default
8023-bj
Specifies the fectype provisioning for the hundredGige client port. Enter this keyword to display
the current setting.
fecbypassind
Syntax
fecbypassind [<value>]
Values
enable - enable FEC_bypass_indication
disable - disable FEC_bypass_indication
Default
disable
Parameter fecbypassind (FEC Bypass Indication) determines whether the corresponding option
as defined in IEEE 802.3 is set or not. If enabled this implies:
• dHISER defect detection based on the number of RS-FEC symbol errors is enabled
• LFI is inserted as a consequent action if dHISER is present.
If fectype=nofec is provisioned then this parameter has no effect/impact.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
Restrictions
The parameter cannot be enabled when moduletype=Q28FR1E is provisioned.
losprop
Syntax

managementmode
Syntax
managementmode [<value>]
Values
otu - line transmission is configured via individual parameter settings
otsig - line transmission is configured in an OTSiG like approach
Default
otu
Specifies the mode for how a user manages the line transmission configuration with values as
follows:
- otu: line transmission configuration is done via the sub-commands:
• config interface <card> <port-aid> <otn> <encoding> or
• config interface <card> <port-aid> <otn> encoding [txshape] or
• config OTU <otu-aid> fectype
- otsig: line transmission configuration is done via the sub-command:
• config interface <card> <port-aid> <otn> otsig
If the managementmode is changed from otu to otsig, then the NE checks whether there exists
an OTSiG profile matching the current line transmission configuration; i.e.:
• The payload rate value of the profile is equal to payload rate derived from configured
type parameter value of the interface (payload rate == 100G for type == otu4, and
payload rate == 200G for type == otu4x2).
• The encoding rate value of the profile is equal to the value as configured for the
encoding parameter of the interface.

7826 Issue 1
<encoding>
Enters the context to display the encoding attributes on the line port. See "show interface
s2ad200 <port-aid> <otun> <encoding>".
fectype
Displays the Forward Error Correction type on the interface port.
managementmode
Displays the mode how a user manages the line transmission configuration.
oprmode
Display the operation mode.
otsig
Displays the current OTSiG setting for the port and covers the following parameters:
• otsigid: identifier for the OTSiG within one card (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• otustruct: OTU structure transported via the line port (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• otsilist: list of ports of the OTSiG (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• profileid: OTSiG profileid assigned for the port (value is settable by user)
• otsigcapacity: capacity of the OTSiG (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• otsipayloadrate: payload rate of the OTSi (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• mgracd: Manager Access Control Domain of the OTSiG (value is settable by user)
If profileid != 0, then also the following transmission parameters of the assigned profile are
shown:
• OTSi baudrate
• OTSi Client OTU Type (clotutype)
• OTSi Forward Error Correction (fectype)
• OTSi modulation format (encoding)
• OTSi Phase Encoding mode (phasenc)
• OTSi Trasmit Shape (txshape)
Note:
• This command displays the line transmission in a similiar way like done via command
"show otsig", but the data is shown on port entity and not on OTSiG entity. No OTSiG
entity will be exist in this case.
regenresp
Display the regeneration response.
power
Displays the transmitted optical output power of the port.
postfecber
Displays the 1-second post-fec BER

prefecber
Syntax
prefecber <period>
Displays the pre-fec BER averaged for the elapsed N seconds.
fecubc
Syntax
fecubc <period>
Displays the FECUBC (uncorrected bits count) accumulated for the elapsed N seconds.
<period>
Values
1..60 - in seconds
Default
1
Specifies the accumulation seconds for preFECBER or FECUBC. These two values (BER &
UBC) are on-demand measurement and the returned results are the values for the elapsed N
seconds.

Values

Values
{-2, -1, 0, 1, 2}
Default
0
Sets the transmit channel frequency offset of the port. The channeltxoffset value is used along

• a cross connect exists (for internal and cluster topologies)

shall be set back to the default value.
When the external topology connection is deleted, the channeltxoffset value shall be set back to
the default value.

Values

where OTSI is a member of it;
2. ODUNIM facility: All ODUNIM facilities related to affected OTU facilities (see item 1).

Values

Restrictions

interface type, see "config otsig".

connection.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
cold - A cold restart reinitializes the module firmware and hardware and is service affecting.
warm - A warm restart re-initializes the module firmware only and is not service affecting.
force - optional parameter together with cold.
Performs a restart of the port/module.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the port AdminState to DOWN or MT.
If it is requested to perform a cold reset and the force option is not specified and the port
AdminState is UP, then the command shall be denied.
The reset command is performed as best effort action; i.e. the command is accepted if no
module is currently present or moduletype user/auto is provisioned.
Restrictions
This action is applicable only for the line port.
Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.

type
Syntax
type [<value>]
Values
Allowed values for Line port:
otsi
unassigned
Allowed values for Client port:
hundredGige
400gbe
otu4
unassigned
Default
unassigned
Specifies the port type for the client or line port.
Client port provisioning rule:
For S5AD400H a mix of client signal types are supported for {C1..C4},
1. The allowed "type" values for client ports {C1..C4} are {hundredgige, otu4,
unassigned}
2. The allowed "type" values for client port C5 are {400gbe, unassigned}.
3. If port C5 is provisioned, then ports {C1..C4} must be unassigned.
4. If ports {C1..C4} are provisioned, then port C5 must be unassigned.
Setting the type to unassigned is rejected,
• if the port has SDEE state qualifier.
• if the port is not in admin state down.
When S5AD400 line port is set to OTSi, the OTSIGID is set to none to indicate it has not been
assigned as member for an OTSiG. Use command "config otsig" to create a OTSiG on the
specified otsi port.

6.1199 config interface s5ad400 <port-aid> hundredGige
6.1199.1 Purpose
This command configures the hundredgige client port attributes on the following S5AD400 subtype
card:
• S5AD400 as card identifier for the subtypes: S5AD400H
Use this command to:
• Set the fectype
• Set the FEC bypass indication
• Set the loss propagation behavior
• Configure the pluggable module type
• Set the laser behavior for server signal degrade
• Configure ssfdelaytimer for LFI holdoff, to insert IDLE in the event of dSSF, up to a maximum of
the delay time. After that, the consequent action is defined by losprop.
• Configure the Ethernet maintenance signal after ODU SSF detection, until ssfdelaytimer expires,
or when dSSF is de-asserted, whichever comes first.
• Configure csfdelaytimer for CSF holdoff, up to a maximum of the delay timer. After that, the
consequent action is defined by losprop.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

csfdelaytimer
Syntax
csfdelaytimer [<value>]
Values
{0..255} - period using 10 milli-second as base unit (value is multiple of 10 ms)
Default
0
This parameter controls the period for which a laseroff CA (via losprop), triggered by a CSF
condition, is delayed. i.e. the laser shut down is performed after CSFDELAYTIMER has
expired, as long as the CSF condition is still present. During the delay time, no replacement
signal is inserted (it is expected that the far-end has inserted LFI). The delay timer is reset if
CSF is deasserted before it has expired and is re-triggered on another occurrence of CSF. If
losprop is configured for laseron, then there is no replacement signal inserted (it is expected
that the far-end still inserts LFI).
Enter this keyword to display the current setting. To change the setting, enter this keyword
followed by an allowed value.
fectype
Syntax
fectype [<value>]
Values
8023-bj - IEEE 802.3bj FEC is configured
nofec - no FEC is configured
Default
8023-bj
Specifies the fectype provisioning for the hundredGige client port. Enter this keyword to display
the current setting.

ssfdelaytimer
Syntax
ssfdelaytimer [<value>]
Values
{0..255} - period using 10 milli-second as base unit (value is multiple of 10 ms)
Default
0
This parameter controls the period for which a laseroff CA (via losprop), triggered by an SSF
condition, is delayed. i.e. the laser shut down is performed after SSFDELAYTIMER has expired,

Default
idle
The parameter controls the inserted Ethernet maintenance signal after ODU SSF detection,
while SSFDELAYTIMER is running (from start of timer until the defect is cleared or the timer
expires).
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by an allowed value.

Values
-5.00 - dBm if OTSI is not member of OTSiG
-11.50..+0.50 - dBm with step size 0.10 if fectype == sdfec-g2 and encoding == qpsk and
modulevariant == Standard and OTSI is member of an OTSiG
-11.50..-1.50 - dBm with step size 0.10 if fectype == sdfec-g2 and encoding != qpsk and
modulevariant == Standard and OTSI is member of an OTSiG
-11.50..+4.00 - dBm with step size 0.10 if fectype == sdfec-g2 and encoding == qpsk and
modulevariant == HighPerformance and OTSI is member of an OTSiG
-11.50..+3.00 - dBm with step size 0.10 if fectype == sdfec-g2 and encoding != qpsk and
modulevariant == HighPerformance and OTSI is member of an OTSiG
-5.00..+0.00 - dBm with step size 0.10 if fectype = ofec and OTSI is member of an OTSiG
Notes:
1. encoding and fectype is configured via OTSiG profile assignment - see "config otsig"
command.
2. modulevariant value is retrieved from the inserted module and is retrievable via "show
interface s5ad400 <port-aid>" command.
3. If power value is in range -1.40 to +0.50 for the case modulevariant == Standard and
encoding is changed to value unequal to qpsk then the value is set to -1.50.
4. If power value is in range +3.10 to +4.00 for the case modulevariant ==
HighPerformance and encoding is changed to value unequal to qpsk then the value is
set to +3.00.
5. If OTSI is removed from OTSiG, then the value -5.00 is set.
6. If a change of a power value is requested violating the specified value constraints,
then the command will be denied.
7. A module mismatch alarm will be raised if a C2DCO4 module with modulevariant ==
HighPerformance is replaced by a C2DCO4 module with modulevariant == Standard
and the currently provisioned power value cannot be supported for the case
modulevariant == Standard.
Default
-5.00 dBm
Sets the transmitted optical output power of the port.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by one allowed value.
If the port is provisioned as otsi w/o being assigned as a member of an OTSiG (i.e. otsigid ==
none), then changing the parameter value shall be denied.

where OTSI is a member of it;
2. ODUNIM facility: All ODUNIM facilities related to affected OTU facilities (see item 1).
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.

6.1207.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..4} - Specifies client ports
Default
Entry required
Specifies the access identifier of the port.
Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot number, a slash, and the port label to access the port.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
ainstimer
Displays the Automatic In-Service Debounce time.
csfdelaytimer
Displays the period (in 10ms units) for which a laseroff CA (via losprop), triggered by a CSF
condition, is delayed. i.e. the laser shut down is performed after CSFDELAYTIMER has
expired, as long as the CSF condition is still present. During the delay time, no replacement
signal is inserted (it is expected that the far-end has inserted LFI). The delay timer is reset if
CSF is deasserted before it has expired and is re-triggered on another occurrence of CSF. If
losprop is configured for laseron, then there is no replacement signal inserted (it is expected
that the far-end still inserts LFI).
fectype
Displays the FEC type on the port.
fecbypassind
Displays the FEC bypass indication setting for the port.
losprop
Displays the loss propagation setting.
moduletype
Displays the pluggable module type to be used on the specified interface port.
ssdca
Displays the laser behavior for server signal degrade setting.
ssfdelaytimer
Displays the period (in 10ms units) for which a laseroff CA (via losprop), triggered by an SSF
condition, is delayed. i.e. the laser shut down is performed after SSFDELAYTIMER has expired,
as long as the SSF condition is still present. During the delay time, IDLE is inserted. The delay
timer is reset if SSF is deasserted before it has expired and is re-triggered on another
occurrence of SSF. LF is inserted after the timer expires, if losprop is configured for laseron.

Values

Performs a restart of the port/module.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the port AdminState to DOWN or MT.
If it is requested to perform a cold reset and the force option is not specified and the port
AdminState is UP, then the command shall be denied.
The reset command is performed as best effort action; i.e. the command is accepted if no
module is currently present or moduletype user/auto is provisioned.
Restrictions
This action is applicable only for the line port.

6.1214 config interface s6ad600 <port-aid> hundredGige
6.1214.1 Purpose
This command configures the hundredgige client port attributes on the following S6AD600 subtype
cards:
• S6AD600 as card identifier for the subtypes: S6AD600E, S6AD600H, S6AD600L
Use this command to:
• Set the fectype.
• Set the FEC bypass indication.
• Set the loss propagation behavior.
• Configure the pluggable module type.
• Configure the hold-off timer for laseroff consequent action of SSF or CSF defects.
• Configure the ssfdelaytimer for LFI holdoff, to insert IDLE in the event of SSF up to a maximum
of the delay time. After that, the consequent action is defined by losprop.
• Configure the Ethernet maintenance signal after ODU SSF detection, while ssfdelaytimer is
running.
• Configure csfdelaytimer for CSF holdoff, up to a maximum of the delay timer. After that, the
consequent action is defined by losprop.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

csfdelaytimer
Syntax
csfdelaytimer [<value>]
Values
{0..255} - period using 10 milli-second as base unit (value is multiple of 10 ms)
Default
0
This parameter controls the period for which a laseroff CA (via losprop), triggered by a CSF
condition, is delayed. i.e. the laser shut down is performed after CSFDELAYTIMER has
expired, as long as the CSF condition is still present. During the delay time, no replacement
signal is inserted (it is expected that the far-end has inserted LFI). The delay timer is reset if
CSF is deasserted before it has expired and is re-triggered on another occurrence of CSF. If
losprop is configured for laseron, then there is no replacement signal inserted (it is expected
that the far-end still inserts LFI).
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
fecbypassind
Syntax
fecbypassind [<value>]
Values
enable - enable FEC_bypass_indication
disable - disable FEC_bypass_indication
Default
enable
Fecbypassind (FEC Bypass Indication) determines whether the corresponding option as
defined in IEEE 802.3 is set or not. If enabled this implies:
• dHISER defect detection based on the number of RS-FEC symbol errors is enabled

user - If the user wants to use a pluggable module that is not on the qualified list of pluggable
modules, without generating an alarm.
If it is requested to change the parameter and the port AdminState is UP, then the command
shall be denied.

6.1217 config interface s6ad600 <port-aid> otsi
6.1217.1 Purpose
This command allows to provision OTSi related parameters on the following S6AD600 subtype
cards:
• S6AD600 as card identifier for the subtypes: S6AD600E, S6AD600H, S6AD600L.
Use this command to:
• Set the receiver channel frequency
• Set the receive channel frequency offset of each line port (subsea application)
• Set the transmit channel frequency
• Set the transmit channel frequency offset of each line port (subsea application)

• Set the AID of partner port if the line port has been in regen designated port mode
• Set the grid step size which is based on the application (subsea or non-subsea)
• Set the link span type
• Set the transmit optical power
• Set the receive channel frequency fine offset of each line port
• Set the transmit channel frequency fine offset of each line port
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

channelrxoffset
Syntax

Values
{-2, -1, 0, 1, 2}
Default
0
Specifies the receive channel frequency offset of the port. The channelrxoffset value is used
along with the rxfineoffset and channelrx parameter to determine the line port Rx channel
frequency. The channelrx is changed by the channelrxoffset value multiplied by 0.125 (1.25
GHz).
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.

the default value, this provisioning is denied.
When a cross connection (for internal and cluster topologies) exists, changing channelrxoffset
is denied.
When the cross-connection (for internal and cluster topologies) is deleted, the channelrxoffset
value is set back to the default value.
When the external topology connection is deleted, the channelrxoffset value is set back to the
default value.
When the port is provisioned as otsi w/o being assigned as a member of an OTSiG (i.e. otsigid
== none), setting the channelrxoffset parameter to a value that is not the default value is
denied.
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable to S6AD600L card.

Syntax

1. OTU facility: All OTU facilities which are configured via OTUSTRUCT of the OTSiG
where OTSI is a member of it;
2. ODUNIM facility: All ODUNIM facilities related to affected OTU facilities (see item 1).
Restrictions

6.1220 show interface s6ad600
6.1220.1 Purpose
This command displays the interface ports on the following S6AD600 subtype cards:
• S6AD600 as card identifier for the subtypes: S6AD600E, S6AD600H, S6AD600L.
Use this command to:
• Enter context to display the configuration of the line port L1.
• Enter context to display the configuration of the client ports C{1..6}.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1220.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
6.1220.3 Input Format
show interface s6ad600 <port-aid>
6.1220.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/L1 - Specifies line port 1
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..6} - Specifies client port 1 ~ port 6
* - display list of ports
Default
Entry required
Specifies the access identifier of the port.
Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot number, a slash, and the port label to access the port.
Enter a * to list all ports of this card type in the system.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
6.1220.5 Examples
# show interface s6ad600 *
Port Admin Oper State
Location Function Description Dir State State Qualifier
--------------------------------------------------------
1/12/L1 Network Bi Up Up
1/12/C1 Client Bi Down Down UAS
OT management commands
S6AD600 interface commands

6.1221 show interface s6ad600 <port-aid>
6.1221.1 Purpose
This command displays the configuration of the client or line ports on the following S6AD600
subtype cards:
• S6AD600 as card identifier for the subtypes: S6AD600E, S6AD600H, S6AD600L.
Use this command to:
• Display the generic port level attributes
• Display the port type {hundredGige, 400gbe, otu4, otsi} attributes
• Display the maximum port rate
• Display the performance monitoring attributes
• Display the current remote connected port.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1221.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
6.1221.3 Input Format

hundredGige
400gbe
maxportrate
otu4
otsi
pm
rmconport

<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/L1 - Specifies line port
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..6} - Specifies client ports
Default
Entry required

Specifies the access identifier of the port.
Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot number, a slash, and the port label to access the port.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
detail
Displays the current settings for the port.
Sub-command: hundredGige
Enters the context to display the hundredGige port attributes. See command "show interface
s6ad600 <port aid> hundredGige".
Sub-command: 400gbe
Enters the context to display the 400GbE port attributes. See command "show interface
s6ad600 <port-aid> 400gbe".
maxportrate
Displays the maximal port rate which can be provisioned for the port (unit: Gb/s)
Sub-command: otu4
Enters the context to display the OTU4 port attributes. See command "show interface s6ad600
<port-aid> otu4".
Sub-command: otsi
Enters the context to display the OTSi port attributes. See command "show interface s6ad600
<port-aid> otsi".
Sub-command: pm
Displays the Performance Monitoring attributes. See "show interface s6ad600 <port-aid> pm".
rmconport
Displays the current configured remote connected port.
Restrictions
This parameter is applicable only for line port.

6.1222 show interface s6ad600 <port-aid> hundredGige
6.1222.1 Purpose
This command displays the client port hundredGige attributes on following S6AD600 subtype cards:
• S6AD600 as card identifier for the subtypes: S6AD600E, S6AD600H, S6AD600L.
Use this command to:
• Display the automatic in-service timer.
• Display the csfdelaytimer value.
• Display the fectype.
• Display the FEC bypass indication.
• Display the loss propagation behavior.
• Display the pluggable module type.
• Display the client laser behavior for server signal degrade.
• Display the ssfdelayca value.
• Display the ssfdelaytimer value.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1222.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
6.1222.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..5} - Specifies client ports
Default
Entry required
Specifies the access identifier of the port.
Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot number, a slash, and the port label to access the port.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
ainstimer
Displays the Automatic In-Service Debounce time.
csfdelaytimer
Displays the period (in 10ms units) for which a laseroff CA (via losprop), triggered by a CSF
condition, is delayed. i.e. the laser shut down is performed after CSFDELAYTIMER has
expired, as long as the CSF condition is still present. During the delay time, no replacement
signal is inserted (it is expected that the far-end has inserted LFI). The delay timer is reset if
CSF is deasserted before it has expired and is re-triggered on another occurrence of CSF. If
losprop is configured for laseron, then there is no replacement signal inserted (it is expected
that the far-end still inserts LFI).
ddm
Displays on demand the digital diagnostics monitoring data of the pluggable module.
fecbypassind
Displays the FEC bypass indication setting for the port.
fectype
Displays the FEC type on the port.
losprop
Displays the loss propagation setting.
moduletype
Displays the pluggable module type to be used on the specified interface port.
ssdca
Displays the laser behavior for server signal degrade setting.
ssfdelayca
Displays the Ethernet maintenance signal that is inserted after ODU SSF detection, while
SSFDELAYTIMER is running (from start of timer until the defect is cleared or the timer expires).
OT management commands
S6AD600 interface commands
show interface s6ad600 <port-aid> hundredGige
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
7998 Issue 1
ssfdelaytimer
Displays the period (in 10ms units) for which a laseroff CA (via losprop), triggered by an SSF
condition, is delayed. i.e. the laser shut down is performed after SSFDELAYTIMER has expired,
as long as the SSF condition is still present. During the delay time, IDLE is inserted. The delay
timer is reset if SSF is deasserted before it has expired and is re-triggered on another
occurrence of SSF. LF is inserted after the timer expires, if losprop is configured for laseron.
6.1222.5 Examples
# show interface s6ad600 1/2/c1 fectype
FEC type : 802-bj

8004 Issue 1
6.1225 show interface s6ad600 <port-aid> otsi
6.1225.1 Purpose
This command displays OTSi attributes for OTSi interfaces under one OTSIG on the following
S6AD600 subtype cards:
• S6AD600 as card identifier for the subtypes: S6AD600E, S6AD600H, S6AD600L.
Use this command to:
• Display the automatic In-Service Debounce time
• Display the receive channel frequency
• Display the receive channel frequency offset of each line port (subsea application)
• Display the transmit channel frequency
• Display the transmit channel frequency offset of each line port (subsea application)
• Display the designated port operation mode of each line port
• Display the AID of partner port if the line port has been in regen designated port mode
• Display the grid step size
• Display the link span type
• Display the transmit power on each line port
• Display the 1-second pre-fec BER
• Display the OTSIGID the port belongs to
• Display the pluggable module type
• Display the name of the module capability file
• Display the receive channel frequency fine offset of each line port
• Display the transmit channel frequency fine offset of each line port
This command can only be applied if the line port type is configured to:
• otsi
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1225.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
6.1225.3 Input Format
show interface s6ad600 <port-aid> otsi
ainstimer
channelrx
channelrxoffset
channeltx

displayed.

6.1226 show interface s6ad600 <port-aid> pm
6.1226.1 Purpose
This command displays the port performance monitoring attributes on the following S6AD600
subtype cards:
• S6AD600 as card identifier for the subtypes: S6AD600E, S6AD600H, S6AD600L.
Use this command to:
• Display the Cycle Slips Ratio group PM options
• Display the received compensated chromatic dispersion PM options
• Display the received compensated Differential Group Display PM options
• Display the Electrical signal-to-noise ratio group PM options
• Display the Ethernet group PM options
• Display the ETHFECPM group PM options
• Display the Error Vector Magnitude group PM options
• Display the FECPM group PM options
• Display the received Frequency Offset PM options
• Display the LanePwrs group PM options
• Display the received optical power group PM
• Display the transmitted optical power group PM
• Display the OTU performance monitoring attributes on an OTU facility
• Display the PCS group PM options
• Display the Polarization Dependent Loss group PM options
• Display the prefecbits Group PM options
• Display the Qfactor group PM options
• Display the Qmargin group PM options
• Display the State of Pol variation rate group PM options
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1226.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
6.1226.3 Input Format

6.1227 config interface svac
6.1227.1 Purpose
This command configures the interface ports on the SVAC card. Use this command to access
subcommands that allow you to configure the client (C1) port or line (L1) port.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1227.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
6.1227.3 Input Format
config interface svac <port-aid>
6.1227.4 Input Parameters
<port-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot>/L1 - Specifies line port 1
<shelf>/<slot>/C1 - Specifies client port 1
* - display list of ports
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number, or * to list all of the svac cards on the network element.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
6.1227.5 Examples
# config interface svac *
Port Admin Oper State
Location Function Description Dir State State Qualifier
---------------------------------------------------------
2/2/L1 Network Bi Up Down
2/2/C1 Client Bi Down Down
2/7/L1 Network Bi Up Down
2/7/C1 Client Bi Up Down

ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <time>]
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Set the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port.
Enter number of hours and minutes
For system default value see "config general ainstimer"
enabled
Set ains for the port to on.
disabled
Set ains for the port to off.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This may
affect service.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Set to up to enable the port.

Values

Default
Entry required
Configures the loopback. For the usage of the individual values refer parameters in this
command.
If it is requested to enable a loopback for one type (e.g. facility) and there is already a loopback
enabled for another type (e.g. terminal), then the enabling of additional loopback request shall
be rejected.
Ports 1..16 of the 18CE300 are divided into 4 port sub-sets as follows:
• port range 1 to 4: first sub-set
• port in range 5 to 8: second sub-set
• port in range 9 to 12: third sub-set
• port in range 13-16: fourth sub-set
Within such a port sub-set the following constraint must be met (otherwise command will be
denied):
• only one facility loopback can be enabled at a time.
Restrictions
The loopback command shall be rejected if a port type is provisioned as otsi.
facility
Syntax
facility [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - enable the facility loopback
disabled - disable the facility loopback
Default
disabled
Configures the facility loopback of the port. Enter this keyword without option to display the
current setting. To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by enabled or disabled.
Restrictions
Facility loopback cannot be enabled if efm-oam is enabled on the port (See "config
packetswitch <packetswitch-id> port <port-aid> ethernet efm-oam").
Facility loopbacks are not supported on the 100G ports of the 18CE300.
Note that port stats are not accumulated during a facility loopback.

rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual

<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote
connection point with the line NE TID and line NE optical port.
rmconport is written as a result of "config interface topology" commands executed on the line
NE.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting.
For exceptional manual cleanup purpose on the tributary NE, the user can modify the
rmconport locally by entering an empty or modified rmconport value together with the force
option.
The manual cleanup is supported for bidirectional, or unidirectional rmconports with the
direction value, which defaults backward compatible to bidirectional.
The user is prompted by a warning message, that the execution can be service affecting. The
command is executed if "yes" is entered.
Restrictions
This parameter is applicable only for OTUk ports, on the 12ce120 and 18ce300, and to
OTSi ports, on the 18ce300, with portrole equal line.

hundredgigelaneth - to set the port to a local area hundredGige signal going into ETH

Specifies the port type.
Command Validation
The following pre-condition are needed when changing the type parameter.
If the administrative state of the card is currently down then any attempt to provision a new port
shall be rejected.
If the card is not member of a packet switch group then setting the type to value unequal to
unassigned shall be rejected.
If the SDEE state is present on the associated ODUPTF in case of provisioned type ==
otukwaneth then setting the type to unassigned shall be rejected.
If the SDEE state is present for the port then setting the type to unassigned shall be rejected.
If a new value is requested to be set for this parameter and rmconport !="" is present, then the
command is denied.
12CE120, 12CE121 - the allowed type configurations in case of modulecfg == 12PLUGS are:
• In general, all ports can be assigned.
• The type == 10gbelaneth2g5ce is not allowed for any port.
12CE120, 12CE121 - the allowed type configurations in case of modulecfg == 9PLUGS are:
• The ports 7, 9, 10 cannot be assigned and must remain unassigned and empty.
• The type == 10gbelaneth2g5ce can be assigned to port 8 only.
• The type == 1gbelaneth can be assigned to port 1..6 and 11,12 (12CE121 card)
• The type == felaneth can be assigned to port 1..6 and 11,12 (12CE121 card)
• The type == tengigelaneth can be assigned to port 1..6 and 11,12
• The type == otu2ewaneth can be assigned to port 1 and 2 only (12CE120 card)
18CE300 - the allowed configurations are:
• type == felaneth AND 1gbelaneth AND tengigelaneth can be assigned to ports 1..6, 8, 11
• type == felaneth AND 1gbelaneth AND tengigelaneth can be assigned to port 7 provided
port 8 is not provisioned with type == 10gbelaneth2g5ce
• type == felaneth AND 1gbelaneth AND tengigelaneth can be assigned to ports 9, 10, 12,
provided ports 8 and 11 are not provisioned with type == 10gbelaneth2g5ce
• type == 10gbelaneth2g5ce can be assigned to port 8 provided ports 7, 9, 10, 12, and 17
are unassigned
• type == 10gbelaneth2g5ce can be assigned to port 11 provided ports 9, 10 and 12 are
unassigned
• type == tengigelaneth can be assigned to ports 13..16 provided there are no ports in the
range 13..16 with type == 25gbelaneth OR otu2ewaneth, AND port 17 is unassigned

8050 Issue 1
Values
help - displays default and valid values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
<time> - set the ainstimer in the format <h> [<m>] to a value ranging between 1m..96h
inclusive.
Default
system
Sets the Automatic In-Service Timer of this port. Enter number of hours and minutes. For
system default value see "config general ainstimer"
enabled
Sets ains for the port to on.
disabled
Sets ains for the port to off.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
force - force the port down
Sets to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This can
affect service.
(Note: for backplane port this does not affect service)
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
mt
Sets to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Sets to up to enable the port.
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to up shall be rejected.

This command configures the OCH related parameters of OTUk interface on the 12CE120 and

• Set ASAP profile
• Set individual alarm severity profile for the port
• Set the receive channel frequency
• Set the transmit channel frequency
• Configure the pluggable moduletype
The OTU layer is managed via card independent logical facility commands. See "config otu".

Values
{enable, disable} - for GBE25 port
Default
disable - for GBE25 port
The parameter fecbypassind (FEC Bypass Indication) determines whether the corresponding
option as defined in IEEE 802.3 is set or not.
If enabled this implies:
• dHISER defect detection based on the number of RS-FEC symbol errors is enabled
• LFI is inserted downstream as a consequent action if dHISER is present.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
Restrictions

synceoppmode
Syntax
synceoppmode [sync | non-sync]
Values
{sync | non-sync}
Default
non-sync.
Configures port Synchronous Ethernet Operation Mode. When the port is in SYNC mode,
recovered clock of its input signal can be selected as a reference clock to the system clock.
When the port is in NON-SYNC mode, the recovered clock of its input signal shall not be a
candidate to system timing references.
Note: Ports that are equipped with a 1000B-T2 module are not supported, since 1000B-T2
modules do not support SyncE.
Restrictions
This parameter takes effect only when "config packetswitch <packetswitch-id>" syncesupp
is set to enable. And the synceoppmode cannot be changed to NON-SYNC mode if the port
is assigned as a line reference.
This parameter is not applicable for the FE port on 18CE300 card

6.1243 config interface <dsw-packetswitch-card> <port-aid> otsi
6.1243.1 Purpose
This command configures the OTSi port attributes on a packet switch card.
Use this command to:
• Set the ASAP profile
• Set the receiver channel frequency
• Set the transmit channel frequency
• Set the pluggable module type
• Set the transmit optical power
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

name of the configured default profile of the corresponding ASAP type.

channelrx
Syntax
channelrx [<freq>]
Values
none - No channel set
9130.000..9610.000 - DWDM center frequencies in steps of 5.000, 191.30 THz = 9130.000
Default
none
Specifies the receive channel frequency in GHz. Enter this keyword to display the current
setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by one of the <freq> value.
If the port is provisioned as otsi w/o being assigned as a member of an OTSiG (i.e. otsigid ==
none), then setting the parameter to a value unequal to none shall be denied.
Restrictions
The parameter channelrx and channeltx need to share the same configured value; i.e. if the
parameter channelrx is changed via the command, then in addition the same value is also
applied for the parameter channeltx.

PSS-<n>x IO card interface commands
6.1253 config interface <csw-card> <port-aid>
6.1253.1 Purpose
This command allows to provision the port/interface of an IO card for PSS-<n>x shelf. These IO
cards are handled as one sub-set of IO cards supporting ODUk switching function by means of a
central switch function. Therefore, the abbreviation csw-card (Central switched IO Card) is used for
this sub-set of cards.
The shelves supporting central ODUk/packet switching are called CSW shelf. This generic term is
used for the following shelf types:
• PSS-24x
• PSS-12x
• PSS-8x
Use this command to:
• set generic port level attributes
• set the interface/port type {equipment, <n>gige, oc<n>, otu<n>, otsi, stm<n>} and attributes
• set the loopback
• set the PM attributes
• set the state
• Overwrite manually the remote connected port
• reset the port/module
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
Restrictions: Changing one of the specified input parameters with exception of type parameter is
denied if an interface type is not provisioned.
6.1253.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

Values
cold - A cold restart reinitializes the module firmware and hardware and is service affecting.
warm - A warm restart re-initializes the module firmware only and is not service affecting.
force - optional parameter together with cold.
Performs a restart of the port/module.
The optional parameter force is only allowed together with cold. It allows a user to perform a
reset cold without first setting the port AdminState to DOWN or MT.
If it is requested to perform a cold reset and the force option is not specified and the port
AdminState is UP, then the command shall be denied.
The reset command is performed as best effort action, i.e. the command is accepted if no
module is currently present or moduletype user/auto is provisioned.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable for the following CSW cards:
• all 1UX500 subtypes
• 2UX500
• all 2UC1T subtypes
• 2UC1TH
• 4UC1T
• 10AN1T - When port type is otsi
• 10AN400 - When port type is otsi
• 4MX200 - When port type is otsi
• 5MX500 - When port type is otsi
Sub-command: rmconport
Syntax
rmconport [<identifier> [force] [<direction>]]
Values
<identifier> - ASCII string 1..64 characters for rmconport identification in the form of <ne-
name>:<cardtype>-<shelf>-<slot>-<port> or "" - empty string
force - forcing a rmconport modification in the exceptional situation, when a manual
clean-up is needed
<direction> - specifies the direction for which the rmconport identification applies: to, from,
bidirectional
Default
"" for <identifier>
bidirectional for <direction>
For a port participating in a cluster connection, the rmconport value identifies the remote

Restrictions
If the administrative state of the card is currently down then any attempt to provision a new
port shall be rejected.
If the type is set to otu4 and this interface is associated with an oduchannelpool and this pool
cannot provide the needed channel resources (i.e. NumberofFreeChan <
NumberOfOTUReservedChan), then the command shall be rejected.
Note:
• The channel resource handling is described in detail in purpose sub-section of command
show oduchannelpool.
If the type is set to hundredgige and this interface is associated with an oduchannelpool and
this pool cannot provide the needed channel resources (i.e. NumberofFreeChan < 1), then the
command shall be rejected.
Note:
• The channel resource handling is described in detail in purpose sub-section of command
show oduchannelpool.
If the type is changed from equipment to value unequal to un-assigned and the provisioned
moduletype is not allowed for the new type value, then the command shall be rejected.
Note:
• The allowed moduletype values are specified as part of moduletype parameter definition
in the type specific interface sub-commands.
• Changing the type from equipment to value unequal to un-assigned is allowed without
setting port admin state to down.
If the type is changed from a value unequal to un-assigned to equipment, then the command
shall be rejected if one of the following constraints is met:
1. The port is used for service.
2. The port is currently assigned to type otsi and is a member of an OTSiG.
3. The parameter value for rmconport is not an empty string.
Note:
1. A port of type otuk/otsi is considered in context of this rule as used for service if for an
associated OTU facility the SDEE state is present.

2. A port of type ocn/stmn, gben is considered in context of this rule as used for service if

If the type is set unequal to <otn> then portrole shall be set to the value client.
If the type is set to unassigned then portrole shall be reset to the specified default value.
If the type value is set to unassigned then the rmconport parameter shall be re-set to the default

If the type is changed from equipment to a value unequal to un-assigned, then the following
behaviour shall be applied (besides the type parameter value change):
1. All parameters as defined for type equipment shall keep the current value for the new
type (e.g. moduletype parameter).
2. All parameters which will become new applicable for the new type shall be set to the
factory default value as specified for this type (for example hundredgige csfca
parameter will be set to 'laseroff').
3. The parameter modulecapfile applicable for type OTSI (see command "show interface
<csw-card> <port aid> <otn>") shall be set in order to reference the module capability
file based on the already configured moduletype value.
4. The portrole parameter shall be re-set to factory default as defined for the card and
new type value.
If the type is changed from value unequal to un-assigned to equipment, then the following
behaviour shall be applied (besides the type parameter value change):
1. All parameters defined for type equipment shall be kept unchanged for the new type
(for example the moduletype parameter).
2. The parameters clearasontopo, loopback, portrole shall be re-set to specified factory
default.
The ports of 4MX200 card support the following type provisioning:
• port range 1, 2: Each port within this sub-set can be assigned a hundredgige or otsi or
otu4 signal type value
• all ports: Each port can be assigned an unassigned type value
The following port rules are valid for 20MX80 card w.r.t. type configuration for sub-10G signal
types:
• The type oc48/stm16 can only be assigned to a port with number <n> if <n> is an odd
number (i.e. 1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15) and the port with number n+1 is not assigned to type
oc3/stm1 or oc12/stm4 or 1gbe/1gbeconv or otu1.
• If a port with number <n> is currently assigned to type oc48/stm16 then a port with
number <n>+1 cannot be assigned to type oc3/stm1 or oc12/stm4 or 1gbe/1gbeconv or
otu1.
• If type configuration is requested violating these port rules then the command shall be
rejected.
The rules as specified above for 20MX80 card are also valid for 20AN80 card w.r.t. type
configuration for sub-10G signal types.
The following deny rules are valid for 20MX80 card w.r.t. type and mapping configuration:

group then setting the type to value unequal to unassigned shall be rejected.
30SE300 - the allowed type configuration in case of modulecfg == 30PLUGS are:
• In general, all ports can be assigned.
• The type == el1gbelaneth is not allowed for any port.
• The type == 1gbelaneth or type == tengigelaneth or type == equipment can be assigned
for any port.
30SE300 - the allowed type configuration in case of modulecfg == ELPLUGS are:
In general, all ports can be assigned.
The type == equipment is not allowed for any port.
The type == el1gbelaneth can be assigned for a port with even port number<i> (<i> = 2, 4..30)
as follows:
• If all ports with port numbers in range (<i>+1) to 30 are unassigned or assigned to type
== el1gbelaneth AND
• all ports with port numbers in range (<i> -1) to (<i> -5) are unassigned or assigned to
type == el1gbelaneth
The type == 1gbelaneth or type == tengigelaneth can be assigned for a port with port number
<i> (<i> = 1..30) as follows:
• If (ports with port numbers in range <i>+1 .. <i>+5 and <i> is odd) OR (ports with port
numbers in range <i>+1 .. <i>+4 and <i> is even) are unassigned or assigned to type ==
1gbelaneth or type == tengigelaneth AND
• all ports with port numbers in range (<i>-1) .. 1 are unassigned or assigned to type ==
1gbelaneth or type == tengigelaneth
Note:
• If port(s) within a range (e.g. <i>+1 to <i>+5) fall outside the card's range (1..30) in the
rules above, then these ports shall be considered as unassigned.
The ports of 6SE300 card support the following type provisioning:
• port range 13, 17, 21: Each port within this sub-set can be assigned a
hundredgigelaneth signal type value

The following port rules are valid for 2UX200 card w.r.t. type configuration:
• port 1: otu4
• port 2: otu4 or otu4x2
Port 1 must be unassigned, before Port 2 can be provisioned to otu4x2.
Port 2 must be different to otu4x2, before Port 1 can be provisioned to otu4.
The following port rules are valid for 10AN1T card:
The ports of 10AN1T can be split into two sub-sets as follows:
• Port sub-set 1 is [1..5]
• Port sub-set 2 is [6..10]
• The first port <i> of a port sub-set (i.e. i := 1 or i := 6) can always be assigned to
hundredgige or otsi or otu4 independent from port assignment of other ports in the sub-
set.
• The first port <i> of a port sub-set (i.e. i := 1 or i := 6) can be assigned to 400gbe if ports
<i>+1 and <i>+2 and <i>+3 are unassigned.
• The last port of a port sub-set can always be assigned to hundredgige or otsi or otu4
independent from port assignment of other ports in the sub-set.
• The ports <i>+1 and <i>+2 and <i>+3 of a port sub-set (i.e. i := 1 or i := 6) can be
assigned to hundredgige or otsi or otu4 if the first port <i> is not assigned to 400gbe.
Note:
The supported configurations for a mixing of 400gbe and hundredgige/otsi/otu4 types are for
example:
• port 1 assigned to 400gbe and port 5 to hundredgige/otsi/otu4
• port 6 assigned to 400gbe and port 10 to hundredgige/otsi/otu4
The ports of 10AN400 can be split into four sub-sets with port rules as follows:
• Port sub-set 1 is [1..4, 9..10, 13..16]
• Port sub-set 2 is [5..8, 11..12, 17..20]
• Port sub-set 3 is [21..24, 29..30, 33..36]
• Port sub-set 4 is [25..28, 31..32, 37..40]
• The first port of a port sub-set can be assigned to hundredgige/otsi/otu4 if all other ports
within the port sub-set are unassigned.
• Every port of a port sub-set can be assigned to tengige, if the first port is not assigned to
hundredgige/otsi/otu4.
The following port rules are valid for 5MX500 card:
• The port 5 can always be assigned to hundredgige or otsi or otu4 independent from port
assignment of other ports.
• The port 5 can be assigned to 400gbe if port 2 or port 3 or port 4 is not assigned to type
hundredgige/otsi/otu4.

odurate
Syntax
odurate <value>
Values
For type 1gbe:
odu0 - GBE signal with CBR mapping into OPU0/ODU0.
oduflex - GBE signal with GFP mapping into OPUflex/ODUflex.
For type 1gbeconv:
odu0 - GBE signal with CBR mapping into OPU0/ODU0.
For type tengige:
odu2e - GBE10 signal with CBR mapping into OPU2e/ODU2e.
odu2 - GBE10 signal with GFP mapping into OPU2/ODU2.
oduflex - GBE10 signal (sub-rate) with GFP mapping into OPUflex/ODUflex.
For type hundredgige:
odu4 - GBE100 signal with mapping into OPU4/ODU4.
oduflex - GBE100 signal (sub-rate) with GFP mapping into OPUflex/ODUflex.
For type 400gbe:
oduflex - GBE400 signal mapped as CBR into OPUflex/ODUflex.
Specifies the ODU rate which is used to transport the GBEn signal type.
Restrictions
The parameter needs to be specified if GBEn type is configured with exception of values
1gbelaneth, el1gbelaneth, 25gbelaneth, tengigelaneth and hundredgigelaneth. For all other
cases the parameter needs to be omitted.
The parameter value ODUflex is not applicable for card 20UC200.

6.1254 config interface <csw-card> <port-aid> state
6.1254.1 Purpose
This command allows to provision the port/interface of an IO card for PSS-<n>x shelf. These IO
cards are handled as one sub-set of IO cards supporting ODUk/packet switching function by means
of a central switch function. Therefore, the abbreviation csw-card (Central switched IO Card) is
used for this sub-set of cards. A shelf supporting central switching is called CSW shelf.
Use this command to:
• Configure the automatic in-service timer
• Set the state for the port
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.

8142 Issue 1
Default
system
The AINS Timer determines how long an input signal must be present on the facility without a
failure condition before the system transitions the port into the In-Service state.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value. For system default
value see "config general ainstimer"
enabled
Sets AINS to enable.
disabled
Sets AINS to disable.
down
Syntax
down [force]
Values
down - sets admin state of the port to down
force - sets admin state of the port to down including all port related facilities
Set to down to disable the port. Follow this keyword with force to force the port down. This can
affect service.
With the force option the admin state of the following port related facilities will also set to down:
1. OTU facility: All OTU facilities related to the port. If the type OTU4xn is provisioned,
then all "n" OTU4 are affected. If type OTSI is provisioned, then all OTUs are affected
which are configured via OTUSTRUCT of the OTSiG where OTSI is a member of.
2. ODUNIM facility: All ODUNIM facilities related to affected OTU facilities (see item 1).
Restrictions
If a loopback is present for the port then setting the state to down shall be rejected.
If a GCC channel associated with the port is enabled then setting the port to down shall be
rejected.
mt
Set to mt to set the admin state to maintenance.
up
Set to up to enable the port.

8144 Issue 1
6.1255 config interface <csw-card> <port-aid> equipment
6.1255.1 Purpose
This command allows to provision an equipment port/interface of an IO card for PSS-<n>x shelf.
These IO cards are handled as one sub-set of IO cards supporting ODUk/packet switching function
by means of a central switch function. Therefore, the abbreviation csw-card (Central switched IO
Card) is used for this sub-set of cards. A shelf supporting central switching is called CSW shelf.
Use this command to:
• set the pluggable module data Equipment
This command can only be applied if interface type is configured to:
• equipment - Equipment port
An equipment port models only the equipment sub-part/parameters of a port on an IO card. This
allows as user to provision the transmission port via two steps:
1. In the first step only the equipment data is provisioned (e.g. moduletype or ASAP).
2. In the second step the transmission port including type is provisioned (e.g. port is configured as
GBE10 port).
Notes:
1. The user can change/convert an equipment port to a transmission port or vice versa while
keeping all equipment configuration data.
2. The user can also convert from one transmission port type (e.g. GBE10) to another
transmission port type (e.g. OTU2) using the equipment type as intermediate step.
3. There are no facilities (i.e. OTU, ODUNIM, ODUPTF) associated with an equipment port. In
context of change/convert of an equipment port the associated facilities are auto-deleted or
auto-created by the NE.
4. The NE will monitor and report all equipment defects/alarms as defined by the equipment alarm
profile (parameter almprof - config interface <csw-card> <port-aid> command).
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1255.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
6.1255.3 Input Format
config interface <csw-card> <port-aid> equipment
moduleproductcode
moduleproductcodesup
moduletype

empty string (i.e. no module is provisioned) and a module is plugged in, then a module
mismatch alarm is raised.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
6.1256 config interface <csw-card> <port-aid> <ngige>
6.1256.1 Purpose
This command allows to provision a GBEn port/interface of an IO card for PSS-<n>x shelf. These
IO cards are handled as one sub-set of IO cards supporting ODUk/packet switching function by
means of a central switch function. Therefore, the abbreviation csw-card (Central switched IO Card)
is used for this sub-set of cards. A shelf supporting central switching is called CSW shelf.
Use this command to:
• set the pluggable module data for GBEn
• set the mapping mode for GBEn
• set LPT parameters
• set ASAP profile
This command can only be applied if interface type is configured to:
• 1gbe/1gbeconv - GBE1 port
• 1gbelaneth - optical GBE1 port
• el1gbelaneth - electrical GBE1 port
• 25gbelaneth - GBE25 port
• tengige - GBE10 port
• tengigelaneth - GBE10 port
• hundredgige - GBE100 port
• hundredgigelaneth - GBE100 port
• 400gbe - GBE400 port
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1256.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
6.1256.3 Input Format
config interface <csw-card> <port-aid> <ngige>

autoneg
Syntax
autoneg [<value>]
Values
disabled - disable auto-negotiation
enabled - enable auto-negotiation
Default
enabled
The parameter autoneg controls whether auto-negotiation is performed for a GBE1 port.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by an allowed value.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable for a port with the following setting:
type == 1gbe and rate == oduflex
For an electrical GBE1 port the standard requests, that auto-negotiation is mandatory and
therefore the user should only provision autoneg == disabled in case of IWK issues with the
connected NE.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
8162 Issue 1
The following GBE1 port setting is advertised via auto-negotiation and is also used for the case
autoneg == disabled:
1. Speed 1000 Mbit/s
2. Full duplex mode
3. No pause mode
If autoneg value is changed from disabled to enabled, then auto-negotiation is re-started and
therefore GBE1 transmission will be interrupted.
A user needs to apply the same auto-negotiation for both GBE1 ports being a member of an
OPSB or a Y-cable protection group. The NE will not deny a command if this constraint is not
met.
If the GBE1 service is protected (e.g. via OPSB protection, Y-cable protection or ODUk SCNP)
then it is recommended to use the setting autoneg == disabled in order to have better GBE1
traffic restoration times in context of a protection switch.
Note:
• After the execution a protection switch caused by a SF/SD event, an auto-negotiation
may be restarted and therefore the traffic restoration time is extended.

Sub-command: modify
Syntax
modify odurate [encmode]
The modify command allows to change the odurate for a GBEn port. The user must specify:
• The parameter odurate with a new value.
• The mapping of the GBEn into OPUk/ODUk (optionally).
See the parameter definition for odurate and encmode for further details.
The following changes are applied if command succeeds:
• delete the ODUPTF facility for the old odu rate.
• create an ODUPTF facility with the new odu rate. This implies all ODUPTF parameters
will have factory default values after creation.
If customer application mode != "openROADM", then the command will be denied. Note:
customer-appl-mode is retrievable via command "show admin"
If the SDEE state is present on the ODUPTF facility to be deleted, then the command will be
denied.
If provisioned type != tengige, then the command will be denied.
If the specified encmode value is not supported for the specified odurate value, then the
command will be denied.
See parameter odurate and encmode for additional restrictions.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
6.1257 config interface <csw-card> <port-aid> <ocn-stmn>
6.1257.1 Purpose
This command allows to provision an OCn/STMn port/interface of an IO card for PSS-<n>x shelf.
These IO cards are handled as one sub-set of IO cards supporting ODUk switching function by
means of a central switch function. Therefore, the abbreviation csw-card (Central switched IO Card)
is used for this sub-set of cards. A shelf supporting central ODUk switching is called CSW shelf.
Use this command to:
• set the pluggable module data for port attribute
• set dTIM configuration
• set the J0 attributes
• set the mapping mode
• set ASAP profile
• set LPT attributes
This command can only be applied if interface/port type is configured to:
• oc3
• oc12
• oc48
• oc192
• stm1
• stm4
• stm16
• stm64
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1257.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
6.1257.3 Input Format
config interface <csw-card> <port-aid> <ocn-stmn>
almprof
channel
csfca
csfdelaytimer
inopsb
j0 [j0_ex | j0_fmt | trccmp | trcconsact]

The following deny rules are valid for 20MX80 card w.r.t. mapping configuration:
• If for STM16/OC48 port in range 1..8 the mappingmode async is requested and for
another port within this port range mappingmode == bitsync/gmp or encmode == cbrlan1
is configured, then the command will be denied.
• If for STM16/OC48 port in range 9..16 the mappingmode async is requested and for
another port within this port range mappingmode == bitsync/gmp or encmode == cbrlan1
is configured, then the command will be denied.
• If for STM16/OC48 port in range 1..8 the mappingmode bitsync is requested and for
another port within this port range mappingmode ==async is configured, then the
command will be denied.
• If for STM16/OC48 port in range 9..16 the mappingmode bitsync is requested and for
another port within this port range mappingmode ==async is configured, then the
command will be denied.
This results in the following constraint:
• It is not allowed to mix mapping async with mappings bitsync/gmp/cbrlan1 within the one
port range group.
The deny rules as specified above for 20MX80 card are also valid for 20AN80 card w.r.t.
mapping configuration.

mismatch alarm is raised.
• If the value enabled is provisioned and the provisioned moduleproductcode value is
empty string (i.e. no module is provisioned) and a module is plugged in, then a module
mismatch alarm is raised.

6.1258 config interface <csw-card> <port-aid> <otn>
6.1258.1 Purpose
This command allows to provision an OTN port/interface of an IO card for PSS-<n>x shelf. The
following sub-classes w.r.t. OTN port/interfaces need to be distinguished:
• type = otuk/otukxn: OTUk port
• type = otsi: OTSi can be configured as member of an OTSiG - see "config otsig"
These IO cards are handled as one sub-set of IO cards supporting ODUk/packet switching function
by means of a central switch function. Therefore, the abbreviation csw-card (Central switched IO
Card) is used for this sub-set of cards. A shelf supporting central switching is called CSW shelf.
Note:
• The OTU layer is managed via non-card specific facility commands "config/show otu".
Use this command to:
• Set the receive channel frequency
• Set the transmit channel frequency
• Set the pluggable module data
• Set LPT attributes
This command can only be applied if interface/port type is configured to:
• otu2
• otu2e
• otu4
• otu4waneth
• otu4x2
• otu4x2waneth
• otsi
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1258.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
