0p1ghz-channelrx
Syntax
0p1ghz-channelrx [<freq>]
Values
Allowed values for 2UC1TH card for moduletype BMDCO12:
none - No channel set
{9130.000..9605.000} - DWDM center frequencies
{9605.600..9610.000} - extended DWDM center frequencies for dangling OT usage
Default
none
Specifies the receive channel frequency using 4.3 format. Enter a value in steps of N x 0.010 to
select a channel frequency on the 0.1GHz grid, or a value in steps of N x 0.625 to select a
center frequency on the 6.25GHz grid, or any value using 4.3 format. Examples are 9130.010,
9130.625, 9130.875 or 9130.250. in GHz. Enter this keyword without option to display the
current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by one of the <freq> value.
The channelrx parameter value is calculated from the 0p1ghz-channelrx value. When photonic
cross-connect has been provisioned, and then afterwards the User selects a 0p1ghz-channelrx
value, if the calculated channelrx value does not match the <itu> value configured by the
photonic cross-connect command, then 0p1ghz-channelrx provisioning is denied.
When the 0p1ghz-channelrx is provisioned before the photonic cross-connect is configured, if
the <itu> value in the photonic cross-connect command does not match the calculated
channelrx value, then the photonic cross-connect provisioning is denied.
When the port is provisioned as otsi w/o being assigned as a member of an OTSiG (i.e. otsigid
== none), setting the 0p1ghz-channelrx parameter to a value that is not the default value is
denied.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable to 2UC1TH card.

managementmode
Syntax
managementmode [<value>]
Values
otu - line transmission is configured via individual parameter settings
otsig - line transmission is configured in an OTSiG like approach
Default
otu
Specifies the mode how a user manages the line transmission configuration with values as
follows:
- otu: line transmission configuration is done via the sub-commands:
• config interface <card> <port-aid> <otn> <encoding> or
• config interface <card> <port-aid> <otn> encoding [txshape | phasenc] or

• config interface <card> <port-aid> <otn> otsig

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
8212 Issue 1
Restrictions
The parameter and parameter values are applicable for CSW cards as follows:
• value otu: This value is applicable for the following cards:
2UC400, 4UC400, 1UX100, 2UX200
• value otsig: This value is applicable for the following cards:
2UC400, 4UC400, 2UX200
• The parameter is not applicable for all other cards not supporting the value otu.
If the managementmode is changed from otu to otsig, then the NE checks whether there exists
an OTSiG profile matching the current line transmission configuration; i.e.:
• The payload rate value of the profile is equal to payload rate derived from configured
type parameter value of the interface (payload rate == 100G for type == otu4, payload
rate == 200G for type == otu4x2).
• The encoding rate value of the profile is equal to the value as configured for the
encoding parameter of the interface.
• The fectype value of the profile is equal to the value as configured for fectype parameter
of one of OTU facilities associated with the interface/port.
• The phase encoding value of the profile is equal to the value as configured for the
encoding parameter of the interface.
• The txshape value of the profile is equal to the value as configured for the txshape
parameter of the interface.
• The clotutype value of the profile is equal to the value "OTU4"
If a matching profile exists, then the NE sets the parameter profileId to the profileid value of the
matching OTSiG profile.
If no matching profile exists, then the value 0 is used for the parameter profileId and the current
line transmission configuration is kept/frozen until a new value profileid value is provisioned by
a user.
If the managementmode is changed from otsig to otu, then the NE re-sets the value for the
parameter profileid to factory default.

Specifies the phase encoding mode applied to the optical carrier of the uplink port with the

• absolute - indicates high performance mode
• differential - indicates compatibility mode

All 2UC400 subtype cards - specific phasenc provisioning behaviour:
Both ports located on all 2UC400 subtype cards need to have the same phasenc provisioning.
This implies:
• phasenc can be changed for port with number 1 or for port with number 2.
• If the phasenc setting for one port is changed then this new phasenc provisioning is also
applied to other port.
All 2UC400 subtype cards - specific phasenc provisioning behaviour:
If a user changes phasenc for one port and for the other port management == otsig is
provisioned, then the profileid of the other port is also changed to the profile matching the new
phasenc value.
If no matching profile is defined for the card, then profileid is set to the value 0.
Changing phasenc parameter will be rejected if:
• This port/interface is used as connection point of an OCH XC.
• An external/cluster connection/topology is configured for the port/interface and the port
state is not down.
Changing phasenc parameter will be rejected if the new specified value is not allowed for the
configured encoding setting.

trackpolar
Syntax
trackpolar [<value>]
Values
fast - fast polarization state tracking
normal - normal polarization state tracking
Default
normal
Specifies the polarization tracking mode applied to the optical carrier of the line port.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by one allowed value.
When the encoding parameter value is changed, then the trackpolar value will be reset to
normal.
Restrictions
This parameter is applicable for all 2UC400 subtype cards.

Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable for an OTU4/OTU4x2 or OTSI uplink port.

== none), then changing the parameter value shall be denied.

WDM node a cluster O-CONN is provisioned to the uplink port).

Sub-command: otsig
Syntax
otsig [mgracd | profileid]
Configures the line port in an OTSiG like approach; i.e.
• OTSiG profile assignment for a line port.
• MGRACD setting of this OTSiG functionality
Note:
• This sub-command allows the user to provision the line transmission in a similar way like
done via command "config otsig ", but the configuration is done on port entity and not on
OTSiG entity. No OTSiG entity will exist in this case.
Restrictions
If managementmode == otu is provisioned, then the command will be denied.
The sub-command is only applicable for the following cards: 2UX200, 2UC400, 4UC400.

Syntax
mgracd [<value>]
Values
none - no management access domain identifier
cp - control plane/GMRE
mngpln - management plane
cp-mngpln - control plane/GMRE and management plane
Default
none
Specifies by whom the OTSiG configuration of the interface is managed.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by one allowed value.
Restrictions
If managementmode == otu is provisioned, then changing this parameter is denied.

profileid
Syntax
profileid [<value>]
Values
{0..1000}
Default
0
Specifies the OTSiG profile identifier assigned to the port entity. The following values are
support:
• value 0: No OTSiG profile is assigned.
• values {1..1000}: The OTSiG profile with the corresponding profileid is assigned to the
port entity.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by one allowed value.
Restrictions
If managementmode == otu is provisioned, then changing this parameter is denied.
If the profile with the specified profileid is not supported by the card where the interface is
located, then the command is denied. See the applicable profiles for each card via "show
profile otsig * brief <cardtype>" command.
If the profile with the specified profileid does not exist, then the command is denied.
The payload rate value derived from the profileid != 0 must match the payload rate as derived
from the provisioned interface type as follows:
• payload rate == 100G: for type == otu4
• payload rate == 200G: for type == otu4x2
In the current release, the system profiles defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables” can be
assigned.
If the managementmode= otsig is provisioned and a user sets a new profileid value, then the
NE changes the values accordingly for:
• the encoding parameter of the interface
• the phaseenc parameter of the interface
• the txshape parameter of the interface
• the fectype parameter of all OTU facilities associated with the interface/port
Note:
• This behaviour ensures, that profile configuration and individual line parameter
configuration have consistent matching values.
All 2UC400 subtype cards - specific phasenc provisioning behaviour:

Release 24.12

8228 Issue 1
Both ports located on all 2UC400 subtype cards need to have the same phasenc provisioning.
This implies:
• If profileid is changed and this causes a phasenc configuration change for one port then
this new phasenc provisioning is also applied to other port.
• If for the other port management == otsig is provisioned, then the profileid of the other
port is also changed to a profileid matching the new phasenc value.
A profile change causing a phasenc change as described above shall be rejected if one of the
following constraints is met:
• This port/interface is used as connection point of an OCH XC.
• An external/cluster connection/topology is configured for the port/interface and the port
state is not down.
ssdca
Syntax
ssdca [<value>]
Values
disabled - no laser shutdown in case of server signal degraded (SSD)
laseroff - laser is switched off in case of server signal degraded (SSD)
Default
disabled
The parameter ssdca controls whether the laser of the OTN port is switched off as part of LPT
function if Server Signal Degrade (ODUk dDEG) defect is present.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by an allowed value.
Notes:
• ODUk dDEG is derived from the egress POM function of the HO-ODUNIM associated
with the OTN port.
• If egress POM is disabled, then no dDEG supversion will take place and therefore laser
will not be switched off due to presence of dDEG defect.
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable for a port with the following setting:
(type== otu4/otu4x2/otsi) and (portrole == line)

Values
disabled - no laser shutdown in case of SSF
laseroff - laser is switched off in case of SSF
Default
disabled
The parameter ssfca controls whether the laser of the OTN port is switched off as part of LPT
function if SSF condition is present.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by an allowed value.
Notes:
• SSF condition is derived from the egress POM function of the HO-ODUNIM associated
with the OTN port.
• If egress POM is disabled, then no defect supervision will take place and therefore laser
will not be switched off due to presence of SSF condition.
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable for a port with the following setting:
(type== otu4/otu4x2/otsi) and (portrole == line)
ssfdelaytimer
Syntax
ssfdelaytimer [<value>]
Values
{0..255} - period using 10 milli-second as base unit (value is multiple of 10 ms)
Default
2
The parameter controls the period for which laser off CA triggered by a SSF condition is
delayed; i.e. the laser shut down is performed after ssfdelaytimer is expired and SSF condition
is still present.
Enter this keyword to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by an allowed value.
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable for a port with the following setting:
(type== otu4/otu4x2/otsi) and (portrole == line)

6.1259 config interface <csw-card> <port-aid> pm
6.1259.1 Purpose
This command allows to provision the performance monitoring parameters for the port/interface of
an IO card for PSS-<n>x shelf.
Use this command to:
• Clear current 15-minute and 1-day bins in all groups on this interface.
• Configure the BERPREFEC Group PM options.
• Configure the CSR group PM options.
• Configure the Chromatic Dispersion group PM options.
• Configure the Differential Group Delay group PM options.
• Configure the ESNR group PM options.
• Configure the Ethernet group PM options.
• Configure the ETHFECPM group PM options.
• Configure the Error Vector Magnitude group PM options.
• Configure the Frequency Offset group PM options.
• Configure the FEC group PM options.
• Configure the LanePwrs group PM options.
• Configure the received channel optical power group PM options.
• Configure the received/transmitted optical power group PM options.
• Configure the prefec error bits group PM options.
• Configure the PCS group PM options.
• Configure the PDL group PM options.
• Configure the Qmargin Group PM options.
• Configure the SDH group PM options.
• Configure the SONET group PM options.
• Configure the SOPR Group PM options.
Refer to PM Montypes tables in the Appendix A, “Reference tables” for applicable Montypes for
each PM group.
Refer to sub-command description for card/port applicability.
6.1259.2 Command Access Level
Impact: The command affects the performance monitoring function.
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

8240 Issue 1
6.1260 show interface <csw-card> <port-aid>
6.1260.1 Purpose
This command allows to retrieve the port/interface information of an IO card for PSS-<n>x shelf.
These IO cards are handled as one sub-set of IO cards supporting ODUk/packet switching function
by means of a central switch function. Therefore, the abbreviation csw-card (Central switched IO
Card) is used for this sub-set of cards.
The shelves supporting central ODUk switching are called CSW shelf. This generic term is used for
the following shelf types:
• PSS-24x
• PSS-12x
• PSS-8x
Use this command to:
• display generic port level attributes
• display the interface/port type {equipment, <n>gige, oc<n>, otu<n>, otsi, stm<n>} and attributes
• display loopback
• display the PM attributes
• display state
• display non-provisionable state attributes
• display the current remote connected port.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1260.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
detail
Displays the current settings and current analog data for the port.
Analog data includes received optical power, transmitted optical power, received channel
optical power, transmitted laser bias current and laser case temperature if applicable.
Displays in addition the provisioned FEC Type parameter value (see "config/show otu"
command) for the port if the following constraints are met:
1. The port is an <otn> port and type != otsi
2. The OTUk rate is greater or equal to OTU4.
3. The port is a line/uplink port.
loopback
Displays current loopback setting for the port.
Restrictions
This parameter is not applicable for type otsi.
Note:
• See command "show otsig" for type == otsi.
maxportrate
Displays the maximal port rate which can be provisioned for the port for the IO card (unit: Gb/s)
Sub-command: equipment
Displays the equipment port attributes. See command "show interface <csw-card> <port-id>
equipment".
Sub-command: <ngige>
Displays the GbEn LAN port attributes. See command "show interface <csw-card> <port-id>
<ngige>".
Sub-command: <ocn-stmn>
Displays the OCn/STMn port attributes. See command "show interface <csw-card> <port-aid>
<ocn-stmn>".
Sub-command: <otn>
Displays the OTN port attributes. See command "show interface <csw-card> <port-aid> <otn>".
Sub-command: pm
Displays the Performance Monitoring attributes. See command "show interface <csw-card>
<port-aid> pm".
rmconport
Displays the current configured remote connected port.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable for an uplink port (i.e. portrole is equal to line).

6.1261 show interface <csw-card> <port-aid> equipment
6.1261.1 Purpose
This command allows to retrieve the equipment port/interface information of an IO card for PSS-
<n>x shelf. These IO cards are handled as one sub-set of IO cards supporting ODUk/packet
switching function by means of a central switch function. Therefore, the abbreviation csw-card
(Central switched IO Card) is used for this sub-set of cards. A shelf supporting central switching is
called CSW shelf.
Use this command to:
• Display the Automatic In-Service Debounce time
• Display the pluggable module data
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
6.1261.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer

moduleproductcodesup
moduletype

6.1263 show interface <csw-card> <port-aid> <ocn-stmn>
6.1263.1 Purpose
This command allows to retrieve the OCn/STMn port/interface information of an IO card for PSS-
<n>x shelf. These IO cards are handled as one sub-set of IO cards supporting ODUk switching
function by means of a central switch function. Therefore, the abbreviation csw-card (Central
switched IO Card) is used for this sub-set of cards. A shelf supporting central ODUk switching is
called CSW shelf.
Use this command to:
• Display the Automatic In-Service Debounce time
• Display the pluggable module data
• Display the J0 attributes
• Display forced laser state
All TTI string values in the show output are converted from an octet string value to an ASCII string
value according to the following rules:
1. The header byte for J0 TTI is removed.
2. Trailing NULL characters will be removed (i.e. not shown in the replied string value).
3. Non-trailing NULL characters will be replaced by "." in the replied string value.
4. Any octet value between 1 hex and 1f hex will be replaced by "?" in the replied string value.
5. Any octet value between 20 hex to 7e hex will be replaced by the corresponding ASCII
character in the replied string value.
6. Any octet value between 7f hex to ff hex will be replaced "?" in the replied string value.
Note:
• J0 TTI strings at the CLI interface have 15 characters as maximal size. Therefore, the TTI
header byte is not included in the TTI string value.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1263.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
6.1263.3 Input Format
show interface <csw-card> <port-aid> <ocn-stmn>
ainstimer
almprof
caplist
channel
csfca

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
6.1264 show interface <csw-card> <port-aid> <otn>
6.1264.1 Purpose
This command allows to retrieve the OTN port/interface information of an IO card for PSS-<n>x
shelf. The following sub-classes w.r.t. OTN port/interfaces need to be distinguished:
• type = otuk/otukxn: OTUk port
• type = otsi: port can be configured as member of an OTSiG - see "config otsig"
These IO cards are handled as one sub-set of IO cards supporting ODUk/packet switching function
by means of a central switch function. Therefore, the abbreviation csw-card (Central switched IO
Card) is used for this sub-set of cards. A shelf supporting central switching is called CSW shelf.
Note:
The OTU layer is managed via non-card specific facility commands "config/show otu".
Use this command to:
• Display the Automatic In-Service Debounce time
• Display the receive channel frequency
• Display the transmit channel frequency of the pluggable module
• Display the pluggable module data
• Display LPT attributes
• Display forced laser state
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
6.1264.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
6.1264.3 Input Format

otsig
Displays the current OTSiG setting for the port and covers the following parameters:
• otsigid: identifier for the OTSiG within one card (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• otustruct: OTU structure transported via the line port (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• otsilist: list of ports of the OTSiG (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• profileid: OTSiG profileid assigned for the port (value is settable by user)
• otsigcapacity: capacity of the OTSiG (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• otsipayloadrate: payload rate of the OTSi (value is fixed assigned by NE)
• mgracd: Manager Access Control Domain of the OTSiG (value is settable by user)
If profileid != 0, then also the following transmission parameters of the assigned profile are
shown:
• OTSi baudrate
• OTSi Client OTU Type (clotutype)
• OTSi Forward Error Correction (fectype)
• OTSi modulation format (encoding)
• OTSi Phase Encoding mode (phasenc)
• OTSi Trasmit Shape (txshape)
Note:
• This command displays the line transmission in a similar way like done via command
"show otsig", but the data is shown on port entity and not on OTSiG entity. No OTSiG
entity will be exist in this case.
Restrictions
The sub-command is only applicable for the following cards: 2UX200, 2UC400,4UC400.
otsigid
Displays the OTSIG ID the port belongs to.
If it does not belong to one OTSiG, then it shall display as "none".
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable for type otsi.
power
Displays the transmitted optical output power of the port.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable for an OTSi/OTU4/OTU4x2 uplink ports.

8290 Issue 1
powerclassmod
Displays the power class information which is needed for a pluggable module in order to be
used for this port:
The following values are supported:
• reduced: only modules with reduced power class can be used.
• any: modules of any power class can be used.
Notes:
• A module mismatch alarm will be raised if powerclassmod == reduced is reported, but
the inserted modules does not support this power class.
• If powerclassmod == any is reported, then power class of an inserted module is not
contributing to a mismatch alarm.
The power class is only applicable for moduletype value 'C4ACO' and is calculated based on
card type as follows:
• value 'any' is reported for each port located on card 2UX200.
• value 'reduced is reported for each port located on card 8UC1T
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable for following cards: 2UX200, 8UC1T.
phasenc
Displays the phase encoding mode applied to the port.
4UC400/1UX100 - behaviour:
The value for this parameter is not provisionable by the user but it is set implicitly be the NE as
follows:
• Fixed value differential is reported for all cases.
2UX200 - behaviour:
The value for this parameter is not provisionable by the user but it is set implicitly be the NE as
follows:
• Value absolute is reported if the provisioned fectype of associated OTU facility is equal
to sdfec-acc.
• Value differential is reported if the provisioned fectype of associated OTU facility is
unequal to sdfec-acc.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable for an OTU4/OTU4x2 uplink ports.
This parameter is not applicable for type otsi.
Note: See command "show otsig" for type == otsi.

8306 Issue 1

11QPA4B card:
<shelf>/<slot>/L{1,3}
Specifies the shelf, slot, and port of the interface. Enter the shelf number, a slash, the slot
number, a slash, and the port number, or * to list all of the OT cards on the network element
with far end topology set to external.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
detail
Displays the current wavekeys (wk1 and wk2) for the specified line port that is configured for an
external connection to a different network element.
<wk1> <wk2>
Values
0..4096 - wk1 in increments of 1
0..4096 - wk2 in increments of 1
Default
[0 0]
Specifies the wavetracker keys [wk1,wk2] that are used for a particular wavelength channel.
Note:
This command will be denied if the connection provisioning is not set to external connection
(set using the "config interface topology" command).
The wavetracker keys [wk1 and wk2] must be set to [0 0] before changing the connection
provisioning from external to either internal or not connected. If the wavetracker key values are
non-zero, then the command to change the connection provisioning will be denied. Connection
provisioning is done via the "config interface topology" command.
Only certain combinations of wk1 and wk2 are supported, depending on the channel
provisioning. If the combination is not supported, this command will be denied.
If wk1=0 and wk2=0, then wavekey modulation is disabled on the transmit port. If this command
is executed for the first time on the selected port, then the optical output power is set to the
default output power value.
If wk1!=0 and wk2!=0, the wavekey modulation is enabled on the transmit port. If this command
is executed for the first time on the selected port, then the optical output power is set to the
default output power value.
The wavetracker keys [wk1 and wk2] must be set to [0 0] before changing the channel
provisioning. If the wavetracker key values are non-zero, then the command to change the
channel frequency will be denied.

8314 Issue 1
7.2 config otu
7.2.1 Purpose
This command modifies the specified facility parameter values for a previously auto-created OTU
facility; i.e. if the OTU facility is not yet provisioned the command will be rejected.
Use this command to:
• Configure the FEC used.
• Set the interworking mode.
• Configure the PM parameters.
• Set the serverport association for the specified otu-id entity.
• Set the state of the facility.
• Set the OTU trail trace attributes.
• Set dDEG detection configuration.
• Set ASAP.
Note: This command shall be executed after the signal type 'OTUk' or 'OTSi' including OTSiG is
provisioned for the corresponding interface.
OT card Behavior:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OT cards are 112SDX11, 11DPM12, 11DPM4M, 11DPM8, 11QPA4B, 12P120, 12P120S, 260SCX2,

DSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to DSW (Distributed SWitch) cards. If a requirement is only applicable for a
sub-set of DSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.
DSW cards are 12CE120, 16P200, 18CE300, 1UD200, 20P200, all 8P20 subtypes, D5X500,
D5X500L, D5X500Q, S13X100E, all S13X100 subtypes, all S13X400 subtypes and all S4X400
subtypes.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to CSW (Central odu/packet SWitched) cards. If a requirement is only
applicable for a sub-set of CSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.
CSW cards are 1UX100, all 1UX500 subtypes, 2UX200, 2UX500, 20AX200, 20MX80, 4MX200,
5MX500, 20AN80, 20UC200, all 2UC400 subtypes, 10AN1T, 10AN400, 30AN300, 4AN400,
4UC400, all 2UC1T subtypes, 2UC1TH, 4UC1T and 8UC1T.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack applicability.

Degrade interval (degintvl) specifies the number of consecutive bad seconds (see parameter
"degthr") to be detected before declaring a dDEG (signal degrade) defect for the OTU facility.
The defect is cleared if degintvl consecutive good seconds (see parameter "degthr") are
detected.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
12CE120 card - specific dDEG provisioning behavior:
If the parameter is changed for OTU facility then this change shall also be applied to
corresponding parameter of the associated ODUPTF facility.
Restrictions
This parameter applies to CSW and DSW cards defined in the purpose.
This parameter applies to the following OT cards: 11DPM8, 12P120, 12P120S, all
D6AD2T4 subtypes, all S2AD200 subtypes, all S5AD400 and all S6AD600 subtypes.

• When the first line port is created and the line port type is changed from unassigned to

Specific behavior when oprmode=regen:
For OTU4, OTU4x2 or OTU4Half line rate:
• When changing from oprmode=adddrop to oprmode=regen, all serverports shall be set
to unassigned manually by user;
If there exists a serverport that is not set to unassigned, and the User tries to change
oprmode=addrop to oprmode=regen, then the command is denied with the error response:
"Error: Request failed - serverport values must be unassigned"
• After oprmode has been changing as regen, the serverport shall be set automatically
with fixed value, any attempt to modify the serverport values will be denied;
• When changing from oprmode=regen to adddrop, all serverports shall be set to
automatically unassigned.
For OTU4Halfx5 line rate:
• The same fixed serverport values are used for oprmode={adddrop, regen}, Therefore,
there is no option to manually set the serverports to unassigned.

7.3 config otu <otu-aid> state
7.3.1 Purpose
This command configures the state parameters for an OTU facility.
Use this command to:
• Configure the automatic in-service timer
• Set the state of the facility
OT Card Behavior:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OT cards are 11DPM12, 11DPM8, 11DPM4M, 11QPA4B, 4QPA8, 112SDX11, 12P120, 12P120S,
260SCX2, all D6AD2T4 subtypes, all S2AD200 subtypes, all S5AD400 subtypes and all S6AD600
subtypes.
DSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to DSW (Distributed SWitch) cards. If a requirement is only applicable for a
sub-set of DSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.
DSW cards are 11QPA4B, 12CE120, 16P200, 18CE300, 1UD200, 20P200, all 8P20 subtypes,
D5X500, D5X500L, D5X500Q, S13X100E, all S13X100 subtypes, all S13X400 subtypes and all
S4X400 subtypes.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to CSW (Central odu/packet SWitched) cards. If a requirement is only
applicable for a sub-set of CSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.
CSW cards are 1UX100, all 1UX500 subtypes, 2UX200, 2UX500, 20AX200, 20MX80, 4MX200,
5MX500, 20AN80, 20UC200, all 2UC400 subtypes, 10AN1T, 10AN400, 30AN300, 4AN400,
4UC400, all 2UC1T subtypes, 2UC1TH, 4UC1T and 8UC1T.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack applicability.
7.3.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
7.3.3 Input Format
config otu <otu-aid> state
ains [ainstimer | enabled | disabled]
down
up

Sub-command: ains
Syntax
ains [ainstimer | disabled | enabled]
Default
disabled
The subcommand to configure Automatic In-Service.
ainstimer
Syntax
ainstimer [help | system | <value>]
Values
system - Configures the AINS timer to use the system value
help - Displays the default and valid range
<value> - Sets the number of hours and minutes for the AINS timer. Format: <h> [<m>];
Range: 1 minute to 96 hours
Default
system
Specifies the properties for the AINS timer.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.
enabled
Set AINS for the OTU to on.
disabled
Set AINS for the OTU to off.
down
Set to down to disable the OTU facility.
up
Set to up to enable the OTU facility.

# config otu 1/7/1 state down

7.4.1 Purpose
This command configures the Performance Monitoring attributes on an OTU facility.
Use this command to:
• Clear the current 15-minute and 1-day bins in all groups on this interface.
• Configure the otupm group PM options.
Refer to PM Montypes tables in the Appendix A, “Reference tables” for applicable Montypes for the
OTU PM group.
OT Card Behavior:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OT cards are 11DPM12, 11DPM8, 11DPM4M, 11QPA4B, 4QPA8, 112SDX11, 12P120, 12P120S,
260SCX2, all D6AD2T4 subtypes, all S2AD200 subtypes, all S5AD400 subtypes and all S6AD600
subtypes.
DSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to DSW (Distributed SWitch) cards. If a requirement is only applicable for a
sub-set of DSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.
DSW cards are 11QPA4B, 12CE120, 16P200, 18CE300, 1UD200, 20P200, all 8P20 subtypes,
D5X500, D5X500L, D5X500Q, S13X100E, all S13X100 subtypes, all S13X400 subtypes and all
S4X400 subtypes.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to CSW (Central odu SWitched) cards. If a requirement is only applicable for
a sub-set of CSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.
CSW cards are 10AN1T, 10AN400, 1UX100, 20AX200, 20AN80, 20MX80, all 2UC1T subtypes,
2UC1TH, 20UC200, all 2UC400 subtypes, 2UX200, 2UX500, 30AN300, 4AN400, 4MX200,
4UC400, 4UC1T, 5MX500 and 8UC1T.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack applicability.

8354 Issue 1
7.5 config odunim
7.5.1 Purpose
This command is used to edit parameters related to the non-terminated ODU path (ODUNIM)
facility that was previously auto-created (auto-provisioned).
The following sub-types can be distinguished for the ODUNIM facility:
1. HO-ODU: The ODUk/ODUCn facility is mapped directly into an OTUk/OTUCn
2. LO-ODU: The ODU facility is mapped into a sub-structured ODUPTF
A High Order ODU (HO-ODU) facility is created when the corresponding OTU facility is created.
A Lower Order ODU (LO-ODU) facility is created when:
1. a ODUPTF is created and the ODUSTRUCT value is unequal to all UAS
2. a new LO-ODU tributary is configured as part of the ODUSTRUCT parameter
The two sub-types imply also different format/syntax w.r.t. addressing the facility; i.e.
1. HO-ODU Syntax: <shelf>/<slot>/<otu-id>
2. LO-ODU Syntax: <shelf>/<plane-slot>/<ho-odu-id>/<lo-odu-id>
For further details see input parameter definition for "<odu-aid>".
Use this command to:
• Set the ASAP profile
• Set the Performance Monitoring attributes.
• Set the ODU Trail Trace Identifier attributes.
• Set the Path Overhead Monitoring.
• Configure the ODUk attributes of ODU.
OT card Behaviour:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OT cards are 11DPM12, 11DPM4M, 11DPM8, 4QPA8, 11QPA4B, 112SDX11, 12P120, 12P120S,
260SCX2, all D6AD2T4 subtypes, all S2AD200 subtypes, all S5AD400 subtypes and all S6AD600
subtypes.
DSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to DSW (Distributed SWitch) cards unless further restriction is clarified for
individual sub-command or parameter within this command.
DSW cards are 12CE120, 16P200, 18CE300, 1UD200, 20P200, all 8P20 subtypes, D5X500,
D5X500L, D5X500Q, S13X100E, all S13X100 subtypes, all S13X400 subtypes and all S4X400
subtypes.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to CSW (Central odu/packet SWitched) cards. If a requirement is only
applicable for a sub-set of CSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.
OTH facility management commands

degintvl
Syntax
degintvl [<value>]
Values
1..10 - indicates 1 to 10 time periods.
Default
7
Degrade interval (degintvl) specifies the number of consecutive bad periods (see parameter
"degperiod" and "degthr") to be detected before declaring a dDEG (signal degrade) defect for
the ODUNIM facility as part of ingress POM/NIM function. The defect is cleared if degintvl
consecutive good periods (see parameter "degperiod" and "degthr") are detected.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.

Egress degrade threshold (egdegthr) specifies a number of errored blocks as used for dDEG
detection for the ODUNIM facility as part of egress POM/NIM function.

7.7 config odunim <facility-type> <odu-aid> pm
7.7.1 Purpose
This command configures the ODU-layer group PM options for an ODUNIM facility.
Use this command to:
• Clear current 15-minute and 1-day bins for this facility.
• Configure the receive (ingress) ODU PM (odurx) group PM options.
• Configure the transmit (egress) ODU PM (odutx) group PM options.
Refer to PM Montypes tables in the Appendix A, “Reference tables” for applicable Montypes for the
ODU PM groups.
OT card Behavior:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OT cards are 11DPM12, 11DPM8, 11DPM4M, 11QPA4B, 4QPA8, 112SDX11, 12P120, 12P120S,
260SCX2, all D6AD2T4 subtypes, all S2AD200 subtypes, all S5AD400 subtypes and all S6AD600
subtypes.
DSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to DSW (Distributed SWitch) cards unless further restriction is clarified for
individual sub-command or parameter within this command.
DSW cards are 12CE120, 16P200, 1UD200, 20P200, all 8P20 subtypes, D5X500, D5X500L,
D5X500Q, S13X100E, all S13X100 subtypes, all S13X400 subtypes and all S4X400 subtypes.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to CSW (Central odu SWitched) cards. If a requirement is only applicable for
a sub-set of CSW card values then, this will be explicitly specified.
CSW cards are 10AN1T, 1UX100, all 1UX500 subtypes, 20AX200, 20MX80, 20UC200, all 2UC400
subtypes, all 2UC1T subtypes, 2UC1TH, 2UX500, 30AN300, 4AN400, 4UC400, 4UC1T, 5MX500,
10AN400, 20AN80, 2UX200, 4MX200 and 8UC1T.
The shelves supporting central ODUk switching are called CSW shelf. This generic term is used for
the following shelf types:
• PSS-24x
• PSS-12x
• PSS-8x
The shelves supporting distributed ODUk switching are called DSW shelf. This generic term is used
for the following shelf types:
• PSS-4II
• PSS-8
• PSS-16II
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack applicability.

7.8 config oduptf
7.8.1 Purpose
This command is used to edit parameters related to a previously provisioned ODUPTF instance. An
ODUPTF instance represents the management view of an ODU path termination function.
Three different sub-types of ODU path termination can be distinguished based on the client signal
carried in the payload of the terminated ODU (ODUPTF):
• Substructured ODUPTF
• Unstructured ODUPTF
• ODU1PTF
Substructured ODUPTF: The ODU payload carries a set of ODUs as clients (that is, LO-ODUs).
The following substructured ODUPTFs and rates are supported:
• Terminated ODU1 entity identified as ODU1 with plane slot number.
• Terminated ODU2 entity identified as ODU2 with plane slot number.
• Terminated ODU4 entity identified as ODU4 with plane slot number.
• Terminated ODUC entity identified as ODUC with plane slot number.
A substructured ODUPTF is created in the following scenarios:
• An ODUPTF instance on virtual plane is automatically created when a non-terminated ODUn is
cross connected to an ODUPOOL.
• An ODUPTF instance on pre-set plane is automatically created when a non-terminated ODUn is
cross connected to an ODUPTF with pre-set ODU AID.
• An ODUPTF instance on virtual plane is manually created with the create sub-command.
Unstructured ODUPTF: The ODU payload carries one non-OTN client signal transparently
mapped into the ODU payload.
The following unstructured ODUPTFs and the corresponding client mappings are supported:
• GbEn/ETH transparently mapped into ODUk
• OCn/STMn transparently mapped into ODUk
• FCn transparently mapped into ODUk
An unstructured ODUPTF with appropriate rate is automatically created/deleted when one of the
above transparently transported client ports is created/deleted as part of interface type
configuration.
When an unstructured ODUPTF is created and more than one mapping is supported for one client
signal (example for STM-64), the mapping can be changed by means of changing the encmode/
mappingmode parameter (see "configure interface" command).
An unstructured ODUPTF with appropriate rate is automatically created/deleted when an uplink port
for an IO card with central packet switching is created/deleted as part of interface type
configuration.
An unstructured ODUPTF with appropriate rate is manually created/deleted for IO cards with
distributed ETH switching - details see create sub-command.
OTH facility management commands
config oduptf

8398 Issue 1
An unstructured ODUPTF with appropriate rate is manually created/deleted for S13X100 which is

ODU1PTF is an ODU1 which consists of 16 timeslots where each timeslot has 155Mb capacity (so
called sub-ODU1 timeslots). It was defined before ODU0 rate was specified by standards for e.g.
STM-1/-4 or OC-3/-12 transport. Since this is a non-standard mapping, it will only be supported by
some dedicated OTs - see parameter "optsg" to configure the sub-ODU1 payload structure.
The substructured and unstructured sub-types imply different format/syntax w.r.t. identification; i.e.
1. Unstructured Syntax: <shelf>/<slot>/<port-id>
2. Substructured Syntax: <shelf>/<plane-slot>/<ho-odu-id>
For further details see input parameter definition for "<oduptf-aid>".
The following LO-ODUk (with k!=flex) and their TS allocation are supported for HO-ODUj:
• ODU1 PTF: ODU0: 1x 1.25G TS (Note: ODU1 PTF has a fixed structure consisting of 2xODU0)
• ODU2 PTF: ODU0: 1x 1.25G TS; ODU1: 2x 1.25G TS
• ODU4 PTF: ODU0: 1x 1.25G TS; ODU1: 2x 1.25G TS; ODU2: 8x 1.25G TS; ODU2E: 8x 1.25G
TS; ODU3: 31x 1.25G TS
The following LO-ODUflex (GFP-F) and their TS allocation are supported for HO-ODUj:
• ODU2 PTF: ODUfgfp: 1 to 8x 1.25G TS
• ODU4 PTF: ODUfgfp: 1 to 80x 1.25G TS
The following LO-ODUflex (CBR) and their TS allocation are supported for HO-ODUj:
• ODUffc400: 4x 1.25G TS in ODU2/ODU4 PTF
• ODUffc800: 7x 1.25G TS in ODU2/ODU4 PTF
• ODUffc1600: 11x 1.25G TS in ODU4 PTF

• ODUfibsdr: 3x 1.25G TS in ODU2 PTF and 2x 1.25G TS ODU4 PTF
• ODUfibddr: 5x 1.25G TS in ODU2 PTF and 4x 1.25G TS ODU4 PTF
• ODUfibqdr: 8x 1.25G TS ODU4 PTF
• ODUf3gsdi18: 3x 1.25G TS in ODU2/ODU4 PTF
• ODUf3gsdi19: 3x 1.25G TS in ODU2/ODU4 PTF

Use this command to:
• set the ASAP profile.
• set the payload type.
• set the Payload Type Mismatch response.
• set the PM attributes.
• set the ODU Trail Trace Identifier attributes.
• set the LO-ODU structure embedded in a HO-ODU.
• set the delay measurement parameters.
• set the timing granularity (260SCX2 and 1UD200).
• create or delete the OPTSG of an ODU1PTF.
• manually create/delete a substructured ODUPTF.
OT Card Behaviour:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OT cards are 11DPM12, 11DPM8, 11DPM4M, 4QPA8, 11QPA4B, 112SDX11, 12P120, 12P120S,
260SCX2, all D6AD2T4 subtypes, all S2AD200 subtypes, all S5AD400 subtypes and all S6AD600
subtypes.
DSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to DSW (Distributed SWitch) cards unless further restriction is clarified for
individual sub-command or parameter within this command.
DSW cards are 12CE120, 1UD200, 16P200, 18CE300, 20P200, all 8P20 subtypes, D5X500,
D5X500L, D5X500Q, S13X100E, all S13X100 subtypes, all S13X400 subtypes and all S4X400
subtypes.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to CSW (Central odu/packet SWitched) cards. If a requirement is only
applicable for a sub-set of CSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.

8410 Issue 1
1 Create substructured ODUPTF
This sub-command manually creates an ODUPTF facility on virtual plane slot. When the
addressed <facility-type> is an oduc the parameter oducnrate must be specified.
When the substructured ODUPTF is created then also the embedded LO-ODUs are created
based on the specified odustruct default value.
The substructured ODUPTF and the embedded LO ODUNIM entities goes into NOIMP&MDLT
state. While the entity carries NOIMP state, no condition will be raised on the entity. When the
ODUPTF is cross connected to an ODUNIM entity (see command "config odukaps" or "config
odukxc") NOIMP will be cleared for these entities. If this cross-connection is deleted, then
ODUPTF and embedded/contained ODUNIM facilities will enter again the NOIMP state.
The MDLT state indicates that the ODUPTF is manually created and therefore needs also to be
manually deleted with the corresponding sub-command.
The NOIMP state indicates that the facilities are not provisioned (i.e. implemented) in the HW,
since the HW relationship is established after the HO-ODU cross-connection is made.
The AID of the substructured ODUPTF can be either auto-assigned by the system (when
ODUPOOLAID is used) or can be manually assigned by the user (when a free <ho-odu-id>
plane AID is used).
The value range for <ho-odu-id> is defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”.
If the maximum number of <ho-odu-id> for ODUPTF located on plane-slot (i.e. the virtual plane
or pre-set plane slot) is reached, no new substructured ODUPTF can be created and the
command is denied.
Note:
The maximum number of ODUPTF entities on plane-slot (virtual and preset) must not exceed
the defined maximum per shelf type. The allowed value range and the maximum number of
entities for <ho-odu-id> are defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”.
If a substructured ODUPTF creation is requested and shelfmode == unknown is set for the
shelf as specified by the <oduptf-aid> value, then the creation shall be denied.
If the specified shelf value as part of the <oduptf-aid> value is a secondary shelf of a PSS-24x
dual shelf configuration (i.e. shelfmode == otn48Tsec is provisioned), then the create sub-
command shall be denied.
Restrictions
Creation of substructured ODUPTF is supported for plane slot in CSW, DSW and PSS-32
shelf.
2 Create unstructured ODUPTF
This sub-command manually creates an unstructured ODUPTF facility on IO cards being a
member of a packet switch group.
When the addressed "<facility-type>" is oduflex the parameter flexsize must be specified.
When the unstructured ODUPTF is created, it goes into MDLT state.
The MDLT state indicates that the ODUPTF is manually created and therefore needs also to be

The AID value range for unstructured ODUPTF determines also the 100G slice where the
ODUPTF is allocated w.r.t. transmission resources.
For 30SE300 and 6SE300 the following value sub-sets are defined/allowed w.r.t. slice
allocation for current release:
• <shelf>/<slot>/{101..150} - first 100G slice
• <shelf>/<slot>/{201..210} - second 100G slice
• <shelf>/<slot>/{301..350} - third 100G slice
• <shelf>/<slot>/{401..410} - fourth 100G slice
If a not allowed value is specified, the NE will deny the create sub-command.
Each slice has 100G bandwidth supporting 80 backplane Time Slots (TS). For an ODUPTF with
rate k the following capacity is needed:
• ODU4: 80 TS
• ODU2e: 8 TS
• ODUflex (GFP and with flexsize 1<= N <=80 tributary slots): N TS
For S13X100 subtypes and S13X100E the backplane BP2N1 port has 100G bandwidth
supporting 80 backplane Time Slots (TS). For an ODUPTF with rate k the following capacity is
needed:
• ODU4: 80 TS
• ODU2e: 8 TS
• ODUflex (GFP and with flexsize 1<= N <=80 tributary slots): N TS
For 20P200 the backplane BP2 port has 100G bandwidth supporting 80 backplane Time Slots
(TS). For an ODUPTF with rate k the following capacity is needed:
• ODUflex (GFP and with flexsize 1<= N <=8 tributary slots): N TS
If the 100G capacity limit (i.e. more than 80 backplane TS are needed) is crossed for the slice
where the ODUPTF shall be located, then no unstructured ODUPTF can be created for this
slice and the command is denied.
If an unstructured ODUPTF creation is requested and this card is not a member of a packet
switch group, then the creation shall be denied.
On a 20P200 card the BP2 port type must be 'interlaken_PIF', otherwise the creation request is
rejected.
Restrictions
Creation of unstructured ODUPTF applies to the following CSW cards: 30SE300, 6SE300
Creation of unstructured ODUPTF applies to the following DSW cards: 20P200, S13X100E,
S13X100 subtypes

The value of the parameter degthr shall be changed in context of a flexsize change as follows:
1. Calculate the ratio R = degthr_current / degthr_max_current, with 0 < R <= 1
2. Determine the threshold multiplier for newsize: M, with M element of {10209, 10252,
10636}
3. Set degthr_new = CEILING (newsize * M * R)
The parameter degthr change shall be applied for the following facilities:
1. The ODUPTF facility
2. The ODUTCM facility associated/contained by the ODUPTF facility
Example:
An ODUflex with size_current = 15 (-> 15 is in the second range) has a degthr_current of
120000 (the allowed maximum would be: 15 * 10252 = 153780).
The newsize shall be 7 (the allowed maximum threshold for this newsize = 7 * 10209 = 71463)
Use of the algorithm above:
1. Calculate the ratio R = degthr_current / degthr_max_current, with 0 < R <= 1
R = 120000 / (15 * 10252) = 120000 / 153780 = 0.780335544
2. Determine the threshold multiplier of newsize: M, with M element of {10209, 10252,
10636}
newsize = 7 -> first range -> M = 10209
3. Set degthr_new = CEILING (newsize * M * R)
degthr_new = CEILING (7 * 10209 * 0.780335544) = CEILING (55765.119) = 55766
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable for ODUflex rate.

The additional value UAS (unassigned) is supported as tributary rate as follows:
• UAS means, that the specified tributary time slots are unallocated as defined in G.709.
• UAS is specified in combination with tributary port number 0; i.e. the value range for PN
is extended if UAS is supported.
• If tributary port number 0 is used for any tributary rate unequal to UAS, then the resulting
odustruct value will be rejected.
• no LO-ODU facility will be associated if is UAS configured.
• if UAS is set for a set of ts which have previously allocated with an ODUk then this LO-
ODU facility will be deleted. No new LO-ODU facility will be created.
• A user can select any sub-set of ts specified for rate UAS and define for this sub-set a
new tributary rate.
The tributary rate value ODUfgfp<n> is used as follows:
• The value <n> determines the size of the ODUflex (GFP) in terms of 1.25G TS; i.e. the
value range is 1..80.
• This tributary rate value is needed for HO-ODUCn PTF since the size of ODUflex (GFP)
cannot be derived anymore from the number of allocated 5G TS.

• a LO-ODU1 can use the same tributary port number as another provisioned LO-ODUj

provisioned LO-ODUj (with j!=1)

invalid for an ODUPTF with rate ODU2.

ODU implies:
• The tributary port number needs to unique among all provisioned LO-ODUk.

ODU implies:
• The tributary port number needs to unique among all provisioned LO-ODUk.

Create or delete a transmitted OPTSG of ODU1PTF attributes.

slots or 8 even time slots.

There is no NE validation.
5. Deleting a transmitted OPTSG will delete the OPTSG facilities and create an ID=0 for
each single timeslot.
6. When an OPTSG is associated with an OPTSG XC, provisioning will be rejected.

• exp_dapi
• exp_sapi
• tx_dapi
• tx_sapi
• tx_os

exp_dapi
Syntax
exp_dapi [<value>]
Values
<value> - 0..15 ASCII character string, enclosed in quotation marks (quotation marks are
optional).
Default
Null character (15 bytes each with hex value 00)
Specifies the expected incoming Destination Access Point Identifier (DAPI).
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
To change the setting, enter this keyword followed by a parameter value.
If the specified string value contains less than 15 characters, then the NE adds NULL
characters to construct a 15-byte TTI string value.

subtypes.

7.8.5 Examples
In the following example the whole new LO-ODU payload structure is configured:
# config oduptf odu2 1/71/1 odustruct odu1#1-1,5&odu1#2-2,6&odu1#3-3,7&odu1#4-4,8
This example shows a partial LO-ODU structure reconfiguration (only time slots 1..8 are affected).
The operator has always to specify all timeslots which are affected in case of partial payload
change. If e.g. an odu1#8-1,9 is already configured and shall be replaced by another signal then all
timeslots need to be contained in the new odustruct value. As a result this command example is
rejected.
# config oduptf odu4 1/71/8 odustruct odu2#1-1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
This example shows deletion of one LO-ODU by using uas as new tributary rate. The operator has
always to specify all timeslots of the LO-ODU to be deleted. If e.g. an odu1#8-1,9 is configured and
this LO-ODU shall be deleted then this can be done via following command.
# config oduptf odu4 1/71/8 odustruct uas#0-1,9
This example shows creation of one LO-ODU by using uas as old tributary rate; e.g.
• currently odustruct == UAS#0-1,2,3,5,6,7,8&odu0#4-4 is provisioned for an ODUPTF with rate
ODU2
• user wants to create one LO-ODU with rate ODU1 and wants to keep odu0#4

In the next example an ODUPTF facility on virtual plane will be manually created. The <oduptf-aid>
value is assigned by the operator. In addition the value 'my-profile' will be assigned as alarm profile
for the newly created facility. All other parameters will be assigned with default values.
# config oduptf odu2 1/71/1 create
# config oduptf oduc 1/71/1 create oduc4
This example shows the creation of one LO-ODU contained in an ODUC4 for tributary rate
ODUfgfp<n>; e.g.
• User wants to create an ODUflex (GFP-F) with size 10 (size 10 means 10x1.25 TS)
• ODUCn is using 5G tributary slots and therefore the size cannot anymore derived by the number
of allocated TS.
• The user has to specify the size as part of the tributary rate value; i.e. the tributary value is
ODUfgfp10 ( ODUfgfp<n> with <n> = 10)
• 3x5G TS are needed to transport one ODUflex (GFP-F) with size 10.
This can be done with the command as specified in next paragraph.
# config oduptf oduc 1/71/8 odustruct odufgfp10#1-101,201,301
# config oduptf oduc 1/71/1 msimresp enabled
WARNING! Please check if S5AD400 cards on far end nodes are working in a SW release beyond
R13.1.
Otherwise this is a service affecting command.
Enter "yes" to confirm, "no" to cancel:

7.9 config oduptf <facility-type> <oduptf-aid> state
7.9.1 Purpose
This command configures the state parameters for an ODUPTF facility.
Use this command to:
• Configure the automatic in-service timer.
• Set the state of the facility.
OT Card Behavior:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OT cards are 11DPM12, 11DPM8, 11DPM4M, 11QPA4B, 4QPA8, 112SDX11 and 260SCX2.
12P120, 12P120S, All D6AD2T4, DS2AD200, S5AD400 and S6AD600 subtype cards are not
supported:
This command does not apply to 12P120, 12P120S, D6AD2T4, S2AD200, S5AD400, S6AD600
subtypes. See state parameter and command purpose in "config oduptf".
DSW card/shelf not supported:
This command does not apply to DSW (Distributed odu SWitch) cards and shelves. See state
parameter and command purpose for DSW card definition in "config oduptf".
CSW card/shelf not supported
This command does not apply to CSW (Central odu SWitched) cards and shelves. See state
parameter and command purpose for CSW card definition in "config oduptf".
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack applicability.
7.9.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
7.9.3 Input Format
config oduptf <facility-type> <oduptf-aid> state
ains [ainstimer | disabled | enabled]
down
up

7.10.1 Purpose
This command configures the Performance Monitoring attributes on an ODUPTF facility.
Use this command to:
• Clear current 15-minute and 1-day bins in all groups on this interface
• Configure the odurx PM group options
Refer to PM Montypes tables in the Appendix A, “Reference tables” for applicable Montypes for the
ODU PM group.
This command is not applicable for 260SCX2 facilities.
OT Card Behavior:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OT cards are 11DPM12, 11DPM8, 11DPM4M, 11QPA4B, 4QPA8, 112SDX11, 12P120, 12P120S,
260SCX2, all D6AD2T4 subtypes, all S2AD200 subtypes, all S5AD400 subtypes and all S6AD600
subtypes.
DSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to DSW (Distributed SWitch) cards unless further restriction is clarified for
individual sub-command or parameter within this command.
DSW cards are 12CE120, 16P200, 18CE300, 20P200, all 8P20 subtypes, D5X500, D5X500L,
D5X500Q, S13X100E, all S13X100 subtypes, all S13X400 subtypes and all S4X400 subtypes.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to CSW (Central odu SWitched) cards. If a requirement is only applicable for
a sub-set of CSW card values then, this will be explicitly specified.
CSW cards are 10AN1T, 10AN400, 20AX200, 20AN80, 20MX80, 20UC200, 30AN300, 30SE300,

the following shelf types:

The shelves supporting distributed ODUk switching are called DSW shelf. This generic term is used
for the following shelf types:
• PSS-4II

Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack applicability.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
7.11 config tcm
7.11.1 Purpose
The config tcm is used to create or delete a TCM entity for a specific ODU. It is also used to edit
parameters related to the TCM facility that was previously created.
The TCM facility will always be located 'below/under' an ODU facility (i.e. the TCM facility is
embedded within the ODUNIM/ODUPTF facility and the ODU AID is used as one component to
identify a TCM facility). Therefore, the following cases can be distinguished w.r.t containing ODU
facility:
1. HO-ODUNIM facility with ODU AID syntax: <shelf>/<slot>/<otu-id>
2. LO-ODUNIM facility with ODU AID syntax: <shelf>/<plane-slot>/<ho-odu-id>/<lo-odu-id>
3. Unstructured ODUPTF facility with ODU AID syntax: <shelf>/<slot>/<port-id>
4. Substructured ODUPTF facility with ODU AID syntax: <shelf>/<plane-slot>/<ho-odu-id>
Use this command to:
• Create the TCM entity under the ODU
• Delete the TCM entity under the ODU
• Set the TCM trail trace identifier attributes
• Set the LTC (loss of TCM connection) response
• Set the consequent action to be taken upon TCM defects
• Determines if the provisioned TCM Overhead is inserted or not at TCM source
• Determines if the received TCM Overhead is discarded or not at TCM sink
• Set the admin state for the TCM
• Set the TCM delay measurement parameters
• Set the PM attributes
The TCM facility can operate in the following main modes:
1. TCM NIM - Non Intrusive Monitor for the provisioned TCM level
2. TCM termination - sink and source termination function for the provisioned TCM level
If a parameter is only applicable for TCM facility operating in termination mode, then this is explicitly
specified as restriction in the parameter definition.
If it is requested to change a parameter for TCM facility provisioned as TCM NIM which is specified
to be applicable only for the termination mode, then the command shall be rejected.
A TCM termination supports additional mode parameters to allow a smooth insertion of a TCM trail
into an existing ODUk trail without service impact; i.e. the TCM termination behaves like a NIM as
intermediate step. But this mode setting is only needed temporarily until the TCM trail is set-up end-
to-end. In this mode setting the facility is still considered as TCM termination (e.g. w.r.t. the
applicability and validation requirements).
OT Card Behaviour:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OTH facility management commands
config tcm

8464 Issue 1
Default

Specifies the TCM level of the TCM facility as defined in G.709. The parameter is used as sub-

<position>
Values
AM - After Matrix
BM - Before Matrix
Default
Entry required
The position of the TCM point w.r.t. matrix (i.e. ODU) connection function. The TCM point can
be located either Before Matrix (BM) connection (i.e. the TCM function is located before matrix
connection and therefore the corresponding matrix connection is outside of the TCM trail) or
After Matrix (AM) connection (i.e. the TCM function is located after matrix connection and
therefore the corresponding matrix connection is inside of the TCM trail).
Restrictions
11QPA4 only supports BM position value
260SCX2 only supports BM position value
create
Syntax
create <tcmmode> <sequence-no>
Enter the keyword followed by a TCM mode and sequence number to create a TCM entity
embedded in the specified ODU.
The TCM mode determines whether the TCM facility operates as TCM NIM (Non-Intrusive
Monitor) or as TCM termination sink and source function. The TCM mode cannot be changed
during life-time of the TCM facility.
If the ODUNIM/ODUPTF facility identified via the odu-aid value is not provisioned, then the
command shall be denied.
If the ODUNIM/ODUPTF facility identified via the odu-aid value is in state NOIMP (Not
Implemented), then the command shall be denied.
If a not allowed combination for sequenceno, position is specified for the ODU type derived
from odu-aid (see parameter definition "sequenceno") then the command shall be denied.
If this command is issued to provision a BM TCM facility and another BM TCM is already
provisioned with the same TCM level as specified in the command, then the command shall be
denied.
If this command is issued to create a TCM facility and another TCM is already provisioned for
the specified sequenceno and position value combination, then the command shall be denied.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
If an additional TCM facility is created and the maximum number of 170000 LO-ODU/TCM
facilities per NE is then exceeded the command shall be rejected.
If the command is issued to provision an AM TCM facility below a substructured ODUPTF
located on plane and there exists already a BM TCM Termination with the same level below an
associated HO-ODUNIM (i.e. HO-ODUNIM and ODUPTF are CPs within one cross-

If the command is issued to provision an AM TCM facility with <facility-type> == otuoductcm,
then the command shall be denied.
If the command is issued to provision a BM TCM Termination below HO-ODUNIM and there
exists already an AM TCM facility with the same level below an associated substructured
ODUPTF located on plane (i.e. HO-ODU-NIM and ODUPTF are CPs within one cross-
connection), then the command shall be denied.
If the command is issued to provision a TCM facility below HO-ODUNIM for an OT card and the
associated port is configured to operate in regenerator mode, then the command shall be
denied.
<tcmmode>
Values
nim - Non-intrusive Monitor
ttp - Trail Termination with sink and source function
Default
Entry required
Determines the operation mode of the TCM facility.
<sequenceno>
Values
1..3 - sequence/position number
Default
Entry required
The sequence number indicates the position of the TCM monitor point within AM or BM context.
The lower the sequence number, the closer is the TCM monitor point located the client/matrix.
This means that the consequent action of the lower numbered sequence TCM termination
affects the higher numbered number TCM monitor point.
Notes:
• The sequence number is only unique in the context of one position value (i.e. AM or
BM).
• The sequence order is (starting from port) is: BM sequence number 1, BM sequence
number 2, BM sequence number 3, AM sequence number 1

7.12 config wanif
7.12.1 Purpose
This command is used to edit parameters related to a previously auto-created (auto-provisioned)
WAN instance.
WANIF instances are auto-created in the context of following command execution:
1. The interface type for a port is assigned to a value ''otu<k>waneth" (see command "config
interface").
2. An unstructured ODUPTF is manually created on IO card with distributed ETH switching (see
command "config oduptf").
Use this command to:
• Configure SyncE related parameter
• Set ASAP
• Set the state of the facility
• Set Synchronous Ethernet Operation Mode
• Set SSM/Quality Level Transmission
DSW card/shelf Behaviour:
This command applies to DSW (Distributed SWitch) cards and shelves. If a requirement is only
applicable for a sub-set of DSW card values then this will be explicitly specified.
DSW cards are 12CE120, 18CE300, 1UD200, 20P200, S13X100E, all S13X100 subtypes.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to CSW (Central oduk/packet SWitched) cards and shelves. If a requirement
is only applicable for a sub-set of CSW card values then this will be explicitly specified.
CSW cards are 30SE300 and 6SE300.

8490 Issue 1
7.14 config otsig
7.14.1 Purpose
This command configures an Optical Tributary Signal Group (OTSiG).
There are two essential elements to be defined for OTSiG:
• The client structure, which can be one of the following mutually exclusive types:
an OTU-based structure, which supports two classes of optical transport unit (OTU) - OTUk
and/or OTUCn
a GBE-based structure, which supports 100GBE client signals
• The OTN optical structure with single or multi optical transport unit interfaces (OTSi)
The corresponding parameters are named OTUSTRUCT, GBESTRUCT and OTSILIST,
respectively. Either OTUSTRUCT or GBESTRUCT, and OTSILIST must be given once OTSiG is
created and these two parameters can be modified on the existing OTSiG, unless otherwise noted.
As the inverse multiplexing function to populate all OTU to multiple OTSi shall be done on one
single device, OTSiG shall be identified on card level as a proprietary way.
If the OTSiG is using a FlexO layer as part of the line transmission function (i.e. for the assigned
profileid ClOTUType == FlexO is specified) then the OTSiG entity covers the management
functionality of the FlexO group as defined in ITU standards.
FlexO group management function means:
• a set of provisionable parameters for a FlexO group
• a set of retrievable state parameters for a FlexO group
• alarms reported for a FlexO group
A FlexO group does not provide any PM monitoring function.
Facility context for OTSiG:
• The OTU facility created by OTUSTRUCT is managed via non-card specific facility commands
"config/show otu".
• The GBE facility created by GBESTRUCT is managed via card specific interface command
"config interface <dsw-packetswitch card> <port-aid> ngige" or "config interface <card-name>
<port-aid> ngige".
• The related OTSi port attributes which shall be provisioned with different value under the same
OTSiG are managed via card specific interface command "config interface <csw-card> <port>
<otn> with <otn> == otsi" or "config interface <dsw-card> <port> otsi" or "config interface
s5ad400 <port> otsi" or "config interface s6ad600 <port> otsi" or "config interface 16p200 <port>
otsi".
• The related OTSi port attributes which shall have the same value are managed via non-card
specific command "config/show otsig".
Use this command to:
• Create an OTSiG
• Delete an OTSiG
• Modify/change the otustruct to re-size the OTSiG
OTH facility management commands
config otsig

Sub-command: create
Syntax
create {gbestruct | otustruct} <string> otsilist <value> [profileid <value>]
The create sub-command is used to create an OTSiG. The User must specify:
• The GBE (gbestruct) or OTU (otustruct) Payload structure for the OTSiG
• The OTSi interfaces (otsilist) to be a member for the OTSiG
In addition, the user can specify as option:
• The profile identifier (profileid) assigned to the OTSiG entity
See the parameter definitions for otustruct, gbestruct, otsilist and profileid for further details.
When the OTSiG is created, the user-defined OTSIGID shall be associated with the OTSi ports
addressed in the OTSiList.
Restrictions
If any interface addressed in the OTSiList parameter is unassigned, then the command is
rejected.
If any interface addressed in the OTSiList is OTSi with OtsigId != none, then the command
is rejected.
If for a port addressed in the OTSiList parameter the moduletype == auto/user is configured
and the port is located on a card unequal to 8UC1T, then the create sub-command is
rejected.
GBESTRUCT Modification
When the OTSiG is created, the embedded GBEs are created based on the gbestruct
information and each GBE has a valid OTSIGID associated.
Restrictions
If any GBE-id addressed in the GBESTRUCT parameter has been already used in other
OTSiG on the same card, then the command is rejected.
OTUSTRUCT Modification
When the OTSiG is created, the embedded OTUs are created based on the otustruct
information and each OTU has a valid OTSIGID associated.

The value <X> is derived from OTU rate as follows:
• <X> = 1 for OTU4 rate
• <X> = n for OTUCn rate
Note:
• The channel resource handling is described in detail in purpose sub-section of command
show oduchannelpool.
delete
Values
delete
Sub-command to delete the addressed OTSiG.
When the OTSiG is deleted, the OTUs addressed in the otustruct shall be automatically
deleted.
When the OTSiG is deleted, the GBEs addressed in the gbestruct shall be automatically
deleted.
When the OTSiG is deleted, the wavekey value parameter under OTSi shall be automatically
reset to zero.
Restrictions
If any OTU addressed in the otustruct is in SDEE state then the command is rejected.
If any GBE addressed in the gbestruct is in SDEE state then the command is rejected.
If a loopback for the OTSiG is provisioned, then the command is rejected.
If any OTSi port has channel rx or tx value which is unequal to none then the command is
rejected.
When the OTSiG is deleted, the power parameter value for an OTSi shall be modified if
needed.
Further details are described as part of input parameter power specification in command:
• config interface <card> <port-aid> <otn> for CSW cards
• config interface <card> <port-aid> otsi for none-CSW cards

Sub-command: loopback
Syntax
loopback [facility | terminal]
Configures the loopback for all OTSi port in one OTSiG.
If the MT state is not present for each OTSi port in one OTSiG, then any loopback command is
rejected.
If it is requested to enable a loopback for one type (e.g. facility) and there is already a loopback
enabled for another type (e.g. terminal), then the enabling of additional loopback request shall
be rejected.
If the OPRMODE of OTSiG is in regen, then the enabling of a loopback request shall be
rejected.
Restrictions
For S6AD600 subtypes, if facility loopback is enabled, the DXC creation or deletion is not
allowed.
Facility loopbacks are not supported on the OTSI port of the 18CE300.
Sub-command: modify
Syntax
modify otustruct <string> [profileid <value>]
The modify command allows the ability to change the transmission capacity of an OTSiG. The
User must specify:
• The parameter otustruct with a new value
• (optionally) a new profile due to the rate change. If the parameter is omitted, then the
currently assigned profileid for the OTSiG is kept as is.
See the parameter definition for otustruct and profileid for further details.
After OTSIG modification is performed, the existing client traffic would have a traffic hit and PM
counters should be manually cleared to get rid of abnormal data due to traffic hit.
OTUSTRUCT Modification
See otustruct and profileid for additional restrictions.

Sub-command: otustruct
Syntax
otustruct <string>
Values
The string must match the pattern [[T#ID][&T#ID]*] with the following values:
"T" - rate of the embedded OTU framer type
"ID" - OTU Index to identify the OTU facility
"T" values for OTU rates are:
OTU4
OTUC1
OTUC2
OTUC3
OTUC4
OTUC5
OTUTC1
OTUTC4
Default
Entry required
Specifies the OTU payload structure for the OTSiG.
The assigned OTSi Payload Rate from the profileID must match the payload rate as derived
from the otustruct value.
As the total capacity can be derived from the otustruct of each OTSiG, it shall not cross the max
capacity which the card can support.
And each OTSi payload rate can also be calculated from OTSiG capacity divided by OTSi port
numbers, each OTSi payload rate shall not cross the max rate which the OTSi port can support.
As the sequence for each OTUs specified in otustruct determines their multiplex order in
OTSiG, the same sequence number should be given on both ends for the same client service.
It must be guaranteed by user as there is no overhead on OTSiG level to transport this
information.
Note:
• The conclusion is, that the otustruct string value must be the same on both ends if ID
part within the string is not considered.
If GCC is enabled for the first OTU for the current OTUSTRUCT value and this OTU is not
anymore the first OTU in the new OTUSTRUCT value, then the command shall be denied.
For changing a payload structure, the NE checks which OTUs are affected. If for one of the
affected OTUs the SDEE state is present, then changing the parameter will be denied.

Values

"ID" - port number
Default
Entry required
Specifies the OTSi interfaces to be a member for OTSiG.
It can be either one or multiple interfaces located in the same slot where OTSiG is created.
As the shelf/slot of the interface are the same as shelf/slot defined in <otsig-aid>, only the port
index is required here.
If the port numbers used in an otsilist parameter value are not specified in ascending order,
then the command shall be denied.
The following general rule is valid for 1UX500 subtypes w.r.t. otsilist configuration:
• port 1 can be used as member for a single carrier OTSiG.
The following port rules are valid for 1UX500 subtypes w.r.t. otsi payload configuration derived
from otustruct value:
• port 1 supports 200G, 300G, 400G or 500G OTSi capacity.
The following general port rules are valid for 2UX500 card w.r.t. otsilist configuration:
• Each port can be used as member for a single carrier OTSiG.
• The port set [1,2] can be used as members for a dual carrier OTSiG.
The following port rules are valid for 2UX500 card w.r.t. otsi payload configuration derived from
otustruct value:
• Each port supports 100G, 200G, 300G or 400G OTSi capacity.
• Port 1 and 2 can support together 500G as maximal capacity. This maximal capacity can
be arbitrarily distributed over the two ports (e.g. first port is configured with 200G
capacity and second port is configured with 300G capacity).
• In case of a dual carrier OTSiG each member port supports 200G capacity.
If it is requested to create an OTSiG with more than one port (i.e. otsilist contains more than
one element) and for the assigned profileid ClOTUType == FlexO is specified, then the
command is rejected.
Note:
• Only single carrier OTSiG with FlexO are supported in the current release.

denied.

demo profiles, this provisioning will be denied.

7.16 config prbstest
7.16.1 Purpose
This command configures a PRBS (Pseudo Random Binary Sequence) test signal which is applied
for an ODUk signal. Applying a PRBS signal for an ODUk means w.r.t. transmission:
1. The ODUk path layer is terminated.
2. A PRBS test signal is inserted as new client into the OPUk.
3. An ODUk-AIS maintenance signal is inserted into the downstream direction after the PRBS test
signal is de-mapped from the ODUk
Note: Applying a test signal is an intrusive action, for example the current provisioned traffic is
replaced by the PRBS test signal.
Use this command to:
• enable/disable the PRBS test signal.
• configure the position of the test signal.
• configure the test pattern.
• reset the PRBS analyzer.
• insert a single BIP8 error.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
The PRBS test signal is only supported for LO-ODUNIM facilities for CSW shelves.
For CSW shelves, this command applies only for PSS-8x and PSS-12x shelf types.
DSW and PSS-32 card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to the following cards:
16P200
OT card/shelf Behavior:
The PRBS test signal is only supported for HO-ODUNIM facilities for the D6AD2T4 subtype cards.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for PSS shelf/circuit pack applicability.
7.16.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
7.16.3 Input Format
config prbstest <facility-type> <facility-aid>
resetanalyzerposition
detail
insertbip8error
OTH facility management commands

7.17 config profile otsig
7.17.1 Purpose
This command is used to create either of the following:
(1) A User-defined Custom profile with a specific baudrate value. There are two essential elements
to be defined for the Custom profile:
• A reference system profile (REFSYSPROFILE) that is used as the starting point for the Custom
profile.
• A baudrate value (BAUDRATE) selected from a list of baudrate values supported by the
reference system profile.
The corresponding parameters named as REFSYSPROFILE and BAUDRATE must be given once
the Custom profile is created.
(2) A User-defined Demo profile, which allows each parameter in the profile to be optionally
provisioned. The essential elements to be defined for the Demo profile:
• The profileID from the OTSIG list of profiles that will be used as the starting point for the demo
profile (parameter name COPYFROMPROFILE)
• The list of optional parameters from the profileID that can be configured for the Demo profile via
User provisioning (BAUDRATE, ClOTUTYPE, PAYLOADRATE, PHASENC, TXSHAPE,
ADDITIONALCONFIG)
Use this command to:
• Create a Custom/demo profile.
• Delete a Custom/demo profile.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack applicability.
7.17.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

7.18 show otu
7.18.1 Purpose
This command displays the facility parameter values for an OTU facility.
Use this command to:
• Display the FEC used.
• Display the interworking mode.
• Display the serverport assocations.
• Display the performance monitoring attributes.
• Display the dDEG detection configuration.
• Display the OTU trail trace attributes.
• Display the facility state.
• Display the otu rate.
• Display the ASAP.
All TTI string values in the show output are converted from an octet string value to an ASCII string
value according to the following rules:
1. The header byte for SAPI (first OH byte of SAPI TTI as transported with OTN overhead) and the
header byte for DAPI (first OH byte of DAPI TTI as transported with OTN overhead) is removed.
2. Trailing NULL characters will be removed (i.e. not shown in the replied string value).
3. Non-trailing NULL characters will be replaced by "." in the replied string value.
4. Any octet value between 1 hex and 1f hex will be replaced by "?" in the replied string value.
5. Any octet value between 20 hex to 7e hex will be replaced by the corresponding ASCII
character in the replied string value.
6. Any octet value between 7f hex to ff hex will be replaced "?" in the replied string value.
Note:
• SAPI/DAPI TTI strings at the CLI interface have 15 characters as maximal size. Therefore, the
TTI header byte is not included in the TTI string value.
OT card Behavior:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OT cards are 11DPM12, 11DPM8, 11DPM4M, 11QPA4B, 4QPA8, 112SDX11, 12P120, 12P120S,
260SCX2, all D6AD2T4 subtypes, all S2AD200 subtypes, all S5AD400 subtypes and all S6AD600
subtypes.
DSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to DSW (Distributed SWitch) cards. If a requirement is only applicable for a
sub-set of DSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.

7.19 show otu <otu-aid> pm
7.19.1 Purpose
This command displays the Performance Monitoring attributes on an OTU facility.
Use this command to:
• Display the OTU PM options
Refer to PM Montypes tables in the Appendix A, “Reference tables” for applicable Montypes for the
OTU PM group.
OT card Behavior:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OT cards are 11DPM12, 11DPM8, 11DPM4M, 11QPA4B, 4QPA8, 112SDX11,12P120,12P120S,
260SCX2, all D6AD2T4 subtypes, all S2AD200 subtypes, all S5AD400 subtypes and all S6AD600
subtypes.
DSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to DSW (Distributed SWitch) cards. If a requirement is only applicable for a
sub-set of DSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.
DSW cards are 11QPA4B, 12CE120, 16P200, 18CE300, 1UD200, 20P200, all 8P20 subtypes,
D5X500, D5X500L, D5X500Q, S13X100E, all S13X100 subtypes, all S13X400 subtypes and all
S4X400 subtypes.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to CSW (Central odu/packet SWitched) cards. If a requirement is only
applicable for a sub-set of CSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.
CSW cards are 1UX100, all 1UX500 subtypes, 2UX200, 2UX500, 20AX200, 20MX80, 4MX200,
5MX500, 20AN80, 20UC200, all 2UC400 subtypes, 10AN1T, 10AN400, 30AN300, 4AN400,
4UC400, all 2UC1T subtypes, 2UC1TH, 4UC1T and 8UC1T.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack applicability.
7.19.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
7.19.3 Input Format
show otu <otu-aid> pm
otupm
OTH facility management commands
show otu <otu-aid> pm
