3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
7.20 show odunim
7.20.1 Purpose
This command is used to display parameters related to the non-terminated ODUk path (ODUNIM)
facility that was previously auto-created (auto-provisioned).
The following sub-types can be distinguished for the ODUNIM facility:
1. HO-ODU: The ODUk facility is mapped in OTUk.
2. LO-ODU: The ODUk facility is mapped in substructured ODUPTF.
Use this command to:
• Display the Performance Monitoring attributes
• Display the ODU Trail Trace Identifier attributes
• Display the Path Overhead Monitoring
• Display the ODUk attributes of ODU
All TTI string values in the show output are converted from an octet string value to an ASCII string
value according to the following rules:
1. The header byte for SAPI (first OH byte of SAPI TTI as transported with OTN overhead) and the
header byte for DAPI (first OH byte of DAPI TTI as transported with OTN overhead) is removed.
2. Trailing NULL characters will be removed (i.e. not shown in the replied string value).
3. Non-trailing NULL characters will be replaced by "." in the replied string value.
4. Any octet value between 1 hex and 1f hex will be replaced by "?" in the replied string value.
5. Any octet value between 20 hex to 7e hex will be replaced by the corresponding ASCII
character in the replied string value.
6. Any octet value between 7f hex to ff hex will be replaced "?" in the replied string value.
Note:
• SAPI/DAPI TTI strings at the CLI interface have 15 characters as maximal size. Therefore, the
TTI header byte is not included in the TTI string value.
OT card Behavior:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OT cards are 11DPM12, 11DPM8, 11DPM4M, 11QPA4B, 4QPA8, 112SDX11, 12P120, 12P120S,
260SCX2, all D6AD2T4 subtypes, all S2AD200 subtypes, all S5AD400 subtypes and all S6AD600
subtypes.
DSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to DSW (Distributed SWitch) cards unless further restriction is clarified for
individual sub-command or parameter within this command.
DSW cards are 12CE120, 16P200, 1UD200, 20P200, all 8P20 subtypes, D5X500, D5X500L,
D5X500Q, S13X100E, all S13X100 subtypes, all S13X400 subtypes and all S4X400 subtypes.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:

“Reference tables”.
Restrictions
If a wildcard value (i.e. a value containing one '*' character) is specified, then all other input
parameters must be omitted.
If a wildcard value (i.e. a value containing one *' character) is specified as input, then a list of
facilities is replied in the output.
For each replied facility the following information is displayed in the output:
1. <facility-type>
2. <odu-aid>
3. direction - value Sink (only ingress NIM is supported) and value Bi (ngress and egress
NIM is supported)
4. flextype - only if ODUk rate == ODUflex
5. flexsize - only if flextype == GFP
6. flexclient - only if flextype == CBR

Displays the name of the ASAP (Alarm Severity Assignment Profile) used for alarm reporting.

7.21 show odunim <facility-type> <odu-aid> pm
7.21.1 Purpose
This command displays the performance monitoring attributes for an ODUNIM facility.
Use this command to:
• display the ODURX group PM options
Refer to PM Montypes tables in the Appendix A, “Reference tables” for applicable Montypes for the
ODU PM groups.
OT card Behavior:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OT cards are 11DPM12, 11DPM8, 11DPM4M, 11QPA4B, 4QPA8, 112SDX11, 12P120, 12P120S,
260SCX2, all D6AD2T4 subtypes, all S2AD200 subtypes, all S5AD400 and all S6AD600 subtypes.
DSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to DSW (Distributed SWitch) cards unless further restriction is clarified for
individual sub-command or parameter within this command.
DSW cards are 12CE120, 16P200, 1UD200, 20P200, all 8P20 subtypes, D5X500, D5X500L,
D5X500Q, S13X100E, all S13X100 subtypes, all S13X400 subtypes, and all S4X400 subtypes.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to CSW (Central odu SWitched) cards. If a requirement is only applicable for
a sub-set of CSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.
CSW cards are 10AN1T, 1UX100, all 1UX500 subtypes, 2UX200, 20AX200, 20MX80, 4MX200,
20AN80, 20UC200, all 2UC400 subtypes, 2UX500, 10AN400, 30AN300, 4AN400, 4UC400, all
2UC1T subtypes, 2UC1TH, 4UC1T, 5MX500 and 8UC1T.
The shelves supporting central ODUk switching are called CSW shelf. This generic term is used for
the following shelf types:
• PSS-24x
• PSS-12x
• PSS-8x
The shelves supporting distributed ODUk switching are called DSW shelf. This generic term is used
for the following shelf types:
• PSS-4II
• PSS-8
• PSS-16II
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack applicability.
OTH facility management commands
show odunim <facility-type> <odu-aid> pm

8602 Issue 1
7.22 show oduptf
7.22.1 Purpose
This command is used to display parameters related to a previously created ODUPTF instance. An
ODUPTF instance represents the management view of OTN path termination functions.
Three different sub-types of ODU termination can be distinguished based on the client signal
carried in the payload of the terminated ODU (ODUPTF):
• Substructured ODUPTF
• unstructured ODUPTF
• ODU1PTF
Substructured ODUPTF: The HO-ODU payload carries a set of ODUs as clients (that is, LO-
ODUs).
Unstructured ODUPTF: The ODU payload carries one non-OTN client signal (e.g. GBEn, OCn/
STMn) transparently mapped into the ODU payload.
ODU1PTF: For 11DPM12 card, logical ODU1PTFs are automatically created when the card is
assigned.
Use this command to:
• Display the payload type
• Display the Payload Type Mismatch response
• Display the timing granularity (260SCX2 and 1UD200 only)
• Display the Performance Monitoring attributes
• Display the ODU Trail Trace Identifier attributes
• Display the LO-ODU structure
• Display the OPTSG structure of an ODUPTF
All TTI string values in the show output are converted from an octet string value to an ASCII string
value according to the following rules:
1. The header byte for SAPI (first OH byte of SAPI TTI as transported with OTN overhead) and the
header byte for DAPI (first OH byte of DAPI TTI as transported with OTN overhead) is removed.
2. Trailing NULL characters will be removed (i.e. not shown in the replied string value).
3. Non-trailing NULL characters will be replaced by "." in the replied string value.
4. Any octet value between 1 hex and 1f hex will be replaced by "?" in the replied string value.
5. Any octet value between 20 hex to 7e hex will be replaced by the corresponding ASCII
character in the replied string value.
6. Any octet value between 7f hex to ff hex will be replaced "?" in the replied string value.
Note:
• SAPI/DAPI TTI strings at the CLI interface have 15 characters as maximal size. Therefore, the
TTI header byte is not included in the TTI string value.

applicable for a sub-set of CSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.
CSW cards are 10AN400, 20AN80, 20AX200, 20MX80, 4MX200, 5MX500, 10AN1T, 10AN400,
20UC200, 30AN300, 30SE300, 4AN400 and 6SE300.
The shelves supporting central ODUk switching are called CSW shelf. This generic term is used for
the following shelf types:
• PSS-24x
• PSS-12x
• PSS-8x
The shelves supporting distributed ODUk switching are called DSW shelf. This generic term is used
for the following shelf types:
• PSS-4II
• PSS-8
• PSS-16II
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack applicability.

All S2AD200 subtype cards - unstructured ODUPTF syntax for client ports:
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..2}
All S4X400 subtype cards - unstructured ODUPTF syntax for client ports:
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..4}
All S5AD400 subtype cards - unstructured ODUPTF syntax for client ports:
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..5}
All S6AD600 subtype cards - unstructured ODUPTF syntax for client ports:
<shelf>/<slot>/C{1..6}
Default
Entry required
Specifies the AID to identify/address the ODUPTF facility.
The value ranges for <shelf>, <slot>, <plane-slot> and <ho-odu-id> are defined in Appendix A,
“Reference tables”.
Restrictions
If a wildcard value (i.e. a value containing one '*' character), then all other input parameters
must be omitted.
If a wildcard value (i.e. a value containing one '*' character) is specified as input, then a list of
facilities is replied in the output.
For each replied facility the following information is displayed in the output:
1. <facility-type>
2. <odu-aid>
3. flextype - only if ODUk rate == ODUflex
4. flexsize - only if flextype == GFP
5. flexclient - only if flextype == CBR

oduchannelpool
Displays information for associated oduchannelpool entities as follows:
1. PoolList: List of oduchannelpool AID values as follows:
• value none if ODUPTF is not cross-connected.
• value none if ODUPTF is cross-connected to ODUNIMs not associated with an
oduchannelpool entity.
• One oduchannelpool AID value if ODUPTF is cross-connected to one ODUNIMs
associated with an oduchannelpool entity.
• Two oduchannelpool AID values if ODUPTF is cross-connected to two ODUNIMs
associated with an oduchannelpool entity.
In this case the two values are separated by '&'.
2. MaxTribNumber: specifies the maximal number of LO-ODU tributaries which can be
supported by the ODUPTF and is calculated as follows:
• If ODUPTF is not cross-connected, then value reflects the maximal number based on
HO-ODUk rate (ODU2: 8, ODU3;32, ODU4: 80, ODUCn: 10*n). This is also the factory/
creation default.
• If PoolList == none, then the value is calculated in the same way as for the case is not
cross-connected.
• If PoolList != none, then the value is calculated based on:
- the actual number of LO-ODU tributaries
- the maximal value of free channels available from all pool entities contained inPoolList
- the maximal number of LO-ODU tributaries based on HO-ODUk rate
• 3. ActualTribNumber: specifies the number of provisioned LO-ODUs and is derived from
odustruct value.
Note:
• The channel resource handling is described in detail in purpose sub-section of command
show oduchannelpool.
Restrictions
This parameter is only applicable for substructured ODUPTF located on CSW shelf plane.

odustruct
Displays the ODU payload structure of the ODUPTF entity (that is, the embedded ODUn
tributaries). The string has the format [T#PN-ts[,ts]*[&T#PN-ts[,ts]*]*], where:
• "T" - rate of the embedded ODUn tributary
• "PN" - tributary Port Number of the embedded ODUn tributary
• "ts" - tributary time slot number
Note:
• The values allowed for T, PN and ts are specified in command "config oduptf" as part of
input parameter definition for odustruct.
The displayed list value is ordered as follows:
• As first element the tributary time slots numbers with T=uas is shown.
• The other elements are shown in ascending order based on the lowest ts value allocated
for the tributary.
Restrictions
The parameter only applies to:
• substructured ODUPTF located on plane (in case of ODU switching)
• substructured ODUPTF located on line port (for OTs)

7.23 show oduptf <facility-type> <oduptf-aid> pm
7.23.1 Purpose
This command displays the Performance monitoring attributes on an ODUPTF facility.
Use this command to
• Display the ODURX group PM options.
Refer to PM Montypes tables in the Appendix A, “Reference tables” for applicable Montypes for the
ODU PM group.
OT card Behavior:
This command applies to OT cards. If a requirement is only applicable for a sub-set of OT card
values then this will be explicitly specified.
OT cards are 11DPM12, 11DPM8, 11DPM4M, 11QPA4B, 4QPA8, 112SDX11, 12P120, 12P120S,
260SCX2, all D6AD2T4 subtypes, all S2AD200 subtypes, all S5AD400 subtypes and all S6AD600
subtypes.
The DSW cards also include the S13X400 subtypes and 18CE300.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to CSW (Central odu SWitched) cards. If a requirement is only applicable for
a sub-set of CSW card values then, this will be explicitly specified.
CSW cards are 10AN1T, 10AN400, 20AX200, 20AN80, 20MX80, 20UC200, 30AN300, 30SE300,
4AN400, 4MX200, 5MX500 and 6SE300.
The shelves supporting central ODUk switching are called CSW shelf. This generic term is used for
the following shelf types:
• PSS-24x
• PSS-12x
• PSS-8x
The shelves supporting distributed ODUk switching are called DSW shelf. This generic term is used
for the following shelf types:
• PSS-4II
• PSS-8
• PSS-16II
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack applicability.
7.23.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer

7.24 show tcm
7.24.1 Purpose
The show tcm is used to display parameters related to the TCM entity that has been previously
created.
Use this command to:
• Display the TCM mode
• Display the ODUk trail trace identifier attributes
• Display the LTC (loss of TCM connection) response
• Display the consequent action to be taken upon TCM defects - AISONDEF
• Display whether the provisioned TCM Overhead need to be inserted at TCM source - OHADD
• Display whether the received TCM Overhead need to be discarded at TCM sink - OHRMV
• Display the admin state for the TCM
• Display the PM attributes
Use this command to:
• Display the TCM mode
• Display the ODUk trail trace identifier attributes
• Display the LTC (loss of TCM connection) response
• Display the consequent action to be taken upon TCM defects - AISONDEF
• Display whether the provisioned TCM Overhead need to be inserted at TCM source - OHADD
• Display whether the received TCM Overhead need to be discarded at TCM sink - OHRMV
• Display the admin state for the TCM
• Display the TCM delay measurement parameter
• Display the PM attributes
OT Card Behaviour:
This command applies to OT cards unless further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command
or parameter within this command.
OT cards are 11QPA4 and 260SCX2.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to CSW (Central odu/packet SWitched) cards. If a requirement is only
applicable for a sub-set of CSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.
CSW cards are 1UX100, all 1UX500 subtypes, 2UX200, 2UX500, 20AX200, 20MX80, 4MX200,
5MX500, 20AN80, 20UC200, all 2UC400 subtypes, 10AN1T, 10AN400, 30AN300, 30SE300,
4AN400, 4UC400, all 2UC1T subtypes, 2UC1TH, 4UC1T, 6SE300 and 8UC1T.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack applicability.

The reported parameter value is a string value of the pattern [FlexONo-ID][&[FlexONo-ID]]* with
the following values:
"FlexONo" - instance number of the FlexO frame within the FlexO group
"ID" - GID (Group Identification) for a FlexO frame instance within FlexO group
If no accepted GID value for a FlexO frame instance is available (e.g. SF condition is present
for FlexO frame), then the term '[FlexONo-ID]' is omitted for this FlexO instance.
If no accepted GID value for all FlexO frame instances is available (e.g. IO card is not
available), then an empty string value is reported.
The displayed parameter value is sorted in ascending order w.r.t. FlexONo.
Restrictions
This parameter applies only for an OTSiG FlexO layer (i.e. for the assigned profileid
ClOTUType == FlexO is specified).

Displays the accepted/incoming IID (Interface Identification) for the FlexO group per FlexO
frame instance as part of the OTSiG.

the following values:
"FlexONo" - instance number of the FlexO frame within the FlexO group

This command is used to display the parameters and test results for a PRBS (Pseudo Random
Binary Sequence) test signal which is applied for an ODUk signal.
Use this command to:
• Display the provisionable attributes of the test signal

The PRBS test signal is only supported for LO-ODUNIM facilities for CSW shelves.
This command applies only for PSS-8x and PSS-12x shelf types.

This command applies to the following DSW (Distributed Switched) cards:
16P200

8678 Issue 1
7.29 show oduchannelpool
7.29.1 Purpose
This command shows the ODUk channel usage within one pool.
An ODUk channel is defined as one ODUk which can be monitored and transported via the
backplane interface of a CSW card. The following cases can be distinguished for CSW cards:
• A CSW card has no ODUk channel restriction; i.e. facility/cross-connect provisioning command
is never denied due missing ODUk channel resources. In this case no oduchannelpool entity will
be shown since no dedicated resource handling is needed.
• A CSW card has ODUk channel restrictions. Then a set of oduchannelpool entities will be
created if such an IO card is provisioned. The oduchannelpool models then the resource
handling/book-keeping for ODUk channels.
ODUk channel resources are needed for the following use cases (for cards with channel
restrictions):
1. OTU facility creation:
• 10 channel resources are needed for OTU4 rate. These channel resources are reserved for HO-
ODUNIM or LO-ODUNIMs associated with OTU (i.e. cannot be used by any other facility
associated with the pool; e.g. an LO-ODUNIM associated with another OTU facility).
For an un-terminated HO-ODUNIM (i.e. the HO-ODUNIM is not cross-connected to a
substructured ODUPTF) one channel resource is allocated.
For a terminated HO-ODUNIM (i.e. the HO-ODUNIM is cross-connected to a substructured
ODUPTF) channel resources are only needed for associated LO-ODUNIMs (i.e. no channel
resource is needed for HO-ODUNIM or associated substructured ODUPTF).
• This ensures, that a user can always configure up to 10 LO-ODUs (e.g. 10 time LO-ODU2)
without needing additional channel.
• Note: OTUk interfaces with k<4 are only supported on CSW cards without channel restrictions
and therefore are not considered for this use case.
2. ODUPTF facility creation as part of GBEn interface assignment:
• 1 channel resource is needed for the unstructured ODUPTF.
3. LO-ODU structure provisioning (odustruct attribute of ODUPTF facility) in transmission HW:
• For each LO-ODUk defined within payload structure 1 channel is needed (only if ODUPTF is not
in NOIMP state).
• ODUk channels are first allocated from the reserved channels of the associated OTU. If no
reserved channel is free any more then shared channel resources of the pool are allocated.
Notes:
• Cross-connection provisioning may also cause implicitly LO-ODU structure provisioning in
transmission HW (e.g. XC creation to manually created oduptf (NoImp state) on virtual plane).
• The show oduptf command reports additional parameters w.r.t. associated oduchannelpool,
actual and maximal number of LO-ODUk based on current ODUk channel usage.
An oduchannelpool entity consists of the following attributes:
1. AID:
OTH facility management commands
show oduchannelpool
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 8679
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
• See input parameter definition <pool-aid>.
2. PortList:
• Ordered list of port numbers associated with the pool.
• A port is present in the list if the port cannot be provisioned as member of an OTSiG (e.g. all
ports of a 10AN1T are members of PortList of an oduchannelpool).
3. OTUIdList:
• Ordered list of otu-ids associated with the pool.
• An otu-id is present in the list if otu-id can be used as ID within the OTU structure of an OTSiG
(e.g. all otu-ids of an 8UC1T are members of OTUIdList of an oduchannelpool).
4. NumberOfChan
• Defines the overall number of available channels for a pool.
• For current IO cards each pool supports a fixed value of 190 channels.
3. NumberOfOTUReservedChan
• Defines the number of reserved channels per OTU4.
• The value is fixed to 10.
4. OTUReservedChanList
• List of provisioned OTU facilities together the reserved channel information.
Each entry in the list consists of:
- <otuid>: last component of OTU AID (<shelf>/<slot> are common for OTU facility and
ODUChannelPool entity).
- NumberOfResChan: number of channels reserved for the OTU.
- NumberOfAllocChan: number of channels which are allocated for ODUs associated with the
OTU.
5. NumberOfSharedChan
• The number of allocated channels as shared resource; i.e. the channels reserved for one OTU
facility are not counted as shared resources.
6. NumberofFreeChan
• The number of channels free for shared allocation.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack applicability.
Use this command to:
• Display the attributes of an oduchannelpool entity.
CSW card/shelf Behavior:
This command applies to CSW (Central odu/packet SWitched) cards. If a requirement is only
applicable for a sub-set of CSW card values, then this will be explicitly specified.
CSW cards using oduchhannelpool entities are: all 1UX500 subtypes, 2UX500, all 2UC1T
subtypes, 2UC1TH, 4UC1T, 8UC1T, 5MX500 and 10AN1T.

7.30 show profile otsig
7.30.1 Purpose
This command is used to display information related to a Profile Identifier (profileid).
Use this command to display the OTSiG Profile attributes:
• description
• OTSi Payload Rate
• A set of OTSi Profile Transmission Parameters
A set of system profiles are auto-created by the NE - see Appendix A, “Reference tables” OTSiG
System Profiles.
7.30.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
7.30.3 Input Format
show profile otsig <profileid>
brief [{description | paramlist} [<category>] [<cardtype>]]
detail
description
otsipayloadrate
otsiparameter
7.30.4 Input Parameters
<profileid>
Values
1..999 - system profiles
1000..2999 - custom profiles
3000..3999 - demo profiles
* - display all existing profiles of the NE, based on the <category> filter
Default
Entry required
The supported system profiles are described in Appendix A, “Reference tables”: OTSiG System
Profiles.
Restrictions
The value * is only allowed in combination with brief.

otsiparameter
Displays the set of transmission parameters for a profile. The set of parameters include:

• OTSi additionalconfig

8700 Issue 1
8.2 alm
8.2.1 Purpose
This command displays a list of all the active alarms on the network element.
8.2.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
8.2.3 Input Format
alm
<shelf-aid>
<slot-aid>
packetswitch
8.2.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
{1..64} - shelf number range
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf for which the alarms are filtered and reported.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric values of <shelf-aid> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
<slot-aid>
Values
<shelf>/<slot> - specific slot in one shelf.
Default
Entry required
Specifies the slot for which the alarms are filtered and reported.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf> and <slot> ranges for each
supported shelf type.
packetswitch
Syntax
packetswitch <packetswitch-id>
Alarm management commands
alm
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 8701
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Values
1..100
Default
Entry required
Specifies a packet switch identifier will be used for the address to filter.
8.2.5 Output Parameters
The following table describes the fields used on the alm output report:
Table 8-1 Fields reported in alm output
Field Description
<NTFCNCDE> Notification Code, identifies the type of alarm generated by the system upon occurrence of
the event identified by the CONDTYPE.
CR Critical alarm
MJ Major alarm
MN Minor alarm
WR Warning alarm
NR Not Reported
NA Not Alarm
<SRVEFF> Service Effect, identifies the effect on service caused by the event.
NSA Nonservice-affecting
SA Service-affecting
<YY-MM-DD> Date
<HH:MM:SS> Time
<AIDTYPE> The general type of entity reporting the alarm.
<CONDTYPE> Condition Type, specifies the reported condition type.
[<RATE>] Signal Rate
<AID> Address of the alarm.
[<DIRN>] Specifies the direction of the alarm if needed.
BTH Both directions
NA Not applicable
In Receive direction only
Out Transmit direction only
<CONDDESCR> Condition Description, a text description of the condition being reported.
<ENTITYTYPE> Type of entity reporting the alarm. Typically the card-name or facility-type.
[<ExtraData>] Optional data that may be defined on a per alarm basis.

8.3 config aco
8.3.1 Purpose
This command operates the NE audible alarm cut-off function (ACO).
Use this command to operate the audible alarm cut-off function (ACO).
This command applies to all shelves.
8.3.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Toggles audible alarms on the NE
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
8.3.3 Input Format
config aco
audibleoff
8.3.4 Input Parameters
audibleoff
This command will release audible alarm contacts if active (silence the alarm bells, lights,
horns, and so on) without dismissing the alarm. If previously silenced alarms are still active
reissuing this command will reactivate audible alarm contacts. This command toggles the
audible alarm relays in the Network Element.
8.3.5 Examples
# config aco audibleoff
8.3.6 Related Commands
show alarmleds
Alarm management commands

8.4 config alm attr
8.4.1 Purpose
This command configures the alarm severity for a unique entity.
This command allows you to:
• Change the alarm severity
• Reset the alarm severity to the system default
8.4.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Settings affect the behavior of the alarm panel
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
8.4.3 Input Format
config alm attr
<facility-type>
interface
l2data
shelf
slot
8.4.4 Input Parameters
Sub-command: <facility-type>
For additional details, see "config alm attr <facility-type>" command.
Sub-command: interface
For additional details, see "config alm attr interface" command.
Sub-command: l2data
For additional details, see "config alm attr l2data" command.
Sub-command: shelf
For additional details, see "config alm attr shelf" command.
Sub-command: slot
For additional details, see "config alm attr slot" command.
8.4.5 Related Commands

8.5 config alm attr <facility-type>
8.5.1 Purpose
This command configures the alarm severity for a unique entity.
This command allows you to:
• Change the alarm severity
• Reset the alarm severity to the system default
8.5.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Settings affect the behavior of the alarm panel
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
8.5.3 Input Format
config alm attr <facility-type>
<address>
<entity>
<condtype>
<ntfcncde>
8.5.4 Input Parameters
<facility-type>
Values
{otu} - OTU
{otuodu4, otuodu2, otuodu2e, otuodu1f, otuodu1, otuoduc} - HO-ODU (non-terminated)
{otuodu4tcm, otuodu2tcm} - HO-ODU (non-terminated)
{odu4, odu2, odu2e, odu3, odu1f, odu1, odu0, oduflex, oduc} - HO-ODU (terminated)
{odu4odu0, odu4odu1, odu4odu2, odu4odu2e, odu4odu3, odu4oduflex, odu2odu0,
odu2odu1, odu2oduflex, odu1odu0, oducoduflex, oducodu4} - LO-ODU (non-terminated)
{odu1ptf, optsg} - {ODUPTF | OPTSG}
wanif - WANIF
otsig - OTSIG
The <facility-type> field values will change based on the entered entity.

<entity>
Values
{odu0, odu1, odu1f, odu2, odu2e, odu3, odu4, oduc, optsg, otu1, otu1f, otu2, otu2e, otu3,

Specifies the alarm entity that you want to configure. Also referred to as the second modifier.
<condtype>
Specifies the alarm condition type that you want to configure. Enter a * to display all available
conditions of the addressed entity. This list may include conditions that do not apply the current
shelf/card configuration.
<ntfcncde>
Values
{critical, default, major, minor, warning, notalarmed, notreported}
Specifies the alarm severity level to assign to the entity and condition type.

8.7 config alm attr l2data
8.7.1 Purpose
This command configures the alarm severity for a unique Layer 2 data (packet) entity.
This command allows you to:
• Change the alarm severity
• Reset the alarm severity to the system default
8.7.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Settings affect the behavior of the alarm panel
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
8.7.3 Input Format
config alm attr l2data [packetswitch] <address-aid> <entity>
<condtype>
<ntfcncde>
8.7.4 Input Parameters
packetswitch
Specifies that the entity belongs to a packetswitch. In the case of a packetswitch, only a subset
of the entities is part of the packetswitch, and the remainder belong to the <shelf>/<slot>, as
described in the <address-aid>.

8.12 config transferlog server
8.12.1 Purpose
This command sets the attributes for the transfer log server.
Use this command to set:
• IP address and root directory of the log server
• Protocol and TCP port used to access the log server
• User identifier and password used to log in to the log server

Impact: Specifies the location for log server
Access Levels: Administrator
8.12.3 Input Format
config transferlog server
hostkey
ip
port
protocol
sshprivkey

8.12.4 Input Parameters
hostkey
Syntax
hostkey <keyindex> <keystring>
Values
For <keyindex>:
{1,2} - index of the public host key
Default
Entry required
Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 characters containing the SSH key string in OpenSSH format.
"" - to clear the string.
Alarm management commands
config transferlog server
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
8728 Issue 1
Default
Entry required
The hostkey parameter provisions the host public keys used for host authentication. The
number of keys configurable per host is defined by the available key indices.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings or spaces only for all key entries - no host key
authentication will be applied.
If at least one key is provisioned, all provisioned keys can be used for user authentication.
Provisioning a second key allows key rotation without service interruption. After a new key is
deployed on server side the old one should be removed. A normal secure configuration applies
one key only.
The format of the string of the ssh key supported is the OpenSSH key format which can be
generated by the ssh-keygen command - "<type name> <base64 coded key string>
[<comment>]" (Ref RFC 4253). The content of the ".pub" file can be directly copied.
The host name, ip address and port, will be taken from the provisioned ip address and port
number.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring>) deletes the provisioned key and removes it
from the system.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin
security ssh" command.
Note: The hostkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.
ip
Syntax
ip [<ip-address>]
Values
<ipv4-address> - IPv4 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”
<ipv6-address> - IPv6 address as defined in Appendix A, “Reference tables”
Default
0.0.0.0
Specifies the IP address of the log server. Follow this keyword with a valid IP address. Without
an address the command displays the current IP address of the transfer log remote host.
Note: See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for allowed IPv4 or IPv6 format.
port
Syntax
port [<port>]

Values

Specifies the TCP port used to access the log server.
Note: The port setting is ignored if protocol is set to ftp.
Note: If the protocol setting is changed, then the port will be set to the default value for the
new protocol setting. Therefore, it is recommended that protocol be set before setting port.
Enter the keyword without option to display the current setting. If the protocol is set to ftp or
not yet provisioned, the current setting is displayed as NA, meaning "Not Applicable."
Warning: Changing the port number may block the service in case the new port is not open by

Syntax

Values

Specifies the type of protocol used to access the log server.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
Note: ftp or http can only be provisioned if admin ui mode is normal.
Warning: If the ui mode is changed, the protocol and port settings remain the same, even if
the protocol is not allowed with the new ui mode (for example, change from normal to
encrypted with protocol ftp). Furthermore, as stated in the description of the config ui mode
command, changing the ui mode will also reset the Access Control List to the system default
settings. Therefore, if you change the ui mode, ensure after changing the ui mode that the
combination of protocol, port, and ACL settings allow traffic for the service.
Restrictions
The protocols http and https are not available when the controller in a PSS-32, PSS-16, or
PSS-4 main shelf is an EC card.

8730 Issue 1
sshprivkey
Syntax
sshprivkey <keystring> [<password>]
Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 character SSH key string.
"" - to clear the string.
Default
Entry required
Values
For <password>:
<string> - UTF-8 string, 1..64 characters in double quotes.
"" - empty string for no password.
Default
""
The sshprivkey parameter provisions the user private keys used for user authentication on
server side.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings - no public user key authentication will be applied.
The format of the string of the SSH key supported is the OpenSSH private key PEM file format
which can be generated by the ssh-keygen command
The format looks like:
"-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----b3BlbnNzaC1rZXktdjEAAA ...
RAQ0VDMi04MS0yAQIDBA==-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----"
The key must be surrounded by quotation marks.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring> = "") deletes the provisioned key and
removes it from the system.
The private key can be protected by a password, which is needed by the system for decryption.
Following behavior of this parameter applies:
• If a password is provided, the key is password or pass phrase protected. If a pass
phrase contains spaces, it must be surrounded by quotation marks.
• If an empty string is provided, the key is not password protected. Empty string means: ""
is provided.
• If no password string is provided, the system asks for a password. If in this case ENTER
is typed without typing a password or pass phrase the key is not password protected.
If the sshprivkey parameter will be typed in without a value, then the fingerprint of the currently

provisioned key will be shown.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin

Note: The sshprivkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.
userid
Syntax
userid [<string>]
Values
<string> - 1..32 characters for existing userid on the remote server

Specifies the user identification for accessing the remote server. After the userid is entered, you

8.23 config alm asap
8.23.1 Purpose
This command configures the alarm severity assignment profiles (ASAP). ASAPs are used to set
the severity of alarms. The system supports ASAP types corresponding to the supported entity
types with each ASAP type comprising the severity settings for the alarms on an entity type. A set of
system defined ASAPs is available by default, to support alarm severity settings for basic
configurations. You can create additional ASAPs of any ASAP type up to a limit of 251 user defined
ASAPs.
This command can be used to:
• create user defined ASAPs
• configure the alarm severity settings in user defined ASAPs
• configure the ASAP's name
• delete user defined ASAPs
• configure the ASAPs to be used as default
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
8.23.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Settings affect the alarming behavior
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
8.23.3 Input Format
config alm asap
create
attr
name
delete
default
8.23.4 Input Parameters
Sub-command: create
For additional details, see "config alm asap create" command
Sub-command: attr
For additional details, see "config alm asap attr" command
Sub-command: name
For additional details, see "config alm asap name" command
Alarm management commands
config alm asap

8.24.1 Purpose
This command creates a new alarm severity assignment profile. The command allows you to
specify:

• The user label,
• The ASAP template
to be used for the new ASAP.
You can create ASAPs of any supported type up to the limit of 251 new ASAPs in total.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Default
Entry required
Specifies the type of the ASAP to be created.
name
Syntax
name <string>
Values
<string> - 1..40 character string consisting of alphanumeric characters and dashes ("-").
The first character must be alphanumeric.
Default
"lbl-<pftype>-<ID>"
Specifies a name for the ASAP.
The default ASAP name is of the form "lbl-<pftype>-<ID>, where ID is a number assigned by
the system in the range 5...255, which is unique for the ASAPs of one profile type.
Restrictions
The ASAP name must be unique within the system. Any existing ASAP of any type must not
have the specified ASAP name. The prefix "lbl-" is reserved for the system and cannot be
used for user created names.
clonefrom
Syntax
clonefrom <ASAP-name>
Values
lbl-<pftype>-none - name of the system defined ASAP for the profile type with NR (Not
Reported) for all conditions
lbl-<pftype>-sysdflt - name of the system defined ASAP for the profile type with General
severity defaults
lbl-<pftype>-notprimary - name of the system defined ASAP for the profile type with not
primary conditions disabled
lbl-<pftype>-ferfais - name of the system defined ASAP for the profile type with FERF and
AIS conditions disabled
lbl-<pftype>-all - name of the system defined ASAP for the profile type with all conditions
enabled
Default
name of the system Default Severities ASAP, "lbl-<pftype>-sysdflt"
Specifies the ASAP which shall be used as source for the creation of the new ASAP. The new
ASAP is created as a copy of the specified ASAP.
Alarm management commands
config alm asap create
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
8764 Issue 1
NOTE: For non-transmission pftypes BITS, COM, ENV, SYNC, and TOD only "none" and
"sysdflt" are supported.
default
Syntax
default <value>
Values
yes - ASAP shall be the default for the profile type
no - ASAP is not the default
Default
no
Specifies if the ASAP shall be used as default for the profile type.
If the parameter is specified as yes, then the newly created ASAP gets the default parameter
set to yes while the default parameter of the previous default ASAP is set to no.
8.24.5 Examples
The following command creates an ASAP of type OTU. The ASAP will be created as a copy of the
OTU system default ASAP with a system assigned name e.g. "lbl-otu-7".
# config alm asap create otu
The following command creates an ASAP of type ODUTCM with the name "newtcmasap" as copy
of the system defined ODUTCM ASAP ALL (has all alarms enabled) and defines it as default ASAP
for TCM entities:
# config alm asap create odutcm name newtcmasap clonefrom lbl-odutcm-all default yes

8.28 config alm asap default
8.28.1 Purpose
This command defines the ASAP specified by <name> as default ASAP for the associated ASAP
type. Note that each ASAP is associated with one unique ASAP type.
When an entity is created with no ASAP specified, the default ASAP of the ASAP type associated
with the created entity will be assigned.
For an ASAP type there can be only one default ASAP. Initially the default ASAP for all ASAP types
is set to lbl-<pftype>-sysdflt.
The command sets the "default" parameter of the specified ASAP to "yes", while the previous
"default" ASAP gets the default parameter set to "no".
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
8.28.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Settings affect the alarming behavior
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
8.28.3 Input Format
config alm asap default <name>
8.28.4 Input Parameters
<name>
Values
<ASAP-name> - name of the ASAP to be set as default
Default
Entry required
Specifies the ASAP which shall be defined as default.
System defined and user defined ASAPs can be defined as default.
8.28.5 Examples
The following command defines the ASAP "lbl-odu-notprimary" (which is of type ODU) as default
ASAP for the ASAPs of type ODU. Note that the ASAP "lbl-odu-notprimary" is one of the system
defined ASAPs.
# config alm asap default lbl-odu-notprimary

show alm asap

8.33 show alm asap default
8.33.1 Purpose
Use this command to list the default ASAP of the specified type.
The output displays the name of the default ASAP for the specified type.
If the command is used with the input parameter "details", the output lists in addition the severity
settings in the default ASAP.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
8.33.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
8.33.3 Input Format
show alm asap default <pftype> [details]

9.2 config encrypt <facility-type> <facility-aid> encryptpm
9.2.1 Purpose
This command configures Encryption group (ENCRYPT) Performance Monitoring options on the
specified facility.
Use this command to:
• Clear the raw counts for this PM group
• Configure the 15-minute and 1-day bins
• Assign a Threshold Crossing Alert profile to this facility
• Enable/disable PM
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
9.2.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Modifies performance monitoring configuration
Access Levels: Crypto
9.2.3 Input Format
config encrypt <facility-type> <facility-aid> encryptpm
clearraw
<interval> {bins | clear | profile}
pmmode
9.2.4 Input Parameters
<facility-type>
Identifies the facility against which this command is executed. For applicable facilities see
facility specific commands.
<facility-aid>
Specifies the aid of the facility. For applicable facilities see facility specific commands
clearraw
Clears the raw counts for this PM group.
<interval>
Values
0 - for 15-minute interval
1 - for 1-day interval
Specifies the interval to be configured.
Performance monitoring commands
config encrypt <facility-type> <facility-aid> encryptpm
Nokia 1830 PSS
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Release 24.12
December 2024
8792 Issue 1
bins
Syntax
bins [<number-of-bins>]
Values
1..8 - for 1-day bins.
1..33 - for 15-minute bins.
Default
8 for 1-day bins.
33 for 15-minute bins.
Specifies the number of bins. Enter this keyword followed by an integer value for the number of
bins. Active statistics are placed into bin 0. At the end of the interval, the statistics are rolled into
subsequent bins, such that the contents of bin 0 are stored in bin 1, bin 1 in bin 2, and so on.
The contents of the last bin are purged.
clear
Clears the data for the parameters in the current bin.
profile
Syntax
profile [<profile-id>]
Values
1..8
0 - to disable all TCAs
* - for list.
Default
8
Specifies the profile identifier. Enter this keyword followed by an integer value for the profile
identifier.
pmmode
Syntax
pmmode [enabled | disabled]
Values
enabled - activate Encryption group (ENCRYPT) PM monitoring (15-minute and 1-day)
disabled - de-activate Encryption group (ENCRYPT) PM monitoring (15-minute and 1-day)
Default
Disabled
Performance monitoring commands

Encryption group (ENCRYPT) PM monitoring (15-minute and 1-day) mode on the addressed

# config encrypt otuodu4 1/2/L1 encryptpm pmmode enabled

specified port.

all S13X400 subtypes, all S2AD200 subtypes, all S5AD400 subtypes, all S6AD600 subtypes unless
further restriction is clarified for individual sub-command or parameter within this command.

9.5 config interface <card> <port-aid> pm csr
9.5.1 Purpose
This command configures the cycle slips ratio (CSR) Performance Monitoring options on the card.
Use this command to:
• Clear the raw counts for this PM group
• Configure the 15-minute and 1-day bins
• Enable/Disable PM
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
9.5.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Modifies performance monitoring configuration
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
9.5.3 Input Format
config interface <card> <port-aid> pm csr
clearraw
<interval> {bins | clear}
pmmode
9.5.4 Input Parameters
<card>
Identifies the card against which this command is executed. For applicable cards see card
specific commands.
<port-aid>
Specifies the aid of the interface. For applicable interfaces see card specific commands.
clearraw
Clears the raw counts for this PM group.
Restrictions
The parameter is not applicable for interfaces on CSW shelf.
<interval>
Values
0 - for 15-minute interval
1 - for 1-day interval
Specifies the interval to be configured.
Performance monitoring commands
config interface <card> <port-aid> pm csr
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 8801
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
bins
Syntax
bins [<number-of-bins>]
Values
1..8 - for 1-day bins.
1..33 - for 15-minute bins.
Default
8 for 1-day bins.
33 for 15-minute bins.
Specifies the number of bins. Enter this keyword followed by an integer value for the number of
bins. Active statistics are placed into bin 0. At the end of the interval, the statistics are rolled into
subsequent bins, such that the contents of bin 0 are stored in bin 1, bin 1 in bin 2, and so on.
The contents of the last bin are purged.
clear
Clears the data for the parameters in the current bin.
pmmode
Syntax
pmmode [<value>]
Values
enabled - activate cycle slips ratio group PM monitoring (15-minute and 1-day)
disabled - de-activate cycle slips ratio group PM monitoring (15-minute and 1-day)
Default
enabled
Received cycle slips ratio (CSR) group PM monitoring (15-minute and 1-day) mode on the
addressed facility. Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
9.5.5 Examples
# config interface d5x500 1/3/L1 pm csr 1 bins 6
9.5.6 Related Commands
show interface <card> <port-aid> pm csr
Performance monitoring commands
config interface <card> <port-aid> pm csr

bins
Syntax

bins
Syntax
bins [<value>]
Values
1..8 - Number for 1-day bins.
1..33 - Number for 15-minute bins.
Default
8 for 1-day bins.
33 for 15-minute bins.
Specifies the number of bins. Enter this keyword followed by an integer value for the number of
bins. Active statistics are placed into bin 0. At the end of the interval, the statistics are rolled into
subsequent bins, such that the contents of bin 0 are stored in bin 1, bin 1 in bin 2, and so on.
The contents of the last bin are purged.
Note the bins shall be set after <interval> is set.
Restrictions
The number of bins is not configurable for interfaces on CSW shelves.
clear
Clears the data for the parameters in the current bin.
Note the clear shall be performed after <interval> is set.
profile
Syntax
profile [<value>]
Values
1..8
0 - to disable all TCAs
* - for list
Default
8
Specifies the profile identifier. Enter this keyword followed by an integer value for the profile
identifier, or enter * for a list, or without additional input to display the current profile identifier.
Note the profile shall be set after <interval> is set.

9.45 config profile pm
9.45.1 Purpose
This command configures the performance monitoring threshold alarm (TCA) profiles used for
performance monitoring. You can configure up to eight profiles for each profile type, each having
different threshold levels. For example, you can configure profiles that raise threshold alarms at
different levels, with each profile representing a different service requirement in the network. After
provisioning the profiles, you can configure a card or interface to use one of the profiles.
Use this command to access subcommands for provisioning TCA profiles per profile type.
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
9.45.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Modifies performance monitoring configuration
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner

9.46 config profile pm <entity>
9.46.1 Purpose
This command configures the performance monitoring threshold alarm (TCA) profiles used for a
performance monitoring entity. You can configure up to eight profiles, each having different
threshold levels. For example, you can configure profiles that raise threshold alarms at different
levels, with each profile representing a different service requirement in the network. After
provisioning the profiles, you can configure the entity to use one of the profiles according to the
service requirements.
Use this command to:
• Specify a text description for a profile

This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.

9.47 config sync <shelf-aid> <syncentity-aid> pm treffoff
9.47.1 Purpose
This command configures the timing reference frequency offset (TREFFOFF) Performance
Monitoring options on the shelf synchronization clock.
Use this command to:
• Clear the raw counts for this PM group
• Configure the 15-minute and 1-day bins
• Assign a Threshold Crossing Alert profile to this interface
• Enable/Disable PM
This command applies to
• 1830 PSS-8 shelf types with 8DC30T power filter.
• 1830 PSS-16II shelf types with 16DC65T power filter.
Refer to Appendix A, “Reference tables” for shelf/circuit pack/port applicability.
9.47.2 Command Access Level
Impact: Modifies performance monitoring configuration
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
9.47.3 Input Format
config sync <shelf-aid> <syncentity-aid> pm treffoff
clearraw
<interval> {bins | clear | profile}
pmmode
9.47.4 Input Parameters
<shelf-aid>
Values
{1..24} - allowed universal shelf number range
Default
Entry required
Specifies the shelf number of an universal shelf for which the synchronization options shall be
configured.
See Appendix A, “Reference tables” for valid numeric <shelf-aid> ranges for each supported
shelf type.

3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
<syncentity-aid>
Values
lineref{0..4} - alternate timing reference
sync0 - active timing reference
Default
Entry required
Configures the timing reference synchronization type.
clearraw
Clear the raw counts for this PM group.
<interval>
Values
0 - for 15-minute interval
1 - for 1-day interval
Specifies the interval to be configured.
bins
Syntax
bins [<number-of-bins>]
Values
1..8 - for 1-day bins.
1..33 - for 15-minute bins.
Default
8 for 1-day bins.
33 for 15-minute bins.
Specifies the number of bins. Enter this keyword followed by an integer value for the number of
bins. Active statistics are placed into bin 0. At the end of the interval, the statistics are rolled into
subsequent bins, such that the contents of bin 0 are stored in bin 1, bin 1 in bin 2, and so on.
The contents of the last bin are purged.
clear
Clears the data for the parameters in the current bin for the specified interval.
profile
Syntax
profile [<profile-id>]

9.54 config sync <shelf-aid> ptp clock1 <port-aid> pm ptoffatt
9.54.1 Purpose
This command configures the PTP time OFFset Alternate TimeTransmitter comparison
(PTOFFATT) Performance Monitoring options on the shelf PTP port.
Use this command for each port configured with portDS.MonitorReceiver TRUE within the ITU-T
G.8275.1 profile version 2.4 to:
• Clear the raw counts for this PM group
• Configure the 15-minute and 1-day bins
• Assign a Threshold Crossing Alert profile to this interface
• Enable/Disable PM
This command applies to all cards supporting PTP with ITU-T profile version 2.4, and when ITU-T
profile is selected.
This command applies to T-BC PTP clock types, i.e., when clockMode is T-BC.
This command applies to non-virtual ports only.

8960 Issue 1
9.62 config transferpmserver
9.62.1 Purpose
This command configures attributes of remote file servers for the Performance Management (PM)
data bulk file transfer. PM data bulk file transfer is an automated process that every 15 minutes
(+offset) will transfer the current PM data to one or more servers.
This command is used to:
• Create up to four server definitions which will receive performance monitoring (PM) data from the
NE to which they are connected. If enabled, the PM data is transferred automatically by the NE
to a specified path on the server when the 15-min or 1-day bin data becomes available.
• Configure per-server parameters to control the behavior of the transfer of data from the NE to
the server.
• Configure per-server parameters like IPaddress, userID, etc.
• Delete a server definition that has been created previously and configured to receive the PM
data.
9.62.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner
9.62.3 Input Format
config transferpmserver <name>
control
create
delete
detail
offset
previous15minbin
previous1daybin
server
9.62.4 Input Parameters
<name>
Values
<name> - {1..32} ASCII or UTF-8 character string
Default
Entry required
Performance monitoring commands
config transferpmserver
Nokia 1830 PSS
Release 24.12
December 2024
Issue 1 8961
© 2024 Nokia. Nokia Confidential Information
Use subject to agreed restrictions on disclosure and use.
3KC-71311-RBAA-THZZA
Specifies the unique identifier string for a destination server. Modification of server parameters
is only possible if the server has already been created.
Note: Amaximum of 4 destination servers are allowed for the PM bulk file transfer.
control
Syntax
control [<value>]
Values
abort
start
stop
Default
stop
Configures the destination control parameter with the option to either start, stop, or abort the file
transfer mechanism.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
Abort - If set, stop any file transfer operation that is in-progress immediately. Should also be
used prior to deletion of a server that has a file transfer in progress. The file transfer will not
start until the user specifically sets the option again to start.
Start - If set, auto PM file upload will commence after the next 15-min/1-day timer expires.
Needs to be specifically set after an abort or stop option has been issued.
Stop - If set, auto PM file upload will not start. This option can be used in case the user wants to
stop the file transfer mechanism. Any ongoing file transfer will not be stopped and will continue
till completion. Any new file transfers will not start until the user specifically sets the option again
to start.
create
Use this option to first create a server with a unique identifier (<name>). The command can
then be used to configure the details of the created server.
delete
Deletes the identifier for a destination server that has been configured for the PM bulk file
transfer.
Note: Deletion of destination server is not allowed when PM transfer is in-progress. It should be
denied with an error message.
detail
Displays the attributes of the specified server that has been configured for the PM bulk file
transfer.
Output details can be found under command "show transferpmserver".
Performance monitoring commands

8962 Issue 1
offset
Syntax
offset [<value>]
Values
0..600 - seconds
Default
0
Configures the file transfer time offset in seconds, where the offset is against the time when a
bin rolls over on the NE (either 15min or 1day). This effectively delays the transfer of the files to
the server by the time specified by the offset.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
previous15minbin
Syntax
previous15minbin [<value>]
Values
0..8
Default
0
Configures the number of previous 15min PM bin files (history bin) that can be transferred to
the server. A value of 0 implies that the current 15min PM history bin will be transferred, a value
of 8 means that the current 15min PM history bin along with eight older 15min PM history bins
will be transferred to the server. The values 1-8 are a one-time-only transfer option that is used
to retrieve previous history bins. After this one-time-only transfer of multiple bins,
previous15minbin will automatically set to the default value of 0.
Enter this keyword without option to display the current setting.
Note:
• When the previous15minbin parameter is configured, the NE shall transfer only the bins
that have valid PM data as part of the file transfer. For example, at the time of command
execution, if the previous15minbin value is set to 5, but only 3 15-min bins with valid PM
data are present on the NE, the NE shall send only these 3 completed bins, and then
when the next bin rollover occurs, 4 completed bins (including the previously sent 3 bins)
shall be transferred. The value of the parameter shall be reset to 0 only after all the bins
have been successfully transferred.
• The file transfer will stop when the file upload has failed for 9 consecutive times.
• To restart the file upload again, we need to delete the server identifier and recreate the
same. NE reboot, NE warm/cold reset or redundancy side switch will also restart the file
upload to happen again if the control command is already set to start.
Performance monitoring commands

hostkey
Syntax
hostkey <keyindex> <keystring>
Values
For <keyindex>:
{1,2} - index of the public host key
Default
Entry required
Values
For <keystring>:
<string> - 1..4000 characters containing the SSH key string in OpenSSH format.
"" - to clear the string.
Default
Entry required
Configures the host public keys used for host authentication. The number of keys configurable
per host is defined by the available key indices.
If no keys are provisioned - empty strings or spaces only for all key entries - no host key
authentication will be applied.
If at least one key is provisioned, all provisioned keys can be used for user authentication.
Provisioning a second key allows key rotation without service interruption. After a new key is
deployed on server side the old one should be removed. A normal secure configuration applies
one key only.
The format of the string of the ssh key supported is the OpenSSH key format which can be
generated by the ssh-keygen command - "<type name> <base64 coded key string>
[<comment>]" (Ref RFC 4253). The content of the ".pub" file can be directly copied.
The host name, ip address and port, will be taken from the provisioned ip address and port
number.
The maximum accepted string length is 4000 characters.
The input of an empty string for a key (<keystring>) deletes the provisioned key and removes it
from the system.
This parameter does not apply for legacy Equipment Controllers (EC).
Note: Only key types which are supported by the NE can be provisioned. See "config admin
security ssh" command.
Note: The hostkey applies for the SFTP protocol only.

Specifies the path name on the server where the PM files will be transferred by the NE when

is a PATH and FILENAME.

<bin>.{inprogress&inprogresscompleted}
<FILENAME> = a name to prepend to every file. See the "path" parameter to determine if there
is a filename and its value.
<NE-Type> = PSS
<DATE-TIME> = YYYY_MM_DD_HH-mm (Year, Month, Day, Hour(0..23), Minute)
Note that mm (minute) could be a time after the 15 minute epoch (0/15/30/45), e.g., 47 instead
of 45 due to the bin rollover time.

Values

Specifies the interval to be configured.

detail

<bin>
Values
0..7 - range of 1-day bin
0..32 - range of 15-minute bin
Displays collected data for the specified bin.
pmmode
Displays the PM mode.

<interval>
Values
0 - for 15-minute interval
1 - for 1-day interval
Specifies the interval to be displayed.
clear
Clears the data for the parameters in the current bin.
Note the clear shall be performed after <interval> is configured
detail
Displays performance monitoring configuration values for the specified interval, including
Number of Bins and assigned TCA profile ID.
<bin>
Values
0..7 - range of 1-day bin
0..32 - range of 15-minute bin
Specified bin number to display the collected data.
Note the <bin> shall be entered after <interval> is configured
pmmode
Values
enabled - ODU PM monitoring (15-minute and 1-day) on this facility is enabled
disabled - ODU PM monitoring (15-minute and 1-day) on this facility is disabled
Displays the PM mode.
Restrictions
The parameter only applies to the following cards:
• all DSW cards
• all CSW cards
• 12P120 card
• 12P120S card
• all D6AD2T4 subtypes
• all S2AD200 subtypes
• all S5AD400 subtypes
• all S6AD600 subtypes
Performance monitoring commands
show odunim <facility-type> <odu-aid> pm odurx

9.103 show odunim <facility-type> <odu-aid> pm odutx
9.103.1 Purpose
This command displays the ODUTX performance monitoring attributes for an ODUNIM facility.
Use this command to:
• Clear PM data for a specified interval
• Display the performance monitoring data for the specified bin
• Display the PM mode
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
9.103.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
9.103.3 Input Format
show odunim <facility-type> <odu-aid> pm odutx
clearraw
raw
<interval> {clear | detail | <bin>}
pmmode
9.103.4 Input Parameters
<facility-type>
Specifies ODUNIM facility type. For applicable facility types see facility specific commands.
<odu-aid>
Specifies the AID to identify/address the ODUNIM facility. For applicable facility AIDs see facility
specific commands.
clearraw
Clears the raw counts for this PM group.
raw
Displays the raw counts for this PM group.
<interval>
Values
0 - for 15-minute interval
1 - for 1-day interval
Specifies the interval to be displayed.
Performance monitoring commands
show odunim <facility-type> <odu-aid> pm odutx

9.104 show oduptf <facility-type> <oduptf-aid> pm odurx
9.104.1 Purpose
This command displays the ODURX performance monitoring attributes for an ODUPTF facility.
Use this command to:
• Clear PM data for a specified interval
• Display the performance monitoring data for the specified bin
• Display the PM mode
This command applies to all 1830 PSS shelf types.
9.104.2 Command Access Level
Impact: None
Access Levels: Administrator, Provisioner, Observer
9.104.3 Input Format
show oduptf <facility-type> <oduptf-aid> pm odurx
clearraw
raw
<interval> {clear | detail | <bin>}
pmmode
9.104.4 Input Parameters
<facility-type>
Specifies ODUPTF facility type. For applicable facility types see facility specific commands.
<oduptf-aid>
Specifies the AID to identify/address the ODUPTF facility. For applicable facility AIDs see facility
specific commands.
clearraw
Clears the raw counts for this PM group.
Restrictions
The parameter is not applicable for interfaces on CSW shelf.
raw
Displays the raw counts for this PM group.
Restrictions
The parameter is not applicable for interfaces on CSW shelf.
